title: 動物農莊
author: George Orwell 喬治·奧威爾
description: 《Animal Farm》(1945)。曼諾農場的動物趕走酗酒的瓊斯先生,建立「動物主義」的理想社會,卻在豬領袖拿破崙的權術下一步步變質:「所有動物一律平等,但有些動物比其他動物更平等」。一則諷刺極權政治的經典寓言。英文原文對照廣東話/普通話翻譯。

chapters.title: Chapter I 第一章:老少校的夢

passages.original: Mr. Jones, of the Manor Farm, had locked the hen-houses for the night, but was too drunk to remember to shut the pop-holes.
passages.vernacular: 曼諾農場嘅瓊斯先生已經把雞舍鎖好過夜,但佢醉得忘咗關上小門洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 曼諾農場的瓊斯先生已經把雞舍鎖好過夜,但他醉得忘了關上小門洞。

passages.original: With the ring of light from his lantern dancing from side to side, he lurched across the yard, kicked off his boots at the back door, drew himself a last glass of beer from the barrel in the scullery, and made his way up to bed, where Mrs. Jones was already snoring.
passages.vernacular: 佢提燈嘅光圈左右跳動,佢踉踉蹌蹌地穿過院子,喺後門踢掉靴子,從洗滌間嘅桶裡畀自己倒咗最後一杯啤酒,然後走上樓去瞓覺,瓊斯太太已經喺嗰度打住鼾喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他提燈的光圈左右跳動,他踉踉蹌蹌地穿過院子,在後門踢掉靴子,從洗滌間的桶裡給自己倒了最後一杯啤酒,然後走上樓去睡覺,瓊斯太太已經在那裡打著鼾了。

passages.original: As soon as the light in the bedroom went out there was a stirring and a fluttering all through the farm buildings.
passages.vernacular: 臥室嘅燈一熄,整個農場嘅建築裡就響起一陣騷動同撲翅聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 臥室的燈一熄,整個農場的建築裡就響起一陣騷動和撲翅聲。

passages.original: Word had gone round during the day that old Major, the prize Middle White boar, had had a strange dream on the previous night and wished to communicate it to the other animals.
passages.vernacular: 白天已經傳開話,講嗰頭獲獎嘅中白豬老少校前一晚做咗一個奇怪嘅夢,想把佢告訴其他動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白天已經傳開話,說那頭獲獎的中白豬老少校前一晚做了一個奇怪的夢,想把它告訴其他動物。

passages.original: It had been agreed that they should all meet in the big barn as soon as Mr. Jones was safely out of the way.
passages.vernacular: 大家已經商定,只要瓊斯先生安全地不喺,佢哋就全都到大穀倉去集合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家已經商定,只要瓊斯先生安全地不在,他們就全都到大穀倉去集合。

passages.original: Old Major (so he was always called, though the name under which he had been exhibited was Willingdon Beauty) was so highly regarded on the farm that everyone was quite ready to lose an hour’s sleep in order to hear what he had to say.
passages.vernacular: 老少校(大家一向咁樣叫佢,雖然佢參展時用嘅名字係威靈頓美人)喺農場上咁受尊敬,以致每個動物都樂意少瞓一小時嚟聽佢要講嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老少校(大家一向這樣叫他,雖然他參展時用的名字是威靈頓美人)在農場上那麼受尊敬,以致每個動物都樂意少睡一小時來聽他要說的話。

passages.original: At one end of the big barn, on a sort of raised platform, Major was already ensconced on his bed of straw, under a lantern which hung from a beam.
passages.vernacular: 喺大穀倉嘅一端,喺一個類似高台嘅地方,少校已經安穩地坐喺佢嘅稻草床上,頭上有一盞掛喺橫樑上嘅燈籠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在大穀倉的一端,在一個類似高台的地方,少校已經安穩地坐在他的稻草床上,頭上有一盞掛在橫樑上的燈籠。

passages.original: He was twelve years old and had lately grown rather stout, but he was still a majestic-looking pig, with a wise and benevolent appearance in spite of the fact that his tushes had never been cut.
passages.vernacular: 佢十二歲,最近長得相當胖,但佢仍然係一頭外表威嚴嘅豬,儘管佢嘅獠牙從未被剪過,仍然顯得睿智而仁慈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他十二歲,最近長得相當胖,但他仍然是一頭外表威嚴的豬,儘管他的獠牙從未被剪過,仍然顯得睿智而仁慈。

passages.original: Before long the other animals began to arrive and make themselves comfortable after their different fashions.
passages.vernacular: 不久,其他動物開始陸續到來,各自以不同嘅方式舒舒服服地坐好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久,其他動物開始陸續到來,各自以不同的方式舒舒服服地坐好。

passages.original: First came the three dogs, Bluebell, Jessie, and Pincher, and then the pigs, who settled down in the straw immediately in front of the platform.
passages.vernacular: 最先嚟嘅係三條狗,藍鈴、潔西和平徹,然後係豬,佢哋喺高台正前方嘅稻草裡安頓下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最先來的是三條狗,藍鈴、潔西和平徹,然後是豬,它們在高台正前方的稻草裡安頓下來。

passages.original: The hens perched themselves on the window-sills, the pigeons fluttered up to the rafters, the sheep and cows lay down behind the pigs and began to chew the cud.
passages.vernacular: 母雞棲喺窗台上,鴿子撲騰住飛上椽子,羊同牛躺喺豬後面,開始反芻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 母雞棲在窗台上,鴿子撲騰著飛上椽子,羊和牛躺在豬後面,開始反芻。

passages.original: The two cart-horses, Boxer and Clover, came in together, walking very slowly and setting down their vast hairy hoofs with great care lest there should be some small animal concealed in the straw.
passages.vernacular: 兩匹拉車嘅馬,拳擊手同三葉草,一起進嚟,走得好慢,把巨大多毛嘅蹄子好小心地放下,生怕稻草裡藏住乜嘢小動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩匹拉車的馬,拳擊手和三葉草,一起進來,走得很慢,把巨大多毛的蹄子非常小心地放下,生怕稻草裡藏著什麼小動物。

passages.original: Clover was a stout motherly mare approaching middle life, who had never quite got her figure back after her fourth foal.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草係一匹粗壯、有母親氣質嘅母馬,已近中年,生咗第四胎後始終冇完全恢復身材。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草是一匹粗壯、有母親氣質的母馬,已近中年,生了第四胎後始終沒完全恢復身材。

passages.original: Boxer was an enormous beast, nearly eighteen hands high, and as strong as any two ordinary horses put together.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手係一頭巨大嘅野獸,身高近十八掌,力氣相當於任何兩匹普通嘅馬加喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手是一頭巨大的野獸,身高近十八掌,力氣相當於任何兩匹普通的馬加在一起。

passages.original: A white stripe down his nose gave him a somewhat stupid appearance, and in fact he was not of first-rate intelligence, but he was universally respected for his steadiness of character and tremendous powers of work.
passages.vernacular: 佢鼻子上嘅一道白條使佢顯得有些愚蠢,事實上佢嘅智力都唔係一流嘅,但佢嘅性格穩重同驚人嘅工作能力使佢受到普遍尊敬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他鼻子上的一道白條使他顯得有些愚蠢,事實上他的智力也不是一流的,但他的性格穩重和驚人的工作能力使他受到普遍尊敬。

passages.original: After the horses came Muriel, the white goat, and Benjamin, the donkey.
passages.vernacular: 馬之後來嘅係白山羊繆麗兒同驢子班傑明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬之後來的是白山羊繆麗兒和驢子班傑明。

passages.original: Benjamin was the oldest animal on the farm, and the worst tempered.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明係農場上年紀最大嘅動物,脾氣都最壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明是農場上年紀最大的動物,脾氣也最壞。

passages.original: He seldom talked, and when he did, it was usually to make some cynical remark--for instance, he would say that God had given him a tail to keep the flies off, but that he would sooner have had no tail and no flies.
passages.vernacular: 佢好少講話,講嘅時候通常係為了發表啲憤世嫉俗嘅話——比如,佢會講上帝畀咗佢一條尾巴係用嚟趕蒼蠅嘅,但佢寧願冇尾巴都冇蒼蠅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很少說話,說的時候通常是為了發表一些憤世嫉俗的話——比如,他會說上帝給了他一條尾巴是用來趕蒼蠅的,但他寧願沒有尾巴也沒有蒼蠅。

passages.original: Alone among the animals on the farm he never laughed.
passages.vernacular: 喺農場嘅所有動物中,只有佢從不笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在農場的所有動物中,只有他從不笑。

passages.original: If asked why, he would say that he saw nothing to laugh at.
passages.vernacular: 如果問佢點解,佢會講佢睇不出有乜嘢可笑嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果問他為什麼,他會說他看不出有什麼可笑的。

passages.original: Nevertheless, without openly admitting it, he was devoted to Boxer; the two of them usually spent their Sundays together in the small paddock beyond the orchard, grazing side by side and never speaking.
passages.vernacular: 然而,佢雖冇公開承認,卻對拳擊手忠心耿耿;佢哋兩個通常喺果園外面嘅小牧場裡一起度過星期天,肩並肩食草,從不講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,他雖沒有公開承認,卻對拳擊手忠心耿耿;他們兩個通常在果園外面的小牧場裡一起度過星期天,肩並肩吃草,從不說話。

passages.original: The two horses had just lain down when a brood of ducklings, which had lost their mother, filed into the barn, cheeping feebly and wandering from side to side to find some place where they would not be trodden on.
passages.vernacular: 兩匹馬剛躺下,一窩失去咗母親嘅小鴨子排隊走進穀倉,微弱地啾啾叫住,左右徘徊,尋找一個唔會被踩到嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩匹馬剛躺下,一窩失去了母親的小鴨子排隊走進穀倉,微弱地啾啾叫著,左右徘徊,尋找一個不會被踩到的地方。

passages.original: Clover made a sort of wall round them with her great foreleg, and the ducklings nestled down inside it and promptly fell asleep.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草用佢巨大嘅前腿喺佢哋周圍圍成一道牆,小鴨子哋喺裡面依偎住,即刻瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草用她巨大的前腿在它們周圍圍成一道牆,小鴨子們在裡面依偎著,立刻睡著了。

passages.original: At the last moment Mollie, the foolish, pretty white mare who drew Mr. Jones’s trap, came mincing daintily in, chewing at a lump of sugar.
passages.vernacular: 最後一刻,茉莉,嗰匹愚蠢而漂亮嘅白母馬,拉瓊斯先生輕馬車嘅,嬌滴滴地邁住碎步走進嚟,嚼住一塊方糖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後一刻,茉莉,那匹愚蠢而漂亮的白母馬,拉瓊斯先生輕馬車的,嬌滴滴地邁著碎步走進來,嚼著一塊方糖。

passages.original: She took a place near the front and began flirting her white mane, hoping to draw attention to the red ribbons it was plaited with.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺靠前嘅地方佔咗一個位置,開始甩動佢嘅白鬃毛,希望吸引人哋注意編喺上面嘅紅絲帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在靠前的地方佔了一個位置,開始甩動她的白鬃毛,希望吸引人們注意編在上面的紅絲帶。

passages.original: Last of all came the cat, who looked round, as usual, for the warmest place, and finally squeezed herself in between Boxer and Clover; there she purred contentedly throughout Major’s speech without listening to a word of what he was saying.
passages.vernacular: 最後來嘅係貓,佢像往常一樣四處找最暖同嘅地方,最後擠到拳擊手同三葉草之間;喺嗰度佢心滿意足地呼嚕呼嚕地叫咗整場少校嘅演講,一個字都冇聽佢講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後來的是貓,她像往常一樣四處找最暖和的地方,最後擠到拳擊手和三葉草之間;在那裡她心滿意足地呼嚕呼嚕地叫了整場少校的演講,一個字也沒聽他說什麼。

passages.original: All the animals were now present except Moses, the tame raven, who slept on a perch behind the back door.
passages.vernacular: 而家所有動物都到齊喇,除咗摩西,嗰隻馴養嘅烏鴉,佢瞓喺後門後面嘅一根棲木上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在所有動物都到齊了,除了摩西,那隻馴養的烏鴉,他睡在後門後面的一根棲木上。

passages.original: When Major saw that they had all made themselves comfortable and were waiting attentively, he cleared his throat and began:
passages.vernacular: 少校睇到佢哋都舒服地坐好,專心等待,就清咗清喉嚨,開始講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 少校看到他們都舒服地坐好,專心等待,就清了清喉嚨,開始說:

passages.original: “Comrades, you have heard already about the strange dream that I had last night.
passages.vernacular: 「同志哋,你哋已經聽講過我琴晚做嘅嗰個奇怪嘅夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志們,你們已經聽說過我昨晚做的那個奇怪的夢。

passages.original: But I will come to the dream later.
passages.vernacular: 但我稍後再講呢個夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我稍後再說這個夢。

passages.original: I have something else to say first.
passages.vernacular: 我首先有別嘅話要講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我首先有別的話要說。

passages.original: I do not think, comrades, that I shall be with you for many months longer, and before I die, I feel it my duty to pass on to you such wisdom as I have acquired.
passages.vernacular: 同志哋,我想我唔會再同你哋喺一起好多個月喇,喺我死之前,我覺得有責任把我所獲得嘅智慧傳畀你哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同志們,我想我不會再同你們在一起很多個月了,在我死之前,我覺得有責任把我所獲得的智慧傳給你們。

passages.original: I have had a long life, I have had much time for thought as I lay alone in my stall, and I think I may say that I understand the nature of life on this earth as well as any animal now living.
passages.vernacular: 我活咗好長嘅一生,獨自躺喺我嘅欄裡時有好多時間思考,我想我可以講,我對世上生活本質嘅理解,不亞於而家任何活住嘅動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我活了很長的一生,獨自躺在我的欄裡時有很多時間思考,我想我可以說,我對世上生活本質的理解,不亞於現在任何活著的動物。

passages.original: It is about this that I wish to speak to you.
passages.vernacular: 我想同你哋談嘅就係呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想同你們談的就是這個。

passages.original: “Now, comrades, what is the nature of this life of ours?
passages.vernacular: 「而家,同志哋,我哋呢種生活嘅本質係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,同志們,我們這種生活的本質是什麼?

passages.original: Let us face it: our lives are miserable, laborious, and short.
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋面對佢吧:我哋嘅生活係悲慘、勞累同短暫嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們面對它吧:我們的生活是悲慘、勞累和短暫的。

passages.original: We are born, we are given just so much food as will keep the breath in our bodies, and those of us who are capable of it are forced to work to the last atom of our strength; and the very instant that our usefulness has come to an end we are slaughtered with hideous cruelty.
passages.vernacular: 我哋出生,得到剛好夠維持呼吸嘅食物,我哋中嗰啲有能力嘅被迫工作到最後一絲力氣;而我哋嘅用處一結束,就被殘酷得令人髮指地屠宰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們出生,得到剛好夠維持呼吸的食物,我們中那些有能力的被迫工作到最後一絲力氣;而我們的用處一結束,就被殘酷得令人髮指地屠宰。

passages.original: No animal in England knows the meaning of happiness or leisure after he is a year old.
passages.vernacular: 喺英格蘭,冇一個動物喺一歲以後知道幸福或閒暇嘅意義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在英格蘭,沒有一個動物在一歲以後知道幸福或閒暇的意義。

passages.original: No animal in England is free.
passages.vernacular: 喺英格蘭,冇一個動物係自由嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在英格蘭,沒有一個動物是自由的。

passages.original: The life of an animal is misery and slavery: that is the plain truth.
passages.vernacular: 動物嘅生活係悲慘同奴役:呢個係簡單嘅真相。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物的生活是悲慘和奴役:這是簡單的真相。

passages.original: “But is this simply part of the order of nature?
passages.vernacular: 「但呢僅僅係自然秩序嘅一部分嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但這僅僅是自然秩序的一部分嗎?

passages.original: Is it because this land of ours is so poor that it cannot afford a decent life to those who dwell upon it?
passages.vernacular: 係唔係因為我哋呢片土地太貧瘠,無法畀居住喺上面嘅我哋提供體面嘅生活?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是不是因為我們這片土地太貧瘠,無法給居住在上面的我們提供體面的生活?

passages.original: No, comrades, a thousand times no!
passages.vernacular: 不,同志哋,絕對唔係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,同志們,絕對不是!

passages.original: The soil of England is fertile, its climate is good, it is capable of affording food in abundance to an enormously greater number of animals than now inhabit it.
passages.vernacular: 英格蘭嘅土壤肥沃,氣候良好,佢能夠為比而家居住喺上面嘅數目大得多嘅動物提供豐富嘅食物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 英格蘭的土壤肥沃,氣候良好,它能夠為比現在居住在上面的數目大得多的動物提供豐富的食物。

passages.original: This single farm of ours would support a dozen horses, twenty cows, hundreds of sheep--and all of them living in a comfort and a dignity that are now almost beyond our imagining.
passages.vernacular: 我哋呢一個農場就能養活十二匹馬、二十頭牛、數百隻羊——而且牠哋全都過住我哋而家幾乎想像唔到嘅舒適同尊嚴嘅生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們這一個農場就能養活十二匹馬、二十頭牛、數百隻羊——而且牠們全都過著我們現在幾乎想像不到的舒適和尊嚴的生活。

passages.original: Why then do we continue in this miserable condition?
passages.vernacular: 咁點解我哋仲繼續處於呢種悲慘嘅境地?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼為什麼我們還繼續處於這種悲慘的境地?

passages.original: Because nearly the whole of the produce of our labour is stolen from us by human beings.
passages.vernacular: 因為我哋勞動嘅幾乎全部產品都被人類偷走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我們勞動的幾乎全部產品都被人類偷走了。

passages.original: There, comrades, is the answer to all our problems.
passages.vernacular: 同志哋,呢個就係我哋所有問題嘅答案。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同志們,這就是我們所有問題的答案。

passages.original: It is summed up in a single word--Man.
passages.vernacular: 佢可以用一個詞概括——人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它可以用一個詞概括——人。

passages.original: Man is the only real enemy we have.
passages.vernacular: 人係我哋唯一真正嘅敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人是我們唯一真正的敵人。

passages.original: Remove Man from the scene, and the root cause of hunger and overwork is abolished for ever.
passages.vernacular: 把人從場景中除去,飢餓同過勞嘅根源就永遠消除喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把人從場景中除去,飢餓和過勞的根源就永遠消除了。

passages.original: “Man is the only creature that consumes without producing.
passages.vernacular: 「人係唯一只消費而不生產嘅生物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「人是唯一只消費而不生產的生物。

passages.original: He does not give milk, he does not lay eggs, he is too weak to pull the plough, he cannot run fast enough to catch rabbits.
passages.vernacular: 佢不產奶,佢不下蛋,佢太弱拉不動犁,佢跑得唔夠快抓唔到兔子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不產奶,他不下蛋,他太弱拉不動犁,他跑得不夠快抓不到兔子。

passages.original: Yet he is lord of all the animals.
passages.vernacular: 然而佢係所有動物嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而他是所有動物的主人。

passages.original: He sets them to work, he gives back to them the bare minimum that will prevent them from starving, and the rest he keeps for himself.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓佢哋工作,只還畀佢哋剛好防止餓死嘅最低限度,其餘嘅都留畀自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他讓它們工作,只還給它們剛好防止餓死的最低限度,其餘的都留給自己。

passages.original: Our labour tills the soil, our dung fertilises it, and yet there is not one of us that owns more than his bare skin.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅勞動耕耘土地,我哋嘅糞便使佢肥沃,然而我哋中冇一個擁有嘅比佢赤裸嘅皮膚更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的勞動耕耘土地,我們的糞便使它肥沃,然而我們中沒有一個擁有的比他赤裸的皮膚更多。

passages.original: You cows that I see before me, how many thousands of gallons of milk have you given during this last year?
passages.vernacular: 我喺面前睇到嘅母牛哋,你哋喺過去呢一年裡產咗多少千加侖嘅牛奶?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在面前看到的母牛們,你們在過去這一年裡產了多少千加侖的牛奶?

passages.original: And what has happened to that milk which should have been breeding up sturdy calves?
passages.vernacular: 而嗰啲本該用嚟養育強壯小牛嘅牛奶點樣喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而那些本該用來養育強壯小牛的牛奶怎麼樣了?

passages.original: Every drop of it has gone down the throats of our enemies.
passages.vernacular: 每一滴都流進咗我哋敵人嘅喉嚨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每一滴都流進了我們敵人的喉嚨。

passages.original: And you hens, how many eggs have you laid in this last year, and how many of those eggs ever hatched into chickens?
passages.vernacular: 仲有你哋母雞,你哋喺過去呢一年裡下咗多少蛋,其中又有多少孵成咗小雞?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有你們母雞,你們在過去這一年裡下了多少蛋,其中又有多少孵成了小雞?

passages.original: The rest have all gone to market to bring in money for Jones and his men.
passages.vernacular: 其餘嘅都送到市場上為瓊斯同佢嘅人賺錢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其餘的都送到市場上為瓊斯和他的人賺錢了。

passages.original: And you, Clover, where are those four foals you bore, who should have been the support and pleasure of your old age?
passages.vernacular: 仲有你,三葉草,你生嘅嗰四匹小馬喺邊度,本該係你晚年嘅支柱同快樂?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有你,三葉草,你生的那四匹小馬在哪裡,本該是你晚年的支柱和快樂?

passages.original: Each was sold at a year old--you will never see one of them again.
passages.vernacular: 每一匹都喺一歲時被賣掉——你再都見唔到佢哋中嘅任何一匹喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每一匹都在一歲時被賣掉——你再也見不到它們中的任何一匹了。

passages.original: In return for your four confinements and all your labour in the fields, what have you ever had except your bare rations and a stall?
passages.vernacular: 作為你四次分娩同喺田裡所有勞動嘅回報,你除咗勉強夠食嘅口糧同一個馬廄之外,仲得到過乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 作為你四次分娩和在田裡所有勞動的回報,你除了勉強夠吃的口糧和一個馬廄之外,還得到過什麼?

passages.original: “And even the miserable lives we lead are not allowed to reach their natural span.
passages.vernacular: 「連我哋所過嘅呢種悲慘生活,都不允許達到佢嘅自然壽命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「連我們所過的這種悲慘生活,也不允許達到它的自然壽命。

passages.original: For myself I do not grumble, for I am one of the lucky ones.
passages.vernacular: 我自己不抱怨,因為我係幸運嘅一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己不抱怨,因為我是幸運的一個。

passages.original: I am twelve years old and have had over four hundred children.
passages.vernacular: 我十二歲,有過四百多個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我十二歲,有過四百多個孩子。

passages.original: Such is the natural life of a pig.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係豬嘅自然生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是豬的自然生活。

passages.original: But no animal escapes the cruel knife in the end.
passages.vernacular: 但冇一個動物最終能逃脫殘酷嘅刀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但沒有一個動物最終能逃脫殘酷的刀。

passages.original: You young porkers who are sitting in front of me, every one of you will scream your lives out at the block within a year.
passages.vernacular: 你哋呢啲坐喺我面前嘅小肉豬,你哋每一個都將喺一年之內喺屠宰台上尖叫住送命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們這些坐在我面前的小肉豬,你們每一個都將在一年之內在屠宰台上尖叫著送命。

passages.original: To that horror we all must come--cows, pigs, hens, sheep, everyone.
passages.vernacular: 我哋都必須面對嗰個恐怖——牛、豬、雞、羊,每一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們都必須面對那個恐怖——牛、豬、雞、羊,每一個。

passages.original: Even the horses and the dogs have no better fate.
passages.vernacular: 連馬同狗都冇更好嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連馬和狗也沒有更好的命運。

passages.original: You, Boxer, the very day that those great muscles of yours lose their power, Jones will sell you to the knacker, who will cut your throat and boil you down for the foxhounds.
passages.vernacular: 你,拳擊手,就喺你嗰啲巨大嘅肌肉失去力量嘅嗰一天,瓊斯會把你賣畀屠馬商,佢會割斷你嘅喉嚨,把你煮咗餵獵狐犬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,拳擊手,就在你那些巨大的肌肉失去力量的那一天,瓊斯會把你賣給屠馬商,他會割斷你的喉嚨,把你煮了餵獵狐犬。

passages.original: As for the dogs, when they grow old and toothless, Jones ties a brick round their necks and drowns them in the nearest pond.
passages.vernacular: 至於狗,當佢哋變老掉牙時,瓊斯會喺佢哋嘅脖子上綁一塊磚,把佢哋淹死喺最近嘅池塘裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於狗,當它們變老掉牙時,瓊斯會在它們的脖子上綁一塊磚,把它們淹死在最近的池塘裡。

passages.original: “Is it not crystal clear, then, comrades, that all the evils of this life of ours spring from the tyranny of human beings?
passages.vernacular: 「咁,同志哋,難道唔係明明白白,我哋呢種生活嘅一切罪惡,都來自人類嘅暴政嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,同志們,難道不是明明白白,我們這種生活的一切罪惡,都來自人類的暴政嗎?

passages.original: Only get rid of Man, and the produce of our labour would be our own.
passages.vernacular: 只要除掉人,我哋勞動嘅產品就會係我哋自己嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要除掉人,我們勞動的產品就會是我們自己的。

passages.original: Almost overnight we could become rich and free.
passages.vernacular: 幾乎一夜之間我哋就能變得富有同自由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾乎一夜之間我們就能變得富有和自由。

passages.original: What then must we do?
passages.vernacular: 咁我哋必須點做?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼我們必須怎麼做?

passages.original: Why, work night and day, body and soul, for the overthrow of the human race!
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,日夜工作,全心全意,為推翻人類而奮鬥!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,日夜工作,全心全意,為推翻人類而奮鬥!

passages.original: That is my message to you, comrades: Rebellion!
passages.vernacular: 同志哋,呢個就係我畀你哋嘅訊息:造反!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同志們,這就是我給你們的訊息:造反!

passages.original: I do not know when that Rebellion will come, it might be in a week or in a hundred years, but I know, as surely as I see this straw beneath my feet, that sooner or later justice will be done.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道嗰次造反乜嘢時候會嚟,可能喺一個星期內,都可能喺一百年後,但我知道,就像我知道我睇到腳下嘅稻草一樣肯定,遲早正義會得到伸張。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道那次造反什麼時候會來,可能在一個星期內,也可能在一百年後,但我知道,就像我知道我看到腳下的稻草一樣肯定,遲早正義會得到伸張。

passages.original: Fix your eyes on that, comrades, throughout the short remainder of your lives!
passages.vernacular: 同志哋,喺你哋短暫嘅餘生中,把眼睛盯住嗰個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同志們,在你們短暫的餘生中,把眼睛盯著那個!

passages.original: And above all, pass on this message of mine to those who come after you, so that future generations shall carry on the struggle until it is victorious.
passages.vernacular: 最重要嘅係,把我呢個訊息傳畀你哋之後嘅人,使將來嘅世代繼續鬥爭直到勝利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最重要的是,把我這個訊息傳給你們之後的人,使將來的世代繼續鬥爭直到勝利。

passages.original: “And remember, comrades, your resolution must never falter.
passages.vernacular: 「同志哋,記住,你哋嘅決心絕唔能夠動搖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志們,記住,你們的決心絕不能動搖。

passages.original: No argument must lead you astray.
passages.vernacular: 任何論點都唔應該使你哋誤入歧途。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何論點都不應使你們誤入歧途。

passages.original: Never listen when they tell you that Man and the animals have a common interest, that the prosperity of the one is the prosperity of the others.
passages.vernacular: 唔好聽佢哋告訴你哋,人同動物有共同嘅利益,一方嘅繁榮就係其他方嘅繁榮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要聽他們告訴你們,人和動物有共同的利益,一方的繁榮就是其他方的繁榮。

passages.original: It is all lies.
passages.vernacular: 呢都係謊言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這都是謊言。

passages.original: Man serves the interests of no creature except himself.
passages.vernacular: 人除咗自己,不為任何生物嘅利益服務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人除了自己,不為任何生物的利益服務。

passages.original: And among us animals let there be perfect unity, perfect comradeship in the struggle.
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋動物之間有完美嘅團結,喺鬥爭中有完美嘅同志情誼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們動物之間有完美的團結,在鬥爭中有完美的同志情誼。

passages.original: All men are enemies.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅人都係敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的人都是敵人。

passages.original: All animals are comrades.”
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅動物都係同志。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的動物都是同志。」

passages.original: At this moment there was a tremendous uproar.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣發生咗巨大嘅騷動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時發生了巨大的騷動。

passages.original: While Major was speaking four large rats had crept out of their holes and were sitting on their hindquarters, listening to him.
passages.vernacular: 少校演講時,四隻大老鼠從洞裡爬咗出嚟,坐喺後腿上聽佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 少校演講時,四隻大老鼠從洞裡爬了出來,坐在後腿上聽他講。

passages.original: The dogs had suddenly caught sight of them, and it was only by a swift dash for their holes that the rats saved their lives.
passages.vernacular: 狗突然睇見咗佢哋,老鼠只係靠迅速衝回洞裡才保住咗性命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗突然看見了它們,老鼠只是靠迅速衝回洞裡才保住了性命。

passages.original: Major raised his trotter for silence.
passages.vernacular: 少校舉起佢嘅蹄子要求安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 少校舉起他的蹄子要求安靜。

passages.original: “Comrades,” he said, “here is a point that must be settled.
passages.vernacular: 「同志哋,」佢講,「呢度有一個必須解決嘅問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志們,」他說,「這裡有一個必須解決的問題。

passages.original: The wild creatures, such as rats and rabbits--are they our friends or our enemies?
passages.vernacular: 野生嘅生物,比如老鼠同兔子——佢哋係我哋嘅朋友定係敵人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 野生的生物,比如老鼠和兔子——它們是我們的朋友還是敵人?

passages.original: Let us put it to the vote.
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋嚟表決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們來表決。

passages.original: I propose this question to the meeting: Are rats comrades?”
passages.vernacular: 我向會議提出呢個問題:老鼠係同志嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向會議提出這個問題:老鼠是同志嗎?」

passages.original: The vote was taken at once, and it was agreed by an overwhelming majority that rats were comrades.
passages.vernacular: 即刻進行咗表決,以壓倒性多數同意老鼠係同志。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 立刻進行了表決,以壓倒性多數同意老鼠是同志。

passages.original: There were only four dissentients, the three dogs and the cat, who was afterwards discovered to have voted on both sides.
passages.vernacular: 只有四個反對者,三條狗同貓,後來發現貓兩邊都投咗票。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有四個反對者,三條狗和貓,後來發現貓兩邊都投了票。

passages.original: Major continued:
passages.vernacular: 少校繼續講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 少校繼續說:

passages.original: “I have little more to say.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇多少話要講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒有多少話要說了。

passages.original: I merely repeat, remember always your duty of enmity towards Man and all his ways.
passages.vernacular: 我只係重複,永遠記住你哋對人同佢一切習慣嘅敵對責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是重複,永遠記住你們對人和他一切習慣的敵對責任。

passages.original: Whatever goes upon two legs is an enemy.
passages.vernacular: 凡是用兩條腿走路嘅都係敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凡是用兩條腿走路的都是敵人。

passages.original: Whatever goes upon four legs, or has wings, is a friend.
passages.vernacular: 凡是用四條腿走路嘅,或有翅膀嘅,係朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凡是用四條腿走路的,或有翅膀的,是朋友。

passages.original: And remember also that in fighting against Man, we must not come to resemble him.
passages.vernacular: 仲要記住,喺同人作鬥爭時,我哋不可變得像佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還要記住,在與人作鬥爭時,我們不可變得像他。

passages.original: Even when you have conquered him, do not adopt his vices.
passages.vernacular: 即使你哋征服咗佢,都唔好沾染佢嘅惡習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使你們征服了他,也不要沾染他的惡習。

passages.original: No animal must ever live in a house, or sleep in a bed, or wear clothes, or drink alcohol, or smoke tobacco, or touch money, or engage in trade.
passages.vernacular: 任何動物都唔得住喺房子裡,或瞓床,或穿衣服,或飲酒,或抽煙,或碰金錢,或從事貿易。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何動物都不得住在房子裡,或睡床,或穿衣服,或喝酒,或抽煙,或碰金錢,或從事貿易。

passages.original: All the habits of Man are evil.
passages.vernacular: 人嘅所有習慣都係邪惡嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人的所有習慣都是邪惡的。

passages.original: And, above all, no animal must ever tyrannise over his own kind.
passages.vernacular: 最重要嘅係,任何動物都唔得暴虐自己嘅同類。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最重要的是,任何動物都不得暴虐自己的同類。

passages.original: Weak or strong, clever or simple, we are all brothers.
passages.vernacular: 無論弱或強,聰明或愚笨,我哋都係兄弟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論弱或強,聰明或愚笨,我們都是兄弟。

passages.original: No animal must ever kill any other animal.
passages.vernacular: 任何動物都唔得殺死任何其他動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何動物都不得殺死任何其他動物。

passages.original: All animals are equal.
passages.vernacular: 所有動物一律平等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物一律平等。

passages.original: “And now, comrades, I will tell you about my dream of last night.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,同志哋,我要告訴你哋我琴晚嘅夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,同志們,我要告訴你們我昨晚的夢。

passages.original: I cannot describe that dream to you.
passages.vernacular: 我無法向你哋描述嗰個夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我無法向你們描述那個夢。

passages.original: It was a dream of the earth as it will be when Man has vanished.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一個關於人消失後大地將會係乜嘢樣子嘅夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一個關於人消失後大地將會是什麼樣子的夢。

passages.original: But it reminded me of something that I had long forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 但佢使我想起一件我早已忘記嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它使我想起一件我早已忘記的事。

passages.original: Many years ago, when I was a little pig, my mother and the other sows used to sing an old song of which they knew only the tune and the first three words.
passages.vernacular: 多年以前,我定係小豬嘅時候,我母親同其他母豬常常唱一首老歌,佢哋只知道調子同頭三個字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多年以前,我還是小豬的時候,我母親和其他母豬常常唱一首老歌,她們只知道調子和頭三個字。

passages.original: I had known that tune in my infancy, but it had long since passed out of my mind.
passages.vernacular: 我喺嬰兒時期知道嗰個調子,但佢好久以前就從我腦海中消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在嬰兒時期知道那個調子,但它很久以前就從我腦海中消失了。

passages.original: Last night, however, it came back to me in my dream.
passages.vernacular: 然而琴晚佢喺我嘅夢裡回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而昨晚它在我的夢裡回來了。

passages.original: And what is more, the words of the song also came back-words, I am certain, which were sung by the animals of long ago and have been lost to memory for generations.
passages.vernacular: 更重要嘅係,歌詞都回嚟喇——我確信,嗰個係好久以前嘅動物哋唱嘅詞,幾代以來已被遺忘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 更重要的是,歌詞也回來了——我確信,那是很久以前的動物們唱的詞,幾代以來已被遺忘。

passages.original: I will sing you that song now, comrades.
passages.vernacular: 同志哋,我而家就唱呢首歌畀你哋聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同志們,我現在就唱這首歌給你們聽。

passages.original: I am old and my voice is hoarse, but when I have taught you the tune, you can sing it better for yourselves.
passages.vernacular: 我老喇,嗓子沙啞,但等我教會你哋調子之後,你哋可以自己唱得更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我老了,嗓子沙啞,但等我教會你們調子之後,你們可以自己唱得更好。

passages.original: It is called ‘Beasts of England’.”
passages.vernacular: 佢叫做《英格蘭之獸》。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它叫做《英格蘭之獸》。」

passages.original: Old Major cleared his throat and began to sing.
passages.vernacular: 老少校清咗清喉嚨,開始唱起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老少校清了清喉嚨,開始唱起來。

passages.original: As he had said, his voice was hoarse, but he sang well enough, and it was a stirring tune, something between ‘Clementine’ and ‘La Cucaracha’.
passages.vernacular: 正如佢所講,佢嘅嗓子係沙啞嘅,但佢唱得相當好,嗰個係一支激動人心嘅調子,介於《克萊門汀》同《小蟑螂》之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正如他所說,他的嗓子是沙啞的,但他唱得相當好,那是一支激動人心的調子,介於《克萊門汀》和《小蟑螂》之間。

passages.original: The words ran:
passages.vernacular: 歌詞係咁樣嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歌詞是這樣的:

passages.original: Beasts of England, beasts of Ireland, Beasts of every land and clime, Hearken to my joyful tidings Of the golden future time.
passages.vernacular: 英格蘭嘅獸,愛爾蘭嘅獸,各地各方嘅獸,請聽我歡樂嘅喜訊,黃金般嘅未來時光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 英格蘭的獸,愛爾蘭的獸,各地各方的獸,請聽我歡樂的喜訊,黃金般的未來時光。

passages.original: Soon or late the day is coming, Tyrant Man shall be o’erthrown, And the fruitful fields of England Shall be trod by beasts alone.
passages.vernacular: 遲早嗰天將到來,暴君人類被推翻,英格蘭豐饒嘅田野,將只有獸類行走其上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遲早那天將到來,暴君人類被推翻,英格蘭豐饒的田野,將只有獸類行走其上。

passages.original: Rings shall vanish from our noses, And the harness from our back, Bit and spur shall rust forever, Cruel whips no more shall crack.
passages.vernacular: 我哋鼻上嘅環將消失,背上嘅馬具都無蹤,嚼子馬刺永遠生鏽,殘酷嘅鞭子唔再響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們鼻上的環將消失,背上的馬具也無蹤,嚼子馬刺永遠生鏽,殘酷的鞭子不再響。

passages.original: Riches more than mind can picture, Wheat and barley, oats and hay, Clover, beans, and mangel-wurzels Shall be ours upon that day.
passages.vernacular: 比想像更多嘅財富,小麥大麥、燕麥乾草,三葉草、豆子同甜菜,喺嗰天將歸我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比想像更多的財富,小麥大麥、燕麥乾草,三葉草、豆子和甜菜,在那天將歸我們。

passages.original: Bright will shine the fields of England, Purer shall its waters be, Sweeter yet shall blow its breezes On the day that sets us free.
passages.vernacular: 英格蘭嘅田野將明亮閃耀,佢嘅水將更純淨,佢嘅微風將吹得更甜,喺使我哋自由嘅嗰一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 英格蘭的田野將明亮閃耀,它的水將更純淨,它的微風將吹得更甜,在使我們自由的那一天。

passages.original: For that day we all must labour, Though we die before it break; Cows and horses, geese and turkeys, All must toil for freedom’s sake.
passages.vernacular: 為嗰一天我哋都必須勞動,即使死喺佢破曉之前;牛馬、鵝火雞,一切都要為自由辛勤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為那一天我們都必須勞動,即使死在它破曉之前;牛馬、鵝火雞,一切都要為自由辛勤。

passages.original: Beasts of England, beasts of Ireland, Beasts of every land and clime, Hearken well and spread my tidings Of the golden future time.
passages.vernacular: 英格蘭嘅獸,愛爾蘭嘅獸,各地各方嘅獸,請好好聽並傳播我嘅喜訊,黃金般嘅未來時光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 英格蘭的獸,愛爾蘭的獸,各地各方的獸,請好好聽並傳播我的喜訊,黃金般的未來時光。

passages.original: The singing of this song threw the animals into the wildest excitement.
passages.vernacular: 唱呢首歌使動物哋陷入咗最瘋狂嘅興奮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唱這首歌使動物們陷入了最瘋狂的興奮。

passages.original: Almost before Major had reached the end, they had begun singing it for themselves.
passages.vernacular: 少校仲冇唱到結尾,佢哋就已經開始自己唱起嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 少校還沒唱到結尾,它們就已經開始自己唱起來了。

passages.original: Even the stupidest of them had already picked up the tune and a few of the words, and as for the clever ones, such as the pigs and dogs, they had the entire song by heart within a few minutes.
passages.vernacular: 連佢哋中最笨嘅都已學會咗曲調和幾個詞,至於聰明嘅,比如豬同狗,幾分鐘之內就把整首歌背下嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連它們中最笨的也已學會了曲調和幾個詞,至於聰明的,比如豬和狗,幾分鐘之內就把整首歌背下來了。

passages.original: And then, after a few preliminary tries, the whole farm burst out into ‘Beasts of England’ in tremendous unison.
passages.vernacular: 然後,經過幾次初步嘗試,整個農場爆發出《英格蘭之獸》嘅巨大齊唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,經過幾次初步嘗試,整個農場爆發出《英格蘭之獸》的巨大齊唱。

passages.original: The cows lowed it, the dogs whined it, the sheep bleated it, the horses whinnied it, the ducks quacked it.
passages.vernacular: 牛哞哞地唱,狗嗚嗚地唱,羊咩咩地唱,馬嘶嘶地唱,鴨子嘎嘎地唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牛哞哞地唱,狗嗚嗚地唱,羊咩咩地唱,馬嘶嘶地唱,鴨子嘎嘎地唱。

passages.original: They were so delighted with the song that they sang it right through five times in succession, and might have continued singing it all night if they had not been interrupted.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋咁鍾意呢首歌,連續一直唱咗五遍,如果冇被打斷,可能會唱一整夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們那麼喜歡這首歌,連續一直唱了五遍,如果沒有被打斷,可能會唱一整夜。

passages.original: Unfortunately, the uproar awoke Mr. Jones, who sprang out of bed, making sure that there was a fox in the yard.
passages.vernacular: 不幸嘅係,騷動吵醒咗瓊斯先生,佢從床上跳起嚟,確定院子裡有一隻狐狸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不幸的是,騷動吵醒了瓊斯先生,他從床上跳起來,確定院子裡有一隻狐狸。

passages.original: He seized the gun which always stood in a corner of his bedroom, and let fly a charge of number 6 shot into the darkness.
passages.vernacular: 佢抓起總是放喺佢臥室角落裡嘅槍,向黑暗中射出一發六號霰彈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他抓起總是放在他臥室角落裡的槍,向黑暗中射出一發六號霰彈。

passages.original: The pellets buried themselves in the wall of the barn and the meeting broke up hurriedly.
passages.vernacular: 彈丸嵌進穀倉嘅牆壁,會議匆匆散喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彈丸嵌進穀倉的牆壁,會議匆匆散了。

passages.original: Everyone fled to his own sleeping-place.
passages.vernacular: 每個動物都逃回自己嘅瞓處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個動物都逃回自己的睡處。

passages.original: The birds jumped on to their perches, the animals settled down in the straw, and the whole farm was asleep in a moment.
passages.vernacular: 鳥跳上佢哋嘅棲木,動物哋喺稻草中安頓下嚟,整個農場頃刻間瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鳥跳上它們的棲木,動物們在稻草中安頓下來,整個農場頃刻間睡著了。

passages.original: Three nights later old Major died peacefully in his sleep.
passages.vernacular: 三天後,老少校喺瞓夢中安詳地死去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三天後,老少校在睡夢中安詳地死去了。

passages.original: His body was buried at the foot of the orchard.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅遺體被埋喺果園腳下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的遺體被埋在果園腳下。

passages.original: This was early in March.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係三月初嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是三月初的事。

passages.original: During the next three months there was much secret activity.
passages.vernacular: 喺接下嚟嘅三個月裡,有許多秘密嘅活動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在接下來的三個月裡,有許多秘密的活動。

passages.original: Major’s speech had given to the more intelligent animals on the farm a completely new outlook on life.
passages.vernacular: 少校嘅演講畀咗農場上比較聰明嘅動物一種全新嘅人生觀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 少校的演講給了農場上比較聰明的動物一種全新的人生觀。

passages.original: They did not know when the Rebellion predicted by Major would take place, they had no reason for thinking that it would be within their own lifetime, but they saw clearly that it was their duty to prepare for it.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔知道少校預言嘅造反乜嘢時候發生,佢哋冇理由認為佢會喺佢哋有生之年發生,但佢哋清楚地睇到,為佢作準備係佢哋嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們不知道少校預言的造反什麼時候發生,它們沒有理由認為它會在它們有生之年發生,但它們清楚地看到,為它作準備是它們的責任。

passages.original: The work of teaching and organising the others fell naturally upon the pigs, who were generally recognised as being the cleverest of the animals.
passages.vernacular: 教導同組織其他動物嘅工作,自然落喺咗豬嘅身上,佢哋被普遍公認為係動物中最聰明嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 教導和組織其他動物的工作,自然落在了豬的身上,它們被普遍公認為是動物中最聰明的。

passages.original: Pre-eminent among the pigs were two young boars named Snowball and Napoleon, whom Mr. Jones was breeding up for sale.
passages.vernacular: 豬中最傑出嘅係兩頭年輕嘅公豬,名叫雪球同拿破崙,瓊斯先生養住佢哋準備出售。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬中最傑出的是兩頭年輕的公豬,名叫雪球和拿破崙,瓊斯先生養著它們準備出售。

passages.original: Napoleon was a large, rather fierce-looking Berkshire boar, the only Berkshire on the farm, not much of a talker, but with a reputation for getting his own way.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙係一頭高大、相貌相當凶猛嘅伯克郡公豬,農場上唯一嘅伯克郡豬,不太會講話,但有隨心所欲達到目的嘅名聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙是一頭高大、相貌相當凶猛的伯克郡公豬,農場上唯一的伯克郡豬,不太會說話,但有隨心所欲達到目的的名聲。

passages.original: Snowball was a more vivacious pig than Napoleon, quicker in speech and more inventive, but was not considered to have the same depth of character.
passages.vernacular: 雪球比拿破崙更活潑,講話更快,更有創造力,但被認為冇同樣深嘅性格。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球比拿破崙更活潑,說話更快,更有創造力,但被認為沒有同樣深的性格。

passages.original: All the other male pigs on the farm were porkers.
passages.vernacular: 農場上所有其他嘅公豬都係肉豬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場上所有其他的公豬都是肉豬。

passages.original: The best known among them was a small fat pig named Squealer, with very round cheeks, twinkling eyes, nimble movements, and a shrill voice.
passages.vernacular: 其中最出名嘅係一頭名叫尖嗓子嘅矮胖豬,臉頰好圓,眼睛閃爍,動作靈活,聲音尖銳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中最出名的是一頭名叫尖嗓子的矮胖豬,臉頰很圓,眼睛閃爍,動作靈活,聲音尖銳。

passages.original: He was a brilliant talker, and when he was arguing some difficult point he had a way of skipping from side to side and whisking his tail which was somehow very persuasive.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個出色嘅演講者,當佢爭論某個難點時,佢有一種左右蹦跳、甩動尾巴嘅方式,唔知怎嘅好有講服力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個出色的演說者,當他爭論某個難點時,他有一種左右蹦跳、甩動尾巴的方式,不知怎的很有說服力。

passages.original: The others said of Squealer that he could turn black into white.
passages.vernacular: 其他動物講尖嗓子能把黑講成白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他動物說尖嗓子能把黑說成白。

passages.original: These three had elaborated old Major’s teachings into a complete system of thought, to which they gave the name of Animalism.
passages.vernacular: 呢三位把老少校嘅教導發展成咗一個完整嘅思想體系,佢哋畀佢取名為動物主義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這三位把老少校的教導發展成了一個完整的思想體系,他們給它取名為動物主義。

passages.original: Several nights a week, after Mr. Jones was asleep, they held secret meetings in the barn and expounded the principles of Animalism to the others.
passages.vernacular: 每週有幾個晚上,瓊斯先生瞓住後,佢哋喺穀倉裡召開秘密會議,向其他動物闡述動物主義嘅原則。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每週有幾個晚上,瓊斯先生睡著後,他們在穀倉裡召開秘密會議,向其他動物闡述動物主義的原則。

passages.original: At the beginning they met with much stupidity and apathy.
passages.vernacular: 開始時,佢哋遇到咗許多愚蠢同冷漠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 開始時,他們遇到了許多愚蠢和冷漠。

passages.original: Some of the animals talked of the duty of loyalty to Mr. Jones, whom they referred to as “Master,” or made elementary remarks such as “Mr. Jones feeds us.
passages.vernacular: 有些動物談論對瓊斯先生嘅忠誠責任,稱佢為「主人」,或講啲初級嘅話,比如「瓊斯先生餵我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些動物談論對瓊斯先生的忠誠責任,稱他為「主人」,或說一些初級的話,比如「瓊斯先生餵我們。

passages.original: If he were gone, we should starve to death.”
passages.vernacular: 如果佢走喇,我哋會餓死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他走了,我們會餓死。」

passages.original: Others asked such questions as “Why should we care what happens after we are dead?” or “If this Rebellion is to happen anyway, what difference does it make whether we work for it or not?”, and the pigs had great difficulty in making them see that this was contrary to the spirit of Animalism.
passages.vernacular: 另啲問咁樣嘅問題:「我哋點解要關心死後發生嘅事?」或「如果呢次造反無論如何都會發生,我哋係咪為佢工作又有乜嘢區別?」豬哋費咗好大嘅力氣才讓佢哋明白呢違背動物主義嘅精神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一些問這樣的問題:「我們為什麼要關心死後發生的事?」或「如果這次造反無論如何都會發生,我們是否為它工作又有什麼區別?」豬們費了很大的力氣才讓它們明白這違背動物主義的精神。

passages.original: The stupidest questions of all were asked by Mollie, the white mare.
passages.vernacular: 最愚蠢嘅問題係由白母馬茉莉問嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最愚蠢的問題是由白母馬茉莉問的。

passages.original: The very first question she asked Snowball was: “Will there still be sugar after the Rebellion?”
passages.vernacular: 佢問雪球嘅第一個問題係:「造反之後仲會有糖嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她問雪球的第一個問題是:「造反之後還會有糖嗎?」

passages.original: “No,” said Snowball firmly.
passages.vernacular: 「唔會,」雪球堅定地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會,」雪球堅定地說。

passages.original: “We have no means of making sugar on this farm.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋喺呢個農場冇製糖嘅方法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們在這個農場沒有製糖的方法。

passages.original: Besides, you do not need sugar.
passages.vernacular: 而且,你不需要糖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,你不需要糖。

passages.original: You will have all the oats and hay you want.”
passages.vernacular: 你會有你想要嘅所有燕麥同乾草。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會有你想要的所有燕麥和乾草。」

passages.original: “And shall I still be allowed to wear ribbons in my mane?” asked Mollie.
passages.vernacular: 「我仲被允許喺鬃毛上戴絲帶嗎?」茉莉問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我還被允許在鬃毛上戴絲帶嗎?」茉莉問。

passages.original: “Comrade,” said Snowball, “those ribbons that you are so devoted to are the badge of slavery.
passages.vernacular: 「同志,」雪球講,「你咁迷戀嘅嗰啲絲帶係奴役嘅標誌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志,」雪球說,「你這麼迷戀的那些絲帶是奴役的標誌。

passages.original: Can you not understand that liberty is worth more than ribbons?”
passages.vernacular: 你難道不明白自由比絲帶更有價值嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你難道不明白自由比絲帶更有價值嗎?」

passages.original: Mollie agreed, but she did not sound very convinced.
passages.vernacular: 茉莉同意喇,但聽起嚟不太信服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 茉莉同意了,但聽起來不太信服。

passages.original: The pigs had an even harder struggle to counteract the lies put about by Moses, the tame raven.
passages.vernacular: 豬哋要抵消馴養嘅烏鴉摩西散佈嘅謊言,鬥爭得更艱難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬們要抵消馴養的烏鴉摩西散佈的謊言,鬥爭得更艱難。

passages.original: Moses, who was Mr. Jones’s especial pet, was a spy and a tale-bearer, but he was also a clever talker.
passages.vernacular: 摩西係瓊斯先生特別嘅寵物,係個間諜同搬弄係非者,但佢都係個能言善辯嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩西是瓊斯先生特別的寵物,是個間諜和搬弄是非者,但他也是個能言善辯的人。

passages.original: He claimed to know of the existence of a mysterious country called Sugarcandy Mountain, to which all animals went when they died.
passages.vernacular: 佢聲稱知道有一個神秘嘅國度,叫做糖果山,所有動物死後都去嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他聲稱知道有一個神秘的國度,叫做糖果山,所有動物死後都去那裡。

passages.original: It was situated somewhere up in the sky, a little distance beyond the clouds, Moses said.
passages.vernacular: 摩西講,佢位於天空上某個地方,喺雲嘅稍遠處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩西說,它位於天空上某個地方,在雲的稍遠處。

passages.original: In Sugarcandy Mountain it was Sunday seven days a week, clover was in season all the year round, and lump sugar and linseed cake grew on the hedges.
passages.vernacular: 喺糖果山,一個星期七天都係星期天,三葉草四季都當季,方糖同亞麻籽餅長喺樹籬上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在糖果山,一個星期七天都是星期天,三葉草四季都當季,方糖和亞麻籽餅長在樹籬上。

passages.original: The animals hated Moses because he told tales and did no work, but some of them believed in Sugarcandy Mountain, and the pigs had to argue very hard to persuade them that there was no such place.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋恨摩西,因為佢搬弄係非又不工作,但其中有些相信糖果山,豬哋唔得不費好大力氣爭辯,才講服佢哋冇嗰樣嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們恨摩西,因為他搬弄是非又不工作,但其中有些相信糖果山,豬們不得不費很大力氣爭辯,才說服它們沒有那樣的地方。

passages.original: Their most faithful disciples were the two cart-horses, Boxer and Clover.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋最忠實嘅門徒係兩匹拉車馬,拳擊手同三葉草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們最忠實的門徒是兩匹拉車馬,拳擊手和三葉草。

passages.original: These two had great difficulty in thinking anything out for themselves, but having once accepted the pigs as their teachers, they absorbed everything that they were told, and passed it on to the other animals by simple arguments.
passages.vernacular: 呢兩匹好難自己思考任何事情,但一旦接受咗豬作為佢哋嘅老師,就吸收咗被告知嘅一切,並以簡單嘅論證傳畀其他動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這兩匹很難自己思考任何事情,但一旦接受了豬作為它們的老師,就吸收了被告知的一切,並以簡單的論證傳給其他動物。

passages.original: They were unfailing in their attendance at the secret meetings in the barn, and led the singing of ‘Beasts of England’, with which the meetings always ended.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺穀倉秘密會議中從不缺席,並領唱《英格蘭之獸》,會議總是以此結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們在穀倉秘密會議中從不缺席,並領唱《英格蘭之獸》,會議總是以此結束。

passages.original: Now, as it turned out, the Rebellion was achieved much earlier and more easily than anyone had expected.
passages.vernacular: 而家,事實證明,造反比任何人預料嘅都早得多、容易得多地實現喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,事實證明,造反比任何人預料的都早得多、容易得多地實現了。

passages.original: In past years Mr. Jones, although a hard master, had been a capable farmer, but of late he had fallen on evil days.
passages.vernacular: 過去幾年,瓊斯先生雖然係個嚴厲嘅主人,卻係個能幹嘅農夫,但最近佢倒咗楣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過去幾年,瓊斯先生雖然是個嚴厲的主人,卻是個能幹的農夫,但最近他倒了楣。

passages.original: He had become much disheartened after losing money in a lawsuit, and had taken to drinking more than was good for him.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺一場官司中輸咗錢之後好沮喪,飲酒飲得超過咗對佢有益嘅程度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在一場官司中輸了錢之後非常沮喪,喝酒喝得超過了對他有益的程度。

passages.original: For whole days at a time he would lounge in his Windsor chair in the kitchen, reading the newspapers, drinking, and occasionally feeding Moses on crusts of bread soaked in beer.
passages.vernacular: 佢會一連幾天懶洋洋地躺喺廚房嘅溫莎椅上,睇報紙,飲酒,偶爾攞浸咗啤酒嘅麵包皮餵摩西。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他會一連幾天懶洋洋地躺在廚房的溫莎椅上,看報紙,喝酒,偶爾拿浸了啤酒的麵包皮餵摩西。

passages.original: His men were idle and dishonest, the fields were full of weeds, the buildings wanted roofing, the hedges were neglected, and the animals were underfed.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅人懶惰又不誠實,田裡長滿咗雜草,建築需要修屋頂,樹籬被忽視喇,動物哋食不飽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的人懶惰又不誠實,田裡長滿了雜草,建築需要修屋頂,樹籬被忽視了,動物們吃不飽。

passages.original: June came and the hay was almost ready for cutting.
passages.vernacular: 六月嚟喇,乾草幾乎可以收割喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 六月來了,乾草幾乎可以收割了。

passages.original: On Midsummer’s Eve, which was a Saturday, Mr. Jones went into Willingdon and got so drunk at the Red Lion that he did not come back till midday on Sunday.
passages.vernacular: 喺仲夏夜前夕,嗰個係個星期六,瓊斯先生去咗威靈頓,喺紅獅酒館飲得爛醉,直到星期天中午才回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在仲夏夜前夕,那是個星期六,瓊斯先生去了威靈頓,在紅獅酒館喝得爛醉,直到星期天中午才回來。

passages.original: The men had milked the cows in the early morning and then had gone out rabbiting, without bothering to feed the animals.
passages.vernacular: 工人哋清早擠咗牛奶,然後出去捕兔子,冇費心餵動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 工人們清早擠了牛奶,然後出去捕兔子,沒有費心餵動物。

passages.original: When Mr. Jones got back he immediately went to sleep on the drawing-room sofa with the News of the World over his face, so that when evening came, the animals were still unfed.
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯先生回嚟後即刻喺客廳沙發上瞓住喇,臉上蓋住《世界新聞報》,所以到咗傍晚,動物哋仍然冇得到餵食。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯先生回來後立刻在客廳沙發上睡著了,臉上蓋著《世界新聞報》,所以到了傍晚,動物們仍然沒有得到餵食。

passages.original: At last they could stand it no longer.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢哋再都無法忍受喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後它們再也無法忍受了。

passages.original: One of the cows broke in the door of the store-shed with her horn and all the animals began to help themselves from the bins.
passages.vernacular: 一頭母牛用角頂破咗儲藏棚嘅門,所有動物都開始從箱子裡自己攞食嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一頭母牛用角頂破了儲藏棚的門,所有動物都開始從箱子裡自己拿吃的。

passages.original: It was just then that Mr. Jones woke up.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,瓊斯先生醒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,瓊斯先生醒了。

passages.original: The next moment he and his four men were in the store-shed with whips in their hands, lashing out in all directions.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻,佢同佢嘅四個人已喺儲藏棚裡,手裡攞住鞭子,四面八方亂抽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻,他和他的四個人已在儲藏棚裡,手裡拿著鞭子,四面八方亂抽。

passages.original: This was more than the hungry animals could bear.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係飢餓嘅動物所無法忍受嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是飢餓的動物所無法忍受的。

passages.original: With one accord, though nothing of the kind had been planned beforehand, they flung themselves upon their tormentors.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋一致地,雖然事前冇計畫過咁樣嘅事,撲向佢哋嘅折磨者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們一致地,雖然事前沒有計畫過這樣的事,撲向它們的折磨者。

passages.original: Jones and his men suddenly found themselves being butted and kicked from all sides.
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯同佢嘅人突然發現自己從四面八方被頂同被踢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯和他的人突然發現自己從四面八方被頂和被踢。

passages.original: The situation was quite out of their control.
passages.vernacular: 局面完全不喺佢哋嘅控制之內。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 局面完全不在他們的控制之內。

passages.original: They had never seen animals behave like this before, and this sudden uprising of creatures whom they were used to thrashing and maltreating just as they chose, frightened them almost out of their wits.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋從未見過動物咁樣行事,呢啲佢哋習慣於隨意鞭打同虐待嘅生物嘅突然起義,幾乎把佢哋嚇得魂不附體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們從未見過動物這樣行事,這些他們習慣於隨意鞭打和虐待的生物的突然起義,幾乎把他們嚇得魂不附體。

passages.original: After only a moment or two they gave up trying to defend themselves and took to their heels.
passages.vernacular: 只過咗一兩分鐘,佢哋就放棄咗自衛,拔腿逃跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只過了一兩分鐘,他們就放棄了自衛,拔腿逃跑。

passages.original: A minute later all five of them were in full flight down the cart-track that led to the main road, with the animals pursuing them in triumph.
passages.vernacular: 一分鐘後,佢哋五個人全都喺沿住通往大路嘅車道全速逃跑,動物哋得意洋洋地追趕佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一分鐘後,他們五個人全都在沿著通往大路的車道全速逃跑,動物們得意洋洋地追趕他們。

passages.original: Mrs. Jones looked out of the bedroom window, saw what was happening, hurriedly flung a few possessions into a carpet bag, and slipped out of the farm by another way.
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯太太從臥室窗子往外睇,睇到正在發生嘅事,匆忙把幾件財物扔進一個地毯包,從另一條路溜出咗農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯太太從臥室窗子往外看,看到正在發生的事,匆忙把幾件財物扔進一個地毯包,從另一條路溜出了農場。

passages.original: Moses sprang off his perch and flapped after her, croaking loudly.
passages.vernacular: 摩西從棲木上跳起,呱呱大叫住拍住翅膀跟住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩西從棲木上跳起,呱呱大叫著拍著翅膀跟著她。

passages.original: Meanwhile the animals had chased Jones and his men out on to the road and slammed the five-barred gate behind them.
passages.vernacular: 同時,動物哋把瓊斯同佢嘅人追到路上,喺佢哋身後砰地關上五柵欄大門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時,動物們把瓊斯和他的人追到路上,在他們身後砰地關上五柵欄大門。

passages.original: And so, almost before they knew what was happening, the Rebellion had been successfully carried through: Jones was expelled, and the Manor Farm was theirs.
passages.vernacular: 於是,幾乎喺佢哋仲冇明白發生咗乜嘢之前,造反就成功地完成喇:瓊斯被驅逐,曼諾農場係佢哋嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是,幾乎在它們還沒明白發生了什麼之前,造反就成功地完成了:瓊斯被驅逐,曼諾農場是它們的了。

passages.original: For the first few minutes the animals could hardly believe in their good fortune.
passages.vernacular: 頭幾分鐘,動物哋幾乎唔能夠相信自己嘅好運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭幾分鐘,動物們幾乎不能相信自己的好運。

passages.original: Their first act was to gallop in a body right round the boundaries of the farm, as though to make quite sure that no human being was hiding anywhere upon it; then they raced back to the farm buildings to wipe out the last traces of Jones’s hated reign.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅第一個行動係一起沿住農場嘅邊界飛奔一圈,好像要完全確定冇人躲喺上面任何地方;然後佢哋跑回農場嘅建築,抹去瓊斯可恨統治嘅最後痕跡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們的第一個行動是一起沿著農場的邊界飛奔一圈,好像要完全確定沒有人躲在上面任何地方;然後它們跑回農場的建築,抹去瓊斯可恨統治的最後痕跡。

passages.original: The harness-room at the end of the stables was broken open; the bits, the nose-rings, the dog-chains, the cruel knives with which Mr. Jones had been used to castrate the pigs and lambs, were all flung down the well.
passages.vernacular: 馬廄盡頭嘅馬具室被打開喇;嚼子、鼻環、狗鏈、瓊斯先生過去閹割豬同羊羔用嘅殘酷刀子,都被扔進咗井裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬廄盡頭的馬具室被打開了;嚼子、鼻環、狗鏈、瓊斯先生過去閹割豬和羊羔用的殘酷刀子,都被扔進了井裡。

passages.original: The reins, the halters, the blinkers, the degrading nosebags, were thrown on to the rubbish fire which was burning in the yard.
passages.vernacular: 韁繩、籠頭、眼罩、侮辱人嘅飼料袋,被扔到院子裡燃燒嘅垃圾火堆上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 韁繩、籠頭、眼罩、侮辱人的飼料袋,被扔到院子裡燃燒的垃圾火堆上。

passages.original: So were the whips.
passages.vernacular: 鞭子都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鞭子也是。

passages.original: All the animals capered with joy when they saw the whips going up in flames.
passages.vernacular: 所有動物睇到鞭子喺火焰中升起時,都歡喜得蹦跳起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物看到鞭子在火焰中升起時,都歡喜得蹦跳起來。

passages.original: Snowball also threw on to the fire the ribbons with which the horses’ manes and tails had usually been decorated on market days.
passages.vernacular: 雪球仲把平常喺市集日裝飾馬鬃毛同尾巴嘅絲帶扔進咗火裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球還把平常在市集日裝飾馬鬃毛和尾巴的絲帶扔進了火裡。

passages.original: “Ribbons,” he said, “should be considered as clothes, which are the mark of a human being.
passages.vernacular: 「絲帶,」佢講,「應該被視為衣服,嗰個係人嘅標誌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「絲帶,」他說,「應該被視為衣服,那是人的標誌。

passages.original: All animals should go naked.”
passages.vernacular: 所有動物都應該赤裸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物都應該赤裸。」

passages.original: When Boxer heard this he fetched the small straw hat which he wore in summer to keep the flies out of his ears, and flung it on to the fire with the rest.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手聽到呢話,就去攞佢夏天戴住擋住耳朵不讓蒼蠅進去嘅小草帽,把佢同其他嘢一起扔進咗火裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手聽到這話,就去拿他夏天戴著擋住耳朵不讓蒼蠅進去的小草帽,把它同其他東西一起扔進了火裡。

passages.original: In a very little while the animals had destroyed everything that reminded them of Mr. Jones.
passages.vernacular: 冇過多久,動物哋已毀掉咗所有使佢哋想起瓊斯先生嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒過多久,動物們已毀掉了所有使它們想起瓊斯先生的東西。

passages.original: Napoleon then led them back to the store-shed and served out a double ration of corn to everybody, with two biscuits for each dog.
passages.vernacular: 然後拿破崙領佢哋回到儲藏棚,畀每個動物發咗雙份嘅玉米,每條狗兩塊餅乾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後拿破崙領它們回到儲藏棚,給每個動物發了雙份的玉米,每條狗兩塊餅乾。

passages.original: Then they sang ‘Beasts of England’ from end to end seven times running, and after that they settled down for the night and slept as they had never slept before.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋把《英格蘭之獸》從頭到尾連唱咗七遍,之後安頓下嚟過夜,瞓得從來冇嗰樣好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後它們把《英格蘭之獸》從頭到尾連唱了七遍,之後安頓下來過夜,睡得從來沒有那樣好。

passages.original: But they woke at dawn as usual, and suddenly remembering the glorious thing that had happened, they all raced out into the pasture together.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋像往常一樣黎明時醒嚟,突然想起發生嘅光榮事件,全都一起衝出去,跑進牧場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它們像往常一樣黎明時醒來,突然想起發生的光榮事件,全都一起衝出去,跑進牧場。

passages.original: A little way down the pasture there was a knoll that commanded a view of most of the farm.
passages.vernacular: 牧場往下不遠處有一個小丘,可以俯瞰農場嘅大部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧場往下不遠處有一個小丘,可以俯瞰農場的大部分。

passages.original: The animals rushed to the top of it and gazed round them in the clear morning light.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋衝上佢嘅頂端,喺清澈嘅晨光中環顧四周。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們衝上它的頂端,在清澈的晨光中環顧四周。

passages.original: Yes, it was theirs--everything that they could see was theirs!
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,佢係佢哋嘅——佢哋所能睇到嘅一切都係佢哋嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,它是它們的——它們所能看到的一切都是它們的!

passages.original: In the ecstasy of that thought they gambolled round and round, they hurled themselves into the air in great leaps of excitement.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢個想法嘅狂喜中,佢哋繞住圈子蹦跳,興奮地一躍而起,躍入空中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這個想法的狂喜中,它們繞著圈子蹦跳,興奮地一躍而起,躍入空中。

passages.original: They rolled in the dew, they cropped mouthfuls of the sweet summer grass, they kicked up clods of the black earth and snuffed its rich scent.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺露水中打滾,啃咗大口大口甜美嘅夏草,踢起黑土塊,嗅住佢濃郁嘅氣味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們在露水中打滾,啃了大口大口甜美的夏草,踢起黑土塊,嗅著它濃郁的氣味。

passages.original: Then they made a tour of inspection of the whole farm and surveyed with speechless admiration the ploughland, the hayfield, the orchard, the pool, the spinney.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋對整個農場進行咗視察,以無言嘅欽佩巡視咗耕地、乾草地、果園、池塘、小樹林。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後它們對整個農場進行了視察,以無言的欽佩巡視了耕地、乾草地、果園、池塘、小樹林。

passages.original: It was as though they had never seen these things before, and even now they could hardly believe that it was all their own.
passages.vernacular: 好像佢哋以前從未見過呢啲嘢一樣,即使而家都幾乎唔能夠相信呢一切都係佢哋自己嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像它們以前從未見過這些東西一樣,即使現在也幾乎不能相信這一切都是它們自己的。

passages.original: Then they filed back to the farm buildings and halted in silence outside the door of the farmhouse.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋排隊回到農場嘅建築,默默地停喺農舍嘅門外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後它們排隊回到農場的建築,默默地停在農舍的門外。

passages.original: That was theirs too, but they were frightened to go inside.
passages.vernacular: 嗰都係佢哋嘅,但佢哋唔敢進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那也是它們的,但它們不敢進去。

passages.original: After a moment, however, Snowball and Napoleon butted the door open with their shoulders and the animals entered in single file, walking with the utmost care for fear of disturbing anything.
passages.vernacular: 不過片刻之後,雪球同拿破崙用肩膀把門撞開,動物哋魚貫而入,極其小心地行走,生怕驚動任何嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過片刻之後,雪球和拿破崙用肩膀把門撞開,動物們魚貫而入,極其小心地行走,生怕驚動任何東西。

passages.original: They tiptoed from room to room, afraid to speak above a whisper and gazing with a kind of awe at the unbelievable luxury, at the beds with their feather mattresses, the looking-glasses, the horsehair sofa, the Brussels carpet, the lithograph of Queen Victoria over the drawing-room mantelpiece.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋踮住腳尖從一個房間走到另一個房間,怕大聲講話,只敢低語,帶住敬畏凝視住嗰難以置信嘅奢華,有羽毛床墊嘅床、鏡子、馬鬃沙發、布魯塞爾地毯、客廳壁爐台上方維多利亞女王嘅石版畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們踮著腳尖從一個房間走到另一個房間,怕大聲說話,只敢低語,帶著敬畏凝視著那難以置信的奢華,有羽毛床墊的床、鏡子、馬鬃沙發、布魯塞爾地毯、客廳壁爐台上方維多利亞女王的石版畫。

passages.original: They were just coming down the stairs when Mollie was discovered to be missing.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋剛下樓梯,就發現茉莉唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們剛下樓梯,就發現茉莉不見了。

passages.original: Going back, the others found that she had remained behind in the best bedroom.
passages.vernacular: 回去一睇,其他動物發現佢留喺咗最好嘅臥室裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回去一看,其他動物發現她留在了最好的臥室裡。

passages.original: She had taken a piece of blue ribbon from Mrs. Jones’s dressing-table, and was holding it against her shoulder and admiring herself in the glass in a very foolish manner.
passages.vernacular: 佢從瓊斯太太嘅梳妝台上攞咗一條藍絲帶,貼喺肩膀上,用一種好愚蠢嘅方式喺鏡子裡欣賞自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她從瓊斯太太的梳妝台上拿了一條藍絲帶,貼在肩膀上,用一種非常愚蠢的方式在鏡子裡欣賞自己。

passages.original: The others reproached her sharply, and they went outside.
passages.vernacular: 其他動物尖銳地責備咗佢,然後佢哋走到外面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他動物尖銳地責備了她,然後它們走到外面。

passages.original: Some hams hanging in the kitchen were taken out for burial, and the barrel of beer in the scullery was stove in with a kick from Boxer’s hoof, otherwise nothing in the house was touched.
passages.vernacular: 掛喺廚房裡嘅幾隻火腿被攞出去埋葬,洗滌間裡嘅啤酒桶被拳擊手嘅蹄子一腳踢破,除此之外,屋裡嘅嘢都冇動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 掛在廚房裡的幾隻火腿被拿出去埋葬,洗滌間裡的啤酒桶被拳擊手的蹄子一腳踢破,除此之外,屋裡的東西都沒有動。

passages.original: A unanimous resolution was passed on the spot that the farmhouse should be preserved as a museum.
passages.vernacular: 當場一致通過決議,農舍應作為博物館保存。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當場一致通過決議,農舍應作為博物館保存。

passages.original: All were agreed that no animal must ever live there.
passages.vernacular: 大家都同意,任何動物都唔得住喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家都同意,任何動物都不得住在那裡。

passages.original: The animals had their breakfast, and then Snowball and Napoleon called them together again.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋食咗早餐,然後雪球同拿破崙又把佢哋召集喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們吃了早餐,然後雪球和拿破崙又把它們召集在一起。

passages.original: “Comrades,” said Snowball, “it is half-past six and we have a long day before us.
passages.vernacular: 「同志哋,」雪球講,「而家係六點半,我哋面前有漫長嘅一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志們,」雪球說,「現在是六點半,我們面前有漫長的一天。

passages.original: Today we begin the hay harvest.
passages.vernacular: 今日我哋開始乾草收割。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天我們開始乾草收割。

passages.original: But there is another matter that must be attended to first.”
passages.vernacular: 但有另一件事必須先處理。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但有另一件事必須先處理。」

passages.original: The pigs now revealed that during the past three months they had taught themselves to read and write from an old spelling book which had belonged to Mr. Jones’s children and which had been thrown on the rubbish heap.
passages.vernacular: 豬哋而家透露,喺過去三個月裡,佢哋從一本屬於瓊斯先生細路哋、被扔到垃圾堆上嘅舊拼讀書自學咗讀同寫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬們現在透露,在過去三個月裡,它們從一本屬於瓊斯先生孩子們、被扔到垃圾堆上的舊拼讀書自學了讀和寫。

passages.original: Napoleon sent for pots of black and white paint and led the way down to the five-barred gate that gave on to the main road.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙叫人攞嚟黑白油漆罐,領頭走向通往大路嘅五柵欄大門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙叫人拿來黑白油漆罐,領頭走向通往大路的五柵欄大門。

passages.original: Then Snowball (for it was Snowball who was best at writing) took a brush between the two knuckles of his trotter, painted out MANOR FARM from the top bar of the gate and in its place painted ANIMAL FARM.
passages.vernacular: 然後雪球(因為雪球係最擅長寫字嘅)用蹄子嘅兩個關節夾住刷子,把大門頂條上嘅「曼諾農場」塗掉,喺原處寫上「動物農莊」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後雪球(因為雪球是最擅長寫字的)用蹄子的兩個關節夾住刷子,把大門頂條上的「曼諾農場」塗掉,在原處寫上「動物農莊」。

passages.original: This was to be the name of the farm from now onwards.
passages.vernacular: 從而家起呢個就係農場嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從現在起這就是農場的名字。

passages.original: After this they went back to the farm buildings, where Snowball and Napoleon sent for a ladder which they caused to be set against the end wall of the big barn.
passages.vernacular: 之後佢哋回到農場嘅建築,雪球同拿破崙叫人攞嚟一架梯子,讓佢靠喺大穀倉嘅盡頭牆上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後它們回到農場的建築,雪球和拿破崙叫人拿來一架梯子,讓它靠在大穀倉的盡頭牆上。

passages.original: They explained that by their studies of the past three months the pigs had succeeded in reducing the principles of Animalism to Seven Commandments.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋解釋講,通過過去三個月嘅研究,豬哋成功地把動物主義嘅原則歸納為七條誡命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們解釋說,通過過去三個月的研究,豬們成功地把動物主義的原則歸納為七條誡命。

passages.original: These Seven Commandments would now be inscribed on the wall; they would form an unalterable law by which all the animals on Animal Farm must live for ever after.
passages.vernacular: 呢七條誡命而家將被銘刻喺牆上;佢哋將構成一條不可改變嘅法則,動物農莊嘅所有動物此後永遠都必須遵循。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這七條誡命現在將被銘刻在牆上;它們將構成一條不可改變的法則,動物農莊的所有動物此後永遠都必須遵循。

passages.original: With some difficulty (for it is not easy for a pig to balance himself on a ladder) Snowball climbed up and set to work, with Squealer a few rungs below him holding the paint-pot.
passages.vernacular: 費咗啲勁(因為豬喺梯子上保持平衡並唔容易),雪球爬上去開始工作,尖嗓子喺佢下面幾級梯階處攞住油漆罐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 費了一些勁(因為豬在梯子上保持平衡並不容易),雪球爬上去開始工作,尖嗓子在他下面幾級梯階處拿著油漆罐。

passages.original: The Commandments were written on the tarred wall in great white letters that could be read thirty yards away.
passages.vernacular: 誡命用大大嘅白色字母寫喺塗咗焦油嘅牆上,三十碼外都能讀到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誡命用大大的白色字母寫在塗了焦油的牆上,三十碼外都能讀到。

passages.original: They ran thus:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋係咁樣嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們是這樣的:

passages.original: THE SEVEN COMMANDMENTS
passages.vernacular: 七誡
passages.vernacularMandarin: 七誡

passages.original: Whatever goes upon two legs is an enemy.
passages.vernacular: 凡是用兩條腿走路嘅都係敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凡是用兩條腿走路的都是敵人。

passages.original: Whatever goes upon four legs, or has wings, is a friend.
passages.vernacular: 凡是用四條腿走路嘅,或有翅膀嘅,係朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凡是用四條腿走路的,或有翅膀的,是朋友。

passages.original: No animal shall wear clothes.
passages.vernacular: 任何動物唔得穿衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何動物不得穿衣服。

passages.original: No animal shall sleep in a bed.
passages.vernacular: 任何動物唔得瞓床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何動物不得睡床。

passages.original: No animal shall drink alcohol.
passages.vernacular: 任何動物唔得飲酒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何動物不得喝酒。

passages.original: No animal shall kill any other animal.
passages.vernacular: 任何動物唔得殺死任何其他動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何動物不得殺死任何其他動物。

passages.original: All animals are equal.
passages.vernacular: 所有動物一律平等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物一律平等。

passages.original: It was very neatly written, and except that “friend” was written “freind” and one of the “S’s” was the wrong way round, the spelling was correct all the way through.
passages.vernacular: 寫得好整齊,除咗「朋友」(friend)寫成咗「freind」,同一個「S」寫反咗之外,拼寫從頭到尾都係正確嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寫得非常整齊,除了「朋友」(friend)寫成了「freind」,和一個「S」寫反了之外,拼寫從頭到尾都是正確的。

passages.original: Snowball read it aloud for the benefit of the others.
passages.vernacular: 雪球為了其他動物嘅好處大聲念出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球為了其他動物的好處大聲念出來。

passages.original: All the animals nodded in complete agreement, and the cleverer ones at once began to learn the Commandments by heart.
passages.vernacular: 所有動物都完全同意地點頭,比較聰明嘅即刻開始背誡命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物都完全同意地點頭,比較聰明的立刻開始背誡命。

passages.original: “Now, comrades,” cried Snowball, throwing down the paint-brush, “to the hayfield!
passages.vernacular: 「而家,同志哋,」雪球喊道,扔下油漆刷,「到乾草地去!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,同志們,」雪球喊道,扔下油漆刷,「到乾草地去!

passages.original: Let us make it a point of honour to get in the harvest more quickly than Jones and his men could do.”
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋把比瓊斯同佢嘅人更快地收進收成當作榮譽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們把比瓊斯和他的人更快地收進收成當作榮譽。」

passages.original: But at this moment the three cows, who had seemed uneasy for some time past, set up a loud lowing.
passages.vernacular: 但呢陣,嗰三頭母牛,過去一直顯得不安,發出響亮嘅哞哞聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這時,那三頭母牛,過去一直顯得不安,發出響亮的哞哞聲。

passages.original: They had not been milked for twenty-four hours, and their udders were almost bursting.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋已經二十四小時冇擠奶喇,乳房幾乎要脹破。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們已經二十四小時沒擠奶了,乳房幾乎要脹破。

passages.original: After a little thought, the pigs sent for buckets and milked the cows fairly successfully, their trotters being well adapted to this task.
passages.vernacular: 豬哋想咗想,叫人攞嚟桶,相當成功地擠咗牛奶,佢哋嘅蹄子好適合呢項任務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬們想了想,叫人拿來桶,相當成功地擠了牛奶,它們的蹄子很適合這項任務。

passages.original: Soon there were five buckets of frothing creamy milk at which many of the animals looked with considerable interest.
passages.vernacular: 好快就有咗五桶冒泡嘅奶油牛奶,許多動物帶住相當大嘅興趣睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很快就有了五桶冒泡的奶油牛奶,許多動物帶著相當大的興趣看著它。

passages.original: “What is going to happen to all that milk?” said someone.
passages.vernacular: 「呢啲牛奶會點處理?」有人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這些牛奶會怎麼處理?」有人說。

passages.original: “Jones used sometimes to mix some of it in our mash,” said one of the hens.
passages.vernacular: 「瓊斯有時會把啲混進我哋嘅飼料中,」一隻母雞講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瓊斯有時會把一些混進我們的飼料中,」一隻母雞說。

passages.original: “Never mind the milk, comrades!” cried Napoleon, placing himself in front of the buckets.
passages.vernacular: 「別管牛奶喇,同志哋!」拿破崙喊道,站到桶前面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別管牛奶了,同志們!」拿破崙喊道,站到桶前面。

passages.original: “That will be attended to.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰會有人處理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那會有人處理。

passages.original: The harvest is more important.
passages.vernacular: 收成更重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收成更重要。

passages.original: Comrade Snowball will lead the way.
passages.vernacular: 雪球同志會領路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球同志會領路。

passages.original: I shall follow in a few minutes.
passages.vernacular: 我幾分鐘後跟上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我幾分鐘後跟上。

passages.original: Forward, comrades!
passages.vernacular: 前進,同志哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前進,同志們!

passages.original: The hay is waiting.”
passages.vernacular: 乾草喺等住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 乾草在等著。」

passages.original: So the animals trooped down to the hayfield to begin the harvest, and when they came back in the evening it was noticed that the milk had disappeared.
passages.vernacular: 於是動物哋成群結隊地到乾草地開始收割,晚上佢哋回嚟時,發現牛奶唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是動物們成群結隊地到乾草地開始收割,晚上它們回來時,發現牛奶不見了。

chapters.title: Chapter III 第三章:收成與七誡

passages.original: How they toiled and sweated to get the hay in!
passages.vernacular: 佢哋為了把乾草收進嚟,係點樣辛勤勞作、汗流浹背!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們為了把乾草收進來,是怎樣辛勤勞作、汗流浹背!

passages.original: But their efforts were rewarded, for the harvest was an even bigger success than they had hoped.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋嘅努力得到咗回報,因為呢次收成比佢哋希望嘅仲要成功得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它們的努力得到了回報,因為這次收成比它們希望的還要成功得多。

passages.original: Sometimes the work was hard; the implements had been designed for human beings and not for animals, and it was a great drawback that no animal was able to use any tool that involved standing on his hind legs.
passages.vernacular: 有時工作好艱難;工具係為人類而唔係為動物設計嘅,而冇動物能夠使用任何需要用後腿站立嘅工具,係個好大嘅障礙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時工作很艱難;工具是為人類而不是為動物設計的,而沒有動物能夠使用任何需要用後腿站立的工具,是個很大的障礙。

passages.original: But the pigs were so clever that they could think of a way round every difficulty.
passages.vernacular: 但豬哋咁聰明,能想出辦法繞過每一個困難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但豬們那麼聰明,能想出辦法繞過每一個困難。

passages.original: As for the horses, they knew every inch of the field, and in fact understood the business of mowing and raking far better than Jones and his men had ever done.
passages.vernacular: 至於馬,佢哋熟悉田地嘅每一寸,事實上比瓊斯同佢嘅人以前所做嘅更懂得割草同耙草嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於馬,它們熟悉田地的每一寸,事實上比瓊斯和他的人以前所做的更懂得割草和耙草的事。

passages.original: The pigs did not actually work, but directed and supervised the others.
passages.vernacular: 豬實際上不工作,而係指揮同監督其他動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬實際上不工作,而是指揮和監督其他動物。

passages.original: With their superior knowledge it was natural that they should assume the leadership.
passages.vernacular: 憑住佢哋更優越嘅知識,由佢哋嚟擔任領導係好自然嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑著它們更優越的知識,由它們來擔任領導是很自然的。

passages.original: Boxer and Clover would harness themselves to the cutter or the horse-rake (no bits or reins were needed in these days, of course) and tramp steadily round and round the field with a pig walking behind and calling out “Gee up, comrade!” or “Whoa back, comrade!” as the case might be.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手同三葉草會把自己套喺割草機或馬耙上(當然,呢啲日子不需要嚼子或韁繩),一圈又一圈穩步地踏遍田地,一頭豬跟喺後面走,視情況喊住「駕,同志!」或「籲,後退,同志!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手和三葉草會把自己套在割草機或馬耙上(當然,這些日子不需要嚼子或韁繩),一圈又一圈穩步地踏遍田地,一頭豬跟在後面走,視情況喊著「駕,同志!」或「籲,後退,同志!」

passages.original: And every animal down to the humblest worked at turning the hay and gathering it.
passages.vernacular: 每個動物,甚至最卑微嘅,都喺翻乾草同收集乾草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個動物,甚至最卑微的,都在翻乾草和收集乾草。

passages.original: Even the ducks and hens toiled to and fro all day in the sun, carrying tiny wisps of hay in their beaks.
passages.vernacular: 連鴨子同母雞都整天喺太陽下嚟回辛勞,用嘴叼住小小嘅乾草束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連鴨子和母雞也整天在太陽下來回辛勞,用嘴叼著小小的乾草束。

passages.original: In the end they finished the harvest in two days’ less time than it had usually taken Jones and his men.
passages.vernacular: 最後,佢哋完成收割所用嘅時間,比瓊斯同佢嘅人通常所需嘅少咗兩天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後,它們完成收割所用的時間,比瓊斯和他的人通常所需的少了兩天。

passages.original: Moreover, it was the biggest harvest that the farm had ever seen.
passages.vernacular: 而且,呢個係農場有史以來最大嘅一次收成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,這是農場有史以來最大的一次收成。

passages.original: There was no wastage whatever; the hens and ducks with their sharp eyes had gathered up the very last stalk.
passages.vernacular: 冇任何浪費;母雞同鴨子憑住敏銳嘅眼睛,收集咗最後一根稈子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有任何浪費;母雞和鴨子憑著敏銳的眼睛,收集了最後一根稈子。

passages.original: And not an animal on the farm had stolen so much as a mouthful.
passages.vernacular: 農場上冇一個動物偷過邊怕一口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場上沒有一個動物偷過哪怕一口。

passages.original: All through that summer the work of the farm went like clockwork.
passages.vernacular: 整個夏天,農場嘅工作像鐘錶一樣運轉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個夏天,農場的工作像鐘錶一樣運轉。

passages.original: The animals were happy as they had never conceived it possible to be.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋快樂得佢哋從未想過可能嘅程度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們快樂得它們從未想過可能的程度。

passages.original: Every mouthful of food was an acute positive pleasure, now that it was truly their own food, produced by themselves and for themselves, not doled out to them by a grudging master.
passages.vernacular: 每一口食物都係一種強烈嘅、積極嘅快樂,因為而家呢個係真正屬於佢哋自己嘅食物,由佢哋自己生產,為佢哋自己而產,唔係由一個吝嗇嘅主人施捨畀佢哋嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每一口食物都是一種強烈的、積極的快樂,因為現在這是真正屬於它們自己的食物,由它們自己生產,為它們自己而產,不是由一個吝嗇的主人施捨給它們的。

passages.original: With the worthless parasitical human beings gone, there was more for everyone to eat.
passages.vernacular: 無用嘅寄生人類走喇,每個動物都有更多嘢食喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無用的寄生人類走了,每個動物都有更多東西吃了。

passages.original: There was more leisure too, inexperienced though the animals were.
passages.vernacular: 雖然動物哋冇經驗,都有咗更多閒暇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然動物們沒有經驗,也有了更多閒暇。

passages.original: They met with many difficulties--for instance, later in the year, when they harvested the corn, they had to tread it out in the ancient style and blow away the chaff with their breath, since the farm possessed no threshing machine--but the pigs with their cleverness and Boxer with his tremendous muscles always pulled them through.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋遇到咗許多困難——例如,喺呢一年稍後,收割玉米時,佢哋唔得不以古老嘅方式踩踏脫粒,用呼氣吹走穀殼,因為農場冇脫粒機——但豬憑住聰明,拳擊手憑住強壯嘅肌肉,總是幫佢哋度過咗難關。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們遇到了許多困難——例如,在這一年稍後,收割玉米時,它們不得不以古老的方式踩踏脫粒,用呼氣吹走穀殼,因為農場沒有脫粒機——但豬憑著聰明,拳擊手憑著強壯的肌肉,總是幫它們度過了難關。

passages.original: Boxer was the admiration of everybody.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手係大家所欽佩嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手是大家所欽佩的。

passages.original: He had been a hard worker even in Jones’s time, but now he seemed more like three horses than one; there were days when the entire work of the farm seemed to rest on his mighty shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 即使喺瓊斯嘅時代,佢都係個辛勤嘅工作者,但而家佢睇起嚟更像三匹馬而唔係一匹;有些日子,農場嘅全部工作似乎都落喺佢強壯嘅肩膀上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使在瓊斯的時代,他也是個辛勤的工作者,但現在他看起來更像三匹馬而不是一匹;有些日子,農場的全部工作似乎都落在他強壯的肩膀上。

passages.original: From morning to night he was pushing and pulling, always at the spot where the work was hardest.
passages.vernacular: 從早到晚,佢一直喺推同拉,總是喺工作最艱難嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從早到晚,他一直在推和拉,總是在工作最艱難的地方。

passages.original: He had made an arrangement with one of the cockerels to call him in the mornings half an hour earlier than anyone else, and would put in some volunteer labour at whatever seemed to be most needed, before the regular day’s work began.
passages.vernacular: 佢同一隻小公雞做咗安排,讓佢早晨比任何人早半小時叫醒佢,喺正式嘅一天工作開始前,佢會喺似乎最需要嘅任何地方做啲義務勞動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他同一隻小公雞做了安排,讓他早晨比任何人早半小時叫醒他,在正式的一天工作開始前,他會在似乎最需要的任何地方做一些義務勞動。

passages.original: His answer to every problem, every setback, was “I will work harder!”--which he had adopted as his personal motto.
passages.vernacular: 佢對每個問題、每次挫折嘅回答都係「我要更努力工作!」——佢採用呢句話作為佢個人嘅座右銘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對每個問題、每次挫折的回答都是「我要更努力工作!」——他採用這句話作為他個人的座右銘。

passages.original: But everyone worked according to his capacity.
passages.vernacular: 但每個動物都按其能力工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但每個動物都按其能力工作。

passages.original: The hens and ducks, for instance, saved five bushels of corn at the harvest by gathering up the stray grains.
passages.vernacular: 例如,母雞同鴨子喺收割時,通過收集散落嘅穀粒,節省咗五蒲式耳嘅玉米。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 例如,母雞和鴨子在收割時,通過收集散落的穀粒,節省了五蒲式耳的玉米。

passages.original: Nobody stole, nobody grumbled over his rations, the quarrelling and biting and jealousy which had been normal features of life in the old days had almost disappeared.
passages.vernacular: 冇人偷嘢,冇人對自己嘅口糧抱怨,喺過去嘅日子裡曾係生活正常特徵嘅爭吵、撕咬同嫉妒幾乎消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人偷東西,沒有人對自己的口糧抱怨,在過去的日子裡曾是生活正常特徵的爭吵、撕咬和嫉妒幾乎消失了。

passages.original: Nobody shirked--or almost nobody.
passages.vernacular: 冇人偷懶——或者幾乎冇人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人偷懶——或者幾乎沒有人。

passages.original: Mollie, it was true, was not good at getting up in the mornings, and had a way of leaving work early on the ground that there was a stone in her hoof.
passages.vernacular: 茉莉確實不善於朝早起床,而且有一種習慣,藉口蹄子裡有塊石頭而提早離開工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 茉莉確實不善於早上起床,而且有一種習慣,藉口蹄子裡有塊石頭而提早離開工作。

passages.original: And the behaviour of the cat was somewhat peculiar.
passages.vernacular: 貓嘅行為都有些特別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貓的行為也有些特別。

passages.original: It was soon noticed that when there was work to be done the cat could never be found.
passages.vernacular: 好快就發現,有工作要做時,總是找唔到貓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很快就發現,有工作要做時,總是找不到貓。

passages.original: She would vanish for hours on end, and then reappear at meal-times, or in the evening after work was over, as though nothing had happened.
passages.vernacular: 佢會一連消失幾個小時,然後喺食飯時,或喺傍晚工作結束後重新出現,好像乜嘢事都冇發生過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會一連消失幾個小時,然後在吃飯時,或在傍晚工作結束後重新出現,好像什麼事也沒發生過。

passages.original: But she always made such excellent excuses, and purred so affectionately, that it was impossible not to believe in her good intentions.
passages.vernacular: 但佢總是找出咁好嘅藉口,呼嚕呼嚕地叫得咁親切,以致唔可能不相信佢嘅好意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她總是找出那麼好的藉口,呼嚕呼嚕地叫得那麼親切,以致不可能不相信她的好意。

passages.original: Old Benjamin, the donkey, seemed quite unchanged since the Rebellion.
passages.vernacular: 老驢子班傑明,似乎自造反以來完全冇變。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老驢子班傑明,似乎自造反以來完全沒變。

passages.original: He did his work in the same slow obstinate way as he had done it in Jones’s time, never shirking and never volunteering for extra work either.
passages.vernacular: 佢以同喺瓊斯時代同樣緩慢固執嘅方式做佢嘅工作,從不偷懶,都從不自願做額外嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他以和在瓊斯時代同樣緩慢固執的方式做他的工作,從不偷懶,也從不自願做額外的工作。

passages.original: About the Rebellion and its results he would express no opinion.
passages.vernacular: 對造反及其結果,佢不發表意見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對造反及其結果,他不發表意見。

passages.original: When asked whether he was not happier now that Jones was gone, he would say only “Donkeys live a long time.
passages.vernacular: 被問到瓊斯走咗佢係咪更快樂時,佢只會講:「驢子活得好長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被問到瓊斯走了他是否更快樂時,他只會說:「驢子活得很長。

passages.original: None of you has ever seen a dead donkey,” and the others had to be content with this cryptic answer.
passages.vernacular: 你哋邊個都冇見過死驢子,」其他動物只得滿足於呢個神秘嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們誰也沒見過死驢子,」其他動物只得滿足於這個神秘的回答。

passages.original: On Sundays there was no work.
passages.vernacular: 星期天不工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期天不工作。

passages.original: Breakfast was an hour later than usual, and after breakfast there was a ceremony which was observed every week without fail.
passages.vernacular: 早餐比平常晚一小時,早餐後有一個每週都不缺嘅儀式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早餐比平常晚一小時,早餐後有一個每週都不缺的儀式。

passages.original: First came the hoisting of the flag.
passages.vernacular: 首先係升旗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先是升旗。

passages.original: Snowball had found in the harness-room an old green tablecloth of Mrs. Jones’s and had painted on it a hoof and a horn in white.
passages.vernacular: 雪球喺馬具室裡找到一塊瓊斯太太嘅舊綠桌布,喺上面用白色畫咗一個蹄子同一隻角。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球在馬具室裡找到一塊瓊斯太太的舊綠桌布,在上面用白色畫了一個蹄子和一隻角。

passages.original: This was run up the flagstaff in the farmhouse garden every Sunday morning.
passages.vernacular: 每個星期天早晨,呢面旗都喺農舍花園嘅旗杆上升起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個星期天早晨,這面旗都在農舍花園的旗杆上升起。

passages.original: The flag was green, Snowball explained, to represent the green fields of England, while the hoof and horn signified the future Republic of the Animals which would arise when the human race had been finally overthrown.
passages.vernacular: 雪球解釋講,旗係綠色嘅,代表英格蘭嘅綠色田野,而蹄子同角象徵將來人類最終被推翻後將興起嘅動物共和國。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球解釋說,旗是綠色的,代表英格蘭的綠色田野,而蹄子和角象徵將來人類最終被推翻後將興起的動物共和國。

passages.original: After the hoisting of the flag all the animals trooped into the big barn for a general assembly which was known as the Meeting.
passages.vernacular: 升旗後,所有動物成群結隊進入大穀倉,參加一個被稱為「大會」嘅全體會議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 升旗後,所有動物成群結隊進入大穀倉,參加一個被稱為「大會」的全體會議。

passages.original: Here the work of the coming week was planned out and resolutions were put forward and debated.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,計畫下一週嘅工作,提出決議並辯論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,計畫下一週的工作,提出決議並辯論。

passages.original: It was always the pigs who put forward the resolutions.
passages.vernacular: 提出決議嘅總是豬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提出決議的總是豬。

passages.original: The other animals understood how to vote, but could never think of any resolutions of their own.
passages.vernacular: 其他動物懂得點樣投票,但自己想不出任何決議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他動物懂得怎樣投票,但自己想不出任何決議。

passages.original: Snowball and Napoleon were by far the most active in the debates.
passages.vernacular: 雪球同拿破崙係辯論中遠遠最積極嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球和拿破崙是辯論中遠遠最積極的。

passages.original: But it was noticed that these two were never in agreement: whatever suggestion either of them made, the other could be counted on to oppose it.
passages.vernacular: 但大家注意到呢兩位從不一致:無論其中一個提出乜嘢建議,另一個必定反對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但大家注意到這兩位從不一致:無論其中一個提出什麼建議,另一個必定反對。

passages.original: Even when it was resolved--a thing no one could object to in itself--to set aside the small paddock behind the orchard as a home of rest for animals who were past work, there was a stormy debate over the correct retiring age for each class of animal.
passages.vernacular: 甚至當通過一項決議時——呢本身係冇人能反對嘅事——把果園後面嘅小牧場留作畀已過工作年齡嘅動物嘅休養所,對每一類動物嘅正確退休年齡都有一場激烈嘅辯論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 甚至當通過一項決議時——這本身是沒人能反對的事——把果園後面的小牧場留作給已過工作年齡的動物的休養所,對每一類動物的正確退休年齡也有一場激烈的辯論。

passages.original: The Meeting always ended with the singing of ‘Beasts of England’, and the afternoon was given up to recreation.
passages.vernacular: 大會總是以唱《英格蘭之獸》結束,下午則用於娛樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大會總是以唱《英格蘭之獸》結束,下午則用於娛樂。

passages.original: The pigs had set aside the harness-room as a headquarters for themselves.
passages.vernacular: 豬哋把馬具室留作佢哋自己嘅總部。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬們把馬具室留作它們自己的總部。

passages.original: Here, in the evenings, they studied blacksmithing, carpentering, and other necessary arts from books which they had brought out of the farmhouse.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,晚上,佢哋從從農舍帶出嚟嘅書上學習打鐵、木工同其他必要嘅技藝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,晚上,它們從從農舍帶出來的書上學習打鐵、木工和其他必要的技藝。

passages.original: Snowball also busied himself with organising the other animals into what he called Animal Committees.
passages.vernacular: 雪球仲忙於把其他動物組織成佢所謂嘅動物委員會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球還忙於把其他動物組織成他所謂的動物委員會。

passages.original: He was indefatigable at this.
passages.vernacular: 佢對此唔知疲倦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對此不知疲倦。

passages.original: He formed the Egg Production Committee for the hens, the Clean Tails League for the cows, the Wild Comrades’ Re-education Committee (the object of this was to tame the rats and rabbits), the Whiter Wool Movement for the sheep, and various others, besides instituting classes in reading and writing.
passages.vernacular: 佢為母雞成立咗產蛋委員會,為母牛成立咗潔尾聯盟,為野生同志成立咗再教育委員會(其目的係馴服老鼠同兔子),為羊成立咗更白羊毛運動,以及其他各種組織,此外仲設立咗讀書寫字班。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他為母雞成立了產蛋委員會,為母牛成立了潔尾聯盟,為野生同志成立了再教育委員會(其目的是馴服老鼠和兔子),為羊成立了更白羊毛運動,以及其他各種組織,此外還設立了讀書寫字班。

passages.original: On the whole, these projects were a failure.
passages.vernacular: 總嘅來講,呢啲計畫係失敗嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總的來說,這些計畫是失敗的。

passages.original: The attempt to tame the wild creatures, for instance, broke down almost immediately.
passages.vernacular: 例如,馴服野生生物嘅嘗試幾乎即刻失敗喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 例如,馴服野生生物的嘗試幾乎立刻失敗了。

passages.original: They continued to behave very much as before, and when treated with generosity, simply took advantage of it.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋繼續像以前一樣行事,被慷慨對待時,只係加以利用。
