passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們繼續像以前一樣行事,被慷慨對待時,只是加以利用。

passages.original: The cat joined the Re-education Committee and was very active in it for some days.
passages.vernacular: 貓加入咗再教育委員會,有幾天好活躍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貓加入了再教育委員會,有幾天很活躍。

passages.original: She was seen one day sitting on a roof and talking to some sparrows who were just out of her reach.
passages.vernacular: 有一天有人睇到佢坐喺屋頂上,同啲剛好夠不住嘅麻雀講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天有人看到她坐在屋頂上,同一些剛好夠不著的麻雀說話。

passages.original: She was telling them that all animals were now comrades and that any sparrow who chose could come and perch on her paw; but the sparrows kept their distance.
passages.vernacular: 佢告訴佢哋,所有動物而家都係同志,任何麻雀只要願意都可以飛嚟棲喺佢嘅爪上;但麻雀哋保持住距離。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她告訴它們,所有動物現在都是同志,任何麻雀只要願意都可以飛來棲在她的爪上;但麻雀們保持著距離。

passages.original: The reading and writing classes, however, were a great success.
passages.vernacular: 不過,讀寫班大獲成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,讀寫班大獲成功。

passages.original: By the autumn almost every animal on the farm was literate in some degree.
passages.vernacular: 到秋天,農場上幾乎每個動物都有某種程度嘅識字能力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到秋天,農場上幾乎每個動物都有某種程度的識字能力。

passages.original: As for the pigs, they could already read and write perfectly.
passages.vernacular: 至於豬,佢哋已經能完美地讀寫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於豬,它們已經能完美地讀寫。

passages.original: The dogs learned to read fairly well, but were not interested in reading anything except the Seven Commandments.
passages.vernacular: 狗學會咗相當好地閱讀,但對七誡以外嘅任何嘢都冇興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗學會了相當好地閱讀,但對七誡以外的任何東西都沒有興趣。

passages.original: Muriel, the goat, could read somewhat better than the dogs, and sometimes used to read to the others in the evenings from scraps of newspaper which she found on the rubbish heap.
passages.vernacular: 山羊繆麗兒比狗讀得好啲,有時晚上會畀其他動物讀佢喺垃圾堆上找到嘅報紙碎片。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 山羊繆麗兒比狗讀得好一些,有時晚上會給其他動物讀她在垃圾堆上找到的報紙碎片。

passages.original: Benjamin could read as well as any pig, but never exercised his faculty.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明讀得同任何豬一樣好,但從不運用佢嘅能力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明讀得和任何豬一樣好,但從不運用他的能力。

passages.original: So far as he knew, he said, there was nothing worth reading.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,據佢所知,冇值得讀嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,據他所知,沒有值得讀的東西。

passages.original: Clover learnt the whole alphabet, but could not put words together.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草學會咗整個字母表,但唔能夠把字拼成詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草學會了整個字母表,但不能把字拼成詞。

passages.original: Boxer could not get beyond the letter D. He would trace out A, B, C, D, in the dust with his great hoof, and then would stand staring at the letters with his ears back, sometimes shaking his forelock, trying with all his might to remember what came next and never succeeding.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手學不過字母D。佢會用佢嘅大蹄子喺塵土中描出A、B、C、D,然後站喺嗰度盯住字母睇,耳朵向後,有時甩動佢嘅額髮,拚命想記起接下嚟係乜嘢,卻始終冇成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手學不過字母D。他會用他的大蹄子在塵土中描出A、B、C、D,然後站在那裡盯著字母看,耳朵向後,有時甩動他的額髮,拚命想記起接下來是什麼,卻始終沒有成功。

passages.original: On several occasions, indeed, he did learn E, F, G, H, but by the time he knew them, it was always discovered that he had forgotten A, B, C, and D. Finally he decided to be content with the first four letters, and used to write them out once or twice every day to refresh his memory.
passages.vernacular: 有幾次,佢確實學會咗E、F、G、H,但等佢學會咗佢哋,總是發現佢已忘咗A、B、C同D。最後佢決定滿足於前四個字母,每天寫一兩遍嚟溫習記憶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有幾次,他確實學會了E、F、G、H,但等他學會了它們,總是發現他已忘了A、B、C和D。最後他決定滿足於前四個字母,每天寫一兩遍來溫習記憶。

passages.original: Mollie refused to learn any but the six letters which spelt her own name.
passages.vernacular: 茉莉拒絕學習除拼寫佢自己名字嘅六個字母之外嘅任何字母。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 茉莉拒絕學習除拼寫她自己名字的六個字母之外的任何字母。

passages.original: She would form these very neatly out of pieces of twig, and would then decorate them with a flower or two and walk round them admiring them.
passages.vernacular: 佢會用小樹枝好整齊地拼出呢啲字母,然後用一兩朵花裝飾佢哋,繞住佢哋走,欣賞佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會用小樹枝很整齊地拼出這些字母,然後用一兩朵花裝飾它們,繞著它們走,欣賞它們。

passages.original: None of the other animals on the farm could get further than the letter A. It was also found that the stupider animals, such as the sheep, hens, and ducks, were unable to learn the Seven Commandments by heart.
passages.vernacular: 農場上冇其他動物能學過字母A。仲發現,比較笨嘅動物,如羊、母雞同鴨子,唔能夠把七誡背下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場上沒有其他動物能學過字母A。還發現,比較笨的動物,如羊、母雞和鴨子,不能把七誡背下來。

passages.original: After much thought Snowball declared that the Seven Commandments could in effect be reduced to a single maxim, namely: “Four legs good, two legs bad.”
passages.vernacular: 雪球想咗好多之後宣布,七誡實際上可以歸結為一條格言,即:「四條腿好,兩條腿壞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球想了很多之後宣布,七誡實際上可以歸結為一條格言,即:「四條腿好,兩條腿壞。」

passages.original: This, he said, contained the essential principle of Animalism.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,呢包含咗動物主義嘅基本原則。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,這包含了動物主義的基本原則。

passages.original: Whoever had thoroughly grasped it would be safe from human influences.
passages.vernacular: 任何徹底領會咗佢嘅,都將不受人類影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何徹底領會了它的,都將不受人類影響。

passages.original: The birds at first objected, since it seemed to them that they also had two legs, but Snowball proved to them that this was not so.
passages.vernacular: 鳥類起初反對,因為喺佢哋睇來佢哋都有兩條腿,但雪球向佢哋證明並非如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鳥類起初反對,因為在它們看來它們也有兩條腿,但雪球向它們證明並非如此。

passages.original: “A bird’s wing, comrades,” he said, “is an organ of propulsion and not of manipulation.
passages.vernacular: 「同志哋,」佢講,「鳥嘅翅膀係推進器官,而唔係操作器官。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志們,」他說,「鳥的翅膀是推進器官,而不是操作器官。

passages.original: It should therefore be regarded as a leg.
passages.vernacular: 因此佢應該被視為腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此它應該被視為腿。

passages.original: The distinguishing mark of man is the HAND, the instrument with which he does all his mischief.”
passages.vernacular: 人嘅特徵標誌係手,佢用佢嚟做所有壞事嘅工具。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人的特徵標誌是手,他用它來做所有壞事的工具。」

passages.original: The birds did not understand Snowball’s long words, but they accepted his explanation, and all the humbler animals set to work to learn the new maxim by heart.
passages.vernacular: 鳥類不懂雪球嘅長詞,但接受咗佢嘅解釋,所有比較卑微嘅動物開始努力背誦呢條新格言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鳥類不懂雪球的長詞,但接受了他的解釋,所有比較卑微的動物開始努力背誦這條新格言。

passages.original: FOUR LEGS GOOD, TWO LEGS BAD, was inscribed on the end wall of the barn, above the Seven Commandments and in bigger letters.
passages.vernacular: 四條腿好,兩條腿壞,被寫喺穀倉盡頭嘅牆上,喺七誡上方,字母更大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四條腿好,兩條腿壞,被寫在穀倉盡頭的牆上,在七誡上方,字母更大。

passages.original: When they had once got it by heart, the sheep developed a great liking for this maxim, and often as they lay in the field they would all start bleating “Four legs good, two legs bad!
passages.vernacular: 羊一旦背熟,就對呢條格言產生咗極大嘅喜愛,佢哋躺喺田裡時,常常全都開始咩咩地叫「四條腿好,兩條腿壞!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羊一旦背熟,就對這條格言產生了極大的喜愛,它們躺在田裡時,常常全都開始咩咩地叫「四條腿好,兩條腿壞!

passages.original: Four legs good, two legs bad!” and keep it up for hours on end, never growing tired of it.
passages.vernacular: 四條腿好,兩條腿壞!」一連幾個小時不停,從不厭倦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四條腿好,兩條腿壞!」一連幾個小時不停,從不厭倦。

passages.original: Napoleon took no interest in Snowball’s committees.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙對雪球嘅委員會不感興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙對雪球的委員會不感興趣。

passages.original: He said that the education of the young was more important than anything that could be done for those who were already grown up.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,年輕一代嘅教育比為已經成年嘅做任何事情都更重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,年輕一代的教育比為已經成年的做任何事情都更重要。

passages.original: It happened that Jessie and Bluebell had both whelped soon after the hay harvest, giving birth between them to nine sturdy puppies.
passages.vernacular: 碰巧潔西同藍鈴喺乾草收割後不久都下咗崽,兩者一共生咗九隻健壯嘅小狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 碰巧潔西和藍鈴在乾草收割後不久都下了崽,兩者一共生了九隻健壯的小狗。

passages.original: As soon as they were weaned, Napoleon took them away from their mothers, saying that he would make himself responsible for their education.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋一斷奶,拿破崙就把佢哋從母親身邊帶走,講佢會負責佢哋嘅教育。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們一斷奶,拿破崙就把它們從母親身邊帶走,說他會負責它們的教育。

passages.original: He took them up into a loft which could only be reached by a ladder from the harness-room, and there kept them in such seclusion that the rest of the farm soon forgot their existence.
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢哋帶到一個只能從馬具室通過梯子到達嘅閣樓上,把佢哋養喺如此隱蔽嘅地方,農場嘅其他動物好快就忘咗佢哋嘅存在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把它們帶到一個只能從馬具室通過梯子到達的閣樓上,把它們養在如此隱蔽的地方,農場的其他動物很快就忘了它們的存在。

passages.original: The mystery of where the milk went to was soon cleared up.
passages.vernacular: 牛奶去向嘅謎團好快就解開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牛奶去向的謎團很快就解開了。

passages.original: It was mixed every day into the pigs’ mash.
passages.vernacular: 佢每天被混進豬嘅飼料。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它每天被混進豬的飼料。

passages.original: The early apples were now ripening, and the grass of the orchard was littered with windfalls.
passages.vernacular: 早熟嘅蘋果而家熟喇,果園嘅草地上到處係落果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早熟的蘋果現在熟了,果園的草地上到處是落果。

passages.original: The animals had assumed as a matter of course that these would be shared out equally; one day, however, the order went forth that all the windfalls were to be collected and brought to the harness-room for the use of the pigs.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋理所當然地認為呢啲會平均分配;然而有一天,命令下嚟,所有落果都要收集起嚟,送到馬具室供豬使用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們理所當然地認為這些會平均分配;然而有一天,命令下來,所有落果都要收集起來,送到馬具室供豬使用。

passages.original: At this some of the other animals murmured, but it was no use.
passages.vernacular: 對此其他啲動物低聲抱怨,但冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對此其他一些動物低聲抱怨,但沒有用。

passages.original: All the pigs were in full agreement on this point, even Snowball and Napoleon.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅豬喺呢啲上完全一致,甚至雪球同拿破崙都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的豬在這一點上完全一致,甚至雪球和拿破崙也是。

passages.original: Squealer was sent to make the necessary explanations to the others.
passages.vernacular: 尖嗓子被派去向其他動物作必要嘅解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尖嗓子被派去向其他動物作必要的解釋。

passages.original: “Comrades!” he cried.
passages.vernacular: 「同志哋!」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志們!」他喊道。

passages.original: “You do not imagine, I hope, that we pigs are doing this in a spirit of selfishness and privilege?
passages.vernacular: 「我希望你哋唔好想像,我哋豬咁樣做係出於自私同特權嘅精神吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望你們不要想像,我們豬這樣做是出於自私和特權的精神吧?

passages.original: Many of us actually dislike milk and apples.
passages.vernacular: 我哋許多人其實不鍾意牛奶同蘋果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們許多人其實不喜歡牛奶和蘋果。

passages.original: I dislike them myself.
passages.vernacular: 我自己就不鍾意佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己就不喜歡它們。

passages.original: Our sole object in taking these things is to preserve our health.
passages.vernacular: 我哋攞呢啲嘢嘅唯一目的係保持我哋嘅健康。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們拿這些東西的唯一目的是保持我們的健康。

passages.original: Milk and apples (this has been proved by Science, comrades) contain substances absolutely necessary to the well-being of a pig.
passages.vernacular: 牛奶同蘋果(呢個係科學證明嘅,同志哋)含有對豬嘅福祉絕對必要嘅物質。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牛奶和蘋果(這是科學證明的,同志們)含有對豬的福祉絕對必要的物質。

passages.original: We pigs are brainworkers.
passages.vernacular: 我哋豬係腦力工作者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們豬是腦力工作者。

passages.original: The whole management and organisation of this farm depend on us.
passages.vernacular: 呢個農場嘅整個管理同組織都靠我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個農場的整個管理和組織都靠我們。

passages.original: Day and night we are watching over your welfare.
passages.vernacular: 日日夜夜我哋都喺照睇你哋嘅福利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 日日夜夜我們都在照看你們的福利。

passages.original: It is for YOUR sake that we drink that milk and eat those apples.
passages.vernacular: 我哋飲嗰牛奶、食嗰啲蘋果,係為了你哋嘅緣故。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們喝那牛奶、吃那些蘋果,是為了你們的緣故。

passages.original: Do you know what would happen if we pigs failed in our duty?
passages.vernacular: 你哋知道,如果我哋豬不盡職責,會發生乜嘢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們知道,如果我們豬不盡職責,會發生什麼嗎?

passages.original: Jones would come back!
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯會回嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯會回來!

passages.original: Yes, Jones would come back!
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,瓊斯會回嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,瓊斯會回來!

passages.original: Surely, comrades,” cried Squealer almost pleadingly, skipping from side to side and whisking his tail, “surely there is no one among you who wants to see Jones come back?”
passages.vernacular: 同志哋,肯定,」尖嗓子幾乎係懇求地喊道,左右蹦跳,甩動住尾巴,「肯定你哋中冇邊個想睇到瓊斯回嚟吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同志們,肯定,」尖嗓子幾乎是懇求地喊道,左右蹦跳,甩動著尾巴,「肯定你們中沒有誰想看到瓊斯回來吧?」

passages.original: Now if there was one thing that the animals were completely certain of, it was that they did not want Jones back.
passages.vernacular: 而家,如果動物哋有乜嘢事完全確定,嗰個就係佢哋唔想要瓊斯回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,如果動物們有什麼事完全確定,那就是它們不想要瓊斯回來。

passages.original: When it was put to them in this light, they had no more to say.
passages.vernacular: 以呢種方式向佢哋提出時,佢哋再冇乜嘢可講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以這種方式向它們提出時,它們再沒什麼可說。

passages.original: The importance of keeping the pigs in good health was all too obvious.
passages.vernacular: 保持豬嘅健康嘅重要性實在太明顯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保持豬的健康的重要性實在太明顯了。

passages.original: So it was agreed without further argument that the milk and the windfall apples (and also the main crop of apples when they ripened) should be reserved for the pigs alone.
passages.vernacular: 所以未經進一步爭論,就一致同意牛奶同落果(以及蘋果成熟時嘅主要收成)應該只留畀豬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以未經進一步爭論,就一致同意牛奶和落果(以及蘋果成熟時的主要收成)應該只留給豬。

chapters.title: Chapter IV 第四章:牛棚之戰

passages.original: By the late summer the news of what had happened on Animal Farm had spread across half the county.
passages.vernacular: 到夏末,動物農莊發生之事嘅消息已傳遍半個郡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到夏末,動物農莊發生之事的消息已傳遍半個郡。

passages.original: Every day Snowball and Napoleon sent out flights of pigeons whose instructions were to mingle with the animals on neighbouring farms, tell them the story of the Rebellion, and teach them the tune of ‘Beasts of England’.
passages.vernacular: 雪球同拿破崙每天都派出成群嘅鴿子,佢哋嘅指示係混入鄰近農場嘅動物中,把造反嘅故事告訴佢哋,教佢哋《英格蘭之獸》嘅調子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球和拿破崙每天都派出成群的鴿子,它們的指示是混入鄰近農場的動物中,把造反的故事告訴它們,教它們《英格蘭之獸》的調子。

passages.original: Most of this time Mr. Jones had spent sitting in the taproom of the Red Lion at Willingdon, complaining to anyone who would listen of the monstrous injustice he had suffered in being turned out of his property by a pack of good-for-nothing animals.
passages.vernacular: 呢段時間,瓊斯先生大部分時間坐喺威靈頓紅獅酒館嘅酒吧間裡,向任何肯聽嘅人抱怨佢因被一群無用嘅動物趕出自己嘅財產而遭受嘅駭人不公。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這段時間,瓊斯先生大部分時間坐在威靈頓紅獅酒館的酒吧間裡,向任何肯聽的人抱怨他因被一群無用的動物趕出自己的財產而遭受的駭人不公。

passages.original: The other farmers sympathised in principle, but they did not at first give him much help.
passages.vernacular: 其他農場主原則上表示同情,但起初冇畀佢多少幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他農場主原則上表示同情,但起初沒有給他多少幫助。

passages.original: At heart, each of them was secretly wondering whether he could not somehow turn Jones’s misfortune to his own advantage.
passages.vernacular: 在內心深處,佢哋每個人都暗暗喺想,能唔能夠以某種方式把瓊斯嘅不幸轉為對自己嘅好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在內心深處,他們每個人都暗暗在想,能不能以某種方式把瓊斯的不幸轉為對自己的好處。

passages.original: It was lucky that the owners of the two farms which adjoined Animal Farm were on permanently bad terms.
passages.vernacular: 幸運嘅係,同動物農莊毗鄰嘅兩個農場嘅主人關係一直好壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸運的是,與動物農莊毗鄰的兩個農場的主人關係一直很壞。

passages.original: One of them, which was named Foxwood, was a large, neglected, old-fashioned farm, much overgrown by woodland, with all its pastures worn out and its hedges in a disgraceful condition.
passages.vernacular: 其中一個名叫狐林,係個大而被忽視嘅老式農場,被林地大量覆蓋,所有牧場都用盡喇,樹籬嘅狀況好不像話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中一個名叫狐林,是個大而被忽視的老式農場,被林地大量覆蓋,所有牧場都用盡了,樹籬的狀況很不像話。

passages.original: Its owner, Mr. Pilkington, was an easy-going gentleman farmer who spent most of his time in fishing or hunting according to the season.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅主人皮爾金頓先生係個隨同嘅紳士農夫,大部分時間按季節用於釣魚或打獵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的主人皮爾金頓先生是個隨和的紳士農夫,大部分時間按季節用於釣魚或打獵。

passages.original: The other farm, which was called Pinchfield, was smaller and better kept.
passages.vernacular: 另一個農場叫平奇菲爾德,比較小,都管理得較好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一個農場叫平奇菲爾德,比較小,也管理得較好。

passages.original: Its owner was a Mr. Frederick, a tough, shrewd man, perpetually involved in lawsuits and with a name for driving hard bargains.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅主人係弗雷德里克先生,一個頑強精明嘅人,永遠捲入官司,以斤斤計較討價仲價出名。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的主人是弗雷德里克先生,一個頑強精明的人,永遠捲入官司,以斤斤計較討價還價出名。

passages.original: These two disliked each other so much that it was difficult for them to come to any agreement, even in defence of their own interests.
passages.vernacular: 呢兩人咁互相不鍾意,即使為了捍衛佢哋自己嘅利益,都好難達成任何協議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這兩人那麼互相不喜歡,即使為了捍衛他們自己的利益,也很難達成任何協議。

passages.original: Nevertheless, they were both thoroughly frightened by the rebellion on Animal Farm, and very anxious to prevent their own animals from learning too much about it.
passages.vernacular: 然而,佢哋都被動物農莊嘅造反徹底嚇壞喇,好急於防止佢哋自己嘅動物對此知道太多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,他們都被動物農莊的造反徹底嚇壞了,非常急於防止他們自己的動物對此知道太多。

passages.original: At first they pretended to laugh to scorn the idea of animals managing a farm for themselves.
passages.vernacular: 起初佢哋假裝嗤笑動物自己管理農場嘅想法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初他們假裝嗤笑動物自己管理農場的想法。

passages.original: The whole thing would be over in a fortnight, they said.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋講,整件事兩個星期內就會結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們說,整件事兩個星期內就會結束。

passages.original: They put it about that the animals on the Manor Farm (they insisted on calling it the Manor Farm; they would not tolerate the name “Animal Farm”) were perpetually fighting among themselves and were also rapidly starving to death.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋散佈講,曼諾農場嘅動物(佢哋堅持叫佢曼諾農場;佢哋唔能夠容忍「動物農莊」呢個名字)不斷互相打鬥,而且正在迅速餓死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們散佈說,曼諾農場的動物(他們堅持叫它曼諾農場;他們不能容忍「動物農莊」這個名字)不斷互相打鬥,而且正在迅速餓死。

passages.original: When time passed and the animals had evidently not starved to death, Frederick and Pilkington changed their tune and began to talk of the terrible wickedness that now flourished on Animal Farm.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一段時間,動物哋顯然冇餓死,弗雷德里克同皮爾金頓改變咗調子,開始談論而家喺動物農莊盛行嘅可怕邪惡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一段時間,動物們顯然沒有餓死,弗雷德里克和皮爾金頓改變了調子,開始談論現在在動物農莊盛行的可怕邪惡。

passages.original: It was given out that the animals there practised cannibalism, tortured one another with red-hot horseshoes, and had their females in common.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋放出消息講,嗰度嘅動物實行食同類嘅習俗,用燒紅嘅馬蹄鐵互相折磨,並且共妻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們放出消息說,那裡的動物實行吃同類的習俗,用燒紅的馬蹄鐵互相折磨,並且共妻。

passages.original: This was what came of rebelling against the laws of Nature, Frederick and Pilkington said.
passages.vernacular: 弗雷德里克同皮爾金頓講,呢個就係反抗自然法則嘅結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗雷德里克和皮爾金頓說,這就是反抗自然法則的結果。

passages.original: However, these stories were never fully believed.
passages.vernacular: 不過,呢啲故事從未被完全相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,這些故事從未被完全相信。

passages.original: Rumours of a wonderful farm, where the human beings had been turned out and the animals managed their own affairs, continued to circulate in vague and distorted forms, and throughout that year a wave of rebelliousness ran through the countryside.
passages.vernacular: 關於一個奇妙農場嘅傳聞,嗰度人類被趕走,動物自己管理自己嘅事,繼續以模糊同扭曲嘅形式流傳,嗰一年整個鄉間掀起咗一股反叛嘅浪潮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 關於一個奇妙農場的傳聞,那裡人類被趕走,動物自己管理自己的事,繼續以模糊和扭曲的形式流傳,那一年整個鄉間掀起了一股反叛的浪潮。

passages.original: Bulls which had always been tractable suddenly turned savage, sheep broke down hedges and devoured the clover, cows kicked the pail over, hunters refused their fences and shot their riders on to the other side.
passages.vernacular: 一向溫順嘅公牛突然變得凶猛,羊弄壞樹籬食掉三葉草,母牛踢翻奶桶,獵馬拒絕跳籬,把騎手摔到另一邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一向溫順的公牛突然變得凶猛,羊弄壞樹籬吃掉三葉草,母牛踢翻奶桶,獵馬拒絕跳籬,把騎手摔到另一邊。

passages.original: Above all, the tune and even the words of ‘Beasts of England’ were known everywhere.
passages.vernacular: 最重要嘅係,《英格蘭之獸》嘅調子,甚至歌詞,到處都知道喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最重要的是,《英格蘭之獸》的調子,甚至歌詞,到處都知道了。

passages.original: It had spread with astonishing speed.
passages.vernacular: 佢以驚人嘅速度傳播。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它以驚人的速度傳播。

passages.original: The human beings could not contain their rage when they heard this song, though they pretended to think it merely ridiculous.
passages.vernacular: 人類聽到呢首歌時按捺不住怒火,雖然佢哋假裝認為佢只係可笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人類聽到這首歌時按捺不住怒火,雖然他們假裝認為它只是可笑。

passages.original: They could not understand, they said, how even animals could bring themselves to sing such contemptible rubbish.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋講,佢哋唔能夠理解,動物點能讓自己唱咁樣可鄙嘅廢話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們說,他們不能理解,動物怎麼能讓自己唱這樣可鄙的廢話。

passages.original: Any animal caught singing it was given a flogging on the spot.
passages.vernacular: 任何被抓到唱呢首歌嘅動物都當場挨一頓鞭打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何被抓到唱這首歌的動物都當場挨一頓鞭打。

passages.original: And yet the song was irrepressible.
passages.vernacular: 然而呢首歌係壓制不住嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而這首歌是壓制不住的。

passages.original: The blackbirds whistled it in the hedges, the pigeons cooed it in the elms, it got into the din of the smithies and the tune of the church bells.
passages.vernacular: 黑鳥喺樹籬裡吹口哨唱佢,鴿子喺榆樹上咕咕地唱佢,佢進入咗鐵匠鋪嘅喧鬧同教堂鐘聲嘅調子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黑鳥在樹籬裡吹口哨唱它,鴿子在榆樹上咕咕地唱它,它進入了鐵匠鋪的喧鬧和教堂鐘聲的調子。

passages.original: And when the human beings listened to it, they secretly trembled, hearing in it a prophecy of their future doom.
passages.vernacular: 人類聽佢時,暗暗顫抖,喺其中聽到佢哋未來厄運嘅預言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人類聽它時,暗暗顫抖,在其中聽到他們未來厄運的預言。

passages.original: Early in October, when the corn was cut and stacked and some of it was already threshed, a flight of pigeons came whirling through the air and alighted in the yard of Animal Farm in the wildest excitement.
passages.vernacular: 十月初,玉米已收割堆好,有些已經脫粒,一群鴿子喺空中盤旋而嚟,喺最瘋狂嘅興奮中降落喺動物農莊嘅院子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十月初,玉米已收割堆好,有些已經脫粒,一群鴿子在空中盤旋而來,在最瘋狂的興奮中降落在動物農莊的院子裡。

passages.original: Jones and all his men, with half a dozen others from Foxwood and Pinchfield, had entered the five-barred gate and were coming up the cart-track that led to the farm.
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯同佢所有嘅人,連同來自狐林和平奇菲爾德嘅六七個人,已經進咗五柵欄大門,正沿住通往農場嘅車道走嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯和他所有的人,連同來自狐林和平奇菲爾德的六七個人,已經進了五柵欄大門,正沿著通往農場的車道走來。

passages.original: They were all carrying sticks, except Jones, who was marching ahead with a gun in his hands.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都攞住棍子,除咗瓊斯,佢走喺前面,手裡攞住一桿槍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們都拿著棍子,除了瓊斯,他走在前面,手裡拿著一桿槍。

passages.original: Obviously they were going to attempt the recapture of the farm.
passages.vernacular: 顯然佢哋要設法奪回農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 顯然他們要設法奪回農場。

passages.original: This had long been expected, and all preparations had been made.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係早就預料到嘅,所有準備都已做好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是早就預料到的,所有準備都已做好。

passages.original: Snowball, who had studied an old book of Julius Caesar’s campaigns which he had found in the farmhouse, was in charge of the defensive operations.
passages.vernacular: 雪球研究過一本佢喺農舍找到嘅關於尤利烏斯·凱撒戰役嘅舊書,負責防禦作戰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球研究過一本他在農舍找到的關於尤利烏斯·凱撒戰役的舊書,負責防禦作戰。

passages.original: He gave his orders quickly, and in a couple of minutes every animal was at his post.
passages.vernacular: 佢迅速下達命令,幾分鐘內每個動物都喺自己嘅崗位上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他迅速下達命令,幾分鐘內每個動物都在自己的崗位上。

passages.original: As the human beings approached the farm buildings, Snowball launched his first attack.
passages.vernacular: 人類走近農場建築時,雪球發動咗佢嘅第一次進攻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人類走近農場建築時,雪球發動了他的第一次進攻。

passages.original: All the pigeons, to the number of thirty-five, flew to and fro over the men’s heads and muted upon them from mid-air; and while the men were dealing with this, the geese, who had been hiding behind the hedge, rushed out and pecked viciously at the calves of their legs.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅鴿子,共三十五隻,喺人哋頭頂嚟回飛翔,從半空中向佢哋排泄;人哋正忙於應付呢個時,一直藏喺樹籬後面嘅鵝衝出嚟,凶狠地啄佢哋嘅小腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的鴿子,共三十五隻,在人們頭頂來回飛翔,從半空中向他們排泄;人們正忙於應付這個時,一直藏在樹籬後面的鵝衝出來,凶狠地啄他們的小腿。

passages.original: However, this was only a light skirmishing manoeuvre, intended to create a little disorder, and the men easily drove the geese off with their sticks.
passages.vernacular: 不過,呢只係一次輕微嘅小規模騷擾行動,目的係製造啲混亂,人哋好容易用棍子把鵝趕走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,這只是一次輕微的小規模騷擾行動,目的是製造一點混亂,人們很容易用棍子把鵝趕走了。

passages.original: Snowball now launched his second line of attack.
passages.vernacular: 雪球而家發動佢嘅第二道攻擊線。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球現在發動他的第二道攻擊線。

passages.original: Muriel, Benjamin, and all the sheep, with Snowball at the head of them, rushed forward and prodded and butted the men from every side, while Benjamin turned around and lashed at them with his small hoofs.
passages.vernacular: 繆麗兒、班傑明,同所有嘅羊,由雪球帶頭,衝上前去,從各個方向戳頂呢啲人,而班傑明轉過身,用佢嘅小蹄子踢佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繆麗兒、班傑明,和所有的羊,由雪球帶頭,衝上前去,從各個方向戳頂這些人,而班傑明轉過身,用他的小蹄子踢他們。

passages.original: But once again the men, with their sticks and their hobnailed boots, were too strong for them; and suddenly, at a squeal from Snowball, which was the signal for retreat, all the animals turned and fled through the gateway into the yard.
passages.vernacular: 但係人哋憑佢哋嘅棍子同釘鞋,又一次太強大喇;突然,隨住雪球嘅一聲尖叫(嗰個係撤退嘅信號),所有動物轉身,穿過大門逃進院子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是人們憑他們的棍子和釘鞋,又一次太強大了;突然,隨著雪球的一聲尖叫(那是撤退的信號),所有動物轉身,穿過大門逃進院子。

passages.original: The men gave a shout of triumph.
passages.vernacular: 人哋發出勝利嘅叫喊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們發出勝利的叫喊。

passages.original: They saw, as they imagined, their enemies in flight, and they rushed after them in disorder.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋睇到,如佢哋所想像嘅,佢哋嘅敵人喺逃跑,就亂糟糟地衝進去追趕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們看到,如他們所想像的,他們的敵人在逃跑,就亂糟糟地衝進去追趕。

passages.original: This was just what Snowball had intended.
passages.vernacular: 呢正是雪球想要嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這正是雪球想要的。

passages.original: As soon as they were well inside the yard, the three horses, the three cows, and the rest of the pigs, who had been lying in ambush in the cowshed, suddenly emerged in their rear, cutting them off.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋剛一深入院子,嗰三匹馬、三頭母牛,同其餘嘅豬,一直埋伏喺牛棚裡,突然出而家佢哋後方,切斷咗佢哋嘅退路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們剛一深入院子,那三匹馬、三頭母牛,和其餘的豬,一直埋伏在牛棚裡,突然出現在他們後方,切斷了他們的退路。

passages.original: Snowball now gave the signal for the charge.
passages.vernacular: 雪球而家發出衝鋒嘅信號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球現在發出衝鋒的信號。

passages.original: He himself dashed straight for Jones.
passages.vernacular: 佢自己直衝向瓊斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他自己直衝向瓊斯。

passages.original: Jones saw him coming, raised his gun and fired.
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯睇到佢衝嚟,舉起槍開火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯看到他衝來,舉起槍開火。

passages.original: The pellets scored bloody streaks along Snowball’s back, and a sheep dropped dead.
passages.vernacular: 彈丸喺雪球嘅背上劃出血淋淋嘅條痕,一隻羊倒地死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彈丸在雪球的背上劃出血淋淋的條痕,一隻羊倒地死了。

passages.original: Without halting for an instant, Snowball flung his fifteen stone against Jones’s legs.
passages.vernacular: 雪球一刻都冇停,把佢十五英石嘅重量撞向瓊斯嘅腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球一刻也沒停,把他十五英石的重量撞向瓊斯的腿。

passages.original: Jones was hurled into a pile of dung and his gun flew out of his hands.
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯被摔進一堆糞便,佢嘅槍從手中飛出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯被摔進一堆糞便,他的槍從手中飛出。

passages.original: But the most terrifying spectacle of all was Boxer, rearing up on his hind legs and striking out with his great iron-shod hoofs like a stallion.
passages.vernacular: 但最可怕嘅景象係拳擊手,用後腿豎起,像種馬一樣用佢巨大嘅鐵蹄子猛擊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但最可怕的景象是拳擊手,用後腿豎起,像種馬一樣用他巨大的鐵蹄子猛擊。

passages.original: His very first blow took a stable-lad from Foxwood on the skull and stretched him lifeless in the mud.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅第一擊就打中咗一個來自狐林嘅馬夫嘅頭骨,把佢毫無生氣地打倒喺泥裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的第一擊就打中了一個來自狐林的馬夫的頭骨,把他毫無生氣地打倒在泥裡。

passages.original: At the sight, several men dropped their sticks and tried to run.
passages.vernacular: 睇到呢景象,幾個人扔下棍子,想逃跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到這景象,幾個人扔下棍子,想逃跑。

passages.original: Panic overtook them, and the next moment all the animals together were chasing them round and round the yard.
passages.vernacular: 恐慌襲上咗佢哋,下一刻所有動物一起追趕佢哋,喺院子裡一圈又一圈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 恐慌襲上了他們,下一刻所有動物一起追趕他們,在院子裡一圈又一圈。

passages.original: They were gored, kicked, bitten, trampled on.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋被頂、被踢、被咬、被踩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們被頂、被踢、被咬、被踩。

passages.original: There was not an animal on the farm that did not take vengeance on them after his own fashion.
passages.vernacular: 農場上冇一個動物不按自己嘅方式向佢哋報復。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場上沒有一個動物不按自己的方式向他們報復。

passages.original: Even the cat suddenly leapt off a roof onto a cowman’s shoulders and sank her claws in his neck, at which he yelled horribly.
passages.vernacular: 連貓都突然從屋頂跳到一個牛倌嘅肩上,把爪子扎進佢嘅脖子,佢可怕地叫起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連貓也突然從屋頂跳到一個牛倌的肩上,把爪子扎進他的脖子,他可怕地叫起來。

passages.original: At a moment when the opening was clear, the men were glad enough to rush out of the yard and make a bolt for the main road.
passages.vernacular: 出口一空出嚟,人哋就好高興地衝出院子,向大路奪路而逃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 出口一空出來,人們就很高興地衝出院子,向大路奪路而逃。

passages.original: And so within five minutes of their invasion they were in ignominious retreat by the same way as they had come, with a flock of geese hissing after them and pecking at their calves all the way.
passages.vernacular: 於是喺入侵後五分鐘內,佢哋就沿住嚟時嘅路屈辱地撤退,一群鵝喺佢哋後面嘶嘶叫住,一路啄佢哋嘅小腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是在入侵後五分鐘內,他們就沿著來時的路屈辱地撤退,一群鵝在他們後面嘶嘶叫著,一路啄他們的小腿。

passages.original: All the men were gone except one.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅人都走喇,除咗一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的人都走了,除了一個。

passages.original: Back in the yard Boxer was pawing with his hoof at the stable-lad who lay face down in the mud, trying to turn him over.
passages.vernacular: 回到院子裡,拳擊手正在用蹄子撥弄嗰個臉朝下躺喺泥裡嘅馬夫,想把佢翻過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回到院子裡,拳擊手正在用蹄子撥弄那個臉朝下躺在泥裡的馬夫,想把他翻過來。

passages.original: The boy did not stir.
passages.vernacular: 嗰男孩一動不動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那男孩一動不動。

passages.original: “He is dead,” said Boxer sorrowfully.
passages.vernacular: 「佢死喇,」拳擊手悲傷地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他死了,」拳擊手悲傷地說。

passages.original: “I had no intention of doing that.
passages.vernacular: 「我無意咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我無意這樣做。

passages.original: I forgot that I was wearing iron shoes.
passages.vernacular: 我忘咗我穿住鐵鞋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忘了我穿著鐵鞋。

passages.original: Who will believe that I did not do this on purpose?”
passages.vernacular: 邊個會相信我唔係故意咁樣做嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰會相信我不是故意這樣做的?」

passages.original: “No sentimentality, comrade!” cried Snowball from whose wounds the blood was still dripping.
passages.vernacular: 「別感情用事,同志!」雪球喊道,佢嘅傷口仍喺滴血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別感情用事,同志!」雪球喊道,他的傷口仍在滴血。

passages.original: “War is war.
passages.vernacular: 「戰爭就係戰爭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「戰爭就是戰爭。

passages.original: The only good human being is a dead one.”
passages.vernacular: 唯一好嘅人係死嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唯一好的人是死的人。」

passages.original: “I have no wish to take life, not even human life,” repeated Boxer, and his eyes were full of tears.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔想奪取生命,連人嘅生命都唔想,」拳擊手重複講,眼裡滿係淚水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不想奪取生命,連人的生命也不想,」拳擊手重複說,眼裡滿是淚水。

passages.original: “Where is Mollie?” exclaimed somebody.
passages.vernacular: 「茉莉喺邊度?」有人喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「茉莉在哪裡?」有人喊道。

passages.original: Mollie in fact was missing.
passages.vernacular: 茉莉確實唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 茉莉確實不見了。

passages.original: For a moment there was great alarm; it was feared that the men might have harmed her in some way, or even carried her off with them.
passages.vernacular: 有一刻好驚慌;擔心嗰啲人可能以某種方式傷害咗佢,甚至把佢帶走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一刻非常驚慌;擔心那些人可能以某種方式傷害了她,甚至把她帶走了。

passages.original: In the end, however, she was found hiding in her stall with her head buried among the hay in the manger.
passages.vernacular: 不過最後,佢被發現躲喺自己嘅馬廄裡,頭埋喺飼槽嘅乾草中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過最後,她被發現躲在自己的馬廄裡,頭埋在飼槽的乾草中。

passages.original: She had taken to flight as soon as the gun went off.
passages.vernacular: 槍一響佢就逃跑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 槍一響她就逃跑了。

passages.original: And when the others came back from looking for her, it was to find that the stable-lad, who in fact was only stunned, had already recovered and made off.
passages.vernacular: 當其他動物找佢回嚟時,發現嗰個馬夫,其實只係被打昏,已經蘇醒並逃走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當其他動物找她回來時,發現那個馬夫,其實只是被打昏,已經蘇醒並逃走了。

passages.original: The animals had now reassembled in the wildest excitement, each recounting his own exploits in the battle at the top of his voice.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋而家喺最瘋狂嘅興奮中重新集合,每個都以最大嘅聲音講述自己喺戰鬥中嘅功績。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們現在在最瘋狂的興奮中重新集合,每個都以最大的聲音講述自己在戰鬥中的功績。

passages.original: An impromptu celebration of the victory was held immediately.
passages.vernacular: 即刻舉行咗一個即興嘅勝利慶祝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 立刻舉行了一個即興的勝利慶祝。

passages.original: The flag was run up and ‘Beasts of England’ was sung a number of times, then the sheep who had been killed was given a solemn funeral, a hawthorn bush being planted on her grave.
passages.vernacular: 旗升起喇,《英格蘭之獸》唱咗好幾遍,然後畀被殺嘅羊舉行咗莊嚴嘅葬禮,喺佢嘅墳上種咗一株山楂樹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 旗升起了,《英格蘭之獸》唱了好幾遍,然後給被殺的羊舉行了莊嚴的葬禮,在她的墳上種了一株山楂樹。

passages.original: At the graveside Snowball made a little speech, emphasising the need for all animals to be ready to die for Animal Farm if need be.
passages.vernacular: 喺墓旁,雪球作咗一個簡短嘅演講,強調所有動物需要準備好必要時為動物農莊獻身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在墓旁,雪球作了一個簡短的演講,強調所有動物需要準備好必要時為動物農莊獻身。

passages.original: The animals decided unanimously to create a military decoration, “Animal Hero, First Class,” which was conferred there and then on Snowball and Boxer.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋一致決定設立一枚軍功勳章,「一級動物英雄」,當場授予雪球同拳擊手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們一致決定設立一枚軍功勳章,「一級動物英雄」,當場授予雪球和拳擊手。

passages.original: It consisted of a brass medal (they were really some old horse-brasses which had been found in the harness-room), to be worn on Sundays and holidays.
passages.vernacular: 佢由一枚黃銅獎章組成(實際上係喺馬具室找到嘅啲舊馬飾銅牌),星期天同節日佩戴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它由一枚黃銅獎章組成(實際上是在馬具室找到的一些舊馬飾銅牌),星期天和節日佩戴。

passages.original: There was also “Animal Hero, Second Class,” which was conferred posthumously on the dead sheep.
passages.vernacular: 仲有「二級動物英雄」,追授畀死去嘅羊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有「二級動物英雄」,追授給死去的羊。

passages.original: There was much discussion as to what the battle should be called.
passages.vernacular: 對呢場戰鬥應該叫乜嘢,有好多討論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對這場戰鬥應該叫什麼,有很多討論。

passages.original: In the end, it was named the Battle of the Cowshed, since that was where the ambush had been sprung.
passages.vernacular: 最後,佢被命名為牛棚之戰,因為埋伏就係喺嗰度發動嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後,它被命名為牛棚之戰,因為埋伏就是在那裡發動的。

passages.original: Mr. Jones’s gun had been found lying in the mud, and it was known that there was a supply of cartridges in the farmhouse.
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯先生嘅槍被發現躺喺泥裡,而且知道農舍裡有一批子彈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯先生的槍被發現躺在泥裡,而且知道農舍裡有一批子彈。

passages.original: It was decided to set the gun up at the foot of the Flagstaff, like a piece of artillery, and to fire it twice a year--once on October the twelfth, the anniversary of the Battle of the Cowshed, and once on Midsummer Day, the anniversary of the Rebellion.
passages.vernacular: 決定把槍像一尊大炮一樣架設喺旗杆腳下,每年開兩次——一次喺十月十二日,牛棚之戰嘅紀念日,一次喺仲夏日,造反嘅紀念日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 決定把槍像一尊大炮一樣架設在旗杆腳下,每年開兩次——一次在十月十二日,牛棚之戰的紀念日,一次在仲夏日,造反的紀念日。

chapters.title: Chapter V 第五章:風車之爭

passages.original: As winter drew on, Mollie became more and more troublesome.
passages.vernacular: 隨住冬天臨近,茉莉越嚟越麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨著冬天臨近,茉莉越來越麻煩。

passages.original: She was late for work every morning and excused herself by saying that she had overslept, and she complained of mysterious pains, although her appetite was excellent.
passages.vernacular: 佢每天早晨上工遲到,以瞓過頭為藉口,抱怨莫名嘅疼痛,儘管佢嘅胃口好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她每天早晨上工遲到,以睡過頭為藉口,抱怨莫名的疼痛,儘管她的胃口很好。

passages.original: On every kind of pretext she would run away from work and go to the drinking pool, where she would stand foolishly gazing at her own reflection in the water.
passages.vernacular: 佢用各種藉口逃避工作,跑到飲水池邊,喺嗰度愚蠢地站住凝視自己喺水中嘅倒影。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她用各種藉口逃避工作,跑到飲水池邊,在那裡愚蠢地站著凝視自己在水中的倒影。

passages.original: But there were also rumours of something more serious.
passages.vernacular: 但都有更嚴重嘅傳聞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但也有更嚴重的傳聞。

passages.original: One day, as Mollie strolled blithely into the yard, flirting her long tail and chewing at a stalk of hay, Clover took her aside.
passages.vernacular: 一天,茉莉歡快地踱進院子,甩住長尾巴,嚼住一根乾草,三葉草把佢拉到一邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天,茉莉歡快地踱進院子,甩著長尾巴,嚼著一根乾草,三葉草把她拉到一邊。

passages.original: “Mollie,” she said, “I have something very serious to say to you.
passages.vernacular: 「茉莉,」佢講,「我有好嚴肅嘅話要對你講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「茉莉,」她說,「我有非常嚴肅的話要對你說。

passages.original: This morning I saw you looking over the hedge that divides Animal Farm from Foxwood.
passages.vernacular: 今日早晨我睇到你喺望住隔開動物農莊同狐林嘅樹籬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天早晨我看到你在望著隔開動物農莊和狐林的樹籬。

passages.original: One of Mr. Pilkington’s men was standing on the other side of the hedge.
passages.vernacular: 皮爾金頓先生嘅一個人站喺樹籬嘅另一邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 皮爾金頓先生的一個人站在樹籬的另一邊。

passages.original: And--I was a long way away, but I am almost certain I saw this--he was talking to you and you were allowing him to stroke your nose.
passages.vernacular: 而且——我離得好遠,但我幾乎肯定我睇到咗呢個——佢喺同你講話,而你允許佢撫摸你嘅鼻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且——我離得很遠,但我幾乎肯定我看到了這個——他在同你說話,而你允許他撫摸你的鼻子。

passages.original: What does that mean, Mollie?”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係乜嘢意思,茉莉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是什麼意思,茉莉?」

passages.original: “He didn’t!
passages.vernacular: 「佢冇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他沒有!

passages.original: I wasn’t!
passages.vernacular: 我冇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有!

passages.original: It isn’t true!” cried Mollie, beginning to prance about and paw the ground.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係真嘅!」茉莉喊道,開始蹦跳、用蹄子刨地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是真的!」茉莉喊道,開始蹦跳、用蹄子刨地。

passages.original: “Mollie!
passages.vernacular: 「茉莉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「茉莉!

passages.original: Look me in the face.
passages.vernacular: 睇住我嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看著我的臉。

passages.original: Do you give me your word of honour that that man was not stroking your nose?”
passages.vernacular: 你能以名譽向我保證嗰個人冇撫摸你嘅鼻子嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能以名譽向我保證那個人沒有撫摸你的鼻子嗎?」

passages.original: “It isn’t true!” repeated Mollie, but she could not look Clover in the face, and the next moment she took to her heels and galloped away into the field.
passages.vernacular: 「呢唔係真嘅!」茉莉重複講,但佢唔敢睇三葉草嘅臉,下一刻佢拔腿飛奔,跑進咗田野。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這不是真的!」茉莉重複說,但她不敢看三葉草的臉,下一刻她拔腿飛奔,跑進了田野。

passages.original: A thought struck Clover.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草心裡有咗一個念頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草心裡有了一個念頭。

passages.original: Without saying anything to the others, she went to Mollie’s stall and turned over the straw with her hoof.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇對其他動物講乜嘢,走到茉莉嘅馬廄,用蹄子翻開稻草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她沒對其他動物說什麼,走到茉莉的馬廄,用蹄子翻開稻草。

passages.original: Hidden under the straw was a little pile of lump sugar and several bunches of ribbon of different colours.
passages.vernacular: 稻草下藏住一小堆方糖同幾捆不同顏色嘅絲帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草下藏著一小堆方糖和幾捆不同顏色的絲帶。

passages.original: Three days later Mollie disappeared.
passages.vernacular: 三天後,茉莉失蹤喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三天後,茉莉失蹤了。

passages.original: For some weeks nothing was known of her whereabouts, then the pigeons reported that they had seen her on the other side of Willingdon.
passages.vernacular: 幾個星期唔知道佢嘅下落,後來鴿子報告講,佢哋喺威靈頓另一邊睇到過佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾個星期不知道她的下落,後來鴿子報告說,它們在威靈頓另一邊看到過她。

passages.original: She was between the shafts of a smart dogcart painted red and black, which was standing outside a public-house.
passages.vernacular: 佢套喺一輛漆成紅黑色嘅漂亮雙輪輕馬車嘅車轅之間,嗰輛車停喺一家酒館外面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她套在一輛漆成紅黑色的漂亮雙輪輕馬車的車轅之間,那輛車停在一家酒館外面。

passages.original: A fat red-faced man in check breeches and gaiters, who looked like a publican, was stroking her nose and feeding her with sugar.
passages.vernacular: 一個肥胖嘅紅臉男人,穿住格子馬褲同綁腿,睇起嚟像酒館老闆,正在撫摸佢嘅鼻子,餵佢食糖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個肥胖的紅臉男人,穿著格子馬褲和綁腿,看起來像酒館老闆,正在撫摸她的鼻子,餵她吃糖。

passages.original: Her coat was newly clipped and she wore a scarlet ribbon round her forelock.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅毛新近剪過,額前嘅鬃毛上繫住一條猩紅色嘅絲帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的毛新近剪過,額前的鬃毛上繫著一條猩紅色的絲帶。

passages.original: She appeared to be enjoying herself, so the pigeons said.
passages.vernacular: 鴿子講,佢似乎玩得好開心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鴿子說,她似乎玩得很開心。

passages.original: None of the animals ever mentioned Mollie again.
passages.vernacular: 冇一個動物再提起茉莉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有一個動物再提起茉莉。

passages.original: In January there came bitterly hard weather.
passages.vernacular: 一月,天氣變得極度嚴寒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一月,天氣變得極度嚴寒。

passages.original: The earth was like iron, and nothing could be done in the fields.
passages.vernacular: 大地像鐵一樣硬,田裡乜嘢都做不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大地像鐵一樣硬,田裡什麼也做不了。

passages.original: Many meetings were held in the big barn, and the pigs occupied themselves with planning out the work of the coming season.
passages.vernacular: 喺大穀倉裡開咗許多次會,豬哋忙於計畫即將到來嘅季節嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在大穀倉裡開了許多次會,豬們忙於計畫即將到來的季節的工作。

passages.original: It had come to be accepted that the pigs, who were manifestly cleverer than the other animals, should decide all questions of farm policy, though their decisions had to be ratified by a majority vote.
passages.vernacular: 大家已經接受,明顯比其他動物聰明嘅豬,應該決定農場政策嘅所有問題,雖然佢哋嘅決定必須經過多數票嘅批准。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家已經接受,明顯比其他動物聰明的豬,應該決定農場政策的所有問題,雖然它們的決定必須經過多數票的批准。

passages.original: This arrangement would have worked well enough if it had not been for the disputes between Snowball and Napoleon.
passages.vernacular: 如果唔係雪球同拿破崙之間嘅爭論,呢個安排本來可以運作得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果不是雪球和拿破崙之間的爭論,這個安排本來可以運作得很好。

passages.original: These two disagreed at every point where disagreement was possible.
passages.vernacular: 呢兩位喺每一個可能有分歧嘅點上都有分歧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這兩位在每一個可能有分歧的點上都有分歧。

passages.original: If one of them suggested sowing a bigger acreage with barley, the other was certain to demand a bigger acreage of oats, and if one of them said that such and such a field was just right for cabbages, the other would declare that it was useless for anything except roots.
passages.vernacular: 如果其中一個建議用更大面積播種大麥,另一個必定要求更大面積嘅燕麥,如果其中一個講某某田正適合種捲心菜,另一個就會宣布佢除咗根莖類,乜嘢都冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果其中一個建議用更大面積播種大麥,另一個必定要求更大面積的燕麥,如果其中一個說某某田正適合種捲心菜,另一個就會宣布它除了根莖類,什麼都沒用。

passages.original: Each had his own following, and there were some violent debates.
passages.vernacular: 各自都有自己嘅追隨者,發生咗啲激烈嘅辯論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 各自都有自己的追隨者,發生了一些激烈的辯論。

passages.original: At the Meetings Snowball often won over the majority by his brilliant speeches, but Napoleon was better at canvassing support for himself in between times.
passages.vernacular: 喺大會上,雪球常常以佢精彩嘅演講爭取到多數,但拿破崙更善於喺兩次會議之間為自己拉票。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在大會上,雪球常常以他精彩的演講爭取到多數,但拿破崙更善於在兩次會議之間為自己拉票。

passages.original: He was especially successful with the sheep.
passages.vernacular: 佢對羊尤其成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對羊尤其成功。

passages.original: Of late the sheep had taken to bleating “Four legs good, two legs bad” both in and out of season, and they often interrupted the Meeting with this.
passages.vernacular: 最近羊養成咗不管係咪合時宜都咩咩叫「四條腿好,兩條腿壞」嘅習慣,佢哋常常用呢個打斷大會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最近羊養成了不管是否合時宜都咩咩叫「四條腿好,兩條腿壞」的習慣,它們常常用這個打斷大會。

passages.original: It was noticed that they were especially liable to break into “Four legs good, two legs bad” at crucial moments in Snowball’s speeches.
passages.vernacular: 大家注意到,佢哋尤其容易喺雪球演講嘅關鍵時刻突然爆發「四條腿好,兩條腿壞」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家注意到,它們尤其容易在雪球演講的關鍵時刻突然爆發「四條腿好,兩條腿壞」。

passages.original: Snowball had made a close study of some back numbers of the ‘Farmer and Stockbreeder’ which he had found in the farmhouse, and was full of plans for innovations and improvements.
passages.vernacular: 雪球仔細研究咗佢喺農舍找到嘅幾期《農夫同牲畜飼養者》舊刊,滿腦子都係創新同改進嘅計畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球仔細研究了他在農舍找到的幾期《農夫與牲畜飼養者》舊刊,滿腦子都是創新和改進的計畫。

passages.original: He talked learnedly about field drains, silage, and basic slag, and had worked out a complicated scheme for all the animals to drop their dung directly in the fields, at a different spot every day, to save the labour of cartage.
passages.vernacular: 佢博學地談論田間排水渠、青貯飼料同鹼性爐渣,並制定咗一個複雜嘅方案,讓所有動物把糞便直接排喺田裡,每天喺不同嘅地點,以節省運送嘅勞力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他博學地談論田間排水渠、青貯飼料和鹼性爐渣,並制定了一個複雜的方案,讓所有動物把糞便直接排在田裡,每天在不同的地點,以節省運送的勞力。

passages.original: Napoleon produced no schemes of his own, but said quietly that Snowball’s would come to nothing, and seemed to be biding his time.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙冇提出自己嘅方案,而係平靜地講雪球嘅方案唔會有結果,似乎喺等待時機。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙沒有提出自己的方案,而是平靜地說雪球的方案不會有結果,似乎在等待時機。

passages.original: But of all their controversies, none was so bitter as the one that took place over the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 但喺佢哋所有嘅爭論中,冇一個像關於風車嘅嗰樣激烈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在他們所有的爭論中,沒有一個像關於風車的那樣激烈。

passages.original: In the long pasture, not far from the farm buildings, there was a small knoll which was the highest point on the farm.
passages.vernacular: 喺長牧場上,離農場建築不遠,有一個小丘,係農場嘅最高點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在長牧場上,離農場建築不遠,有一個小丘,是農場的最高點。

passages.original: After surveying the ground, Snowball declared that this was just the place for a windmill, which could be made to operate a dynamo and supply the farm with electrical power.
passages.vernacular: 勘察咗地面後,雪球宣布呢正是建風車嘅地方,風車可以驅動一台發電機,為農場提供電力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勘察了地面後,雪球宣布這正是建風車的地方,風車可以驅動一台發電機,為農場提供電力。

passages.original: This would light the stalls and warm them in winter, and would also run a circular saw, a chaff-cutter, a mangel-slicer, and an electric milking machine.
passages.vernacular: 呢將為馬廄照明,冬天為佢哋取暖,仲能驅動一台圓鋸、一台切草機、一台甜菜切片機同一台電動擠奶機。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這將為馬廄照明,冬天為它們取暖,還能驅動一台圓鋸、一台切草機、一台甜菜切片機和一台電動擠奶機。

passages.original: The animals had never heard of anything of this kind before (for the farm was an old-fashioned one and had only the most primitive machinery), and they listened in astonishment while Snowball conjured up pictures of fantastic machines which would do their work for them while they grazed at their ease in the fields or improved their minds with reading and conversation.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋以前從冇聽講過呢類嘢(因為農場係老式嘅,只有最原始嘅機器),佢哋驚訝地聽住雪球描繪各種奇妙機器嘅畫面,呢啲機器會為佢哋幹活,而佢哋悠閒地喺田野裡食草,或通過閱讀同交談嚟增長心智。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們以前從沒聽說過這類東西(因為農場是老式的,只有最原始的機器),它們驚訝地聽著雪球描繪各種奇妙機器的畫面,這些機器會為它們幹活,而它們悠閒地在田野裡吃草,或通過閱讀和交談來增長心智。

passages.original: Within a few weeks Snowball’s plans for the windmill were fully worked out.
passages.vernacular: 幾個星期內,雪球嘅風車計畫就完全制定出嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾個星期內,雪球的風車計畫就完全制定出來了。

passages.original: The mechanical details came mostly from three books which had belonged to Mr. Jones--‘One Thousand Useful Things to Do About the House’, ‘Every Man His Own Bricklayer’, and ‘Electricity for Beginners’.
passages.vernacular: 機械細節大多來自三本屬於瓊斯先生嘅書——《家居一千件實用事》、《人人自己砌磚》同《電學入門》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 機械細節大多來自三本屬於瓊斯先生的書——《家居一千件實用事》、《人人自己砌磚》和《電學入門》。

passages.original: Snowball used as his study a shed which had once been used for incubators and had a smooth wooden floor, suitable for drawing on.
passages.vernacular: 雪球把一間曾用於孵蛋器、有光滑木地板、適合喺上面畫圖嘅棚子當作佢嘅書房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球把一間曾用於孵蛋器、有光滑木地板、適合在上面畫圖的棚子當作他的書房。

passages.original: He was closeted there for hours at a time.
passages.vernacular: 佢一次就喺嗰度關上幾小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一次就在那裡關上幾小時。

passages.original: With his books held open by a stone, and with a piece of chalk gripped between the knuckles of his trotter, he would move rapidly to and fro, drawing in line after line and uttering little whimpers of excitement.
passages.vernacular: 佢用一塊石頭把書壓開,用蹄子嘅兩個關節夾住一塊粉筆,迅速嚟回移動,一條線接一條線地畫,同時發出興奮嘅小嗚咽聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他用一塊石頭把書壓開,用蹄子的兩個關節夾著一塊粉筆,迅速來回移動,一條線接一條線地畫,同時發出興奮的小嗚咽聲。

passages.original: Gradually the plans grew into a complicated mass of cranks and cog-wheels, covering more than half the floor, which the other animals found completely unintelligible but very impressive.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地,計畫發展成一大團複雜嘅曲柄同齒輪,蓋滿咗一半以上嘅地板,其他動物覺得完全無法理解,卻留下深刻嘅印象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地,計畫發展成一大團複雜的曲柄和齒輪,蓋滿了一半以上的地板,其他動物覺得完全無法理解,卻留下深刻的印象。

passages.original: All of them came to look at Snowball’s drawings at least once a day.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋所有嘅都每天至少嚟睇一次雪球嘅圖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們所有的都每天至少來看一次雪球的圖。

passages.original: Even the hens and ducks came, and were at pains not to tread on the chalk marks.
passages.vernacular: 連母雞同鴨子都嚟喇,小心不去踩粉筆嘅痕跡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連母雞和鴨子也來了,小心不去踩粉筆的痕跡。

passages.original: Only Napoleon held aloof.
passages.vernacular: 只有拿破崙保持疏遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有拿破崙保持疏遠。

passages.original: He had declared himself against the windmill from the start.
passages.vernacular: 佢從一開始就聲明反對風車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他從一開始就聲明反對風車。

passages.original: One day, however, he arrived unexpectedly to examine the plans.
passages.vernacular: 然而,有一天,佢出乎意料地嚟檢查計畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,有一天,他出乎意料地來檢查計畫。

passages.original: He walked heavily round the shed, looked closely at every detail of the plans and snuffed at them once or twice, then stood for a little while contemplating them out of the corner of his eye; then suddenly he lifted his leg, urinated over the plans, and walked out without uttering a word.
passages.vernacular: 佢沉重地繞住棚子走咗一圈,仔細察睇計畫嘅每個細節,聞咗一兩下,然後站咗一會兒,斜住眼睛端詳,然後突然抬起一條腿,喺計畫上撒尿,一言不發地走咗出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沉重地繞著棚子走了一圈,仔細察看計畫的每個細節,聞了一兩下,然後站了一會兒,斜著眼睛端詳,然後突然抬起一條腿,在計畫上撒尿,一言不發地走了出去。

passages.original: The whole farm was deeply divided on the subject of the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 整個農場喺風車嘅問題上深深分裂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個農場在風車的問題上深深分裂。

passages.original: Snowball did not deny that to build it would be a difficult business.
passages.vernacular: 雪球並不否認建造佢會係件困難嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球並不否認建造它會是件困難的事。

passages.original: Stone would have to be carried and built up into walls, then the sails would have to be made and after that there would be need for dynamos and cables.
passages.vernacular: 必須搬運石頭,砌成牆,然後必須製造風帆,之後仲需要發電機同電纜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 必須搬運石頭,砌成牆,然後必須製造風帆,之後還需要發電機和電纜。

passages.original: (How these were to be procured, Snowball did not say.)
passages.vernacular: (呢啲如何得到,雪球冇講。)
passages.vernacularMandarin: (這些如何得到,雪球沒有說。)

passages.original: But he maintained that it could all be done in a year.
passages.vernacular: 但佢堅持講呢一切一年之內都可以完成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他堅持說這一切一年之內都可以完成。

passages.original: And thereafter, he declared, so much labour would be saved that the animals would only need to work three days a week.
passages.vernacular: 佢宣稱,此後將節省咁多勞力,動物哋每週只需工作三天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他宣稱,此後將節省那麼多勞力,動物們每週只需工作三天。

passages.original: Napoleon, on the other hand, argued that the great need of the moment was to increase food production, and that if they wasted time on the windmill they would all starve to death.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙則爭辯講,當前嘅主要需要係增加糧食產量,如果佢哋喺風車上浪費時間,就都會餓死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙則爭辯說,當前的主要需要是增加糧食產量,如果它們在風車上浪費時間,就都會餓死。

passages.original: The animals formed themselves into two factions under the slogan, “Vote for Snowball and the three-day week” and “Vote for Napoleon and the full manger.”
passages.vernacular: 動物哋分成兩派,口號係「投雪球同三日工作週一票」同「投拿破崙同滿槽一票」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們分成兩派,口號是「投雪球和三日工作週一票」和「投拿破崙和滿槽一票」。

passages.original: Benjamin was the only animal who did not side with either faction.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明係唯一不站喺任何一派嘅動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明是唯一不站在任何一派的動物。

passages.original: He refused to believe either that food would become more plentiful or that the windmill would save work.
passages.vernacular: 佢既唔肯相信糧食會變得更豐富,都不相信風車會節省工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他既不肯相信糧食會變得更豐富,也不相信風車會節省工作。

passages.original: Windmill or no windmill, he said, life would go on as it had always gone on--that is, badly.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,有冇風車,生活都會照舊繼續——都就係講,糟糕地繼續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,有沒有風車,生活都會照舊繼續——也就是說,糟糕地繼續。

passages.original: Apart from the disputes over the windmill, there was the question of the defence of the farm.
passages.vernacular: 除咗風車嘅爭論之外,仲有農場防衛嘅問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了風車的爭論之外,還有農場防衛的問題。

passages.original: It was fully realised that though the human beings had been defeated in the Battle of the Cowshed they might make another and more determined attempt to recapture the farm and reinstate Mr. Jones.
passages.vernacular: 大家充分認識到,雖然人類喺牛棚之戰中被打敗喇,佢哋可能會再作一次更堅決嘅嘗試,奪回農場,讓瓊斯先生復位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家充分認識到,雖然人類在牛棚之戰中被打敗了,他們可能會再作一次更堅決的嘗試,奪回農場,讓瓊斯先生復位。

passages.original: They had all the more reason for doing so because the news of their defeat had spread across the countryside and made the animals on the neighbouring farms more restive than ever.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋有更多理由咁樣做,因為佢哋失敗嘅消息已傳遍鄉間,使鄰近農場嘅動物比以前更不安分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們有更多理由這樣做,因為他們失敗的消息已傳遍鄉間,使鄰近農場的動物比以前更不安分。

passages.original: As usual, Snowball and Napoleon were in disagreement.
passages.vernacular: 像往常一樣,雪球同拿破崙意見不同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像往常一樣,雪球和拿破崙意見不同。

passages.original: According to Napoleon, what the animals must do was to procure firearms and train themselves in the use of them.
passages.vernacular: 按照拿破崙嘅講法,動物哋必須做嘅係取得槍械並訓練自己使用佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 按照拿破崙的說法,動物們必須做的是取得槍械並訓練自己使用它們。

passages.original: According to Snowball, they must send out more and more pigeons and stir up rebellion among the animals on the other farms.
passages.vernacular: 按照雪球嘅講法,佢哋必須派出越嚟越多嘅鴿子,喺其他農場嘅動物中煽動造反。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 按照雪球的說法,它們必須派出越來越多的鴿子,在其他農場的動物中煽動造反。

passages.original: The one argued that if they could not defend themselves they were bound to be conquered, the other argued that if rebellions happened everywhere they would have no need to defend themselves.
passages.vernacular: 一個爭辯講,如果佢哋唔能夠保衛自己,必然被征服,另一個爭辯講,如果到處都發生造反,佢哋就不需要保衛自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個爭辯說,如果它們不能保衛自己,必然被征服,另一個爭辯說,如果到處都發生造反,它們就不需要保衛自己。

passages.original: The animals listened first to Napoleon, then to Snowball, and could not make up their minds which was right; indeed, they always found themselves in agreement with the one who was speaking at the moment.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋先聽拿破崙,再聽雪球,無法決定邊個對;事實上,佢哋總是發現自己同當時講話嘅嗰個一致。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們先聽拿破崙,再聽雪球,無法決定哪個對;事實上,它們總是發現自己同當時說話的那個一致。

passages.original: At last the day came when Snowball’s plans were completed.
passages.vernacular: 終於到咗雪球嘅計畫完成嘅嗰一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於到了雪球的計畫完成的那一天。

passages.original: At the Meeting on the following Sunday the question of whether or not to begin work on the windmill was to be put to the vote.
passages.vernacular: 喺下個星期天嘅大會上,係咪開始風車工程嘅問題將付諸表決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在下個星期天的大會上,是否開始風車工程的問題將付諸表決。

passages.original: When the animals had assembled in the big barn, Snowball stood up and, though occasionally interrupted by bleating from the sheep, set forth his reasons for advocating the building of the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋喺大穀倉集合後,雪球站起嚟,雖然不時被羊嘅咩咩聲打斷,闡述咗佢主張建造風車嘅理由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們在大穀倉集合後,雪球站起來,雖然不時被羊的咩咩聲打斷,闡述了他主張建造風車的理由。

passages.original: Then Napoleon stood up to reply.
passages.vernacular: 然後拿破崙站起嚟回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後拿破崙站起來回答。

passages.original: He said very quietly that the windmill was nonsense and that he advised nobody to vote for it, and promptly sat down again; he had spoken for barely thirty seconds, and seemed almost indifferent as to the effect he produced.
passages.vernacular: 佢好平靜地講風車係胡講八道,佢勸告冇人投票贊成佢,然後即刻又坐下喇;佢只講咗唔到三十秒,似乎對自己產生嘅效果幾乎漠不關心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他非常平靜地說風車是胡說八道,他勸告沒有人投票贊成它,然後立刻又坐下了;他只說了不到三十秒,似乎對自己產生的效果幾乎漠不關心。

passages.original: At this Snowball sprang to his feet, and shouting down the sheep, who had begun bleating again, broke into a passionate appeal in favour of the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 雪球聽咗跳起嚟,壓過咗又開始咩咩叫嘅羊嘅聲音,發表咗一篇贊成風車嘅熱情呼籲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球聽了跳起來,壓過了又開始咩咩叫的羊的聲音,發表了一篇贊成風車的熱情呼籲。

passages.original: Until now the animals had been about equally divided in their sympathies, but in a moment Snowball’s eloquence had carried them away.
passages.vernacular: 直到而家,動物哋嘅同情大致平分,但一轉眼雪球嘅口才就把佢哋帶走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到現在,動物們的同情大致平分,但一轉眼雪球的口才就把它們帶走了。

passages.original: In glowing sentences he painted a picture of Animal Farm as it might be when sordid labour was lifted from the animals’ backs.
passages.vernacular: 佢用熱烈嘅句子描繪咗一幅動物農莊嘅畫面,當卑賤嘅勞役從動物哋嘅背上卸下時,佢可能係乜嘢樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他用熱烈的句子描繪了一幅動物農莊的畫面,當卑賤的勞役從動物們的背上卸下時,它可能是什麼樣子。

passages.original: His imagination had now run far beyond chaff-cutters and turnip-slicers.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅想像力而家已遠遠超出咗切草機同蘿蔔切片機。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的想像力現在已遠遠超出了切草機和蘿蔔切片機。

passages.original: Electricity, he said, could operate threshing machines, ploughs, harrows, rollers, and reapers and binders, besides supplying every stall with its own electric light, hot and cold water, and an electric heater.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,電可以驅動脫粒機、犁、耙、滾壓機、收割機同捆紮機,此外仲可以為每個馬廄提供佢自己嘅電燈、冷熱水同電暖爐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,電可以驅動脫粒機、犁、耙、滾壓機、收割機和捆紮機,此外還可以為每個馬廄提供它自己的電燈、冷熱水和電暖爐。

passages.original: By the time he had finished speaking, there was no doubt as to which way the vote would go.
passages.vernacular: 等佢講完時,毫無疑問表決會往邊個方向。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等他說完時,毫無疑問表決會往哪個方向。

passages.original: But just at this moment Napoleon stood up and, casting a peculiar sidelong look at Snowball, uttered a high-pitched whimper of a kind no one had ever heard him utter before.
passages.vernacular: 但就喺呢陣,拿破崙站起嚟,向雪球投去奇特嘅斜視,發出一聲冇人聽過佢發出嘅嗰種尖細嘅嗚咽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但就在這時,拿破崙站起來,向雪球投去奇特的斜視,發出一聲沒有人聽過他發出的那種尖細的嗚咽。

passages.original: At this there was a terrible baying sound outside, and nine enormous dogs wearing brass-studded collars came bounding into the barn.
passages.vernacular: 聽到呢聲音,外面傳嚟可怕嘅吠叫聲,九條戴住銅釘項圈嘅巨大嘅狗蹦進咗穀倉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到這聲音,外面傳來可怕的吠叫聲,九條戴著銅釘項圈的巨大的狗蹦進了穀倉。

passages.original: They dashed straight for Snowball, who only sprang from his place just in time to escape their snapping jaws.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋徑直衝向雪球,雪球剛好及時從座位上跳起,逃過咗佢哋咬合嘅下顎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們徑直衝向雪球,雪球剛好及時從座位上跳起,逃過了它們咬合的下顎。

passages.original: In a moment he was out of the door and they were after him.
passages.vernacular: 轉眼間佢已出咗門,佢哋緊追喺後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轉眼間他已出了門,它們緊追在後。

passages.original: Too amazed and frightened to speak, all the animals crowded through the door to watch the chase.
passages.vernacular: 所有動物驚訝害怕得講不出話,擠過門去睇追逐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物驚訝害怕得說不出話,擠過門去看追逐。

passages.original: Snowball was racing across the long pasture that led to the road.
passages.vernacular: 雪球正飛奔穿過通往大路嘅長牧場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球正飛奔穿過通往大路的長牧場。

passages.original: He was running as only a pig can run, but the dogs were close on his heels.
passages.vernacular: 佢跑得只有豬才能跑得嗰樣,但狗緊跟喺佢嘅腳後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他跑得只有豬才能跑得那樣,但狗緊跟在他的腳後。

passages.original: Suddenly he slipped and it seemed certain that they had him.
passages.vernacular: 突然佢滑咗一跤,似乎肯定佢哋抓住佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然他滑了一跤,似乎肯定它們抓住他了。

passages.original: Then he was up again, running faster than ever, then the dogs were gaining on him again.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢又起嚟,跑得比以前更快,然後狗又追近佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他又起來,跑得比以前更快,然後狗又追近他。

passages.original: One of them all but closed his jaws on Snowball’s tail, but Snowball whisked it free just in time.
passages.vernacular: 其中一條幾乎咬住雪球嘅尾巴,但雪球及時把佢甩開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中一條幾乎咬住雪球的尾巴,但雪球及時把它甩開了。

passages.original: Then he put on an extra spurt and, with a few inches to spare, slipped through a hole in the hedge and was seen no more.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢加速衝刺,差幾英寸,從樹籬嘅一個洞鑽過去,再都冇出現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他加速衝刺,差幾英寸,從樹籬的一個洞鑽過去,再也沒有出現。

passages.original: Silent and terrified, the animals crept back into the barn.
passages.vernacular: 沉默而恐懼嘅動物哋爬回穀倉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沉默而恐懼的動物們爬回穀倉。

passages.original: In a moment the dogs came bounding back.
passages.vernacular: 轉眼間狗蹦回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轉眼間狗蹦回來了。

passages.original: At first no one had been able to imagine where these creatures came from, but the problem was soon solved: they were the puppies whom Napoleon had taken away from their mothers and reared privately.
passages.vernacular: 起初冇人能想像呢啲生物係從邊度嚟嘅,但問題好快解決喇:佢哋就係拿破崙從母親身邊帶走並私下養大嘅嗰啲小狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初沒有人能想像這些生物是從哪裡來的,但問題很快解決了:它們就是拿破崙從母親身邊帶走並私下養大的那些小狗。

passages.original: Though not yet full-grown, they were huge dogs, and as fierce-looking as wolves.
passages.vernacular: 雖然仲冇完全長大,佢哋係巨大嘅狗,睇起嚟像狼一樣凶猛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然還沒完全長大,它們是巨大的狗,看起來像狼一樣凶猛。

passages.original: They kept close to Napoleon.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋緊靠住拿破崙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們緊靠著拿破崙。

passages.original: It was noticed that they wagged their tails to him in the same way as the other dogs had been used to do to Mr. Jones.
passages.vernacular: 大家注意到,佢哋向佢搖尾巴,就像其他狗過去向瓊斯先生搖尾巴一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家注意到,它們向他搖尾巴,就像其他狗過去向瓊斯先生搖尾巴一樣。

passages.original: Napoleon, with the dogs following him, now mounted on to the raised portion of the floor where Major had previously stood to deliver his speech.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙,後面跟住嗰啲狗,而家登上地板嘅凸起部分,嗰個係少校以前站住發表演講嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙,後面跟著那些狗,現在登上地板的凸起部分,那是少校以前站著發表演講的地方。

passages.original: He announced that from now on the Sunday-morning Meetings would come to an end.
passages.vernacular: 佢宣布從而家起,星期天早晨嘅大會將結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他宣布從現在起,星期天早晨的大會將結束。

passages.original: They were unnecessary, he said, and wasted time.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,佢哋係唔使要嘅,浪費時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,它們是不必要的,浪費時間。

passages.original: In future all questions relating to the working of the farm would be settled by a special committee of pigs, presided over by himself.
passages.vernacular: 今後所有同農場運作有關嘅問題將由一個特別嘅豬委員會解決,由佢自己主持。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今後所有與農場運作有關的問題將由一個特別的豬委員會解決,由他自己主持。

passages.original: These would meet in private and afterwards communicate their decisions to the others.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋將私下開會,然後把決定通知其他動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們將私下開會,然後把決定通知其他動物。

passages.original: The animals would still assemble on Sunday mornings to salute the flag, sing ‘Beasts of England’, and receive their orders for the week; but there would be no more debates.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋仍將喺星期天早晨集合,向旗致敬,唱《英格蘭之獸》,接受一週嘅命令;但唔再有辯論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們仍將在星期天早晨集合,向旗致敬,唱《英格蘭之獸》,接受一週的命令;但不再有辯論。

passages.original: In spite of the shock that Snowball’s expulsion had given them, the animals were dismayed by this announcement.
passages.vernacular: 儘管雪球被驅逐畀佢哋嘅震驚,動物哋對呢個宣布感到沮喪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管雪球被驅逐給它們的震驚,動物們對這個宣布感到沮喪。

passages.original: Several of them would have protested if they could have found the right arguments.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋能找到正確嘅論據,有幾個會提出抗議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果它們能找到正確的論據,有幾個會提出抗議。

passages.original: Even Boxer was vaguely troubled.
passages.vernacular: 連拳擊手都隱隱不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連拳擊手也隱隱不安。

passages.original: He set his ears back, shook his forelock several times, and tried hard to marshal his thoughts; but in the end he could not think of anything to say.
passages.vernacular: 佢把耳朵向後,甩咗幾次額髮,努力整理思緒;但最後佢想不出任何話要講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把耳朵向後,甩了幾次額髮,努力整理思緒;但最後他想不出任何話要說。

passages.original: Some of the pigs themselves, however, were more articulate.
passages.vernacular: 不過,啲豬自己比較能言善道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,一些豬自己比較能言善道。

passages.original: Four young porkers in the front row uttered shrill squeals of disapproval, and all four of them sprang to their feet and began speaking at once.
passages.vernacular: 前排嘅四頭年輕肉豬發出尖銳嘅反對尖叫,四頭全都跳起嚟,同時開始講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前排的四頭年輕肉豬發出尖銳的反對尖叫,四頭全都跳起來,同時開始說話。

passages.original: But suddenly the dogs sitting round Napoleon let out deep, menacing growls, and the pigs fell silent and sat down again.
passages.vernacular: 但突然圍住拿破崙坐嘅狗發出深沉嘅威脅性低吼,豬哋沉默下嚟,又坐下喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但突然圍著拿破崙坐的狗發出深沉的威脅性低吼,豬們沉默下來,又坐下了。

passages.original: Then the sheep broke out into a tremendous bleating of “Four legs good, two legs bad!” which went on for nearly a quarter of an hour and put an end to any chance of discussion.
passages.vernacular: 然後羊爆發出巨大嘅咩咩叫「四條腿好,兩條腿壞!」持續咗近一刻鐘,結束咗任何討論嘅可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後羊爆發出巨大的咩咩叫「四條腿好,兩條腿壞!」持續了近一刻鐘,結束了任何討論的可能。

passages.original: Afterwards Squealer was sent round the farm to explain the new arrangement to the others.
passages.vernacular: 之後尖嗓子被派到農場各處向其他動物解釋新安排。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後尖嗓子被派到農場各處向其他動物解釋新安排。

passages.original: “Comrades,” he said, “I trust that every animal here appreciates the sacrifice that Comrade Napoleon has made in taking this extra labour upon himself.
passages.vernacular: 「同志哋,」佢講,「我相信呢度嘅每個動物都感激拿破崙同志為承擔呢額外嘅勞役所作嘅犧牲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志們,」他說,「我相信這裡的每個動物都感激拿破崙同志為承擔這額外的勞役所作的犧牲。

passages.original: Do not imagine, comrades, that leadership is a pleasure!
passages.vernacular: 同志哋,唔好以為領導係一種樂趣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同志們,不要以為領導是一種樂趣!

passages.original: On the contrary, it is a deep and heavy responsibility.
passages.vernacular: 恰恰相反,佢係深重嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 恰恰相反,它是深重的責任。

passages.original: No one believes more firmly than Comrade Napoleon that all animals are equal.
passages.vernacular: 冇人比拿破崙同志更堅定地相信所有動物一律平等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人比拿破崙同志更堅定地相信所有動物一律平等。

passages.original: He would be only too happy to let you make your decisions for yourselves.
passages.vernacular: 佢好樂意讓你哋自己做決定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他非常樂意讓你們自己做決定。

passages.original: But sometimes you might make the wrong decisions, comrades, and then where should we be?
passages.vernacular: 但有時你哋可能做錯決定,同志哋,嗰我哋會點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但有時你們可能做錯決定,同志們,那我們會怎樣?

passages.original: Suppose you had decided to follow Snowball, with his moonshine of windmills--Snowball, who, as we now know, was no better than a criminal?”
passages.vernacular: 假設你哋決定追隨雪球,同佢嘅風車胡講——雪球,我哋而家知道,不比罪犯好?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假設你們決定追隨雪球,和他的風車胡說——雪球,我們現在知道,不比罪犯好?」

passages.original: “He fought bravely at the Battle of the Cowshed,” said somebody.
passages.vernacular: 「佢喺牛棚之戰中英勇作戰,」有人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他在牛棚之戰中英勇作戰,」有人說。

passages.original: “Bravery is not enough,” said Squealer.
passages.vernacular: 「英勇係唔夠嘅,」尖嗓子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「英勇是不夠的,」尖嗓子說。

passages.original: “Loyalty and obedience are more important.
passages.vernacular: 「忠誠同服從更重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「忠誠和服從更重要。

passages.original: And as to the Battle of the Cowshed, I believe the time will come when we shall find that Snowball’s part in it was much exaggerated.
passages.vernacular: 至於牛棚之戰,我相信總有一天我哋會發現雪球喺其中嘅作用被大大誇大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於牛棚之戰,我相信總有一天我們會發現雪球在其中的作用被大大誇大了。

passages.original: Discipline, comrades, iron discipline!
passages.vernacular: 紀律,同志哋,鐵嘅紀律!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紀律,同志們,鐵的紀律!

passages.original: That is the watchword for today.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係今日嘅口號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是今天的口號。

passages.original: One false step, and our enemies would be upon us.
passages.vernacular: 走錯一步,我哋嘅敵人就會撲到我哋身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走錯一步,我們的敵人就會撲到我們身上。

passages.original: Surely, comrades, you do not want Jones back?”
passages.vernacular: 同志哋,肯定你哋唔想瓊斯回嚟吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同志們,肯定你們不想瓊斯回來吧?」

passages.original: Once again this argument was unanswerable.
passages.vernacular: 呢個論點又一次無法回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個論點又一次無法回答。

passages.original: Certainly the animals did not want Jones back; if the holding of debates on Sunday mornings was liable to bring him back, then the debates must stop.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋當然唔想要瓊斯回嚟;如果星期天早晨舉行辯論可能使佢回嚟,咁辯論就必須停止。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們當然不想要瓊斯回來;如果星期天早晨舉行辯論可能使他回來,那麼辯論就必須停止。

passages.original: Boxer, who had now had time to think things over, voiced the general feeling by saying: “If Comrade Napoleon says it, it must be right.”
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手,佢而家有時間考慮,講出咗大家嘅感受,佢講:「如果拿破崙同志咁樣講,嗰一定係對嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手,他現在有時間考慮,說出了大家的感受,他說:「如果拿破崙同志這樣說,那一定是對的。」

passages.original: And from then on he adopted the maxim, “Napoleon is always right,” in addition to his private motto of “I will work harder.”
passages.vernacular: 從嗰時起,佢除咗佢個人嘅座右銘「我要更努力工作」之外,又採用咗格言「拿破崙總是對嘅」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那時起,他除了他個人的座右銘「我要更努力工作」之外,又採用了格言「拿破崙總是對的」。

passages.original: By this time the weather had broken and the spring ploughing had begun.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣天氣已經轉變,春耕開始喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時天氣已經轉變,春耕開始了。

passages.original: The shed where Snowball had drawn his plans of the windmill had been shut up and it was assumed that the plans had been rubbed off the floor.
passages.vernacular: 雪球畫風車計畫嘅嗰間棚子已被關閉,據推測計畫已從地板上擦掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球畫風車計畫的那間棚子已被關閉,據推測計畫已從地板上擦掉。

passages.original: Every Sunday morning at ten o’clock the animals assembled in the big barn to receive their orders for the week.
passages.vernacular: 每個星期天早晨十點鐘,動物哋喺大穀倉集合,接受一週嘅命令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個星期天早晨十點鐘,動物們在大穀倉集合,接受一週的命令。

passages.original: The skull of old Major, now clean of flesh, had been disinterred from the orchard and set up on a stump at the foot of the flagstaff, beside the gun.
passages.vernacular: 老少校嘅頭骨,而家已無肉,從果園裡被挖出嚟,立喺旗杆腳下嘅一個樹樁上,喺槍旁邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老少校的頭骨,現在已無肉,從果園裡被挖出來,立在旗杆腳下的一個樹樁上,在槍旁邊。

passages.original: After the hoisting of the flag, the animals were required to file past the skull in a reverent manner before entering the barn.
passages.vernacular: 升旗之後,動物哋進入穀倉之前,被要求恭敬地列隊走過頭骨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 升旗之後,動物們進入穀倉之前,被要求恭敬地列隊走過頭骨。

passages.original: Nowadays they did not sit all together as they had done in the past.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢哋不像過去嗰樣全部坐喺一起喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在它們不像過去那樣全部坐在一起了。

passages.original: Napoleon, with Squealer and another pig named Minimus, who had a remarkable gift for composing songs and poems, sat on the front of the raised platform, with the nine young dogs forming a semicircle round them, and the other pigs sitting behind.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙,連同尖嗓子同另一頭名叫米尼默斯、有非凡嘅作歌作詩天賦嘅豬,坐喺高台嘅前面,九條年輕嘅狗喺佢哋周圍形成半圓,其他豬坐喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙,連同尖嗓子和另一頭名叫米尼默斯、有非凡的作歌作詩天賦的豬,坐在高台的前面,九條年輕的狗在他們周圍形成半圓,其他豬坐在後面。

passages.original: The rest of the animals sat facing them in the main body of the barn.
passages.vernacular: 其餘嘅動物坐喺穀倉主體部分,面對住佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其餘的動物坐在穀倉主體部分,面對著他們。

passages.original: Napoleon read out the orders for the week in a gruff soldierly style, and after a single singing of ‘Beasts of England’, all the animals dispersed.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙以粗聲嘅軍人風格宣讀咗一週嘅命令,唱咗一次《英格蘭之獸》後,所有動物就散去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙以粗聲的軍人風格宣讀了一週的命令,唱了一次《英格蘭之獸》後,所有動物就散去了。

passages.original: On the third Sunday after Snowball’s expulsion, the animals were somewhat surprised to hear Napoleon announce that the windmill was to be built after all.
passages.vernacular: 雪球被驅逐後嘅第三個星期天,動物哋聽到拿破崙宣布畢竟要建風車,有些驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球被驅逐後的第三個星期天,動物們聽到拿破崙宣布畢竟要建風車,有些驚訝。

passages.original: He did not give any reason for having changed his mind, but merely warned the animals that this extra task would mean very hard work, it might even be necessary to reduce their rations.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇畀出改變主意嘅任何理由,只係警告動物哋,呢項額外嘅任務意味住好辛苦嘅工作,甚至可能需要減少佢哋嘅口糧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有給出改變主意的任何理由,只是警告動物們,這項額外的任務意味著非常辛苦的工作,甚至可能需要減少它們的口糧。

passages.original: The plans, however, had all been prepared, down to the last detail.
passages.vernacular: 不過,計畫都已準備好,連最後一個細節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,計畫都已準備好,連最後一個細節。

passages.original: A special committee of pigs had been at work upon them for the past three weeks.
passages.vernacular: 一個特別嘅豬委員會喺過去三個星期一直喺製作佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個特別的豬委員會在過去三個星期一直在製作它們。

passages.original: The building of the windmill, with various other improvements, was expected to take two years.
passages.vernacular: 風車嘅建造,連同其他各種改進,預計需要兩年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風車的建造,連同其他各種改進,預計需要兩年。

passages.original: That evening Squealer explained privately to the other animals that Napoleon had never in reality been opposed to the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,尖嗓子私下向其他動物解釋講,拿破崙實際上從未反對過風車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,尖嗓子私下向其他動物解釋說,拿破崙實際上從未反對過風車。

passages.original: On the contrary, it was he who had advocated it in the beginning, and the plan which Snowball had drawn on the floor of the incubator shed had actually been stolen from among Napoleon’s papers.
passages.vernacular: 恰恰相反,係佢喺開始時主張佢嘅,雪球喺孵蛋器棚地板上畫嘅計畫實際上係從拿破崙嘅文件中偷嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 恰恰相反,是他在開始時主張它的,雪球在孵蛋器棚地板上畫的計畫實際上是從拿破崙的文件中偷來的。

passages.original: The windmill was, in fact, Napoleon’s own creation.
passages.vernacular: 風車實際上係拿破崙自己嘅創造。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風車實際上是拿破崙自己的創造。

passages.original: Why, then, asked somebody, had he spoken so strongly against it?
passages.vernacular: 咁,有人問,佢點解咁樣強烈地反對佢呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,有人問,他為什麼這樣強烈地反對它呢?

passages.original: Here Squealer looked very sly.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣尖嗓子顯得好狡猾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時尖嗓子顯得非常狡猾。

passages.original: That, he said, was Comrade Napoleon’s cunning.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,嗰個係拿破崙同志嘅狡計。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,那是拿破崙同志的狡計。

passages.original: He had SEEMED to oppose the windmill, simply as a manoeuvre to get rid of Snowball, who was a dangerous character and a bad influence.
passages.vernacular: 佢表面上反對風車,純粹係一種策略,為了擺脫雪球,嗰個係個危險人物同壞影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他表面上反對風車,純粹是一種策略,為了擺脫雪球,那是個危險人物和壞影響。

passages.original: Now that Snowball was out of the way, the plan could go forward without his interference.
passages.vernacular: 而家雪球已經不喺,計畫可以不受佢嘅干擾而向前推進。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在雪球已經不在,計畫可以不受他的干擾而向前推進。

passages.original: This, said Squealer, was something called tactics.
passages.vernacular: 尖嗓子講,呢叫做戰術。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尖嗓子說,這叫做戰術。

passages.original: He repeated a number of times, “Tactics, comrades, tactics!” skipping round and whisking his tail with a merry laugh.
passages.vernacular: 佢重複咗好幾遍「戰術,同志哋,戰術!」邊笑邊蹦跳,甩住尾巴,好開心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他重複了好幾遍「戰術,同志們,戰術!」邊笑邊蹦跳,甩著尾巴,非常開心。

passages.original: The animals were not certain what the word meant, but Squealer spoke so persuasively, and the three dogs who happened to be with him growled so threateningly, that they accepted his explanation without further questions.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋不確定呢個詞係乜嘢意思,但尖嗓子講得咁有講服力,碰巧同佢喺一起嘅三條狗咁威脅地低吼,佢哋冇進一步嘅問題就接受咗佢嘅解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們不確定這個詞是什麼意思,但尖嗓子說得那麼有說服力,碰巧和他在一起的三條狗那麼威脅地低吼,它們沒有進一步的問題就接受了他的解釋。

chapters.title: Chapter VI 第六章:與人類往來

passages.original: All that year the animals worked like slaves.
passages.vernacular: 嗰一整年,動物哋像奴隸一樣工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那一整年,動物們像奴隸一樣工作。

passages.original: But they were happy in their work; they grudged no effort or sacrifice, well aware that everything that they did was for the benefit of themselves and those of their kind who would come after them, and not for a pack of idle, thieving human beings.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋喺工作中係快樂嘅;佢哋不吝惜任何努力或犧牲,清楚地知道佢哋所做嘅一切,都係為了佢哋自己同佢哋以後嘅同類嘅利益,而唔係為了一群懶惰、偷竊嘅人類。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它們在工作中是快樂的;它們不吝惜任何努力或犧牲,清楚地知道它們所做的一切,都是為了它們自己和它們以後的同類的利益,而不是為了一群懶惰、偷竊的人類。

passages.original: Throughout the spring and summer they worked a sixty-hour week, and in August Napoleon announced that there would be work on Sunday afternoons as well.
passages.vernacular: 整個春季同夏季,佢哋每週工作六十小時,八月,拿破崙宣布星期天下午都要工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個春季和夏季,它們每週工作六十小時,八月,拿破崙宣布星期天下午也要工作。

passages.original: This work was strictly voluntary, but any animal who absented himself from it would have his rations reduced by half.
passages.vernacular: 呢項工作係嚴格自願嘅,但任何缺席嘅動物,口糧將減半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這項工作是嚴格自願的,但任何缺席的動物,口糧將減半。

passages.original: Even so, it was found necessary to leave certain tasks undone.
passages.vernacular: 即使咁樣,仍發現有必要把某些任務留住不做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使這樣,仍發現有必要把某些任務留著不做。

passages.original: The harvest was a little less successful than in the previous year, and two fields which should have been sown with roots in the early summer were not sown because the ploughing had not been completed early enough.
passages.vernacular: 收成比前一年稍微差啲,兩塊本該喺初夏種上根莖類作物嘅田,由於耕作冇及早完成而冇播種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收成比前一年稍微差一點,兩塊本該在初夏種上根莖類作物的田,由於耕作沒有及早完成而沒有播種。

passages.original: It was possible to foresee that the coming winter would be a hard one.
passages.vernacular: 可以預見即將到來嘅冬天會好艱難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可以預見即將到來的冬天會很艱難。

passages.original: The windmill presented unexpected difficulties.
passages.vernacular: 風車遇到咗意想唔到嘅困難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風車遇到了意想不到的困難。

passages.original: There was a good quarry of limestone on the farm, and plenty of sand and cement had been found in one of the outhouses, so that all the materials for building were at hand.
passages.vernacular: 農場上有一個好嘅石灰岩採石場,喺一間外屋裡發現咗大量沙同水泥,所以所有建築材料都喺手邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場上有一個好的石灰岩採石場,在一間外屋裡發現了大量沙和水泥,所以所有建築材料都在手邊。

passages.original: But the problem the animals could not at first solve was how to break up the stone into pieces of suitable size.
passages.vernacular: 但動物哋起初無法解決嘅問題,係點樣把石頭打碎成適當大小嘅塊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但動物們起初無法解決的問題,是怎樣把石頭打碎成適當大小的塊。

passages.original: There seemed no way of doing this except with picks and crowbars, which no animal could use, because no animal could stand on his hind legs.
passages.vernacular: 似乎除咗用鎬同撬棍外冇辦法,而冇動物能用佢哋,因為冇動物能用後腿站立。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 似乎除了用鎬和撬棍外沒有辦法,而沒有動物能用它們,因為沒有動物能用後腿站立。

passages.original: Only after weeks of vain effort did the right idea occur to somebody-namely, to utilise the force of gravity.
passages.vernacular: 只經過幾個星期嘅徒勞努力之後,正確嘅主意才出而家某個動物腦中——即利用重力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只經過幾個星期的徒勞努力之後,正確的主意才出現在某個動物腦中——即利用重力。

passages.original: Huge boulders, far too big to be used as they were, were lying all over the bed of the quarry.
passages.vernacular: 巨大嘅圓石,遠比原樣可用嘅大得多,散落喺採石場嘅各處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巨大的圓石,遠比原樣可用的大得多,散落在採石場的各處。

passages.original: The animals lashed ropes round these, and then all together, cows, horses, sheep, any animal that could lay hold of the rope--even the pigs sometimes joined in at critical moments--they dragged them with desperate slowness up the slope to the top of the quarry, where they were toppled over the edge, to shatter to pieces below.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋把繩子綁喺呢啲石頭周圍,然後全體一起,牛、馬、羊,任何能抓住繩子嘅動物——連豬有時喺關鍵時刻都加入——以絕望嘅緩慢速度把佢哋拖上斜坡到採石場頂,喺嗰度把佢哋推翻過邊緣,喺下面摔成碎片。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們把繩子綁在這些石頭周圍,然後全體一起,牛、馬、羊,任何能抓住繩子的動物——連豬有時在關鍵時刻也加入——以絕望的緩慢速度把它們拖上斜坡到採石場頂,在那裡把它們推翻過邊緣,在下面摔成碎片。

passages.original: Transporting the stone when it was once broken was comparatively simple.
passages.vernacular: 石頭一旦打碎,搬運相對簡單。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 石頭一旦打碎,搬運相對簡單。

passages.original: The horses carried it off in cart-loads, the sheep dragged single blocks, even Muriel and Benjamin yoked themselves into an old governess-cart and did their share.
passages.vernacular: 馬一車一車地運走,羊拖單個石塊,連繆麗兒同班傑明都把自己套進一輛舊嘅家庭教師馬車,盡咗佢哋嘅一份力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬一車一車地運走,羊拖單個石塊,連繆麗兒和班傑明也把自己套進一輛舊的家庭教師馬車,盡了他們的一份力。

passages.original: By late summer a sufficient store of stone had accumulated, and then the building began, under the superintendence of the pigs.
passages.vernacular: 到夏末,積累咗足夠嘅石頭儲備,然後喺豬嘅監督下開始建造。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到夏末,積累了足夠的石頭儲備,然後在豬的監督下開始建造。

passages.original: But it was a slow, laborious process.
passages.vernacular: 但呢個係一個緩慢而辛苦嘅過程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這是一個緩慢而辛苦的過程。

passages.original: Frequently it took a whole day of exhausting effort to drag a single boulder to the top of the quarry, and sometimes when it was pushed over the edge it failed to break.
passages.vernacular: 常常要花上一整天筋疲力盡嘅努力才能把一塊圓石拖到採石場頂,有時把佢推下邊緣時佢仲冇裂開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 常常要花上一整天筋疲力盡的努力才能把一塊圓石拖到採石場頂,有時把它推下邊緣時它還沒有裂開。

passages.original: Nothing could have been achieved without Boxer, whose strength seemed equal to that of all the rest of the animals put together.
passages.vernacular: 冇拳擊手,乜嘢都做不成,佢嘅力量似乎等於其他所有動物加喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有拳擊手,什麼也做不成,他的力量似乎等於其他所有動物加在一起。

passages.original: When the boulder began to slip and the animals cried out in despair at finding themselves dragged down the hill, it was always Boxer who strained himself against the rope and brought the boulder to a stop.
passages.vernacular: 當圓石開始滑動,動物哋絕望地喊叫發現自己被拖下山時,總是拳擊手把身體繃緊靠喺繩子上,使圓石停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當圓石開始滑動,動物們絕望地喊叫發現自己被拖下山時,總是拳擊手把身體繃緊靠在繩子上,使圓石停下。

passages.original: To see him toiling up the slope inch by inch, his breath coming fast, the tips of his hoofs clawing at the ground, and his great sides matted with sweat, filled everyone with admiration.
passages.vernacular: 睇到佢一寸一寸地艱難爬上斜坡,呼吸急促,蹄尖扒住地面,巨大嘅兩側被汗水浸透,使每個動物都充滿欽佩。
