passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到他一寸一寸地艱難爬上斜坡,呼吸急促,蹄尖扒著地面,巨大的兩側被汗水浸透,使每個動物都充滿欽佩。

passages.original: Clover warned him sometimes to be careful not to overstrain himself, but Boxer would never listen to her.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草有時警告佢要小心,唔好過度勞累,但拳擊手從不聽佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草有時警告他要小心,不要過度勞累,但拳擊手從不聽她的。

passages.original: His two slogans, “I will work harder” and “Napoleon is always right,” seemed to him a sufficient answer to all problems.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅兩句口號,「我要更努力工作」同「拿破崙總是對嘅」,喺佢睇來係對所有問題嘅充分回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的兩句口號,「我要更努力工作」和「拿破崙總是對的」,在他看來是對所有問題的充分回答。

passages.original: He had made arrangements with the cockerel to call him three-quarters of an hour earlier in the mornings instead of half an hour.
passages.vernacular: 佢安排咗嗰隻小公雞,早晨提前四分之三小時叫佢,而唔係半小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他安排了那隻小公雞,早晨提前四分之三小時叫他,而不是半小時。

passages.original: And in his spare moments, of which there were not many nowadays, he would go alone to the quarry, collect a load of broken stone, and drag it down to the site of the windmill unassisted.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢嘅空閒時刻(而家不多喇),佢會獨自去採石場,收集一車碎石,唔使幫助把佢拖下去到風車嘅工地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他的空閒時刻(現在不多了),他會獨自去採石場,收集一車碎石,不用幫助把它拖下去到風車的工地。

passages.original: The animals were not badly off throughout that summer, in spite of the hardness of their work.
passages.vernacular: 整個夏天,儘管工作辛苦,動物哋嘅境況並不壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個夏天,儘管工作辛苦,動物們的境況並不壞。

passages.original: If they had no more food than they had had in Jones’s day, at least they did not have less.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋嘅食物冇比瓊斯嗰個時代多,至少冇少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果它們的食物沒有比瓊斯那個時代多,至少沒有少。

passages.original: The advantage of only having to feed themselves, and not having to support five extravagant human beings as well, was so great that it would have taken a lot of failures to outweigh it.
passages.vernacular: 只需養活自己,而唔使同時供養五個揮霍嘅人類嘅好處係咁大,需要好多次失敗才能抵消。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只需養活自己,而不必同時供養五個揮霍的人類的好處是那麼大,需要很多次失敗才能抵消。

passages.original: And in many ways the animal method of doing things was more efficient and saved labour.
passages.vernacular: 喺許多方面,動物做事嘅方式更有效率,並節省勞力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在許多方面,動物做事的方式更有效率,並節省勞力。

passages.original: Such jobs as weeding, for instance, could be done with a thoroughness impossible to human beings.
passages.vernacular: 例如除草咁樣嘅工作,可以做得人類唔可能做到嘅徹底。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 例如除草這樣的工作,可以做得人類不可能做到的徹底。

passages.original: And again, since no animal now stole, it was unnecessary to fence off pasture from arable land, which saved a lot of labour on the upkeep of hedges and gates.
passages.vernacular: 仲有,既然而家冇動物偷嘢,就唔使把牧場同耕地用圍欄隔開,呢節省咗維護樹籬同大門嘅許多勞力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,既然現在沒有動物偷東西,就不必把牧場與耕地用圍欄隔開,這節省了維護樹籬和大門的許多勞力。

passages.original: Nevertheless, as the summer wore on, various unforeseen shortages began to make them selves felt.
passages.vernacular: 然而,隨住夏天嘅推移,各種意想唔到嘅短缺開始顯現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,隨著夏天的推移,各種意想不到的短缺開始顯現。

passages.original: There was need of paraffin oil, nails, string, dog biscuits, and iron for the horses’ shoes, none of which could be produced on the farm.
passages.vernacular: 需要煤油、釘子、繩子、狗餅乾,同馬蹄鐵用嘅鐵,呢啲都唔能夠喺農場上生產。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 需要煤油、釘子、繩子、狗餅乾,和馬蹄鐵用的鐵,這些都不能在農場上生產。

passages.original: Later there would also be need for seeds and artificial manures, besides various tools and, finally, the machinery for the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 以後仲需要種子同化學肥料,以及各種工具,最後仲有風車嘅機器。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以後還需要種子和化學肥料,以及各種工具,最後還有風車的機器。

passages.original: How these were to be procured, no one was able to imagine.
passages.vernacular: 如何得到呢啲,冇人能想像。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如何得到這些,沒有人能想像。

passages.original: One Sunday morning, when the animals assembled to receive their orders, Napoleon announced that he had decided upon a new policy.
passages.vernacular: 一個星期天早晨,動物哋集合接受命令時,拿破崙宣布佢決定咗一項新政策。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個星期天早晨,動物們集合接受命令時,拿破崙宣布他決定了一項新政策。

passages.original: From now onwards Animal Farm would engage in trade with the neighbouring farms: not, of course, for any commercial purpose, but simply in order to obtain certain materials which were urgently necessary.
passages.vernacular: 從而家起,動物農莊將同鄰近農場進行貿易:當然唔係為了任何商業目的,而僅僅係為了獲得某些急需嘅材料。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從現在起,動物農莊將與鄰近農場進行貿易:當然不是為了任何商業目的,而僅僅是為了獲得某些急需的材料。

passages.original: The needs of the windmill must override everything else, he said.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,風車嘅需要必須壓倒一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,風車的需要必須壓倒一切。

passages.original: He was therefore making arrangements to sell a stack of hay and part of the current year’s wheat crop, and later on, if more money were needed, it would have to be made up by the sale of eggs, for which there was always a market in Willingdon.
passages.vernacular: 因此佢正在安排出售一堆乾草同本年度小麥收成嘅一部分,以後如果需要更多嘅錢,就必須靠賣蛋嚟補足,威靈頓總有蛋嘅市場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此他正在安排出售一堆乾草和本年度小麥收成的一部分,以後如果需要更多的錢,就必須靠賣蛋來補足,威靈頓總有蛋的市場。

passages.original: The hens, said Napoleon, should welcome this sacrifice as their own special contribution towards the building of the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙講,母雞應該歡迎呢種犧牲,作為佢哋對建造風車嘅特別貢獻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙說,母雞應該歡迎這種犧牲,作為它們對建造風車的特別貢獻。

passages.original: Once again the animals were conscious of a vague uneasiness.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋又一次感到隱隱嘅不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們又一次感到隱隱的不安。

passages.original: Never to have any dealings with human beings, never to engage in trade, never to make use of money--had not these been among the earliest resolutions passed at that first triumphant Meeting after Jones was expelled?
passages.vernacular: 永遠不同人類打交道,永遠不從事貿易,永遠不使用金錢——呢唔係瓊斯被驅逐後嗰次最初嘅勝利大會上通過嘅最早決議之一嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 永遠不與人類打交道,永遠不從事貿易,永遠不使用金錢——這不是瓊斯被驅逐後那次最初的勝利大會上通過的最早決議之一嗎?

passages.original: All the animals remembered passing such resolutions: or at least they thought that they remembered it.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅動物都記得通過過咁樣嘅決議:或者至少佢哋認為佢哋記得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的動物都記得通過過這樣的決議:或者至少它們認為它們記得。

passages.original: The four young pigs who had protested when Napoleon abolished the Meetings raised their voices timidly, but they were promptly silenced by a tremendous growling from the dogs.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙廢除大會時提出抗議嘅嗰四頭年輕豬,膽怯地提高咗聲音,但即刻被狗嘅巨大低吼壓下去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙廢除大會時提出抗議的那四頭年輕豬,膽怯地提高了聲音,但立刻被狗的巨大低吼壓下去了。

passages.original: Then, as usual, the sheep broke into “Four legs good, two legs bad!” and the momentary awkwardness was smoothed over.
passages.vernacular: 然後,像往常一樣,羊爆發出「四條腿好,兩條腿壞!」暫時嘅尷尬被抹平喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,像往常一樣,羊爆發出「四條腿好,兩條腿壞!」暫時的尷尬被抹平了。

passages.original: Finally Napoleon raised his trotter for silence and announced that he had already made all the arrangements.
passages.vernacular: 最後拿破崙舉起蹄子要求安靜,宣布佢已作好咗所有安排。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後拿破崙舉起蹄子要求安靜,宣布他已作好了所有安排。

passages.original: There would be no need for any of the animals to come in contact with human beings, which would clearly be most undesirable.
passages.vernacular: 任何動物都不需要同人類接觸,嗰顯然係最不可取嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何動物都不需要同人類接觸,那顯然是最不可取的。

passages.original: He intended to take the whole burden upon his own shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 佢打算把全部負擔放喺自己肩上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他打算把全部負擔放在自己肩上。

passages.original: A Mr. Whymper, a solicitor living in Willingdon, had agreed to act as intermediary between Animal Farm and the outside world, and would visit the farm every Monday morning to receive his instructions.
passages.vernacular: 一位溫珀先生,住喺威靈頓嘅律師,已同意擔任動物農莊同外界之間嘅中間人,每個星期一早晨將來農場接受佢嘅指示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一位溫珀先生,住在威靈頓的律師,已同意擔任動物農莊與外界之間的中間人,每個星期一早晨將來農場接受他的指示。

passages.original: Napoleon ended his speech with his usual cry of “Long live Animal Farm!” and after the singing of ‘Beasts of England’ the animals were dismissed.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙以佢慣常嘅喊聲「動物農莊萬歲!」結束咗佢嘅演講,唱咗《英格蘭之獸》後,動物哋被遣散喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙以他慣常的喊聲「動物農莊萬歲!」結束了他的演講,唱了《英格蘭之獸》後,動物們被遣散了。

passages.original: Afterwards Squealer made a round of the farm and set the animals’ minds at rest.
passages.vernacular: 之後尖嗓子喺農場巡視咗一圈,讓動物哋放心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後尖嗓子在農場巡視了一圈,讓動物們放心。

passages.original: He assured them that the resolution against engaging in trade and using money had never been passed, or even suggested.
passages.vernacular: 佢向佢哋保證,反對從事貿易同使用金錢嘅決議從未通過,甚至從未被提出過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他向它們保證,反對從事貿易和使用金錢的決議從未通過,甚至從未被提出過。

passages.original: It was pure imagination, probably traceable in the beginning to lies circulated by Snowball.
passages.vernacular: 呢純屬想像,大概最初可以追溯到雪球散佈嘅謊言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這純屬想像,大概最初可以追溯到雪球散佈的謊言。

passages.original: A few animals still felt faintly doubtful, but Squealer asked them shrewdly, “Are you certain that this is not something that you have dreamed, comrades?
passages.vernacular: 有幾個動物仍然隱隱懷疑,但尖嗓子精明地問佢哋:「你哋確定呢唔係你哋夢到嘅嘢嗎,同志哋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有幾個動物仍然隱隱懷疑,但尖嗓子精明地問它們:「你們確定這不是你們夢到的東西嗎,同志們?

passages.original: Have you any record of such a resolution?
passages.vernacular: 你哋有嗰樣一項決議嘅任何記錄嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們有那樣一項決議的任何記錄嗎?

passages.original: Is it written down anywhere?”
passages.vernacular: 佢被寫喺邊度咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它被寫在哪裡了嗎?」

passages.original: And since it was certainly true that nothing of the kind existed in writing, the animals were satisfied that they had been mistaken.
passages.vernacular: 而既然確實冇任何類似嘅嘢以書面形式存在,動物哋就滿意地相信自己搞錯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而既然確實沒有任何類似的東西以書面形式存在,動物們就滿意地相信自己搞錯了。

passages.original: Every Monday Mr. Whymper visited the farm as had been arranged.
passages.vernacular: 每個星期一,溫珀先生按安排拜訪農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個星期一,溫珀先生按安排拜訪農場。

passages.original: He was a sly-looking little man with side whiskers, a solicitor in a very small way of business, but sharp enough to have realised earlier than anyone else that Animal Farm would need a broker and that the commissions would be worth having.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個外表狡猾嘅小個子,留住絡腮鬍,係個業務好小嘅律師,但夠精明,比任何人更早意識到動物農莊需要一個經紀人,佣金係值得攞嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個外表狡猾的小個子,留著絡腮鬍,是個業務很小的律師,但夠精明,比任何人更早意識到動物農莊需要一個經紀人,佣金是值得拿的。

passages.original: The animals watched his coming and going with a kind of dread, and avoided him as much as possible.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋帶住一種恐懼睇住佢嘅嚟去,盡可能避開佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們帶著一種恐懼看著他的來去,盡可能避開他。

passages.original: Nevertheless, the sight of Napoleon, on all fours, delivering orders to Whymper, who stood on two legs, roused their pride and partly reconciled them to the new arrangement.
passages.vernacular: 然而,睇到拿破崙四腳住地向用兩條腿站立嘅溫珀發號施令,激起咗佢哋嘅自豪,使佢哋部分地對新安排釋然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,看到拿破崙四腳著地向用兩條腿站立的溫珀發號施令,激起了它們的自豪,使它們部分地對新安排釋然。

passages.original: Their relations with the human race were now not quite the same as they had been before.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋同人類嘅關係而家同以前不完全一樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們與人類的關係現在與以前不完全一樣了。

passages.original: The human beings did not hate Animal Farm any less now that it was prospering; indeed, they hated it more than ever.
passages.vernacular: 人類並冇因為動物農莊而家繁榮而少恨佢啲;事實上,佢哋比以前更恨佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人類並沒有因為動物農莊現在繁榮而少恨它一點;事實上,他們比以前更恨它。

passages.original: Every human being held it as an article of faith that the farm would go bankrupt sooner or later, and, above all, that the windmill would be a failure.
passages.vernacular: 每個人類都把農場遲早會破產當作信條,最重要嘅係,風車會失敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個人類都把農場遲早會破產當作信條,最重要的是,風車會失敗。

passages.original: They would meet in the public-houses and prove to one another by means of diagrams that the windmill was bound to fall down, or that if it did stand up, then that it would never work.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋會喺酒館見面,借助圖表互相證明風車必然倒塌,或者即使站住,佢都永遠唔會運轉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們會在酒館見面,借助圖表互相證明風車必然倒塌,或者即使站住,它也永遠不會運轉。

passages.original: And yet, against their will, they had developed a certain respect for the efficiency with which the animals were managing their own affairs.
passages.vernacular: 然而,違背佢哋嘅意願,佢哋對動物哋管理自己事務嘅效率,已產生咗某種尊敬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,違背他們的意願,他們對動物們管理自己事務的效率,已產生了某種尊敬。

passages.original: One symptom of this was that they had begun to call Animal Farm by its proper name and ceased to pretend that it was called the Manor Farm.
passages.vernacular: 其中一個症狀係,佢哋開始稱動物農莊為佢正確嘅名字,唔再假裝佢叫曼諾農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中一個症狀是,他們開始稱動物農莊為它正確的名字,不再假裝它叫曼諾農場。

passages.original: They had also dropped their championship of Jones, who had given up hope of getting his farm back and gone to live in another part of the county.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋仲放棄咗對瓊斯嘅支持,瓊斯已放棄奪回農場嘅希望,去郡嘅另一處居住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們還放棄了對瓊斯的支持,瓊斯已放棄奪回農場的希望,去郡的另一處居住了。

passages.original: Except through Whymper, there was as yet no contact between Animal Farm and the outside world, but there were constant rumours that Napoleon was about to enter into a definite business agreement either with Mr. Pilkington of Foxwood or with Mr. Frederick of Pinchfield--but never, it was noticed, with both simultaneously.
passages.vernacular: 除咗通過溫珀之外,動物農莊同外界仲冇接觸,但不斷有傳聞講拿破崙即將同狐林嘅皮爾金頓先生或平奇菲爾德嘅弗雷德里克先生達成明確嘅商業協議——但有人注意到,從唔係同兩人同時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了通過溫珀之外,動物農莊與外界還沒有接觸,但不斷有傳聞說拿破崙即將與狐林的皮爾金頓先生或平奇菲爾德的弗雷德里克先生達成明確的商業協議——但有人注意到,從不是與兩人同時。

passages.original: It was about this time that the pigs suddenly moved into the farmhouse and took up their residence there.
passages.vernacular: 大約喺呢個時候,豬哋突然搬進農舍,喺嗰度住咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約在這個時候,豬們突然搬進農舍,在那裡住了下來。

passages.original: Again the animals seemed to remember that a resolution against this had been passed in the early days, and again Squealer was able to convince them that this was not the case.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋似乎又記得,早期通過過反對呢個嘅決議,尖嗓子又一次能夠講服佢哋情況並非如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們似乎又記得,早期通過過反對這個的決議,尖嗓子又一次能夠說服它們情況並非如此。

passages.original: It was absolutely necessary, he said, that the pigs, who were the brains of the farm, should have a quiet place to work in.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,絕對必要嘅係,作為農場大腦嘅豬,應該有一個安靜嘅工作地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,絕對必要的是,作為農場大腦的豬,應該有一個安靜的工作地方。

passages.original: It was also more suited to the dignity of the Leader (for of late he had taken to speaking of Napoleon under the title of “Leader”) to live in a house than in a mere sty.
passages.vernacular: 領袖(因為最近佢開始以「領袖」嘅頭銜稱呼拿破崙)住喺房子裡而唔係僅僅住喺豬圈裡,都更符合佢嘅尊嚴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 領袖(因為最近他開始以「領袖」的頭銜稱呼拿破崙)住在房子裡而不是僅僅住在豬圈裡,也更符合他的尊嚴。

passages.original: Nevertheless, some of the animals were disturbed when they heard that the pigs not only took their meals in the kitchen and used the drawing-room as a recreation room, but also slept in the beds.
passages.vernacular: 然而,當啲動物聽講豬不僅喺廚房食飯,把客廳當作娛樂室,而且瞓喺床上時,佢哋感到不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,當一些動物聽說豬不僅在廚房吃飯,把客廳當作娛樂室,而且睡在床上時,它們感到不安。

passages.original: Boxer passed it off as usual with “Napoleon is always right!”, but Clover, who thought she remembered a definite ruling against beds, went to the end of the barn and tried to puzzle out the Seven Commandments which were inscribed there.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手像往常一樣用「拿破崙總是對嘅!」把佢搪塞過去,但三葉草,佢認為佢記得有一條明確反對床嘅規定,走到穀倉盡頭,試圖琢磨銘刻喺嗰度嘅七誡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手像往常一樣用「拿破崙總是對的!」把它搪塞過去,但三葉草,她認為她記得有一條明確反對床的規定,走到穀倉盡頭,試圖琢磨銘刻在那裡的七誡。

passages.original: Finding herself unable to read more than individual letters, she fetched Muriel.
passages.vernacular: 發現自己只能讀單個嘅字母,佢去叫咗繆麗兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 發現自己只能讀單個的字母,她去叫了繆麗兒。

passages.original: “Muriel,” she said, “read me the Fourth Commandment.
passages.vernacular: 「繆麗兒,」佢講,「畀我讀第四條誡命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「繆麗兒,」她說,「給我讀第四條誡命。

passages.original: Does it not say something about never sleeping in a bed?”
passages.vernacular: 佢係唔係講過乜嘢關於永遠不瞓喺床上?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是不是說過什麼關於永遠不睡在床上?」

passages.original: With some difficulty Muriel spelt it out.
passages.vernacular: 繆麗兒費咗啲勁拼讀出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繆麗兒費了一些勁拼讀出來。

passages.original: “It says, ‘No animal shall sleep in a bed with sheets,”’ she announced finally.
passages.vernacular: 「佢講,『任何動物唔得瞓喺有床單嘅床上,』」佢最後宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它說,『任何動物不得睡在有床單的床上,』」她最後宣布。

passages.original: Curiously enough, Clover had not remembered that the Fourth Commandment mentioned sheets; but as it was there on the wall, it must have done so.
passages.vernacular: 奇怪嘅係,三葉草不記得第四條誡命提到過床單;但既然佢就喺牆上,嗰一定係咁樣提嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇怪的是,三葉草不記得第四條誡命提到過床單;但既然它就在牆上,那一定是這樣提的。

passages.original: And Squealer, who happened to be passing at this moment, attended by two or three dogs, was able to put the whole matter in its proper perspective.
passages.vernacular: 而碰巧呢陣經過嘅尖嗓子,有兩三條狗陪伴,能夠把整個事情放喺適當嘅角度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而碰巧這時經過的尖嗓子,有兩三條狗陪伴,能夠把整個事情放在適當的角度。

passages.original: “You have heard then, comrades,” he said, “that we pigs now sleep in the beds of the farmhouse?
passages.vernacular: 「咁,同志哋,你哋聽講喇,」佢講,「我哋豬而家瞓喺農舍嘅床上?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,同志們,你們聽說了,」他說,「我們豬現在睡在農舍的床上?

passages.original: And why not?
passages.vernacular: 點解不呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼不呢?

passages.original: You did not suppose, surely, that there was ever a ruling against beds?
passages.vernacular: 你哋肯定冇想過,曾有反對床嘅規定吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們肯定沒有想過,曾有反對床的規定吧?

passages.original: A bed merely means a place to sleep in.
passages.vernacular: 床只係瞓覺嘅地方嘅意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 床只是睡覺的地方的意思。

passages.original: A pile of straw in a stall is a bed, properly regarded.
passages.vernacular: 馬廄裡一堆稻草,嚴格地講就係一張床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬廄裡一堆稻草,嚴格地說就是一張床。

passages.original: The rule was against sheets, which are a human invention.
passages.vernacular: 規定係反對床單,嗰個係人類嘅發明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 規定是反對床單,那是人類的發明。

passages.original: We have removed the sheets from the farmhouse beds, and sleep between blankets.
passages.vernacular: 我哋已把床單從農舍嘅床上攞走,瞓喺毯子之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們已把床單從農舍的床上拿走,睡在毯子之間。

passages.original: And very comfortable beds they are too!
passages.vernacular: 而且佢哋係好舒適嘅床!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且它們是非常舒適的床!

passages.original: But not more comfortable than we need, I can tell you, comrades, with all the brainwork we have to do nowadays.
passages.vernacular: 但係,我可以告訴你哋,同志哋,考慮到我哋而家要做嘅所有腦力工作,並冇比我哋需要嘅更舒適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,我可以告訴你們,同志們,考慮到我們現在要做的所有腦力工作,並沒有比我們需要的更舒適。

passages.original: You would not rob us of our repose, would you, comrades?
passages.vernacular: 你哋唔會剝奪我哋嘅休息,對吧,同志哋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們不會剝奪我們的休息,對吧,同志們?

passages.original: You would not have us too tired to carry out our duties?
passages.vernacular: 你哋唔想讓我哋累得無法履行職責吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們不想讓我們累得無法履行職責吧?

passages.original: Surely none of you wishes to see Jones back?”
passages.vernacular: 肯定你哋冇人希望睇到瓊斯回嚟吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 肯定你們沒有人希望看到瓊斯回來吧?」

passages.original: The animals reassured him on this point immediately, and no more was said about the pigs sleeping in the farmhouse beds.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋即刻喺呢啲上讓佢放心喇,關於豬瞓喺農舍床上嘅事就唔再講乜嘢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們立刻在這一點上讓他放心了,關於豬睡在農舍床上的事就不再說什麼了。

passages.original: And when, some days afterwards, it was announced that from now on the pigs would get up an hour later in the mornings than the other animals, no complaint was made about that either.
passages.vernacular: 幾天後宣布,從而家起,豬早晨比其他動物晚起一個小時,對此都冇人抱怨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾天後宣布,從現在起,豬早晨比其他動物晚起一個小時,對此也沒有人抱怨。

passages.original: By the autumn the animals were tired but happy.
passages.vernacular: 到秋天,動物哋雖疲倦但快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到秋天,動物們雖疲倦但快樂。

passages.original: They had had a hard year, and after the sale of part of the hay and corn, the stores of food for the winter were none too plentiful, but the windmill compensated for everything.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋度過咗艱辛嘅一年,賣掉一部分乾草同玉米後,過冬嘅食物儲備並不太充足,但風車補償咗一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們度過了艱辛的一年,賣掉一部分乾草和玉米後,過冬的食物儲備並不太充足,但風車補償了一切。

passages.original: It was almost half built now.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家幾乎建成咗一半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它現在幾乎建成了一半。

passages.original: After the harvest there was a stretch of clear dry weather, and the animals toiled harder than ever, thinking it well worth while to plod to and fro all day with blocks of stone if by doing so they could raise the walls another foot.
passages.vernacular: 收割後有一段晴朗乾燥嘅天氣,動物哋比以前更賣力地工作,覺得整天嚟回費力地搬石塊,只要咁樣能把牆再升高一英尺,就好值得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收割後有一段晴朗乾燥的天氣,動物們比以前更賣力地工作,覺得整天來回費力地搬石塊,只要這樣能把牆再升高一英尺,就非常值得。

passages.original: Boxer would even come out at nights and work for an hour or two on his own by the light of the harvest moon.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手甚至會喺夜裡出嚟,借住收穫月嘅光,獨自工作一兩個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手甚至會在夜裡出來,借著收穫月的光,獨自工作一兩個小時。

passages.original: In their spare moments the animals would walk round and round the half-finished mill, admiring the strength and perpendicularity of its walls and marvelling that they should ever have been able to build anything so imposing.
passages.vernacular: 喺空閒時刻,動物哋會一圈又一圈地繞住半完工嘅磨坊走,欣賞佢嘅牆壁嘅堅固同垂直,驚歎佢哋竟能建造如此宏偉嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在空閒時刻,動物們會一圈又一圈地繞著半完工的磨坊走,欣賞它的牆壁的堅固和垂直,驚歎它們竟能建造如此宏偉的東西。

passages.original: Only old Benjamin refused to grow enthusiastic about the windmill, though, as usual, he would utter nothing beyond the cryptic remark that donkeys live a long time.
passages.vernacular: 只有老班傑明拒絕對風車熱心起嚟,雖然像往常一樣,佢只講咗驢子活得好長呢句神秘嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有老班傑明拒絕對風車熱心起來,雖然像往常一樣,他只說了驢子活得很長這句神秘的話。

passages.original: November came, with raging south-west winds.
passages.vernacular: 十一月嚟喇,颳住狂暴嘅西南風。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十一月來了,颳著狂暴的西南風。

passages.original: Building had to stop because it was now too wet to mix the cement.
passages.vernacular: 建造唔得不停止,因為而家太濕,無法攪拌水泥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 建造不得不停止,因為現在太濕,無法攪拌水泥。

passages.original: Finally there came a night when the gale was so violent that the farm buildings rocked on their foundations and several tiles were blown off the roof of the barn.
passages.vernacular: 最後有一個晚上,大風咁猛烈,農場嘅建築喺地基上搖晃,穀倉屋頂吹掉咗幾片瓦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後有一個晚上,大風那麼猛烈,農場的建築在地基上搖晃,穀倉屋頂吹掉了幾片瓦。

passages.original: The hens woke up squawking with terror because they had all dreamed simultaneously of hearing a gun go off in the distance.
passages.vernacular: 母雞醒嚟,驚恐地尖叫,因為佢哋全都同時夢見遠處槍響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 母雞醒來,驚恐地尖叫,因為它們全都同時夢見遠處槍響。

passages.original: In the morning the animals came out of their stalls to find that the flagstaff had been blown down and an elm tree at the foot of the orchard had been plucked up like a radish.
passages.vernacular: 早晨,動物哋走出馬廄,發現旗杆被吹倒喇,果園腳下嘅一棵榆樹像蘿蔔一樣被連根拔起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨,動物們走出馬廄,發現旗杆被吹倒了,果園腳下的一棵榆樹像蘿蔔一樣被連根拔起。

passages.original: They had just noticed this when a cry of despair broke from every animal’s throat.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋剛注意到呢個,每個動物嘅喉嚨裡就迸出一聲絕望嘅喊叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們剛注意到這個,每個動物的喉嚨裡就迸出一聲絕望的喊叫。

passages.original: A terrible sight had met their eyes.
passages.vernacular: 一幅可怕嘅景象映入佢哋眼簾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一幅可怕的景象映入它們眼簾。

passages.original: The windmill was in ruins.
passages.vernacular: 風車成咗廢墟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風車成了廢墟。

passages.original: With one accord they dashed down to the spot.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋一致衝向嗰個地點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們一致衝向那個地點。

passages.original: Napoleon, who seldom moved out of a walk, raced ahead of them all.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙,好少從步行加快嘅,比佢哋都跑喺前面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙,很少從步行加快的,比它們都跑在前面。

passages.original: Yes, there it lay, the fruit of all their struggles, levelled to its foundations, the stones they had broken and carried so laboriously scattered all around.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,佢就躺喺嗰度,佢哋所有奮鬥嘅成果,被夷平到地基,佢哋咁辛苦打碎同搬運嘅石頭散落四周。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,它就躺在那裡,它們所有奮鬥的成果,被夷平到地基,它們那麼辛苦打碎和搬運的石頭散落四周。

passages.original: Unable at first to speak, they stood gazing mournfully at the litter of fallen stone.
passages.vernacular: 起初講不出話嚟,佢哋站住悲傷地凝視住倒塌石頭嘅垃圾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初說不出話來,它們站著悲傷地凝視著倒塌石頭的垃圾。

passages.original: Napoleon paced to and fro in silence, occasionally snuffing at the ground.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙默默地嚟回踱步,偶爾聞聞地面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙默默地來回踱步,偶爾聞聞地面。

passages.original: His tail had grown rigid and twitched sharply from side to side, a sign in him of intense mental activity.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅尾巴已經變得僵硬,向兩邊急促地抽動,嗰個係佢強烈腦力活動嘅標誌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的尾巴已經變得僵硬,向兩邊急促地抽動,那是他強烈腦力活動的標誌。

passages.original: Suddenly he halted as though his mind were made up.
passages.vernacular: 突然佢停住喇,好像已下定決心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然他停住了,好像已下定決心。

passages.original: “Comrades,” he said quietly, “do you know who is responsible for this?
passages.vernacular: 「同志哋,」佢平靜地講,「你哋知道邊個要為此負責嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志們,」他平靜地說,「你們知道誰要為此負責嗎?

passages.original: Do you know the enemy who has come in the night and overthrown our windmill?
passages.vernacular: 你哋知道喺夜裡嚟推翻我哋風車嘅敵人係邊個嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們知道在夜裡來推翻我們風車的敵人是誰嗎?

passages.original: SNOWBALL!” he suddenly roared in a voice of thunder.
passages.vernacular: 雪球!」佢突然以雷鳴般嘅聲音吼道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球!」他突然以雷鳴般的聲音吼道。

passages.original: “Snowball has done this thing!
passages.vernacular: 「雪球幹咗呢件事!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「雪球幹了這件事!

passages.original: In sheer malignity, thinking to set back our plans and avenge himself for his ignominious expulsion, this traitor has crept here under cover of night and destroyed our work of nearly a year.
passages.vernacular: 完全出於惡意,想要推遲我哋嘅計畫,為佢可恥嘅被驅逐報仇,呢個叛徒趁夜色掩護爬到呢度,毀掉咗我哋近一年嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 完全出於惡意,想要推遲我們的計畫,為他可恥的被驅逐報仇,這個叛徒趁夜色掩護爬到這裡,毀掉了我們近一年的工作。

passages.original: Comrades, here and now I pronounce the death sentence upon Snowball.
passages.vernacular: 同志哋,我喺此時此地對雪球宣判死刑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同志們,我在此時此地對雪球宣判死刑。

passages.original: ‘Animal Hero, Second Class,’ and half a bushel of apples to any animal who brings him to justice.
passages.vernacular: 任何動物把佢繩之以法,可得『二級動物英雄』同半蒲式耳蘋果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何動物把他繩之以法,可得『二級動物英雄』和半蒲式耳蘋果。

passages.original: A full bushel to anyone who captures him alive!”
passages.vernacular: 任何活捉佢嘅,一整蒲式耳!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何活捉他的,一整蒲式耳!」

passages.original: The animals were shocked beyond measure to learn that even Snowball could be guilty of such an action.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋得知連雪球都會犯下咁樣嘅行為,震驚得無以復加。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們得知連雪球也會犯下這樣的行為,震驚得無以復加。

passages.original: There was a cry of indignation, and everyone began thinking out ways of catching Snowball if he should ever come back.
passages.vernacular: 一陣憤怒嘅叫喊,每個動物開始琢磨,如果雪球回嚟,點樣抓住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣憤怒的叫喊,每個動物開始琢磨,如果雪球回來,怎樣抓住他。

passages.original: Almost immediately the footprints of a pig were discovered in the grass at a little distance from the knoll.
passages.vernacular: 幾乎即刻,喺離小丘不遠嘅草地上發現咗一頭豬嘅足跡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾乎立刻,在離小丘不遠的草地上發現了一頭豬的足跡。

passages.original: They could only be traced for a few yards, but appeared to lead to a hole in the hedge.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋只能追蹤幾碼,但似乎通向樹籬嘅一個洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們只能追蹤幾碼,但似乎通向樹籬的一個洞。

passages.original: Napoleon snuffed deeply at them and pronounced them to be Snowball’s.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙深深地聞咗聞,宣布佢哋係雪球嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙深深地聞了聞,宣布它們是雪球的。

passages.original: He gave it as his opinion that Snowball had probably come from the direction of Foxwood Farm.
passages.vernacular: 佢發表意見講,雪球可能係從狐林農場嘅方向來嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他發表意見說,雪球可能是從狐林農場的方向來的。

passages.original: “No more delays, comrades!” cried Napoleon when the footprints had been examined.
passages.vernacular: 「唔好再耽擱喇,同志哋!」足跡被檢查後,拿破崙喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不要再耽擱了,同志們!」足跡被檢查後,拿破崙喊道。

passages.original: “There is work to be done.
passages.vernacular: 「有工作要做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有工作要做。

passages.original: This very morning we begin rebuilding the windmill, and we will build all through the winter, rain or shine.
passages.vernacular: 就喺今日早晨,我哋開始重建風車,我哋要整個冬天不停地建,風雨無阻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在今天早晨,我們開始重建風車,我們要整個冬天不停地建,風雨無阻。

passages.original: We will teach this miserable traitor that he cannot undo our work so easily.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要教呢個卑鄙嘅叛徒,佢唔能夠咁容易地毀掉我哋嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要教這個卑鄙的叛徒,他不能這麼容易地毀掉我們的工作。

passages.original: Remember, comrades, there must be no alteration in our plans: they shall be carried out to the day.
passages.vernacular: 記住,同志哋,我哋嘅計畫唔能夠有任何改變:佢哋將按日期執行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 記住,同志們,我們的計畫不能有任何改變:它們將按日期執行。

passages.original: Forward, comrades!
passages.vernacular: 前進,同志哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前進,同志們!

passages.original: Long live the windmill!
passages.vernacular: 風車萬歲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風車萬歲!

passages.original: Long live Animal Farm!”
passages.vernacular: 動物農莊萬歲!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物農莊萬歲!」

chapters.title: Chapter VII 第七章:大清洗

passages.original: It was a bitter winter.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個嚴酷嘅冬天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個嚴酷的冬天。

passages.original: The stormy weather was followed by sleet and snow, and then by a hard frost which did not break till well into February.
passages.vernacular: 暴風雨嘅天氣之後係凍雨同雪,然後係一場嚴霜,直到二月中旬才解凍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暴風雨的天氣之後是凍雨和雪,然後是一場嚴霜,直到二月中旬才解凍。

passages.original: The animals carried on as best they could with the rebuilding of the windmill, well knowing that the outside world was watching them and that the envious human beings would rejoice and triumph if the mill were not finished on time.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋盡最大嘅努力繼續重建風車,清楚地知道外界正在注視佢哋,如果磨坊唔能夠按時完工,嫉妒嘅人類會欣喜同得意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們盡最大的努力繼續重建風車,清楚地知道外界正在注視它們,如果磨坊不能按時完工,嫉妒的人類會欣喜和得意。

passages.original: Out of spite, the human beings pretended not to believe that it was Snowball who had destroyed the windmill: they said that it had fallen down because the walls were too thin.
passages.vernacular: 出於惡意,人類假裝不相信毀掉風車嘅係雪球:佢哋講佢倒塌係因為牆太薄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 出於惡意,人類假裝不相信毀掉風車的是雪球:他們說它倒塌是因為牆太薄。

passages.original: The animals knew that this was not the case.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋知道並非如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們知道並非如此。

passages.original: Still, it had been decided to build the walls three feet thick this time instead of eighteen inches as before, which meant collecting much larger quantities of stone.
passages.vernacular: 不過,呢次已決定把牆建成三英尺厚,而唔係以前嘅十八英寸,呢意味住要收集大得多嘅石頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,這次已決定把牆建成三英尺厚,而不是以前的十八英寸,這意味著要收集大得多的石頭。

passages.original: For a long time the quarry was full of snowdrifts and nothing could be done.
passages.vernacular: 好長一段時間,採石場裡積滿雪堆,乜嘢都唔能夠做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很長一段時間,採石場裡積滿雪堆,什麼也不能做。

passages.original: Some progress was made in the dry frosty weather that followed, but it was cruel work, and the animals could not feel so hopeful about it as they had felt before.
passages.vernacular: 隨後乾燥霜凍嘅天氣裡取得咗啲進展,但呢個係殘酷嘅工作,動物哋對此感到不如以前嗰樣有希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨後乾燥霜凍的天氣裡取得了一些進展,但這是殘酷的工作,動物們對此感到不如以前那樣有希望。

passages.original: They were always cold, and usually hungry as well.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋總是冷,通常都餓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們總是冷,通常也餓。

passages.original: Only Boxer and Clover never lost heart.
passages.vernacular: 只有拳擊手同三葉草從不灰心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有拳擊手和三葉草從不灰心。

passages.original: Squealer made excellent speeches on the joy of service and the dignity of labour, but the other animals found more inspiration in Boxer’s strength and his never-failing cry of “I will work harder!”
passages.vernacular: 尖嗓子發表咗關於服務嘅快樂同勞動嘅尊嚴嘅精彩演講,但其他動物喺拳擊手嘅力量同佢永不失敗嘅喊聲「我要更努力工作!」中找到咗更多靈感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尖嗓子發表了關於服務的快樂和勞動的尊嚴的精彩演講,但其他動物在拳擊手的力量和他永不失敗的喊聲「我要更努力工作!」中找到了更多靈感。

passages.original: In January food fell short.
passages.vernacular: 一月,食物唔夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一月,食物不夠了。

passages.original: The corn ration was drastically reduced, and it was announced that an extra potato ration would be issued to make up for it.
passages.vernacular: 玉米口糧大幅減少,並宣布將額外發放馬鈴薯口糧作為補償。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 玉米口糧大幅減少,並宣布將額外發放馬鈴薯口糧作為補償。

passages.original: Then it was discovered that the greater part of the potato crop had been frosted in the clamps, which had not been covered thickly enough.
passages.vernacular: 然後發現大部分馬鈴薯收成喺窖裡被凍壞喇,窖冇蓋得足夠厚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後發現大部分馬鈴薯收成在窖裡被凍壞了,窖沒有蓋得足夠厚。

passages.original: The potatoes had become soft and discoloured, and only a few were edible.
passages.vernacular: 馬鈴薯變軟變色,只有少數能食。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬鈴薯變軟變色,只有少數能吃。

passages.original: For days at a time the animals had nothing to eat but chaff and mangels.
passages.vernacular: 有連續幾天,動物哋除咗穀殼同甜菜之外冇嘢可食。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有連續幾天,動物們除了穀殼和甜菜之外沒有東西可吃。

passages.original: Starvation seemed to stare them in the face.
passages.vernacular: 飢餓似乎正盯住佢哋嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 飢餓似乎正盯著它們的臉。

passages.original: It was vitally necessary to conceal this fact from the outside world.
passages.vernacular: 必須向外界隱瞞呢個事實,呢至關重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 必須向外界隱瞞這個事實,這至關重要。

passages.original: Emboldened by the collapse of the windmill, the human beings were inventing fresh lies about Animal Farm.
passages.vernacular: 人類被風車倒塌所鼓舞,喺編造關於動物農莊嘅新謊言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人類被風車倒塌所鼓舞,在編造關於動物農莊的新謊言。

passages.original: Once again it was being put about that all the animals were dying of famine and disease, and that they were continually fighting among themselves and had resorted to cannibalism and infanticide.
passages.vernacular: 又一次散佈講所有動物都死於飢荒同疾病,講佢哋不斷互相打鬥,並訴諸食人同殺嬰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一次散佈說所有動物都死於飢荒和疾病,說它們不斷互相打鬥,並訴諸吃人和殺嬰。

passages.original: Napoleon was well aware of the bad results that might follow if the real facts of the food situation were known, and he decided to make use of Mr. Whymper to spread a contrary impression.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙好清楚如果食物狀況嘅真實情況被知道,可能產生嘅壞結果,佢決定利用溫珀先生來傳播相反嘅印象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙很清楚如果食物狀況的真實情況被知道,可能產生的壞結果,他決定利用溫珀先生來傳播相反的印象。

passages.original: Hitherto the animals had had little or no contact with Whymper on his weekly visits: now, however, a few selected animals, mostly sheep, were instructed to remark casually in his hearing that rations had been increased.
passages.vernacular: 到目前為止,動物哋喺溫珀每週嚟訪時同佢幾乎冇接觸:然而而家,幾個被挑選嘅動物,大多係羊,被指示喺佢聽得見嘅地方隨意地講口糧增加喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到目前為止,動物們在溫珀每週來訪時與他幾乎沒有接觸:然而現在,幾個被挑選的動物,大多是羊,被指示在他聽得見的地方隨意地說口糧增加了。

passages.original: In addition, Napoleon ordered the almost empty bins in the store-shed to be filled nearly to the brim with sand, which was then covered up with what remained of the grain and meal.
passages.vernacular: 此外,拿破崙命令把儲藏棚裡幾乎空咗嘅箱子幾乎用沙子填到邊緣,然後用剩下嘅穀物同粗粉蓋住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,拿破崙命令把儲藏棚裡幾乎空了的箱子幾乎用沙子填到邊緣,然後用剩下的穀物和粗粉蓋住。

passages.original: On some suitable pretext Whymper was led through the store-shed and allowed to catch a glimpse of the bins.
passages.vernacular: 以某個適當嘅藉口,溫珀被領住穿過儲藏棚,允許佢瞥見嗰啲箱子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以某個適當的藉口,溫珀被領著穿過儲藏棚,允許他瞥見那些箱子。

passages.original: He was deceived, and continued to report to the outside world that there was no food shortage on Animal Farm.
passages.vernacular: 佢被騙喇,繼續向外界報告講動物農莊冇食物短缺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他被騙了,繼續向外界報告說動物農莊沒有食物短缺。

passages.original: Nevertheless, towards the end of January it became obvious that it would be necessary to procure some more grain from somewhere.
passages.vernacular: 然而,一月底顯然有必要從某處再弄些穀物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,一月底顯然有必要從某處再弄些穀物。

passages.original: In these days Napoleon rarely appeared in public, but spent all his time in the farmhouse, which was guarded at each door by fierce-looking dogs.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲日子,拿破崙好少公開露面,而係把所有時間都花喺農舍裡,每道門都有睇起嚟凶猛嘅狗守衛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些日子,拿破崙很少公開露面,而是把所有時間都花在農舍裡,每道門都有看起來凶猛的狗守衛。

passages.original: When he did emerge, it was in a ceremonial manner, with an escort of six dogs who closely surrounded him and growled if anyone came too near.
passages.vernacular: 當佢確實出現時,係以儀式化嘅方式,有六條狗護衛,緊緊圍住佢,如果有人靠得太近就低吼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他確實出現時,是以儀式化的方式,有六條狗護衛,緊緊圍著他,如果有人靠得太近就低吼。

passages.original: Frequently he did not even appear on Sunday mornings, but issued his orders through one of the other pigs, usually Squealer.
passages.vernacular: 佢經常連星期天早晨都不出現,而係通過其他豬之一,通常係尖嗓子,發布佢嘅命令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他經常連星期天早晨也不出現,而是通過其他豬之一,通常是尖嗓子,發布他的命令。

passages.original: One Sunday morning Squealer announced that the hens, who had just come in to lay again, must surrender their eggs.
passages.vernacular: 一個星期天早晨,尖嗓子宣布,剛又開始下蛋嘅母雞,必須交出佢哋嘅蛋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個星期天早晨,尖嗓子宣布,剛又開始下蛋的母雞,必須交出它們的蛋。

passages.original: Napoleon had accepted, through Whymper, a contract for four hundred eggs a week.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙通過溫珀接受咗一份每週四百個蛋嘅合同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙通過溫珀接受了一份每週四百個蛋的合同。

passages.original: The price of these would pay for enough grain and meal to keep the farm going till summer came on and conditions were easier.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲蛋嘅價錢可以買足夠嘅穀物同粗粉維持農場,直到夏天來臨、情況變得容易。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些蛋的價錢可以買足夠的穀物和粗粉維持農場,直到夏天來臨、情況變得容易。

passages.original: When the hens heard this, they raised a terrible outcry.
passages.vernacular: 母雞哋聽到呢個,發出可怕嘅抗議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 母雞們聽到這個,發出可怕的抗議。

passages.original: They had been warned earlier that this sacrifice might be necessary, but had not believed that it would really happen.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋早先被警告過呢種犧牲可能係必要嘅,但不相信真嘅會發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們早先被警告過這種犧牲可能是必要的,但不相信真的會發生。

passages.original: They were just getting their clutches ready for the spring sitting, and they protested that to take the eggs away now was murder.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋剛好喺為春季孵蛋準備卵窩,佢哋抗議講而家把蛋攞走就係謀殺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們剛好在為春季孵蛋準備卵窩,它們抗議說現在把蛋拿走就是謀殺。

passages.original: For the first time since the expulsion of Jones, there was something resembling a rebellion.
passages.vernacular: 自瓊斯被驅逐以來,第一次出現咗類似造反嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自瓊斯被驅逐以來,第一次出現了類似造反的東西。

passages.original: Led by three young Black Minorca pullets, the hens made a determined effort to thwart Napoleon’s wishes.
passages.vernacular: 由三隻年輕嘅黑米諾卡小母雞帶領,母雞哋堅決努力挫敗拿破崙嘅願望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 由三隻年輕的黑米諾卡小母雞帶領,母雞們堅決努力挫敗拿破崙的願望。

passages.original: Their method was to fly up to the rafters and there lay their eggs, which smashed to pieces on the floor.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅方法係飛到椽子上,喺嗰度下蛋,蛋掉喺地板上摔碎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們的方法是飛到椽子上,在那裡下蛋,蛋掉在地板上摔碎。

passages.original: Napoleon acted swiftly and ruthlessly.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙迅速而無情地行動喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙迅速而無情地行動了。

passages.original: He ordered the hens’ rations to be stopped, and decreed that any animal giving so much as a grain of corn to a hen should be punished by death.
passages.vernacular: 佢命令停止母雞嘅口糧,並下令,任何動物畀母雞邊怕一粒玉米,將被處死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他命令停止母雞的口糧,並下令,任何動物給母雞哪怕一粒玉米,將被處死。

passages.original: The dogs saw to it that these orders were carried out.
passages.vernacular: 狗負責確保呢啲命令被執行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗負責確保這些命令被執行。

passages.original: For five days the hens held out, then they capitulated and went back to their nesting boxes.
passages.vernacular: 母雞堅持咗五天,然後投降,回到佢哋嘅巢箱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 母雞堅持了五天,然後投降,回到它們的巢箱。

passages.original: Nine hens had died in the meantime.
passages.vernacular: 喺此期間有九隻母雞死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在此期間有九隻母雞死了。

passages.original: Their bodies were buried in the orchard, and it was given out that they had died of coccidiosis.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅屍體被埋喺果園裡,對外宣稱佢哋死於球蟲病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們的屍體被埋在果園裡,對外宣稱它們死於球蟲病。

passages.original: Whymper heard nothing of this affair, and the eggs were duly delivered, a grocer’s van driving up to the farm once a week to take them away.
passages.vernacular: 溫珀冇聽講呢件事,蛋按時交付喇,一輛雜貨商嘅貨車每週開到農場一次把佢哋運走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫珀沒有聽說這件事,蛋按時交付了,一輛雜貨商的貨車每週開到農場一次把它們運走。

passages.original: All this while no more had been seen of Snowball.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢期間,冇再睇到雪球。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這期間,沒有再看到雪球。

passages.original: He was rumoured to be hiding on one of the neighbouring farms, either Foxwood or Pinchfield.
passages.vernacular: 傳聞佢躲喺鄰近農場之一,狐林或平奇菲爾德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傳聞他躲在鄰近農場之一,狐林或平奇菲爾德。

passages.original: Napoleon was by this time on slightly better terms with the other farmers than before.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣拿破崙同其他農場主嘅關係比以前稍好啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時拿破崙與其他農場主的關係比以前稍好一些。

passages.original: It happened that there was in the yard a pile of timber which had been stacked there ten years earlier when a beech spinney was cleared.
passages.vernacular: 碰巧院子裡有一堆木材,係十年前清理一片山毛櫸小樹林時堆喺嗰度嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 碰巧院子裡有一堆木材,是十年前清理一片山毛櫸小樹林時堆在那裡的。

passages.original: It was well seasoned, and Whymper had advised Napoleon to sell it; both Mr. Pilkington and Mr. Frederick were anxious to buy it.
passages.vernacular: 佢已經好好地風乾喇,溫珀建議拿破崙賣掉佢;皮爾金頓先生同弗雷德里克先生都急於買佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它已經很好地風乾了,溫珀建議拿破崙賣掉它;皮爾金頓先生和弗雷德里克先生都急於買它。

passages.original: Napoleon was hesitating between the two, unable to make up his mind.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙喺兩者之間猶豫,無法下決心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙在兩者之間猶豫,無法下決心。

passages.original: It was noticed that whenever he seemed on the point of coming to an agreement with Frederick, Snowball was declared to be in hiding at Foxwood, while, when he inclined toward Pilkington, Snowball was said to be at Pinchfield.
passages.vernacular: 大家注意到,每當佢似乎即將同弗雷德里克達成協議時,就宣布雪球躲喺狐林,而當佢傾向皮爾金頓時,據講雪球喺平奇菲爾德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家注意到,每當他似乎即將同弗雷德里克達成協議時,就宣布雪球躲在狐林,而當他傾向皮爾金頓時,據說雪球在平奇菲爾德。

passages.original: Suddenly, early in the spring, an alarming thing was discovered.
passages.vernacular: 突然,喺初春,發現咗一件令人警覺嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然,在初春,發現了一件令人警覺的事。

passages.original: Snowball was secretly frequenting the farm by night!
passages.vernacular: 雪球夜裡秘密地常嚟農場!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球夜裡秘密地常來農場!

passages.original: The animals were so disturbed that they could hardly sleep in their stalls.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋咁不安,幾乎無法喺馬廄裡瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們那麼不安,幾乎無法在馬廄裡睡覺。

passages.original: Every night, it was said, he came creeping in under cover of darkness and performed all kinds of mischief.
passages.vernacular: 據講佢每夜喺黑暗掩護下悄悄溜進嚟,幹各種壞事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據說他每夜在黑暗掩護下悄悄溜進來,幹各種壞事。

passages.original: He stole the corn, he upset the milk-pails, he broke the eggs, he trampled the seedbeds, he gnawed the bark off the fruit trees.
passages.vernacular: 佢偷玉米,打翻奶桶,打破蛋,踐踏苗床,啃掉果樹嘅皮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他偷玉米,打翻奶桶,打破蛋,踐踏苗床,啃掉果樹的皮。

passages.original: Whenever anything went wrong it became usual to attribute it to Snowball.
passages.vernacular: 每當出咗乜嘢問題,就習慣歸咎於雪球。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每當出了什麼問題,就習慣歸咎於雪球。

passages.original: If a window was broken or a drain was blocked up, someone was certain to say that Snowball had come in the night and done it, and when the key of the store-shed was lost, the whole farm was convinced that Snowball had thrown it down the well.
passages.vernacular: 如果一扇窗子破咗或一條排水溝堵喇,必定有人講係雪球夜裡嚟幹嘅,當儲藏棚嘅鑰匙丟喇,整個農場都確信係雪球把佢扔進咗井裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果一扇窗子破了或一條排水溝堵了,必定有人說是雪球夜裡來幹的,當儲藏棚的鑰匙丟了,整個農場都確信是雪球把它扔進了井裡。

passages.original: Curiously enough, they went on believing this even after the mislaid key was found under a sack of meal.
passages.vernacular: 奇怪嘅係,甚至喺放錯地方嘅鑰匙喺一袋粗粉下面被找到後,佢哋仍繼續相信呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇怪的是,甚至在放錯地方的鑰匙在一袋粗粉下面被找到後,它們仍繼續相信這個。

passages.original: The cows declared unanimously that Snowball crept into their stalls and milked them in their sleep.
passages.vernacular: 母牛哋一致宣稱,雪球溜進佢哋嘅馬廄,喺佢哋瞓覺時擠佢哋嘅奶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 母牛們一致宣稱,雪球溜進它們的馬廄,在它們睡覺時擠它們的奶。

passages.original: The rats, which had been troublesome that winter, were also said to be in league with Snowball.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個冬天一直好麻煩嘅老鼠,據講都同雪球勾結。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個冬天一直很麻煩的老鼠,據說也與雪球勾結。

passages.original: Napoleon decreed that there should be a full investigation into Snowball’s activities.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙下令,要對雪球嘅活動進行全面調查。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙下令,要對雪球的活動進行全面調查。

passages.original: With his dogs in attendance he set out and made a careful tour of inspection of the farm buildings, the other animals following at a respectful distance.
passages.vernacular: 佢帶住佢嘅狗出發,對農場建築進行仔細嘅巡視,其他動物以尊敬嘅距離跟喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他帶著他的狗出發,對農場建築進行仔細的巡視,其他動物以尊敬的距離跟在後面。

passages.original: At every few steps Napoleon stopped and snuffed the ground for traces of Snowball’s footsteps, which, he said, he could detect by the smell.
passages.vernacular: 每走幾步,拿破崙就停下嚟聞地面尋找雪球嘅足跡,佢講,佢能憑氣味發覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每走幾步,拿破崙就停下來聞地面尋找雪球的足跡,他說,他能憑氣味發覺。

passages.original: He snuffed in every corner, in the barn, in the cow-shed, in the henhouses, in the vegetable garden, and found traces of Snowball almost everywhere.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺每個角落聞,喺穀倉、牛棚、雞舍、菜園,幾乎喺每一處都發現咗雪球嘅痕跡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在每個角落聞,在穀倉、牛棚、雞舍、菜園,幾乎在每一處都發現了雪球的痕跡。

passages.original: He would put his snout to the ground, give several deep sniffs, ad exclaim in a terrible voice, “Snowball!
passages.vernacular: 佢會把鼻子貼喺地上,深深嗅幾下,然後以可怕嘅聲音喊道:「雪球!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他會把鼻子貼在地上,深深嗅幾下,然後以可怕的聲音喊道:「雪球!

passages.original: He has been here!
passages.vernacular: 佢到過呢度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他到過這裡!

passages.original: I can smell him distinctly!” and at the word “Snowball” all the dogs let out blood-curdling growls and showed their side teeth.
passages.vernacular: 我能清楚地聞到佢!」一聽到「雪球」呢個詞,所有嘅狗都發出令人毛骨悚然嘅低吼,露出側面嘅牙齒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能清楚地聞到他!」一聽到「雪球」這個詞,所有的狗都發出令人毛骨悚然的低吼,露出側面的牙齒。

passages.original: The animals were thoroughly frightened.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋被徹底嚇壞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們被徹底嚇壞了。

passages.original: It seemed to them as though Snowball were some kind of invisible influence, pervading the air about them and menacing them with all kinds of dangers.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢哋睇來,好像雪球係某種無形嘅影響,瀰漫喺佢哋周圍嘅空氣中,以各種危險威脅住佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在它們看來,好像雪球是某種無形的影響,瀰漫在它們周圍的空氣中,以各種危險威脅著它們。

passages.original: In the evening Squealer called them together, and with an alarmed expression on his face told them that he had some serious news to report.
passages.vernacular: 傍晚,尖嗓子把佢哋召集喺一起,臉上帶住驚恐嘅表情,告訴佢哋佢有嚴重嘅消息要報告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傍晚,尖嗓子把它們召集在一起,臉上帶著驚恐的表情,告訴它們他有嚴重的消息要報告。

passages.original: “Comrades!” cried Squealer, making little nervous skips, “a most terrible thing has been discovered.
passages.vernacular: 「同志哋!」尖嗓子喊道,神經質地小蹦跳,「發現咗一件最可怕嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志們!」尖嗓子喊道,神經質地小蹦跳,「發現了一件最可怕的事。

passages.original: Snowball has sold himself to Frederick of Pinchfield Farm, who is even now plotting to attack us and take our farm away from us!
passages.vernacular: 雪球已經把自己賣畀咗平奇菲爾德農場嘅弗雷德里克,佢而家就喺密謀攻擊我哋,把我哋嘅農場從我哋手中奪走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球已經把自己賣給了平奇菲爾德農場的弗雷德里克,他現在就在密謀攻擊我們,把我們的農場從我們手中奪走!

passages.original: Snowball is to act as his guide when the attack begins.
passages.vernacular: 攻擊開始時,雪球將作佢嘅嚮導。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 攻擊開始時,雪球將作他的嚮導。

passages.original: But there is worse than that.
passages.vernacular: 但仲有比嗰更壞嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但還有比那更壞的。

passages.original: We had thought that Snowball’s rebellion was caused simply by his vanity and ambition.
passages.vernacular: 我哋原以為雪球嘅造反只係出於佢嘅虛榮同野心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們原以為雪球的造反只是出於他的虛榮和野心。

passages.original: But we were wrong, comrades.
passages.vernacular: 但我哋錯喇,同志哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們錯了,同志們。

passages.original: Do you know what the real reason was?
passages.vernacular: 你哋知道真正嘅原因係乜嘢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們知道真正的原因是什麼嗎?

passages.original: Snowball was in league with Jones from the very start!
passages.vernacular: 雪球從一開始就同瓊斯勾結!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球從一開始就與瓊斯勾結!

passages.original: He was Jones’s secret agent all the time.
passages.vernacular: 佢一直係瓊斯嘅秘密特工。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一直是瓊斯的秘密特工。

passages.original: It has all been proved by documents which he left behind him and which we have only just discovered.
passages.vernacular: 呢一切都已經被佢留下嘅、我哋剛發現嘅文件證明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切都已經被他留下的、我們剛發現的文件證明。

passages.original: To my mind this explains a great deal, comrades.
passages.vernacular: 喺我睇來呢解釋咗好多事情,同志哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我看來這解釋了很多事情,同志們。

passages.original: Did we not see for ourselves how he attempted--fortunately without success--to get us defeated and destroyed at the Battle of the Cowshed?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔係親眼睇到佢點樣試圖——幸運嘅係冇成功——喺牛棚之戰中使我哋被打敗、被消滅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不是親眼看到他怎樣試圖——幸運的是沒有成功——在牛棚之戰中使我們被打敗、被消滅嗎?」

passages.original: The animals were stupefied.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋驚呆喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們驚呆了。

passages.original: This was a wickedness far outdoing Snowball’s destruction of the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一種遠遠超過雪球毀壞風車嘅邪惡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一種遠遠超過雪球毀壞風車的邪惡。

passages.original: But it was some minutes before they could fully take it in.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋過咗幾分鐘才能完全領會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它們過了幾分鐘才能完全領會。

passages.original: They all remembered, or thought they remembered, how they had seen Snowball charging ahead of them at the Battle of the Cowshed, how he had rallied and encouraged them at every turn, and how he had not paused for an instant even when the pellets from Jones’s gun had wounded his back.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都記得,或者認為記得,佢哋點樣睇到雪球喺牛棚之戰中衝喺佢哋前面,佢點樣喺每個轉折點集結同鼓勵佢哋,甚至喺瓊斯嘅槍彈打傷佢嘅背時佢都冇停頓一刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們都記得,或者認為記得,它們怎樣看到雪球在牛棚之戰中衝在它們前面,他怎樣在每個轉折點集結和鼓勵它們,甚至在瓊斯的槍彈打傷他的背時他也沒有停頓一刻。

passages.original: At first it was a little difficult to see how this fitted in with his being on Jones’s side.
passages.vernacular: 起初有點難以理解呢點樣同佢站喺瓊斯一邊相吻合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初有點難以理解這怎樣與他站在瓊斯一邊相吻合。

passages.original: Even Boxer, who seldom asked questions, was puzzled.
passages.vernacular: 連好少提問嘅拳擊手都感到困惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連很少提問的拳擊手也感到困惑。

passages.original: He lay down, tucked his fore hoofs beneath him, shut his eyes, and with a hard effort managed to formulate his thoughts.
passages.vernacular: 佢躺下,把前蹄縮喺身下,閉上眼睛,費咗好大力氣才設法整理出佢嘅想法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他躺下,把前蹄縮在身下,閉上眼睛,費了很大力氣才設法整理出他的想法。

passages.original: “I do not believe that,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「我不相信,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不相信,」他說。

passages.original: “Snowball fought bravely at the Battle of the Cowshed.
passages.vernacular: 「雪球喺牛棚之戰中英勇作戰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「雪球在牛棚之戰中英勇作戰。

passages.original: I saw him myself.
passages.vernacular: 我自己睇到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己看到了。

passages.original: Did we not give him ‘Animal Hero, first Class,’ immediately afterwards?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔係喺嗰之後即刻授予佢『一級動物英雄』嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不是在那之後立刻授予他『一級動物英雄』嗎?」

passages.original: “That was our mistake, comrade.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係我哋嘅錯誤,同志。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是我們的錯誤,同志。

passages.original: For we know now--it is all written down in the secret documents that we have found--that in reality he was trying to lure us to our doom.”
passages.vernacular: 因為我哋而家知道——呢一切都寫喺我哋找到嘅秘密文件中——佢實際上係想引誘我哋走向毀滅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我們現在知道——這一切都寫在我們找到的秘密文件中——他實際上是想引誘我們走向毀滅。」

passages.original: “But he was wounded,” said Boxer.
passages.vernacular: 「但佢受傷喇,」拳擊手講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但他受傷了,」拳擊手說。

passages.original: “We all saw him running with blood.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋都睇到佢流住血跑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們都看到他流著血跑。」

passages.original: “That was part of the arrangement!” cried Squealer.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係安排嘅一部分!」尖嗓子喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是安排的一部分!」尖嗓子喊道。

passages.original: “Jones’s shot only grazed him.
passages.vernacular: 「瓊斯嘅槍彈只擦傷咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瓊斯的槍彈只擦傷了他。

passages.original: I could show you this in his own writing, if you were able to read it.
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋能讀,我可以畀你哋睇佢自己嘅筆跡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們能讀,我可以給你們看他自己的筆跡。

passages.original: The plot was for Snowball, at the critical moment, to give the signal for flight and leave the field to the enemy.
passages.vernacular: 陰謀係讓雪球喺關鍵時刻發出逃跑嘅信號,把戰場讓畀敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 陰謀是讓雪球在關鍵時刻發出逃跑的信號,把戰場讓給敵人。

passages.original: And he very nearly succeeded--I will even say, comrades, he WOULD have succeeded if it had not been for our heroic Leader, Comrade Napoleon.
passages.vernacular: 佢幾乎成功喇——我甚至要講,同志哋,如果唔係我哋英雄嘅領袖拿破崙同志,佢就成功喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他幾乎成功了——我甚至要說,同志們,如果不是我們英雄的領袖拿破崙同志,他就成功了。

passages.original: Do you not remember how, just at the moment when Jones and his men had got inside the yard, Snowball suddenly turned and fled, and many animals followed him?
passages.vernacular: 你哋不記得,就喺瓊斯同佢嘅人進咗院子嘅時刻,雪球突然轉身逃跑,許多動物跟住佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們不記得,就在瓊斯和他的人進了院子的時刻,雪球突然轉身逃跑,許多動物跟著他嗎?

passages.original: And do you not remember, too, that it was just at that moment, when panic was spreading and all seemed lost, that Comrade Napoleon sprang forward with a cry of ‘Death to Humanity!’ and sank his teeth in Jones’s leg?
passages.vernacular: 你哋都不記得,正是喺嗰一刻,當恐慌蔓延、一切似乎都失去時,拿破崙同志喊住『人類去死!』向前躍起,一口咬住瓊斯嘅腿嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們也不記得,正是在那一刻,當恐慌蔓延、一切似乎都失去時,拿破崙同志喊著『人類去死!』向前躍起,一口咬住瓊斯的腿嗎?

passages.original: Surely you remember THAT, comrades?” exclaimed Squealer, frisking from side to side.
passages.vernacular: 你哋肯定記得嗰個,同志哋?」尖嗓子左右蹦跳住喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們肯定記得那個,同志們?」尖嗓子左右蹦跳著喊道。

passages.original: Now when Squealer described the scene so graphically, it seemed to the animals that they did remember it.
passages.vernacular: 而家,當尖嗓子如此生動地描述呢個場面時,動物哋似乎覺得佢哋確實記得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,當尖嗓子如此生動地描述這個場面時,動物們似乎覺得它們確實記得。

passages.original: At any rate, they remembered that at the critical moment of the battle Snowball had turned to flee.
passages.vernacular: 無論如何,佢哋記得喺戰鬥嘅關鍵時刻,雪球轉身逃跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何,它們記得在戰鬥的關鍵時刻,雪球轉身逃跑。

passages.original: But Boxer was still a little uneasy.
passages.vernacular: 但拳擊手仍有點不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但拳擊手仍有點不安。

passages.original: “I do not believe that Snowball was a traitor at the beginning,” he said finally.
passages.vernacular: 「我不相信雪球一開始就係叛徒,」佢最後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不相信雪球一開始就是叛徒,」他最後說。

passages.original: “What he has done since is different.
passages.vernacular: 「佢後來所做嘅係另一回事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他後來所做的是另一回事。

passages.original: But I believe that at the Battle of the Cowshed he was a good comrade.”
passages.vernacular: 但我相信喺牛棚之戰中佢係個好同志。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我相信在牛棚之戰中他是個好同志。」

passages.original: “Our Leader, Comrade Napoleon,” announced Squealer, speaking very slowly and firmly, “has stated categorically--categorically, comrade--that Snowball was Jones’s agent from the very beginning--yes, and from long before the Rebellion was ever thought of.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋嘅領袖拿破崙同志,」尖嗓子講,講得好緩慢而堅定,「已斷然宣布——斷然,同志——雪球從一開始就係瓊斯嘅特工——係嘅,而且係從遠喺造反被想到之前。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們的領袖拿破崙同志,」尖嗓子說,說得非常緩慢而堅定,「已斷然宣布——斷然,同志——雪球從一開始就是瓊斯的特工——是的,而且是從遠在造反被想到之前。」

passages.original: “Ah, that is different!” said Boxer.
passages.vernacular: 「啊,嗰就不同喇!」拳擊手講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,那就不同了!」拳擊手說。

passages.original: “If Comrade Napoleon says it, it must be right.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果拿破崙同志咁樣講,嗰一定係對嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果拿破崙同志這樣說,那一定是對的。」

passages.original: “That is the true spirit, comrade!” cried Squealer, but it was noticed he cast a very ugly look at Boxer with his little twinkling eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「呢才係真正嘅精神,同志!」尖嗓子喊道,但大家注意到佢用佢閃爍嘅小眼睛向拳擊手投去咗好難睇嘅一瞥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這才是真正的精神,同志!」尖嗓子喊道,但大家注意到他用他閃爍的小眼睛向拳擊手投去了很難看的一瞥。

passages.original: He turned to go, then paused and added impressively: “I warn every animal on this farm to keep his eyes very wide open.
passages.vernacular: 佢轉身要走,又停下嚟,令人印象深刻地補充講:「我警告呢個農場上嘅每個動物都要睜大眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他轉身要走,又停下來,令人印象深刻地補充說:「我警告這個農場上的每個動物都要睜大眼睛。

passages.original: For we have reason to think that some of Snowball’s secret agents are lurking among us at this moment!”
passages.vernacular: 因為我哋有理由認為,雪球嘅啲秘密特工此刻正潛伏喺我哋中間!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我們有理由認為,雪球的一些秘密特工此刻正潛伏在我們中間!」

passages.original: Four days later, in the late afternoon, Napoleon ordered all the animals to assemble in the yard.
passages.vernacular: 四天後,喺傍晚,拿破崙命令所有動物喺院子裡集合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四天後,在傍晚,拿破崙命令所有動物在院子裡集合。

passages.original: When they were all gathered together, Napoleon emerged from the farmhouse, wearing both his medals (for he had recently awarded himself “Animal Hero, First Class”, and “Animal Hero, Second Class”), with his nine huge dogs frisking round him and uttering growls that sent shivers down all the animals’ spines.
passages.vernacular: 大家聚齊後,拿破崙從農舍裡出嚟,戴住佢嘅兩枚勳章(因為佢最近授予咗自己「一級動物英雄」同「二級動物英雄」),佢嘅九條巨大嘅狗喺佢周圍蹦跳,發出使所有動物脊背發涼嘅低吼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家聚齊後,拿破崙從農舍裡出來,戴著他的兩枚勳章(因為他最近授予了自己「一級動物英雄」和「二級動物英雄」),他的九條巨大的狗在他周圍蹦跳,發出使所有動物脊背發涼的低吼。

passages.original: They all cowered silently in their places, seeming to know in advance that some terrible thing was about to happen.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋全都默默地蜷縮喺自己嘅位置,似乎預先知道某件可怕嘅事即將發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們全都默默地蜷縮在自己的位置,似乎預先知道某件可怕的事即將發生。

passages.original: Napoleon stood sternly surveying his audience; then he uttered a high-pitched whimper.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙嚴厲地站住環視佢嘅聽眾;然後佢發出一聲高音嘅嗚咽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙嚴厲地站著環視他的聽眾;然後他發出一聲高音的嗚咽。

passages.original: Immediately the dogs bounded forward, seized four of the pigs by the ear and dragged them, squealing with pain and terror, to Napoleon’s feet.
passages.vernacular: 狗即刻衝上前,咬住四頭豬嘅耳朵,把佢哋拖到拿破崙腳下,佢哋因痛苦同恐懼尖叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗立刻衝上前,咬住四頭豬的耳朵,把他們拖到拿破崙腳下,他們因痛苦和恐懼尖叫。

passages.original: The pigs’ ears were bleeding, the dogs had tasted blood, and for a few moments they appeared to go quite mad.
passages.vernacular: 豬嘅耳朵喺流血,狗嚐到咗血,有幾分鐘佢哋似乎完全發咗瘋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬的耳朵在流血,狗嚐到了血,有幾分鐘它們似乎完全發了瘋。

passages.original: To the amazement of everybody, three of them flung themselves upon Boxer.
passages.vernacular: 令所有人驚訝嘅係,其中三條撲向拳擊手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令所有人驚訝的是,其中三條撲向拳擊手。

passages.original: Boxer saw them coming and put out his great hoof, caught a dog in mid-air, and pinned him to the ground.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手睇到佢哋嚟喇,伸出佢巨大嘅蹄子,喺半空中抓住一條狗,把佢按喺地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手看到它們來了,伸出他巨大的蹄子,在半空中抓住一條狗,把它按在地上。

passages.original: The dog shrieked for mercy and the other two fled with their tails between their legs.
passages.vernacular: 嗰條狗尖叫求饒,另外兩條夾住尾巴逃走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那條狗尖叫求饒,另外兩條夾著尾巴逃走了。

passages.original: Boxer looked at Napoleon to know whether he should crush the dog to death or let it go.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手睇住拿破崙,想知道應該把狗踩死定係放咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手看著拿破崙,想知道應該把狗踩死還是放了它。

passages.original: Napoleon appeared to change countenance, and sharply ordered Boxer to let the dog go, whereat Boxer lifted his hoof, and the dog slunk away, bruised and howling.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙似乎改變咗臉色,尖銳地命令拳擊手放開狗,於是拳擊手抬起咗蹄子,嗰條狗悄悄溜走,受咗傷,嚎叫住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙似乎改變了臉色,尖銳地命令拳擊手放開狗,於是拳擊手抬起了蹄子,那條狗悄悄溜走,受了傷,嚎叫著。

passages.original: Presently the tumult died down.
passages.vernacular: 不久騷動平息喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久騷動平息了。

passages.original: The four pigs waited, trembling, with guilt written on every line of their countenances.
passages.vernacular: 嗰四頭豬等住,顫抖住,罪過寫喺佢哋臉上嘅每一條線上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那四頭豬等著,顫抖著,罪過寫在他們臉上的每一條線上。

passages.original: Napoleon now called upon them to confess their crimes.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙而家要求佢哋招供罪行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙現在要求他們招供罪行。

passages.original: They were the same four pigs as had protested when Napoleon abolished the Sunday Meetings.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋就係拿破崙廢除星期天大會時提出抗議嘅嗰四頭豬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們就是拿破崙廢除星期天大會時提出抗議的那四頭豬。

passages.original: Without any further prompting they confessed that they had been secretly in touch with Snowball ever since his expulsion, that they had collaborated with him in destroying the windmill, and that they had entered into an agreement with him to hand over Animal Farm to Mr. Frederick.
passages.vernacular: 唔使進一步催促,佢哋就招供講,自從雪球被驅逐,佢哋就一直秘密同佢保持聯繫,佢哋同佢合作毀壞咗風車,並同佢達成協議把動物農莊交畀弗雷德里克先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不用進一步催促,他們就招供說,自從雪球被驅逐,他們就一直秘密與他保持聯繫,他們同他合作毀壞了風車,並與他達成協議把動物農莊交給弗雷德里克先生。

passages.original: They added that Snowball had privately admitted to them that he had been Jones’s secret agent for years past.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋補充講,雪球私下向佢哋承認,佢多年嚟一直係瓊斯嘅秘密特工。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們補充說,雪球私下向他們承認,他多年來一直是瓊斯的秘密特工。

passages.original: When they had finished their confession, the dogs promptly tore their throats out, and in a terrible voice Napoleon demanded whether any other animal had anything to confess.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋招供完畢,狗即刻撕開咗佢哋嘅喉嚨,拿破崙以可怕嘅聲音要求係咪仲有其他動物有乜嘢要招供。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們招供完畢,狗立刻撕開了他們的喉嚨,拿破崙以可怕的聲音要求是否還有其他動物有什麼要招供。

passages.original: The three hens who had been the ringleaders in the attempted rebellion over the eggs now came forward and stated that Snowball had appeared to them in a dream and incited them to disobey Napoleon’s orders.
passages.vernacular: 嗰三隻喺蛋嘅企圖造反中領頭嘅母雞,而家走上前來講,雪球喺夢中向佢哋顯現,煽動佢哋違抗拿破崙嘅命令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那三隻在蛋的企圖造反中領頭的母雞,現在走上前來說,雪球在夢中向它們顯現,煽動它們違抗拿破崙的命令。

passages.original: They, too, were slaughtered.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都被屠殺喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們也被屠殺了。

passages.original: Then a goose came forward and confessed to having secreted six ears of corn during the last year’s harvest and eaten them in the night.
passages.vernacular: 然後一隻鵝走上前嚟,招供去年收成時藏咗六穗玉米,喺夜裡食掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後一隻鵝走上前來,招供去年收成時藏了六穗玉米,在夜裡吃掉。

passages.original: Then a sheep confessed to having urinated in the drinking pool--urged to do this, so she said, by Snowball--and two other sheep confessed to having murdered an old ram, an especially devoted follower of Napoleon, by chasing him round and round a bonfire when he was suffering from a cough.
passages.vernacular: 然後一隻羊招供喺飲水池裡撒尿——據佢講,係雪球慫恿佢咁樣做嘅——另外兩隻羊招供殺害咗一隻老公羊,拿破崙嘅一個特別忠誠嘅追隨者,係喺佢咳嗽時,圍住篝火追佢一圈又一圈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後一隻羊招供在飲水池裡撒尿——據她說,是雪球慫恿她這樣做的——另外兩隻羊招供殺害了一隻老公羊,拿破崙的一個特別忠誠的追隨者,是在他咳嗽時,圍著篝火追他一圈又一圈。

passages.original: They were all slain on the spot.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋全都當場被殺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們全都當場被殺。

passages.original: And so the tale of confessions and executions went on, until there was a pile of corpses lying before Napoleon’s feet and the air was heavy with the smell of blood, which had been unknown there since the expulsion of Jones.
passages.vernacular: 招供同處決嘅故事就咁樣繼續,直到拿破崙腳前堆滿咗屍體,空氣中瀰漫住血腥味,嗰個係自瓊斯被驅逐以來呢度從未有過嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 招供和處決的故事就這樣繼續,直到拿破崙腳前堆滿了屍體,空氣中瀰漫著血腥味,那是自瓊斯被驅逐以來這裡從未有過的。

passages.original: When it was all over, the remaining animals, except for the pigs and dogs, crept away in a body.
passages.vernacular: 一切結束後,其餘嘅動物,除咗豬同狗,成群結隊地悄悄離去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切結束後,其餘的動物,除了豬和狗,成群結隊地悄悄離去。

passages.original: They were shaken and miserable.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋顫抖而悲慘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們顫抖而悲慘。

passages.original: They did not know which was more shocking--the treachery of the animals who had leagued themselves with Snowball, or the cruel retribution they had just witnessed.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔知道邊個更令人震驚——同雪球勾結嘅動物嘅背叛,定係佢哋剛睇到嘅殘酷報復。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們不知道哪個更令人震驚——與雪球勾結的動物的背叛,還是它們剛看到的殘酷報復。

passages.original: In the old days there had often been scenes of bloodshed equally terrible, but it seemed to all of them that it was far worse now that it was happening among themselves.
passages.vernacular: 喺過去嘅日子裡,都常有同樣可怕嘅流血場面,但喺佢哋睇來,而家發生喺佢哋自己之間,要壞得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在過去的日子裡,也常有同樣可怕的流血場面,但在它們看來,現在發生在它們自己之間,要壞得多。

passages.original: Since Jones had left the farm, until today, no animal had killed another animal.
passages.vernacular: 自從瓊斯離開農場到今日,冇任何動物殺過另一個動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從瓊斯離開農場到今天,沒有任何動物殺過另一個動物。

passages.original: Not even a rat had been killed.
passages.vernacular: 連一隻老鼠都冇被殺過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連一隻老鼠也沒有被殺過。

passages.original: They had made their way on to the little knoll where the half-finished windmill stood, and with one accord they all lay down as though huddling together for warmth--Clover, Muriel, Benjamin, the cows, the sheep, and a whole flock of geese and hens--everyone, indeed, except the cat, who had suddenly disappeared just before Napoleon ordered the animals to assemble.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋走到半完工風車所在嘅小丘上,一致躺下,好像擠喺一起取暖——三葉草、繆麗兒、班傑明、牛、羊,同一大群鵝同母雞——事實上,除咗貓,佢喺拿破崙命令動物哋集合之前突然消失喇,其他每個都喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們走到半完工風車所在的小丘上,一致躺下,好像擠在一起取暖——三葉草、繆麗兒、班傑明、牛、羊,和一大群鵝和母雞——事實上,除了貓,她在拿破崙命令動物們集合之前突然消失了,其他每個都在。

passages.original: For some time nobody spoke.
passages.vernacular: 有一段時間冇人講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一段時間沒有人說話。

passages.original: Only Boxer remained on his feet.
passages.vernacular: 只有拳擊手仍站住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有拳擊手仍站著。

passages.original: He fidgeted to and fro, swishing his long black tail against his sides and occasionally uttering a little whinny of surprise.
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟回不安地走動,用佢長長嘅黑尾巴抽打住兩側,偶爾發出一聲驚訝嘅小嘶鳴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他來回不安地走動,用他長長的黑尾巴抽打著兩側,偶爾發出一聲驚訝的小嘶鳴。

passages.original: Finally he said:
passages.vernacular: 最後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他說:

passages.original: “I do not understand it.
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白。

passages.original: I would not have believed that such things could happen on our farm.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會相信咁樣嘅事會發生喺我哋嘅農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會相信這樣的事會發生在我們的農場。

passages.original: It must be due to some fault in ourselves.
passages.vernacular: 一定係因為我哋自己嘅某種過錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一定是因為我們自己的某種過錯。

passages.original: The solution, as I see it, is to work harder.
passages.vernacular: 喺我睇來,解決辦法係更努力工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我看來,解決辦法是更努力工作。

passages.original: From now onwards I shall get up a full hour earlier in the mornings.”
passages.vernacular: 從而家起,我每天早晨要早起整整一小時。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從現在起,我每天早晨要早起整整一小時。」

passages.original: And he moved off at his lumbering trot and made for the quarry.
passages.vernacular: 佢以笨重嘅小跑走開,朝採石場去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他以笨重的小跑走開,朝採石場去了。

passages.original: Having got there, he collected two successive loads of stone and dragged them down to the windmill before retiring for the night.
passages.vernacular: 到咗嗰度,佢連續收集咗兩車石頭,拖到風車,然後才去過夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到了那裡,他連續收集了兩車石頭,拖到風車,然後才去過夜。

passages.original: The animals huddled about Clover, not speaking.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋擠喺三葉草周圍,不講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們擠在三葉草周圍,不說話。

passages.original: The knoll where they were lying gave them a wide prospect across the countryside.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋躺嘅小丘讓佢哋可以遍覽廣闊嘅鄉間景色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們躺的小丘讓它們可以遍覽廣闊的鄉間景色。

passages.original: Most of Animal Farm was within their view--the long pasture stretching down to the main road, the hayfield, the spinney, the drinking pool, the ploughed fields where the young wheat was thick and green, and the red roofs of the farm buildings with the smoke curling from the chimneys.
passages.vernacular: 動物農莊嘅大部分都喺佢哋嘅視野之內——延伸到大路嘅長牧場、乾草地、小樹林、飲水池、小麥幼苗茂密翠綠嘅耕地,同農場建築嘅紅屋頂,煙從煙囪裡盤旋而上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物農莊的大部分都在它們的視野之內——延伸到大路的長牧場、乾草地、小樹林、飲水池、小麥幼苗茂密翠綠的耕地,和農場建築的紅屋頂,煙從煙囪裡盤旋而上。

passages.original: It was a clear spring evening.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個晴朗嘅春日傍晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個晴朗的春日傍晚。

passages.original: The grass and the bursting hedges were gilded by the level rays of the sun.
passages.vernacular: 草地同正在綻放嘅樹籬被太陽嘅平射光鍍成金色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 草地和正在綻放的樹籬被太陽的平射光鍍成金色。

passages.original: Never had the farm--and with a kind of surprise they remembered that it was their own farm, every inch of it their own property--appeared to the animals so desirable a place.
passages.vernacular: 農場——佢哋帶住某種驚訝記起呢個係佢哋自己嘅農場,每一寸都係佢哋自己嘅財產——從來冇喺動物哋睇來係咁可愛嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場——它們帶著某種驚訝記起這是它們自己的農場,每一寸都是它們自己的財產——從來沒有在動物們看來是這麼可愛的地方。

passages.original: As Clover looked down the hillside her eyes filled with tears.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草望住山坡下時,眼裡滿係淚水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草望著山坡下時,眼裡滿是淚水。

passages.original: If she could have spoken her thoughts, it would have been to say that this was not what they had aimed at when they had set themselves years ago to work for the overthrow of the human race.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢能講出佢嘅想法,嗰個就係講,呢唔係佢哋多年前開始為推翻人類而工作時所瞄準嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她能說出她的想法,那就是說,這不是它們多年前開始為推翻人類而工作時所瞄準的。

passages.original: These scenes of terror and slaughter were not what they had looked forward to on that night when old Major first stirred them to rebellion.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲恐怖同屠殺嘅場面唔係喺老少校第一次激起佢哋造反嘅嗰個晚上佢哋所期待嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些恐怖和屠殺的場面不是在老少校第一次激起它們造反的那個晚上它們所期待的。

passages.original: If she herself had had any picture of the future, it had been of a society of animals set free from hunger and the whip, all equal, each working according to his capacity, the strong protecting the weak, as she had protected the lost brood of ducklings with her foreleg on the night of Major’s speech.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢自己對未來有過乜嘢圖景,嗰個就係一個擺脫咗飢餓同鞭子、人人平等、每個按其能力工作、強者保護弱者嘅動物社會,就像少校演講嗰晚,佢用前腿保護嗰窩失去母親嘅小鴨子一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她自己對未來有過什麼圖景,那就是一個擺脫了飢餓和鞭子、人人平等、每個按其能力工作、強者保護弱者的動物社會,就像少校演講那晚,她用前腿保護那窩失去母親的小鴨子一樣。

passages.original: Instead--she did not know why--they had come to a time when no one dared speak his mind, when fierce, growling dogs roamed everywhere, and when you had to watch your comrades torn to pieces after confessing to shocking crimes.
passages.vernacular: 相反——佢唔知道點解——佢哋嚟到咗一個冇人敢講出自己心裡話嘅時代,凶猛低吼嘅狗到處遊蕩,你必須眼睇住你嘅同志喺招供令人震驚嘅罪行後被撕成碎片。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相反——她不知道為什麼——它們來到了一個沒有人敢說出自己心裡話的時代,凶猛低吼的狗到處遊蕩,你必須眼看著你的同志在招供令人震驚的罪行後被撕成碎片。

passages.original: There was no thought of rebellion or disobedience in her mind.
passages.vernacular: 佢心中冇造反或不服從嘅念頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她心中沒有造反或不服從的念頭。

passages.original: She knew that, even as things were, they were far better off than they had been in the days of Jones, and that before all else it was needful to prevent the return of the human beings.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道,即使就目前嘅情況,佢哋都比瓊斯嘅時代好得多,首先必須防止人類回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她知道,即使就目前的情況,它們也比瓊斯的時代好得多,首先必須防止人類回來。

passages.original: Whatever happened she would remain faithful, work hard, carry out the orders that were given to her, and accept the leadership of Napoleon.
passages.vernacular: 無論發生乜嘢,佢都會保持忠誠,努力工作,執行畀佢嘅命令,接受拿破崙嘅領導。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論發生什麼,她都會保持忠誠,努力工作,執行給她的命令,接受拿破崙的領導。

passages.original: But still, it was not for this that she and all the other animals had hoped and toiled.
passages.vernacular: 但係,佢同所有其他動物所希望同辛勞嘅並唔係為了呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,她和所有其他動物所希望和辛勞的並不是為了這個。

passages.original: It was not for this that they had built the windmill and faced the bullets of Jones’s gun.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋建造風車、面對瓊斯槍彈,唔係為了呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們建造風車、面對瓊斯槍彈,不是為了這個。

passages.original: Such were her thoughts, though she lacked the words to express them.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係佢嘅想法,儘管佢缺乏表達佢哋嘅言語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是她的想法,儘管她缺乏表達它們的言語。

passages.original: At last, feeling this to be in some way a substitute for the words she was unable to find, she began to sing ‘Beasts of England’.
passages.vernacular: 最後,覺得呢喺某種程度上可以代替佢找唔到嘅話語,佢開始唱《英格蘭之獸》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後,覺得這在某種程度上可以代替她找不到的話語,她開始唱《英格蘭之獸》。

passages.original: The other animals sitting round her took it up, and they sang it three times over--very tunefully, but slowly and mournfully, in a way they had never sung it before.
passages.vernacular: 坐喺佢周圍嘅其他動物接咗過去,佢哋唱咗三遍——好有調子,但緩慢而悲傷,以佢哋從未嗰樣唱過嘅方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 坐在她周圍的其他動物接了過去,它們唱了三遍——非常有調子,但緩慢而悲傷,以它們從未那樣唱過的方式。

passages.original: They had just finished singing it for the third time when Squealer, attended by two dogs, approached them with the air of having something important to say.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋剛唱完第三遍,尖嗓子喺兩條狗嘅陪伴下,帶住有重要嘅話要講嘅神態走近佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們剛唱完第三遍,尖嗓子在兩條狗的陪伴下,帶著有重要的話要說的神態走近它們。

passages.original: He announced that, by a special decree of Comrade Napoleon, ‘Beasts of England’ had been abolished.
passages.vernacular: 佢宣布,根據拿破崙同志嘅特別法令,《英格蘭之獸》已被廢除。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他宣布,根據拿破崙同志的特別法令,《英格蘭之獸》已被廢除。

passages.original: From now onwards it was forbidden to sing it.
passages.vernacular: 從而家起禁止唱佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從現在起禁止唱它。

passages.original: The animals were taken aback.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋食咗一驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們吃了一驚。

passages.original: “Why?” cried Muriel.
passages.vernacular: 「點解?」繆麗兒喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼?」繆麗兒喊道。

passages.original: “It’s no longer needed, comrade,” said Squealer stiffly.
passages.vernacular: 「佢唔再需要喇,同志,」尖嗓子僵硬地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它不再需要了,同志,」尖嗓子僵硬地說。

passages.original: “‘Beasts of England’ was the song of the Rebellion.
passages.vernacular: 「《英格蘭之獸》係造反之歌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「《英格蘭之獸》是造反之歌。

passages.original: But the Rebellion is now completed.
passages.vernacular: 但造反而家已經完成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但造反現在已經完成。

passages.original: The execution of the traitors this afternoon was the final act.
passages.vernacular: 今日下午對叛徒嘅處決係最後嘅行動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天下午對叛徒的處決是最後的行動。

passages.original: The enemy both external and internal has been defeated.
passages.vernacular: 內外敵人都已被打敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 內外敵人都已被打敗。

passages.original: In ‘Beasts of England’ we expressed our longing for a better society in days to come.
passages.vernacular: 喺《英格蘭之獸》中,我哋表達咗對未來更好社會嘅嚮往。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在《英格蘭之獸》中,我們表達了對未來更好社會的嚮往。

passages.original: But that society has now been established.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰個社會而家已經建立。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那個社會現在已經建立。

passages.original: Clearly this song has no longer any purpose.”
passages.vernacular: 顯然呢首歌唔再有任何目的。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 顯然這首歌不再有任何目的。」

passages.original: Frightened though they were, some of the animals might possibly have protested, but at this moment the sheep set up their usual bleating of “Four legs good, two legs bad,” which went on for several minutes and put an end to the discussion.
passages.vernacular: 儘管害怕,啲動物或者可能提出抗議,但此刻羊發出佢哋通常嘅咩咩叫「四條腿好,兩條腿壞」,持續咗好幾分鐘,結束咗討論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管害怕,一些動物也許可能提出抗議,但此刻羊發出它們通常的咩咩叫「四條腿好,兩條腿壞」,持續了好幾分鐘,結束了討論。

passages.original: So ‘Beasts of England’ was heard no more.
passages.vernacular: 於是《英格蘭之獸》唔再被聽到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是《英格蘭之獸》不再被聽到。

passages.original: In its place Minimus, the poet, had composed another song which began:
passages.vernacular: 取而代之嘅係,詩人米尼默斯作咗另一首歌,開頭係:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 取而代之的是,詩人米尼默斯作了另一首歌,開頭是:

passages.original: Animal Farm, Animal Farm, Never through me shalt thou come to harm!
passages.vernacular: 動物農莊,動物農莊,絕唔會因我而受傷!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物農莊,動物農莊,絕不會因我而受傷!

passages.original: and this was sung every Sunday morning after the hoisting of the flag.
passages.vernacular: 呢首歌每個星期天早晨升旗之後唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這首歌每個星期天早晨升旗之後唱。

passages.original: But somehow neither the words nor the tune ever seemed to the animals to come up to ‘Beasts of England’.
passages.vernacular: 但唔知點嘅,歌詞同曲調喺動物哋睇來都比不上《英格蘭之獸》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但不知怎麼的,歌詞和曲調在動物們看來都比不上《英格蘭之獸》。

chapters.title: Chapter VIII 第八章:風車的毀滅

passages.original: A few days later, when the terror caused by the executions had died down, some of the animals remembered--or thought they remembered--that the Sixth Commandment decreed “No animal shall kill any other animal.”
passages.vernacular: 幾天後,處決引起嘅恐怖平息下嚟,啲動物記得——或者認為記得——第六條誡命規定「任何動物唔得殺死任何其他動物」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾天後,處決引起的恐怖平息下來,一些動物記得——或者認為記得——第六條誡命規定「任何動物不得殺死任何其他動物」。

passages.original: And though no one cared to mention it in the hearing of the pigs or the dogs, it was felt that the killings which had taken place did not square with this.
passages.vernacular: 雖然冇人願意喺豬或狗聽得見嘅地方提到佢,但大家覺得已經發生嘅殺戮同此不符。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然沒有人願意在豬或狗聽得見的地方提到它,但大家覺得已經發生的殺戮與此不符。

passages.original: Clover asked Benjamin to read her the Sixth Commandment, and when Benjamin, as usual, said that he refused to meddle in such matters, she fetched Muriel.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草請班傑明畀佢讀第六條誡命,班傑明像往常一樣講佢拒絕干預呢類事情,佢就去叫咗繆麗兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草請班傑明給她讀第六條誡命,班傑明像往常一樣說他拒絕干預這類事情,她就去叫了繆麗兒。

passages.original: Muriel read the Commandment for her.
passages.vernacular: 繆麗兒畀佢讀咗誡命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繆麗兒給她讀了誡命。

passages.original: It ran: “No animal shall kill any other animal WITHOUT CAUSE.”
passages.vernacular: 佢係咁樣嘅:「任何動物唔得無緣無故殺死任何其他動物。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是這樣的:「任何動物不得無緣無故殺死任何其他動物。」

passages.original: Somehow or other, the last two words had slipped out of the animals’ memory.
passages.vernacular: 唔知怎嘅,最後四個字已從動物哋嘅記憶中溜走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知怎的,最後四個字已從動物們的記憶中溜走了。

passages.original: But they saw now that the Commandment had not been violated; for clearly there was good reason for killing the traitors who had leagued themselves with Snowball.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋而家睇到,誡命並冇被違反;因為顯然有充分理由殺死嗰啲同雪球勾結嘅叛徒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它們現在看到,誡命並沒有被違反;因為顯然有充分理由殺死那些與雪球勾結的叛徒。

passages.original: Throughout the year the animals worked even harder than they had worked in the previous year.
passages.vernacular: 整年裡,動物哋比前一年工作得更努力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整年裡,動物們比前一年工作得更努力。

passages.original: To rebuild the windmill, with walls twice as thick as before, and to finish it by the appointed date, together with the regular work of the farm, was a tremendous labour.
passages.vernacular: 重建風車,牆比以前厚一倍,並喺規定日期前完成佢,連同農場嘅日常工作,係一項巨大嘅勞役。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 重建風車,牆比以前厚一倍,並在規定日期前完成它,連同農場的日常工作,是一項巨大的勞役。

passages.original: There were times when it seemed to the animals that they worked longer hours and fed no better than they had done in Jones’s day.
passages.vernacular: 有時動物哋覺得,佢哋工作嘅時間更長,食得卻不比瓊斯時代好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時動物們覺得,它們工作的時間更長,吃得卻不比瓊斯時代好。

passages.original: On Sunday mornings Squealer, holding down a long strip of paper with his trotter, would read out to them lists of figures proving that the production of every class of foodstuff had increased by two hundred per cent, three hundred per cent, or five hundred per cent, as the case might be.
passages.vernacular: 星期天早晨,尖嗓子用蹄子按住一長條紙,畀佢哋讀出一串串數字,證明各類食品嘅產量已增加咗百分之二百、百分之三百或百分之五百,視情況而定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期天早晨,尖嗓子用蹄子按住一長條紙,給它們讀出一串串數字,證明各類食品的產量已增加了百分之二百、百分之三百或百分之五百,視情況而定。

passages.original: The animals saw no reason to disbelieve him, especially as they could no longer remember very clearly what conditions had been like before the Rebellion.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋睇不出有理由不相信佢,尤其係佢哋已經唔能夠好清楚地記得造反前嘅情況係乜嘢樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們看不出有理由不相信他,尤其是它們已經不能很清楚地記得造反前的情況是什麼樣了。

passages.original: All the same, there were days when they felt that they would sooner have had less figures and more food.
passages.vernacular: 儘管如此,有些日子佢哋覺得,寧可要少些數字、多些食物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管如此,有些日子它們覺得,寧可要少些數字、多些食物。

passages.original: All orders were now issued through Squealer or one of the other pigs.
passages.vernacular: 所有命令而家都通過尖嗓子或其他豬之一發布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有命令現在都通過尖嗓子或其他豬之一發布。

passages.original: Napoleon himself was not seen in public as often as once in a fortnight.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙本人兩個星期內都難得公開露面一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙本人兩個星期內也難得公開露面一次。

passages.original: When he did appear, he was attended not only by his retinue of dogs but by a black cockerel who marched in front of him and acted as a kind of trumpeter, letting out a loud “cock-a-doodle-doo” before Napoleon spoke.
passages.vernacular: 佢出現時,不僅有佢嘅狗隨從,而且有一隻黑公雞走喺佢前面,充當一種號手,喺拿破崙講話前發出響亮嘅「喔喔喔」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他出現時,不僅有他的狗隨從,而且有一隻黑公雞走在他前面,充當一種號手,在拿破崙說話前發出響亮的「喔喔喔」。

passages.original: Even in the farmhouse, it was said, Napoleon inhabited separate apartments from the others.
passages.vernacular: 據講,即使喺農舍裡,拿破崙都住喺同其他豬分開嘅套房裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據說,即使在農舍裡,拿破崙也住在同其他豬分開的套房裡。

passages.original: He took his meals alone, with two dogs to wait upon him, and always ate from the Crown Derby dinner service which had been in the glass cupboard in the drawing-room.
passages.vernacular: 佢獨自用餐,由兩條狗伺候,總是用原來放喺客廳玻璃櫥裡嘅皇冠德比餐具食飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他獨自用餐,由兩條狗伺候,總是用原來放在客廳玻璃櫥裡的皇冠德比餐具吃飯。

passages.original: It was also announced that the gun would be fired every year on Napoleon’s birthday, as well as on the other two anniversaries.
passages.vernacular: 仲宣布,除咗另外兩個紀念日,每年喺拿破崙嘅生日都要鳴槍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還宣布,除了另外兩個紀念日,每年在拿破崙的生日也要鳴槍。

passages.original: Napoleon was now never spoken of simply as “Napoleon.”
