passages.vernacular: 而家永遠唔再簡單地講「拿破崙」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在永遠不再簡單地說「拿破崙」。

passages.original: He was always referred to in formal style as “our Leader, Comrade Napoleon,” and this pigs liked to invent for him such titles as Father of All Animals, Terror of Mankind, Protector of the Sheep-fold, Ducklings’ Friend, and the like.
passages.vernacular: 總是以正式風格稱佢為「我哋嘅領袖,拿破崙同志」,豬哋鍾意為佢發明咁樣嘅頭銜,如所有動物之父、人類嘅恐怖、羊群嘅保護者、小鴨嘅朋友,同類似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總是以正式風格稱他為「我們的領袖,拿破崙同志」,豬們喜歡為他發明這樣的頭銜,如所有動物之父、人類的恐怖、羊群的保護者、小鴨的朋友,和類似的。

passages.original: In his speeches, Squealer would talk with the tears rolling down his cheeks of Napoleon’s wisdom the goodness of his heart, and the deep love he bore to all animals everywhere, even and especially the unhappy animals who still lived in ignorance and slavery on other farms.
passages.vernacular: 喺演講中,尖嗓子會淚水順住臉頰流下地談論拿破崙嘅智慧、佢嘅好心腸,同佢對各處所有動物深沉嘅愛,甚至特別係對嗰啲喺其他農場仍生活喺無知同奴役中嘅不幸動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在演講中,尖嗓子會淚水順著臉頰流下地談論拿破崙的智慧、他的好心腸,和他對各處所有動物深沉的愛,甚至特別是對那些在其他農場仍生活在無知和奴役中的不幸動物。

passages.original: It had become usual to give Napoleon the credit for every successful achievement and every stroke of good fortune.
passages.vernacular: 把每項成功嘅成就同每次好運都歸功於拿破崙,已成咗習慣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把每項成功的成就和每次好運都歸功於拿破崙,已成了習慣。

passages.original: You would often hear one hen remark to another, “Under the guidance of our Leader, Comrade Napoleon, I have laid five eggs in six days”; or two cows, enjoying a drink at the pool, would exclaim, “Thanks to the leadership of Comrade Napoleon, how excellent this water tastes!”
passages.vernacular: 你常會聽到一隻母雞對另一隻講:「喺我哋嘅領袖拿破崙同志嘅指引下,我六天下咗五個蛋」;或者兩頭母牛喺池邊飲水時喊道:「多虧拿破崙同志嘅領導,呢水嚐起嚟幾咁棒!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你常會聽到一隻母雞對另一隻說:「在我們的領袖拿破崙同志的指引下,我六天下了五個蛋」;或者兩頭母牛在池邊喝水時喊道:「多虧拿破崙同志的領導,這水嚐起來多麼棒!」

passages.original: The general feeling on the farm was well expressed in a poem entitled Comrade Napoleon, which was composed by Minimus and which ran as follows:
passages.vernacular: 農場上嘅普遍感情,好好地表達喺一首名為《拿破崙同志》嘅詩中,佢由米尼默斯所作,內容如下:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場上的普遍感情,很好地表達在一首名為《拿破崙同志》的詩中,它由米尼默斯所作,內容如下:

passages.original: Friend of fatherless!
passages.vernacular: 無父者之友!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無父者之友!

passages.original: Fountain of happiness!
passages.vernacular: 幸福之源泉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸福之源泉!

passages.original: Lord of the swill-bucket!
passages.vernacular: 泔水桶之主!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 泔水桶之主!

passages.original: Oh, how my soul is on Fire when I gaze at thy Calm and commanding eye, Like the sun in the sky, Comrade Napoleon!
passages.vernacular: 哦,當我注視你,平靜而威嚴嘅目光,如天空中嘅太陽,拿破崙同志,我嘅靈魂係幾咁火熱!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,當我注視你,平靜而威嚴的目光,如天空中的太陽,拿破崙同志,我的靈魂是多麼火熱!

passages.original: Thou are the giver of All that thy creatures love, Full belly twice a day, clean straw to roll upon; Every beast great or small Sleeps at peace in his stall, Thou watchest over all, Comrade Napoleon!
passages.vernacular: 你係賜予者,賜予你嘅造物所愛嘅一切,一日兩次飽肚子,乾淨稻草供打滾;每個野獸,無論大小,喺馬廄裡安瞓,你睇護住一切,拿破崙同志!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是賜予者,賜予你的造物所愛的一切,一日兩次飽肚子,乾淨稻草供打滾;每個野獸,無論大小,在馬廄裡安睡,你看護著一切,拿破崙同志!

passages.original: Had I a sucking-pig, Ere he had grown as big Even as a pint bottle or as a rolling-pin, He should have learned to be Faithful and true to thee, Yes, his first squeak should be “Comrade Napoleon!”
passages.vernacular: 如果我有一頭乳豬,喺佢長大到邊怕像一品脫瓶子或擀麵棍咁大以前,佢就應學會忠誠地對你,係嘅,佢嘅第一聲尖叫應該係「拿破崙同志!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我有一頭乳豬,在他長大到哪怕像一品脫瓶子或擀麵棍那麼大以前,他就應學會忠誠地對你,是的,他的第一聲尖叫應該是「拿破崙同志!」

passages.original: Napoleon approved of this poem and caused it to be inscribed on the wall of the big barn, at the opposite end from the Seven Commandments.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙讚許呢首詩,並下令把佢刻喺大穀倉嘅牆上,喺七誡嘅對面一端。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙讚許這首詩,並下令把它刻在大穀倉的牆上,在七誡的對面一端。

passages.original: It was surmounted by a portrait of Napoleon, in profile, executed by Squealer in white paint.
passages.vernacular: 上方有一幅拿破崙嘅側面像,由尖嗓子用白漆畫成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上方有一幅拿破崙的側面像,由尖嗓子用白漆畫成。

passages.original: Meanwhile, through the agency of Whymper, Napoleon was engaged in complicated negotiations with Frederick and Pilkington.
passages.vernacular: 同時,通過溫珀嘅中介,拿破崙正同弗雷德里克同皮爾金頓進行複雜嘅談判。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時,通過溫珀的中介,拿破崙正與弗雷德里克和皮爾金頓進行複雜的談判。

passages.original: The pile of timber was still unsold.
passages.vernacular: 嗰堆木材仍未賣掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那堆木材仍未賣掉。

passages.original: Of the two, Frederick was the more anxious to get hold of it, but he would not offer a reasonable price.
passages.vernacular: 兩人中,弗雷德里克更急於得到佢,但佢唔肯出合理嘅價錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩人中,弗雷德里克更急於得到它,但他不肯出合理的價錢。

passages.original: At the same time there were renewed rumours that Frederick and his men were plotting to attack Animal Farm and to destroy the windmill, the building of which had aroused furious jealousy in him.
passages.vernacular: 同時又有新嘅傳聞,講弗雷德里克同佢嘅人喺密謀攻擊動物農莊並摧毀風車,風車嘅建造激起咗佢猛烈嘅嫉妒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時又有新的傳聞,說弗雷德里克和他的人在密謀攻擊動物農莊並摧毀風車,風車的建造激起了他猛烈的嫉妒。

passages.original: Snowball was known to be still skulking on Pinchfield Farm.
passages.vernacular: 眾所周知,雪球仍鬼鬼祟祟地躲喺平奇菲爾德農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 眾所周知,雪球仍鬼鬼祟祟地躲在平奇菲爾德農場。

passages.original: In the middle of the summer the animals were alarmed to hear that three hens had come forward and confessed that, inspired by Snowball, they had entered into a plot to murder Napoleon.
passages.vernacular: 仲夏時,動物哋驚恐地聽講,三隻母雞站出嚟招供,講佢哋受雪球啟發,參與咗謀殺拿破崙嘅陰謀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仲夏時,動物們驚恐地聽說,三隻母雞站出來招供,說她們受雪球啟發,參與了謀殺拿破崙的陰謀。

passages.original: They were executed immediately, and fresh precautions for Napoleon’s safety were taken.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋被即刻處決喇,並採取咗保護拿破崙安全嘅新預防措施。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們被立刻處決了,並採取了保護拿破崙安全的新預防措施。

passages.original: Four dogs guarded his bed at night, one at each corner, and a young pig named Pinkeye was given the task of tasting all his food before he ate it, lest it should be poisoned.
passages.vernacular: 夜裡四條狗守護佢嘅床,每個角落一條,一頭名叫粉眼嘅年輕豬,被賦予喺佢食飯前先嚐所有食物嘅任務,以防被下毒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜裡四條狗守護他的床,每個角落一條,一頭名叫粉眼的年輕豬,被賦予在他吃飯前先嚐所有食物的任務,以防被下毒。

passages.original: At about the same time it was given out that Napoleon had arranged to sell the pile of timber to Mr. Pilkington; he was also going to enter into a regular agreement for the exchange of certain products between Animal Farm and Foxwood.
passages.vernacular: 大約同時宣布,拿破崙已安排把嗰堆木材賣畀皮爾金頓先生;佢仲將就動物農莊同狐林之間交換某些產品訂立一項正式協議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約同時宣布,拿破崙已安排把那堆木材賣給皮爾金頓先生;他還將就動物農莊與狐林之間交換某些產品訂立一項正式協議。

passages.original: The relations between Napoleon and Pilkington, though they were only conducted through Whymper, were now almost friendly.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙同皮爾金頓之間嘅關係,雖然只係通過溫珀進行,而家已幾乎友好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙與皮爾金頓之間的關係,雖然只是通過溫珀進行,現在已幾乎友好。

passages.original: The animals distrusted Pilkington, as a human being, but greatly preferred him to Frederick, whom they both feared and hated.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋不信任皮爾金頓,因為佢係人類,但遠比弗雷德里克更鍾意佢,佢哋既怕又恨弗雷德里克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們不信任皮爾金頓,因為他是人類,但遠比弗雷德里克更喜歡他,它們既怕又恨弗雷德里克。

passages.original: As the summer wore on, and the windmill neared completion, the rumours of an impending treacherous attack grew stronger and stronger.
passages.vernacular: 隨住夏天嘅推移,風車接近完成,關於即將到來嘅背信攻擊嘅傳聞越嚟越強烈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨著夏天的推移,風車接近完成,關於即將到來的背信攻擊的傳聞越來越強烈。

passages.original: Frederick, it was said, intended to bring against them twenty men all armed with guns, and he had already bribed the magistrates and police, so that if he could once get hold of the title-deeds of Animal Farm they would ask no questions.
passages.vernacular: 據講,弗雷德里克打算帶二十個全副武裝嘅人嚟對付佢哋,佢已經收買咗法官同警察,所以只要佢一弄到動物農莊嘅地契,佢哋就唔會過問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據說,弗雷德里克打算帶二十個全副武裝的人來對付它們,他已經收買了法官和警察,所以只要他一弄到動物農莊的地契,他們就不會過問。

passages.original: Moreover, terrible stories were leaking out from Pinchfield about the cruelties that Frederick practised upon his animals.
passages.vernacular: 此外,從平奇菲爾德洩露出關於弗雷德里克對佢嘅動物所施殘酷行為嘅可怕故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,從平奇菲爾德洩露出關於弗雷德里克對他的動物所施殘酷行為的可怕故事。

passages.original: He had flogged an old horse to death, he starved his cows, he had killed a dog by throwing it into the furnace, he amused himself in the evenings by making cocks fight with splinters of razor-blade tied to their spurs.
passages.vernacular: 佢把一匹老馬鞭打致死,佢讓母牛挨餓,佢把一條狗扔進爐裡殺死,佢晚上以讓公雞喺腿距上綁住刀片碎片打鬥來自娛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把一匹老馬鞭打致死,他讓母牛挨餓,他把一條狗扔進爐裡殺死,他晚上以讓公雞在腿距上綁著刀片碎片打鬥來自娛。

passages.original: The animals’ blood boiled with rage when they heard of these things being done to their comrades, and sometimes they clamoured to be allowed to go out in a body and attack Pinchfield Farm, drive out the humans, and set the animals free.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋聽到呢啲事發生喺佢哋嘅同志身上,血因憤怒而沸騰,有時佢哋叫喊住要求被允許集體出去攻擊平奇菲爾德農場,趕走人類,解放動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們聽到這些事發生在它們的同志身上,血因憤怒而沸騰,有時它們叫喊著要求被允許集體出去攻擊平奇菲爾德農場,趕走人類,解放動物。

passages.original: But Squealer counselled them to avoid rash actions and trust in Comrade Napoleon’s strategy.
passages.vernacular: 但尖嗓子勸告佢哋避免魯莽行動,相信拿破崙同志嘅戰略。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但尖嗓子勸告它們避免魯莽行動,相信拿破崙同志的戰略。

passages.original: Nevertheless, feeling against Frederick continued to run high.
passages.vernacular: 儘管如此,對弗雷德里克嘅情緒仍然高漲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管如此,對弗雷德里克的情緒仍然高漲。

passages.original: One Sunday morning Napoleon appeared in the barn and explained that he had never at any time contemplated selling the pile of timber to Frederick; he considered it beneath his dignity, he said, to have dealings with scoundrels of that description.
passages.vernacular: 一個星期天早晨,拿破崙出而家穀倉,解釋講佢從未喺任何時候考慮過把嗰堆木材賣畀弗雷德里克;佢講,佢認為同嗰種惡棍打交道有失佢嘅尊嚴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個星期天早晨,拿破崙出現在穀倉,解釋說他從未在任何時候考慮過把那堆木材賣給弗雷德里克;他說,他認為與那種惡棍打交道有失他的尊嚴。

passages.original: The pigeons who were still sent out to spread tidings of the Rebellion were forbidden to set foot anywhere on Foxwood, and were also ordered to drop their former slogan of “Death to Humanity” in favour of “Death to Frederick.”
passages.vernacular: 仍被派出去傳播造反消息嘅鴿子被禁止踏足狐林嘅任何地方,並被命令放棄佢哋以前嘅口號「人類去死」,改為「弗雷德里克去死」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仍被派出去傳播造反消息的鴿子被禁止踏足狐林的任何地方,並被命令放棄它們以前的口號「人類去死」,改為「弗雷德里克去死」。

passages.original: In the late summer yet another of Snowball’s machinations was laid bare.
passages.vernacular: 夏末,雪球嘅另一個陰謀被揭露。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏末,雪球的另一個陰謀被揭露。

passages.original: The wheat crop was full of weeds, and it was discovered that on one of his nocturnal visits Snowball had mixed weed seeds with the seed corn.
passages.vernacular: 麥田裡長滿雜草,發現雪球喺一次夜間嚟訪時把雜草種子混進咗種子玉米。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥田裡長滿雜草,發現雪球在一次夜間來訪時把雜草種子混進了種子玉米。

passages.original: A gander who had been privy to the plot had confessed his guilt to Squealer and immediately committed suicide by swallowing deadly nightshade berries.
passages.vernacular: 一隻知道此陰謀嘅公鵝向尖嗓子承認咗佢嘅罪行,並即刻吞食致命嘅顛茄漿果自殺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻知道此陰謀的公鵝向尖嗓子承認了他的罪行,並立刻吞食致命的顛茄漿果自殺。

passages.original: The animals now also learned that Snowball had never--as many of them had believed hitherto--received the order of “Animal Hero, First Class.”
passages.vernacular: 動物哋而家仲得知,雪球從未——如佢哋中許多迄今所信——得到過「一級動物英雄」勳章。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們現在還得知,雪球從未——如它們中許多迄今所信——得到過「一級動物英雄」勳章。

passages.original: This was merely a legend which had been spread some time after the Battle of the Cowshed by Snowball himself.
passages.vernacular: 呢只係牛棚之戰後不久由雪球自己散佈嘅一個傳講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這只是牛棚之戰後不久由雪球自己散佈的一個傳說。

passages.original: So far from being decorated, he had been censured for showing cowardice in the battle.
passages.vernacular: 佢不但冇被授勳,反而因喺戰鬥中表現怯懦而受到譴責。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不但沒有被授勳,反而因在戰鬥中表現怯懦而受到譴責。

passages.original: Once again some of the animals heard this with a certain bewilderment, but Squealer was soon able to convince them that their memories had been at fault.
passages.vernacular: 又一次,啲動物帶住某種困惑聽到咗呢個,但尖嗓子好快就講服佢哋,佢哋嘅記憶有誤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一次,一些動物帶著某種困惑聽到了這個,但尖嗓子很快就說服它們,它們的記憶有誤。

passages.original: In the autumn, by a tremendous, exhausting effort--for the harvest had to be gathered at almost the same time--the windmill was finished.
passages.vernacular: 秋天,通過巨大而令人筋疲力盡嘅努力——因為收割幾乎喺同一時間必須進行——風車建成喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 秋天,通過巨大而令人筋疲力盡的努力——因為收割幾乎在同一時間必須進行——風車建成了。

passages.original: The machinery had still to be installed, and Whymper was negotiating the purchase of it, but the structure was completed.
passages.vernacular: 機器仲要安裝,溫珀正在洽談購買,但結構已經完成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 機器還要安裝,溫珀正在洽談購買,但結構已經完成。

passages.original: In the teeth of every difficulty, in spite of inexperience, of primitive implements, of bad luck and of Snowball’s treachery, the work had been finished punctually to the very day!
passages.vernacular: 面對各種困難,不顧經驗不足、工具原始、運氣不好,同雪球嘅背叛,工作竟然準確地按日期完成喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 面對各種困難,不顧經驗不足、工具原始、運氣不好,和雪球的背叛,工作竟然準確地按日期完成了!

passages.original: Tired out but proud, the animals walked round and round their masterpiece, which appeared even more beautiful in their eyes than when it had been built the first time.
passages.vernacular: 疲憊但自豪,動物哋一圈又一圈地繞住佢哋嘅傑作走,喺佢哋眼中佢顯得比第一次建成時更美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 疲憊但自豪,動物們一圈又一圈地繞著它們的傑作走,在它們眼中它顯得比第一次建成時更美。

passages.original: Moreover, the walls were twice as thick as before.
passages.vernacular: 而且,牆比以前厚一倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,牆比以前厚一倍。

passages.original: Nothing short of explosives would lay them low this time!
passages.vernacular: 呢一次,除咗炸藥,乜嘢都唔能夠把佢哋推倒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一次,除了炸藥,什麼也不能把它們推倒!

passages.original: And when they thought of how they had laboured, what discouragements they had overcome, and the enormous difference that would be made in their lives when the sails were turning and the dynamos running--when they thought of all this, their tiredness forsook them and they gambolled round and round the windmill, uttering cries of triumph.
passages.vernacular: 當佢哋想到佢哋係點樣辛勤勞動,克服咗乜嘢樣嘅挫折,風帆轉動、發電機運轉時,佢哋嘅生活將發生多大嘅變化——想到呢一切,佢哋嘅疲倦消失喇,繞住風車蹦跳,發出勝利嘅叫喊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當它們想到它們是怎樣辛勤勞動,克服了什麼樣的挫折,風帆轉動、發電機運轉時,它們的生活將發生多大的變化——想到這一切,它們的疲倦消失了,繞著風車蹦跳,發出勝利的叫喊。

passages.original: Napoleon himself, attended by his dogs and his cockerel, came down to inspect the completed work; he personally congratulated the animals on their achievement, and announced that the mill would be named Napoleon Mill.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙本人,喺佢嘅狗同公雞嘅陪伴下,下嚟視察完工嘅作品;佢親自祝賀動物哋嘅成就,並宣布磨坊將被命名為拿破崙磨坊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙本人,在他的狗和公雞的陪伴下,下來視察完工的作品;他親自祝賀動物們的成就,並宣布磨坊將被命名為拿破崙磨坊。

passages.original: Two days later the animals were called together for a special meeting in the barn.
passages.vernacular: 兩天後,動物哋被召集到穀倉開特別會議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩天後,動物們被召集到穀倉開特別會議。

passages.original: They were struck dumb with surprise when Napoleon announced that he had sold the pile of timber to Frederick.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙宣布佢已把嗰堆木材賣畀咗弗雷德里克,佢哋驚訝得啞口無言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙宣布他已把那堆木材賣給了弗雷德里克,它們驚訝得啞口無言。

passages.original: Tomorrow Frederick’s wagons would arrive and begin carting it away.
passages.vernacular: 聽日弗雷德里克嘅貨車將到達,開始把佢運走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天弗雷德里克的貨車將到達,開始把它運走。

passages.original: Throughout the whole period of his seeming friendship with Pilkington, Napoleon had really been in secret agreement with Frederick.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢同皮爾金頓睇似友好嘅整個時期,拿破崙實際上一直同弗雷德里克有秘密協議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他與皮爾金頓看似友好的整個時期,拿破崙實際上一直與弗雷德里克有秘密協議。

passages.original: All relations with Foxwood had been broken off; insulting messages had been sent to Pilkington.
passages.vernacular: 同狐林嘅所有關係都已斷絕;侮辱性嘅信息已送畀皮爾金頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 與狐林的所有關係都已斷絕;侮辱性的信息已送給皮爾金頓。

passages.original: The pigeons had been told to avoid Pinchfield Farm and to alter their slogan from “Death to Frederick” to “Death to Pilkington.”
passages.vernacular: 鴿子哋被告知要避開平奇菲爾德農場,並把口號從「弗雷德里克去死」改為「皮爾金頓去死」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鴿子們被告知要避開平奇菲爾德農場,並把口號從「弗雷德里克去死」改為「皮爾金頓去死」。

passages.original: At the same time Napoleon assured the animals that the stories of an impending attack on Animal Farm were completely untrue, and that the tales about Frederick’s cruelty to his own animals had been greatly exaggerated.
passages.vernacular: 同時,拿破崙向動物哋保證,關於即將攻擊動物農莊嘅故事完全不真實,關於弗雷德里克對佢自己動物殘酷嘅故事被大大誇大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時,拿破崙向動物們保證,關於即將攻擊動物農莊的故事完全不真實,關於弗雷德里克對他自己動物殘酷的故事被大大誇大了。

passages.original: All these rumours had probably originated with Snowball and his agents.
passages.vernacular: 所有呢啲傳聞好可能係起源於雪球同佢嘅特工。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有這些傳聞很可能是起源於雪球和他的特工。

passages.original: It now appeared that Snowball was not, after all, hiding on Pinchfield Farm, and in fact had never been there in his life: he was living--in considerable luxury, so it was said--at Foxwood, and had in reality been a pensioner of Pilkington for years past.
passages.vernacular: 而家睇來,雪球畢竟冇躲喺平奇菲爾德農場,事實上佢一生中從冇到過嗰度:佢住喺狐林——據講生活相當奢華,而且實際上多年嚟一直係皮爾金頓嘅受養人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在看來,雪球畢竟沒有躲在平奇菲爾德農場,事實上他一生中從沒到過那裡:他住在狐林——據說生活相當奢華,而且實際上多年來一直是皮爾金頓的受養人。

passages.original: The pigs were in ecstasies over Napoleon’s cunning.
passages.vernacular: 豬哋為拿破崙嘅狡猾欣喜若狂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬們為拿破崙的狡猾欣喜若狂。

passages.original: By seeming to be friendly with Pilkington he had forced Frederick to raise his price by twelve pounds.
passages.vernacular: 通過假裝同皮爾金頓友好,佢迫使弗雷德里克把價錢提高咗十二鎊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 通過假裝與皮爾金頓友好,他迫使弗雷德里克把價錢提高了十二鎊。

passages.original: But the superior quality of Napoleon’s mind, said Squealer, was shown in the fact that he trusted nobody, not even Frederick.
passages.vernacular: 但尖嗓子講,拿破崙頭腦嘅卓越體而家呢個事實中:佢不信任任何人,甚至不信任弗雷德里克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但尖嗓子說,拿破崙頭腦的卓越體現在這個事實中:他不信任任何人,甚至不信任弗雷德里克。

passages.original: Frederick had wanted to pay for the timber with something called a cheque, which, it seemed, was a piece of paper with a promise to pay written upon it.
passages.vernacular: 弗雷德里克想用一種叫做支票嘅嘢支付木材,嗰似乎係一張寫住支付承諾嘅紙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗雷德里克想用一種叫做支票的東西支付木材,那似乎是一張寫著支付承諾的紙。

passages.original: But Napoleon was too clever for him.
passages.vernacular: 但拿破崙太聰明,佢騙不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但拿破崙太聰明,他騙不了。

passages.original: He had demanded payment in real five-pound notes, which were to be handed over before the timber was removed.
passages.vernacular: 佢要求用真正嘅五鎊鈔票支付,喺木材搬走之前交出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他要求用真正的五鎊鈔票支付,在木材搬走之前交出來。

passages.original: Already Frederick had paid up; and the sum he had paid was just enough to buy the machinery for the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 弗雷德里克已經付咗錢;佢付嘅數額剛好夠買風車嘅機器。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗雷德里克已經付了錢;他付的數額剛好夠買風車的機器。

passages.original: Meanwhile the timber was being carted away at high speed.
passages.vernacular: 同時木材正在被高速運走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時木材正在被高速運走。

passages.original: When it was all gone, another special meeting was held in the barn for the animals to inspect Frederick’s bank-notes.
passages.vernacular: 全部運走後,喺穀倉裡又舉行咗一次特別會議,讓動物哋檢視弗雷德里克嘅鈔票。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全部運走後,在穀倉裡又舉行了一次特別會議,讓動物們檢視弗雷德里克的鈔票。

passages.original: Smiling beatifically, and wearing both his decorations, Napoleon reposed on a bed of straw on the platform, with the money at his side, neatly piled on a china dish from the farmhouse kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙喜氣洋洋地微笑住,戴住佢嘅兩枚勳章,躺喺高台上嘅一張稻草床上,錢喺佢身旁,整齊地堆喺從農舍廚房攞嚟嘅一個瓷盤上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙喜氣洋洋地微笑著,戴著他的兩枚勳章,躺在高台上的一張稻草床上,錢在他身旁,整齊地堆在從農舍廚房拿來的一個瓷盤上。

passages.original: The animals filed slowly past, and each gazed his fill.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋慢慢排隊走過,每個都睇夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們慢慢排隊走過,每個都看夠了。

passages.original: And Boxer put out his nose to sniff at the bank-notes, and the flimsy white things stirred and rustled in his breath.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手伸出鼻子去聞嗰啲鈔票,嗰啲單薄嘅白色嘢喺佢嘅呼吸中顫動、沙沙作響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手伸出鼻子去聞那些鈔票,那些單薄的白色東西在他的呼吸中顫動、沙沙作響。

passages.original: Three days later there was a terrible hullabaloo.
passages.vernacular: 三天後,發生咗一場可怕嘅喧鬧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三天後,發生了一場可怕的喧鬧。

passages.original: Whymper, his face deadly pale, came racing up the path on his bicycle, flung it down in the yard and rushed straight into the farmhouse.
passages.vernacular: 溫珀,臉色死一般蒼白,騎住自行車沿小路飛馳而嚟,把佢扔喺院子裡,直衝進農舍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫珀,臉色死一般蒼白,騎著自行車沿小路飛馳而來,把它扔在院子裡,直衝進農舍。

passages.original: The next moment a choking roar of rage sounded from Napoleon’s apartments.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻,從拿破崙嘅套房裡傳嚟一聲令人窒息嘅憤怒吼聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻,從拿破崙的套房裡傳來一聲令人窒息的憤怒吼聲。

passages.original: The news of what had happened sped round the farm like wildfire.
passages.vernacular: 所發生之事嘅消息像野火一樣傳遍咗農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所發生之事的消息像野火一樣傳遍了農場。

passages.original: The banknotes were forgeries!
passages.vernacular: 鈔票係偽造嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鈔票是偽造的!

passages.original: Frederick had got the timber for nothing!
passages.vernacular: 弗雷德里克白白得到咗木材!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗雷德里克白白得到了木材!

passages.original: Napoleon called the animals together immediately and in a terrible voice pronounced the death sentence upon Frederick.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙即刻召集動物哋,以可怕嘅聲音對弗雷德里克宣判咗死刑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙立刻召集動物們,以可怕的聲音對弗雷德里克宣判了死刑。

passages.original: When captured, he said, Frederick should be boiled alive.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,抓到弗雷德里克時,要把佢活活煮死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,抓到弗雷德里克時,要把他活活煮死。

passages.original: At the same time he warned them that after this treacherous deed the worst was to be expected.
passages.vernacular: 同時佢警告佢哋,呢一背信嘅行為之後,將會有最壞嘅情況。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時他警告它們,這一背信的行為之後,將會有最壞的情況。

passages.original: Frederick and his men might make their long-expected attack at any moment.
passages.vernacular: 弗雷德里克同佢嘅人可能隨時發動佢哋期待已久嘅攻擊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗雷德里克和他的人可能隨時發動他們期待已久的攻擊。

passages.original: Sentinels were placed at all the approaches to the farm.
passages.vernacular: 農場所有通道都布置咗哨兵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場所有通道都布置了哨兵。

passages.original: In addition, four pigeons were sent to Foxwood with a conciliatory message, which it was hoped might re-establish good relations with Pilkington.
passages.vernacular: 此外,四隻鴿子帶住一個和解嘅信息被送往狐林,希望可能同皮爾金頓重建良好關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,四隻鴿子帶著一個和解的信息被送往狐林,希望可能與皮爾金頓重建良好關係。

passages.original: The very next morning the attack came.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨攻擊就嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨攻擊就來了。

passages.original: The animals were at breakfast when the look-outs came racing in with the news that Frederick and his followers had already come through the five-barred gate.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋正在食早餐,呢陣瞭望哨飛奔進嚟報告講,弗雷德里克同佢嘅追隨者已經進咗五柵欄大門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們正在吃早餐,這時瞭望哨飛奔進來報告說,弗雷德里克和他的追隨者已經進了五柵欄大門。

passages.original: Boldly enough the animals sallied forth to meet them, but this time they did not have the easy victory that they had had in the Battle of the Cowshed.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋相當大膽地衝出去迎戰,但呢一次佢哋冇像牛棚之戰中嗰樣輕易取勝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們相當大膽地衝出去迎戰,但這一次它們沒有像牛棚之戰中那樣輕易取勝。

passages.original: There were fifteen men, with half a dozen guns between them, and they opened fire as soon as they got within fifty yards.
passages.vernacular: 有十五個人,共有六七桿槍,佢哋一到五十碼之內就開火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有十五個人,共有六七桿槍,他們一到五十碼之內就開火。

passages.original: The animals could not face the terrible explosions and the stinging pellets, and in spite of the efforts of Napoleon and Boxer to rally them, they were soon driven back.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋無法面對可怕嘅爆炸聲同刺痛嘅彈丸,儘管拿破崙同拳擊手努力集結佢哋,佢哋好快被打退喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們無法面對可怕的爆炸聲和刺痛的彈丸,儘管拿破崙和拳擊手努力集結它們,它們很快被打退了。

passages.original: A number of them were already wounded.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋中已有許多受咗傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們中已有許多受了傷。

passages.original: They took refuge in the farm buildings and peeped cautiously out from chinks and knot-holes.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋躲進農場嘅建築,小心地從縫隙同節孔中窺視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們躲進農場的建築,小心地從縫隙和節孔中窺視。

passages.original: The whole of the big pasture, including the windmill, was in the hands of the enemy.
passages.vernacular: 包括風車在內嘅整個大牧場都喺敵人手中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 包括風車在內的整個大牧場都在敵人手中。

passages.original: For the moment even Napoleon seemed at a loss.
passages.vernacular: 此刻連拿破崙似乎都唔知所措。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此刻連拿破崙似乎也不知所措。

passages.original: He paced up and down without a word, his tail rigid and twitching.
passages.vernacular: 佢一言不發地嚟回踱步,尾巴僵硬而抽動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一言不發地來回踱步,尾巴僵硬而抽動。

passages.original: Wistful glances were sent in the direction of Foxwood.
passages.vernacular: 渴望嘅目光投向狐林嘅方向。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 渴望的目光投向狐林的方向。

passages.original: If Pilkington and his men would help them, the day might yet be won.
passages.vernacular: 如果皮爾金頓同佢嘅人肯幫助佢哋,呢一天或者仲能贏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果皮爾金頓和他的人肯幫助它們,這一天也許還能贏。

passages.original: But at this moment the four pigeons, who had been sent out on the day before, returned, one of them bearing a scrap of paper from Pilkington.
passages.vernacular: 但就喺呢陣,前一天派出嘅四隻鴿子回嚟喇,其中一隻帶住皮爾金頓嘅一張紙條。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但就在這時,前一天派出的四隻鴿子回來了,其中一隻帶著皮爾金頓的一張紙條。

passages.original: On it was pencilled the words: “Serves you right.”
passages.vernacular: 上面用鉛筆寫住:「活該。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面用鉛筆寫著:「活該。」

passages.original: Meanwhile Frederick and his men had halted about the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 同時,弗雷德里克同佢嘅人已喺風車周圍停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時,弗雷德里克和他的人已在風車周圍停下。

passages.original: The animals watched them, and a murmur of dismay went round.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋睇住佢哋,一陣驚慌嘅低語傳開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們看著他們,一陣驚慌的低語傳開。

passages.original: Two of the men had produced a crowbar and a sledge hammer.
passages.vernacular: 其中兩個人攞出咗一根撬棍同一把大錘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中兩個人拿出了一根撬棍和一把大錘。

passages.original: They were going to knock the windmill down.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋要把風車砸倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們要把風車砸倒。

passages.original: “Impossible!” cried Napoleon.
passages.vernacular: 「唔可能!」拿破崙喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不可能!」拿破崙喊道。

passages.original: “We have built the walls far too thick for that.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋把牆建得太厚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們把牆建得太厚了。

passages.original: They could not knock it down in a week.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋一星期都砸不倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們一星期也砸不倒。

passages.original: Courage, comrades!”
passages.vernacular: 勇敢些,同志哋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勇敢些,同志們!」

passages.original: But Benjamin was watching the movements of the men intently.
passages.vernacular: 但班傑明專注地觀察住嗰啲人嘅動作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但班傑明專注地觀察著那些人的動作。

passages.original: The two with the hammer and the crowbar were drilling a hole near the base of the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 嗰兩個攞住錘子同撬棍嘅人,正在風車底部附近鑽一個洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那兩個拿著錘子和撬棍的人,正在風車底部附近鑽一個洞。

passages.original: Slowly, and with an air almost of amusement, Benjamin nodded his long muzzle.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明緩慢地、帶住近乎覺得有趣嘅神氣,點咗點佢嘅長嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明緩慢地、帶著近乎覺得有趣的神氣,點了點他的長嘴。

passages.original: “I thought so,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「我就知道,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就知道,」他說。

passages.original: “Do you not see what they are doing?
passages.vernacular: 「你哋冇睇到佢哋喺做乜嘢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們沒看到他們在做什麼嗎?

passages.original: In another moment they are going to pack blasting powder into that hole.”
passages.vernacular: 過一會兒佢哋就要把炸藥塞進嗰個洞裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過一會兒他們就要把炸藥塞進那個洞裡。」

passages.original: Terrified, the animals waited.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋恐懼地等待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們恐懼地等待。

passages.original: It was impossible now to venture out of the shelter of the buildings.
passages.vernacular: 而家唔可能冒險走出建築物嘅庇護。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在不可能冒險走出建築物的庇護。

passages.original: After a few minutes the men were seen to be running in all directions.
passages.vernacular: 過咗幾分鐘,睇到嗰啲人向四面八方跑開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了幾分鐘,看到那些人向四面八方跑開。

passages.original: Then there was a deafening roar.
passages.vernacular: 然後係震耳欲聾嘅一聲巨響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後是震耳欲聾的一聲巨響。

passages.original: The pigeons swirled into the air, and all the animals, except Napoleon, flung themselves flat on their bellies and hid their faces.
passages.vernacular: 鴿子哋喺空中盤旋,所有動物,除咗拿破崙,都撲倒趴喺地上,蒙住臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鴿子們在空中盤旋,所有動物,除了拿破崙,都撲倒趴在地上,蒙住臉。

passages.original: When they got up again, a huge cloud of black smoke was hanging where the windmill had been.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋重新站起嚟時,一大團黑煙懸喺風車原來嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們重新站起來時,一大團黑煙懸在風車原來的地方。

passages.original: Slowly the breeze drifted it away.
passages.vernacular: 微風慢慢把佢吹散。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 微風慢慢把它吹散。

passages.original: The windmill had ceased to exist!
passages.vernacular: 風車不復存在喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風車不復存在了!

passages.original: At this sight the animals’ courage returned to them.
passages.vernacular: 睇到呢景象,動物哋嘅勇氣回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到這景象,動物們的勇氣回來了。

passages.original: The fear and despair they had felt a moment earlier were drowned in their rage against this vile, contemptible act.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋片刻前感到嘅恐懼同絕望,淹沒喺佢哋對呢個卑鄙可恥行為嘅憤怒中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們片刻前感到的恐懼和絕望,淹沒在它們對這個卑鄙可恥行為的憤怒中。

passages.original: A mighty cry for vengeance went up, and without waiting for further orders they charged forth in a body and made straight for the enemy.
passages.vernacular: 一聲強有力嘅復仇呼喊響起,不等進一步命令,佢哋就集體衝出去,直撲敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一聲強有力的復仇呼喊響起,不等進一步命令,它們就集體衝出去,直撲敵人。

passages.original: This time they did not heed the cruel pellets that swept over them like hail.
passages.vernacular: 呢一次佢哋不顧像冰雹一樣掃過佢哋嘅殘酷彈丸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一次它們不顧像冰雹一樣掃過它們的殘酷彈丸。

passages.original: It was a savage, bitter battle.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一場野蠻而痛苦嘅戰鬥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一場野蠻而痛苦的戰鬥。

passages.original: The men fired again and again, and, when the animals got to close quarters, lashed out with their sticks and their heavy boots.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲人一次又一次開火,動物哋靠近之後,佢哋就用棍子同沉重嘅靴子亂打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些人一次又一次開火,動物們靠近之後,他們就用棍子和沉重的靴子亂打。

passages.original: A cow, three sheep, and two geese were killed, and nearly everyone was wounded.
passages.vernacular: 一頭母牛、三隻羊同兩隻鵝被殺,幾乎每個都受咗傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一頭母牛、三隻羊和兩隻鵝被殺,幾乎每個都受了傷。

passages.original: Even Napoleon, who was directing operations from the rear, had the tip of his tail chipped by a pellet.
passages.vernacular: 連喺後方指揮作戰嘅拿破崙,尾巴尖都被一顆彈丸削掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連在後方指揮作戰的拿破崙,尾巴尖也被一顆彈丸削掉了。

passages.original: But the men did not go unscathed either.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰啲人都冇毫髮無傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那些人也沒有毫髮無傷。

passages.original: Three of them had their heads broken by blows from Boxer’s hoofs; another was gored in the belly by a cow’s horn; another had his trousers nearly torn off by Jessie and Bluebell.
passages.vernacular: 有三個人嘅頭被拳擊手嘅蹄子打破喇;另一個被母牛嘅角頂穿咗肚子;另一個嘅褲子幾乎被潔西同藍鈴撕掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有三個人的頭被拳擊手的蹄子打破了;另一個被母牛的角頂穿了肚子;另一個的褲子幾乎被潔西和藍鈴撕掉。

passages.original: And when the nine dogs of Napoleon’s own bodyguard, whom he had instructed to make a detour under cover of the hedge, suddenly appeared on the men’s flank, baying ferociously, panic overtook them.
passages.vernacular: 當拿破崙自己嘅衛隊嘅九條狗,佢指示佢哋借樹籬掩護繞路,突然出而家嗰啲人嘅側翼,凶猛地吠叫時,恐慌襲上咗佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當拿破崙自己的衛隊的九條狗,他指示它們借樹籬掩護繞路,突然出現在那些人的側翼,凶猛地吠叫時,恐慌襲上了他們。

passages.original: They saw that they were in danger of being surrounded.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋睇出自己有被包圍嘅危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們看出自己有被包圍的危險。

passages.original: Frederick shouted to his men to get out while the going was good, and the next moment the cowardly enemy was running for dear life.
passages.vernacular: 弗雷德里克對佢嘅人大喊,趁仲能走時趕緊撤出,下一刻呢膽怯嘅敵人就拚命地逃跑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗雷德里克對他的人大喊,趁還能走時趕緊撤出,下一刻這膽怯的敵人就拚命地逃跑了。

passages.original: The animals chased them right down to the bottom of the field, and got in some last kicks at them as they forced their way through the thorn hedge.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋一直追到田嘅底部,喺佢哋強行穿過荊棘樹籬時,又向佢哋踢咗最後幾腳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們一直追到田的底部,在他們強行穿過荊棘樹籬時,又向他們踢了最後幾腳。

passages.original: They had won, but they were weary and bleeding.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋贏喇,但疲憊而流血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們贏了,但疲憊而流血。

passages.original: Slowly they began to limp back towards the farm.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋慢慢開始一瘸一拐地走回農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們慢慢開始一瘸一拐地走回農場。

passages.original: The sight of their dead comrades stretched upon the grass moved some of them to tears.
passages.vernacular: 睇到佢哋死去嘅同志躺喺草地上,啲動物感動得流淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到它們死去的同志躺在草地上,一些動物感動得流淚。

passages.original: And for a little while they halted in sorrowful silence at the place where the windmill had once stood.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺風車曾經所在嘅地方,喺悲傷嘅沉默中停咗一小會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們在風車曾經所在的地方,在悲傷的沉默中停了一小會兒。

passages.original: Yes, it was gone; almost the last trace of their labour was gone!
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,佢唔見喇;佢哋勞動嘅幾乎最後啲痕跡唔見喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,它不見了;它們勞動的幾乎最後一點痕跡不見了!

passages.original: Even the foundations were partially destroyed.
passages.vernacular: 連地基都部分被毀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連地基也部分被毀。

passages.original: And in rebuilding it they could not this time, as before, make use of the fallen stones.
passages.vernacular: 呢一次重建時,佢哋唔能夠像以前嗰樣利用倒下嘅石頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一次重建時,它們不能像以前那樣利用倒下的石頭。

passages.original: This time the stones had vanished too.
passages.vernacular: 呢一次石頭都消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一次石頭也消失了。

passages.original: The force of the explosion had flung them to distances of hundreds of yards.
passages.vernacular: 爆炸嘅力量把佢哋拋到咗數百碼遠嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爆炸的力量把它們拋到了數百碼遠的地方。

passages.original: It was as though the windmill had never been.
passages.vernacular: 好像風車從來冇存在過一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像風車從來沒有存在過一樣。

passages.original: As they approached the farm Squealer, who had unaccountably been absent during the fighting, came skipping towards them, whisking his tail and beaming with satisfaction.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋走近農場時,喺戰鬥中唔知為何一直缺席嘅尖嗓子,蹦蹦跳跳地朝佢哋走嚟,甩住尾巴,滿臉得意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們走近農場時,在戰鬥中不知為何一直缺席的尖嗓子,蹦蹦跳跳地朝它們走來,甩著尾巴,滿臉得意。

passages.original: And the animals heard, from the direction of the farm buildings, the solemn booming of a gun.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋聽到,從農場建築嘅方向傳嚟一聲莊嚴嘅炮響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們聽到,從農場建築的方向傳來一聲莊嚴的炮響。

passages.original: “What is that gun firing for?” said Boxer.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰槍點解開火?」拳擊手講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那槍為什麼開火?」拳擊手說。

passages.original: “To celebrate our victory!” cried Squealer.
passages.vernacular: 「慶祝我哋嘅勝利!」尖嗓子喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「慶祝我們的勝利!」尖嗓子喊道。

passages.original: “What victory?” said Boxer.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢勝利?」拳擊手講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼勝利?」拳擊手說。

passages.original: His knees were bleeding, he had lost a shoe and split his hoof, and a dozen pellets had lodged themselves in his hind leg.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅膝蓋喺流血,佢掉咗一隻蹄鐵,蹄子裂開喇,後腿裡嵌住十幾顆彈丸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的膝蓋在流血,他掉了一隻蹄鐵,蹄子裂開了,後腿裡嵌著十幾顆彈丸。

passages.original: “What victory, comrade?
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢勝利,同志?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼勝利,同志?

passages.original: Have we not driven the enemy off our soil--the sacred soil of Animal Farm?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔係把敵人趕出咗我哋嘅土地——動物農莊嘅神聖土地嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不是把敵人趕出了我們的土地——動物農莊的神聖土地嗎?」

passages.original: “But they have destroyed the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 「但佢哋毀咗風車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但他們毀了風車。

passages.original: And we had worked on it for two years!”
passages.vernacular: 而我哋為佢工作咗兩年!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我們為它工作了兩年!」

passages.original: “What matter?
passages.vernacular: 「有乜嘢關係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有什麼關係?

passages.original: We will build another windmill.
passages.vernacular: 我哋會再建一座風車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會再建一座風車。

passages.original: We will build six windmills if we feel like it.
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋願意,我哋會建六座風車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們願意,我們會建六座風車。

passages.original: You do not appreciate, comrade, the mighty thing that we have done.
passages.vernacular: 同志,你不領會我哋所做嘅偉大事情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同志,你不領會我們所做的偉大事情。

passages.original: The enemy was in occupation of this very ground that we stand upon.
passages.vernacular: 敵人佔領咗我哋站住嘅呢片土地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 敵人佔領了我們站著的這片土地。

passages.original: And now--thanks to the leadership of Comrade Napoleon--we have won every inch of it back again!”
passages.vernacular: 而而家——多虧拿破崙同志嘅領導——我哋把佢嘅每一寸都贏回嚟喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而現在——多虧拿破崙同志的領導——我們把它的每一寸都贏回來了!」

passages.original: “Then we have won back what we had before,” said Boxer.
passages.vernacular: 「咁我哋贏回咗我哋以前有嘅,」拳擊手講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼我們贏回了我們以前有的,」拳擊手說。

passages.original: “That is our victory,” said Squealer.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個就係我哋嘅勝利,」尖嗓子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就是我們的勝利,」尖嗓子說。

passages.original: They limped into the yard.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋一瘸一拐地走進院子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們一瘸一拐地走進院子。

passages.original: The pellets under the skin of Boxer’s leg smarted painfully.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手腿皮下嘅彈丸痛得厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手腿皮下的彈丸痛得厲害。

passages.original: He saw ahead of him the heavy labour of rebuilding the windmill from the foundations, and already in imagination he braced himself for the task.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇到前面係從地基重建風車嘅繁重勞動,喺想像中已經為呢個任務繃緊咗身體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看到前面是從地基重建風車的繁重勞動,在想像中已經為這個任務繃緊了身體。

passages.original: But for the first time it occurred to him that he was eleven years old and that perhaps his great muscles were not quite what they had once been.
passages.vernacular: 但佢第一次想到,佢已經十一歲喇,或者佢強大嘅肌肉已不完全像以前喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他第一次想到,他已經十一歲了,也許他強大的肌肉已不完全像以前了。

passages.original: But when the animals saw the green flag flying, and heard the gun firing again--seven times it was fired in all--and heard the speech that Napoleon made, congratulating them on their conduct, it did seem to them after all that they had won a great victory.
passages.vernacular: 但係,當動物哋睇到綠旗飄揚,又聽到炮響——總共鳴咗七響——聽到拿破崙發表嘅、祝賀佢哋表現嘅講話,佢哋畢竟覺得佢哋贏得咗一場巨大嘅勝利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,當動物們看到綠旗飄揚,又聽到炮響——總共鳴了七響——聽到拿破崙發表的、祝賀它們表現的講話,它們畢竟覺得它們贏得了一場巨大的勝利。

passages.original: The animals slain in the battle were given a solemn funeral.
passages.vernacular: 喺戰鬥中被殺嘅動物哋得到咗莊嚴嘅葬禮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在戰鬥中被殺的動物們得到了莊嚴的葬禮。

passages.original: Boxer and Clover pulled the wagon which served as a hearse, and Napoleon himself walked at the head of the procession.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手同三葉草拉住充當靈車嘅貨車,拿破崙親自走喺隊伍嘅前頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手和三葉草拉著充當靈車的貨車,拿破崙親自走在隊伍的前頭。

passages.original: Two whole days were given over to celebrations.
passages.vernacular: 整整兩天用嚟慶祝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整整兩天用來慶祝。

passages.original: There were songs, speeches, and more firing of the gun, and a special gift of an apple was bestowed on every animal, with two ounces of corn for each bird and three biscuits for each dog.
passages.vernacular: 有歌曲、演講同更多嘅鳴槍,仲特別賞賜每個動物一個蘋果,每隻鳥兩盎司玉米,每條狗三塊餅乾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有歌曲、演講和更多的鳴槍,還特別賞賜每個動物一個蘋果,每隻鳥兩盎司玉米,每條狗三塊餅乾。

passages.original: It was announced that the battle would be called the Battle of the Windmill, and that Napoleon had created a new decoration, the Order of the Green Banner, which he had conferred upon himself.
passages.vernacular: 宣布呢場戰鬥將被稱為風車之戰,拿破崙設立咗一枚新勳章,綠旗勳章,佢授予咗自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 宣布這場戰鬥將被稱為風車之戰,拿破崙設立了一枚新勳章,綠旗勳章,他授予了自己。

passages.original: In the general rejoicings the unfortunate affair of the banknotes was forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 喺普遍嘅歡慶中,鈔票嘅不幸事件被忘記喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在普遍的歡慶中,鈔票的不幸事件被忘記了。

passages.original: It was a few days later than this that the pigs came upon a case of whisky in the cellars of the farmhouse.
passages.vernacular: 喺此之後幾天,豬哋喺農舍嘅地窖裡發現咗一箱威士忌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在此之後幾天,豬們在農舍的地窖裡發現了一箱威士忌。

passages.original: It had been overlooked at the time when the house was first occupied.
passages.vernacular: 喺房子最初被佔據時,佢被忽略喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在房子最初被佔據時,它被忽略了。

passages.original: That night there came from the farmhouse the sound of loud singing, in which, to everyone’s surprise, the strains of ‘Beasts of England’ were mixed up.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天夜裡,農舍裡傳嚟大聲歌唱,令所有人驚訝嘅係,其中混雜住《英格蘭之獸》嘅曲調。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天夜裡,農舍裡傳來大聲歌唱,令所有人驚訝的是,其中混雜著《英格蘭之獸》的曲調。

passages.original: At about half past nine Napoleon, wearing an old bowler hat of Mr. Jones’s, was distinctly seen to emerge from the back door, gallop rapidly round the yard, and disappear indoors again.
passages.vernacular: 大約九點半,明顯睇到拿破崙戴住瓊斯先生嘅一頂舊圓頂禮帽,從後門出嚟,迅速繞院子奔跑一圈,又消失喺室內。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約九點半,明顯看到拿破崙戴著瓊斯先生的一頂舊圓頂禮帽,從後門出來,迅速繞院子奔跑一圈,又消失在室內。

passages.original: But in the morning a deep silence hung over the farmhouse.
passages.vernacular: 但早晨,一片深深嘅寂靜籠罩住農舍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但早晨,一片深深的寂靜籠罩著農舍。

passages.original: Not a pig appeared to be stirring.
passages.vernacular: 冇一頭豬似乎喺動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有一頭豬似乎在動。

passages.original: It was nearly nine o’clock when Squealer made his appearance, walking slowly and dejectedly, his eyes dull, his tail hanging limply behind him, and with every appearance of being seriously ill.
passages.vernacular: 將近九點,尖嗓子出現喇,緩慢而沮喪地走住,眼睛暗淡,尾巴軟綿綿地垂喺身後,一副生咗重病嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將近九點,尖嗓子出現了,緩慢而沮喪地走著,眼睛暗淡,尾巴軟綿綿地垂在身後,一副生了重病的樣子。

passages.original: He called the animals together and told them that he had a terrible piece of news to impart.
passages.vernacular: 佢把動物哋召集喺一起,告訴佢哋佢有一個可怕嘅消息要告知。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把動物們召集在一起,告訴它們他有一個可怕的消息要告知。

passages.original: Comrade Napoleon was dying!
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙同志快要死喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙同志快要死了!

passages.original: A cry of lamentation went up.
passages.vernacular: 一陣哀嘆聲響起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣哀嘆聲響起。

passages.original: Straw was laid down outside the doors of the farmhouse, and the animals walked on tiptoe.
passages.vernacular: 農舍門外鋪上咗稻草,動物哋踮住腳走路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農舍門外鋪上了稻草,動物們踮著腳走路。

passages.original: With tears in their eyes they asked one another what they should do if their Leader were taken away from them.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋含住淚互相問,如果佢哋嘅領袖被奪走,佢哋該點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們含著淚互相問,如果它們的領袖被奪走,它們該怎麼辦。

passages.original: A rumour went round that Snowball had after all contrived to introduce poison into Napoleon’s food.
passages.vernacular: 傳開一個傳聞,講雪球畢竟設法把毒藥放進咗拿破崙嘅食物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傳開一個傳聞,說雪球畢竟設法把毒藥放進了拿破崙的食物。

passages.original: At eleven o’clock Squealer came out to make another announcement.
passages.vernacular: 十啲,尖嗓子出嚟作另一次宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十一點,尖嗓子出來作另一次宣布。

passages.original: As his last act upon earth, Comrade Napoleon had pronounced a solemn decree: the drinking of alcohol was to be punished by death.
passages.vernacular: 作為佢在世上嘅最後一個行動,拿破崙同志宣布咗一項莊嚴嘅法令:飲酒將被處以死刑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 作為他在世上的最後一個行動,拿破崙同志宣布了一項莊嚴的法令:飲酒將被處以死刑。

passages.original: By the evening, however, Napoleon appeared to be somewhat better, and the following morning Squealer was able to tell them that he was well on the way to recovery.
passages.vernacular: 不過到傍晚,拿破崙似乎好咗啲,第二天早晨尖嗓子能夠告訴佢哋,佢正在康復嘅路上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過到傍晚,拿破崙似乎好了一些,第二天早晨尖嗓子能夠告訴它們,他正在康復的路上。

passages.original: By the evening of that day Napoleon was back at work, and on the next day it was learned that he had instructed Whymper to purchase in Willingdon some booklets on brewing and distilling.
passages.vernacular: 到嗰天傍晚,拿破崙又回去工作,第二天得知,佢指示溫珀喺威靈頓買幾本關於釀造同蒸餾嘅小冊子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到那天傍晚,拿破崙又回去工作,第二天得知,他指示溫珀在威靈頓買幾本關於釀造和蒸餾的小冊子。

passages.original: A week later Napoleon gave orders that the small paddock beyond the orchard, which it had previously been intended to set aside as a grazing-ground for animals who were past work, was to be ploughed up.
passages.vernacular: 一週後,拿破崙下令,果園外面原打算留作畀已過工作年齡嘅動物嘅牧場嘅小牧場,要被犁平。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一週後,拿破崙下令,果園外面原打算留作給已過工作年齡的動物的牧場的小牧場,要被犁平。

passages.original: It was given out that the pasture was exhausted and needed re-seeding; but it soon became known that Napoleon intended to sow it with barley.
passages.vernacular: 對外宣稱牧場已耗盡,需要重新播種;但好快就知道,拿破崙打算喺上面播種大麥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對外宣稱牧場已耗盡,需要重新播種;但很快就知道,拿破崙打算在上面播種大麥。

passages.original: About this time there occurred a strange incident which hardly anyone was able to understand.
passages.vernacular: 大約呢陣發生咗一件奇怪嘅事件,幾乎冇人能理解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約這時發生了一件奇怪的事件,幾乎沒有人能理解。

passages.original: One night at about twelve o’clock there was a loud crash in the yard, and the animals rushed out of their stalls.
passages.vernacular: 一天夜裡大約十二點,院子裡傳嚟一聲巨響,動物哋衝出馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天夜裡大約十二點,院子裡傳來一聲巨響,動物們衝出馬廄。

passages.original: It was a moonlit night.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個月夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個月夜。

passages.original: At the foot of the end wall of the big barn, where the Seven Commandments were written, there lay a ladder broken in two pieces.
passages.vernacular: 喺寫住七誡嘅大穀倉盡頭牆腳下,躺住一架斷成兩截嘅梯子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在寫著七誡的大穀倉盡頭牆腳下,躺著一架斷成兩截的梯子。

passages.original: Squealer, temporarily stunned, was sprawling beside it, and near at hand there lay a lantern, a paint-brush, and an overturned pot of white paint.
passages.vernacular: 尖嗓子暫時被打昏,四肢攤開躺喺佢旁邊,附近躺住一盞燈籠、一把油漆刷,同一翻倒嘅白漆罐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尖嗓子暫時被打昏,四肢攤開躺在它旁邊,附近躺著一盞燈籠、一把油漆刷,和一翻倒的白漆罐。

passages.original: The dogs immediately made a ring round Squealer, and escorted him back to the farmhouse as soon as he was able to walk.
passages.vernacular: 狗即刻圍成一圈圍住尖嗓子,佢能走路後就護送佢回到農舍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗立刻圍成一圈圍住尖嗓子,他能走路後就護送他回到農舍。

passages.original: None of the animals could form any idea as to what this meant, except old Benjamin, who nodded his muzzle with a knowing air, and seemed to understand, but would say nothing.
passages.vernacular: 冇一個動物能對呢意味住乜嘢形成任何想法,除咗老班傑明,佢帶住心照不宣嘅神氣點點嘴,似乎明白喇,卻乜嘢都不講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有一個動物能對這意味著什麼形成任何想法,除了老班傑明,他帶著心照不宣的神氣點點嘴,似乎明白了,卻什麼也不說。

passages.original: But a few days later Muriel, reading over the Seven Commandments to herself, noticed that there was yet another of them which the animals had remembered wrong.
passages.vernacular: 但幾天後,繆麗兒自己重讀七誡時,注意到其中又有一條動物哋記錯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但幾天後,繆麗兒自己重讀七誡時,注意到其中又有一條動物們記錯了。

passages.original: They had thought the Fifth Commandment was “No animal shall drink alcohol,” but there were two words that they had forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋以為第五條誡命係「任何動物唔得飲酒」,但有兩個詞佢哋忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們以為第五條誡命是「任何動物不得喝酒」,但有兩個詞它們忘了。

passages.original: Actually the Commandment read: “No animal shall drink alcohol TO EXCESS.”
passages.vernacular: 實際上誡命係咁樣嘅:「任何動物唔得飲酒過量。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 實際上誡命是這樣的:「任何動物不得飲酒過量。」

chapters.title: Chapter IX 第九章:拳擊手的末路

passages.original: Boxer’s split hoof was a long time in healing.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手裂開嘅蹄子好久才癒合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手裂開的蹄子很久才癒合。

passages.original: They had started the rebuilding of the windmill the day after the victory celebrations were ended.
passages.vernacular: 慶祝勝利結束後嘅第二天,佢哋就開始咗風車嘅重建。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 慶祝勝利結束後的第二天,它們就開始了風車的重建。

passages.original: Boxer refused to take even a day off work, and made it a point of honour not to let it be seen that he was in pain.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手拒絕休息邊怕一天,並把不讓人睇出佢喺痛作為一件榮譽嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手拒絕休息哪怕一天,並把不讓人看出他在痛作為一件榮譽的事。

passages.original: In the evenings he would admit privately to Clover that the hoof troubled him a great deal.
passages.vernacular: 晚上,佢私下向三葉草承認蹄子讓佢好痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚上,他私下向三葉草承認蹄子讓他很痛。

passages.original: Clover treated the hoof with poultices of herbs which she prepared by chewing them, and both she and Benjamin urged Boxer to work less hard.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草用佢咀嚼製成嘅草藥膏藥處理蹄子,佢同班傑明都勸拳擊手少工作啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草用她咀嚼製成的草藥膏藥處理蹄子,她和班傑明都勸拳擊手少工作一些。

passages.original: “A horse’s lungs do not last for ever,” she said to him.
passages.vernacular: 「馬嘅肺唔係永遠耐用嘅,」佢對佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬的肺不是永遠耐用的,」她對他說。

passages.original: But Boxer would not listen.
passages.vernacular: 但拳擊手不聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但拳擊手不聽。

passages.original: He had, he said, only one real ambition left--to see the windmill well under way before he reached the age for retirement.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,佢只剩下一個真正嘅願望——喺佢到退休年齡之前,睇到風車已經順利進行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,他只剩下一個真正的願望——在他到退休年齡之前,看到風車已經順利進行。

passages.original: At the beginning, when the laws of Animal Farm were first formulated, the retiring age had been fixed for horses and pigs at twelve, for cows at fourteen, for dogs at nine, for sheep at seven, and for hens and geese at five.
passages.vernacular: 最初,動物農莊嘅法律剛制定時,退休年齡確定為:馬同豬十二歲,牛十四歲,狗九歲,羊七歲,母雞同鵝五歲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最初,動物農莊的法律剛制定時,退休年齡確定為:馬和豬十二歲,牛十四歲,狗九歲,羊七歲,母雞和鵝五歲。

passages.original: Liberal old-age pensions had been agreed upon.
passages.vernacular: 已同意發放豐厚嘅養老金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 已同意發放豐厚的養老金。

passages.original: As yet no animal had actually retired on pension, but of late the subject had been discussed more and more.
passages.vernacular: 到目前仲冇動物真正領養老金退休,但最近呢個話題討論得越嚟越多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到目前還沒有動物真正領養老金退休,但最近這個話題討論得越來越多。

passages.original: Now that the small field beyond the orchard had been set aside for barley, it was rumoured that a corner of the large pasture was to be fenced off and turned into a grazing-ground for superannuated animals.
passages.vernacular: 既然果園外面嘅小田已留作大麥,傳聞講大牧場嘅一角將被圍起嚟,變成畀退役動物嘅牧地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然果園外面的小田已留作大麥,傳聞說大牧場的一角將被圍起來,變成給退役動物的牧地。

passages.original: For a horse, it was said, the pension would be five pounds of corn a day and, in winter, fifteen pounds of hay, with a carrot or possibly an apple on public holidays.
passages.vernacular: 據講,對馬來講,養老金將係每天五磅玉米,冬天十五磅乾草,公共假日有一根胡蘿蔔,或可能有一個蘋果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據說,對馬來說,養老金將是每天五磅玉米,冬天十五磅乾草,公共假日有一根胡蘿蔔,或可能有一個蘋果。

passages.original: Boxer’s twelfth birthday was due in the late summer of the following year.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手嘅十二歲生日定喺嚟年夏末。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手的十二歲生日定在來年夏末。

passages.original: Meanwhile life was hard.
passages.vernacular: 同時生活艱難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時生活艱難。

passages.original: The winter was as cold as the last one had been, and food was even shorter.
passages.vernacular: 冬天同去年一樣冷,食物更短缺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冬天和去年一樣冷,食物更短缺。

passages.original: Once again all rations were reduced, except those of the pigs and the dogs.
passages.vernacular: 所有口糧再次減少,除咗豬同狗嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有口糧再次減少,除了豬和狗的。

passages.original: A too rigid equality in rations, Squealer explained, would have been contrary to the principles of Animalism.
passages.vernacular: 尖嗓子解釋講,口糧上過於嚴格嘅平等,會違背動物主義嘅原則。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尖嗓子解釋說,口糧上過於嚴格的平等,會違背動物主義的原則。

passages.original: In any case he had no difficulty in proving to the other animals that they were NOT in reality short of food, whatever the appearances might be.
passages.vernacular: 無論如何,佢毫不費力地向其他動物證明,佢哋實際上並不缺乏食物,無論表面如何。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何,他毫不費力地向其他動物證明,它們實際上並不缺乏食物,無論表面如何。

passages.original: For the time being, certainly, it had been found necessary to make a readjustment of rations (Squealer always spoke of it as a “readjustment,” never as a “reduction”), but in comparison with the days of Jones, the improvement was enormous.
passages.vernacular: 當然,目前有必要對口糧作一次重新調整(尖嗓子總是講「調整」,從不講「減少」),但同瓊斯嘅時代相比,改善係巨大嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,目前有必要對口糧作一次重新調整(尖嗓子總是說「調整」,從不說「減少」),但與瓊斯的時代相比,改善是巨大的。

passages.original: Reading out the figures in a shrill, rapid voice, he proved to them in detail that they had more oats, more hay, more turnips than they had had in Jones’s day, that they worked shorter hours, that their drinking water was of better quality, that they lived longer, that a larger proportion of their young ones survived infancy, and that they had more straw in their stalls and suffered less from fleas.
passages.vernacular: 佢以尖銳快速嘅聲音讀出數字,詳細地向佢哋證明,佢哋比喺瓊斯時代有更多嘅燕麥、更多嘅乾草、更多嘅蘿蔔,佢哋工作嘅時間更短,飲水質量更好,佢哋活得更長,更大比例嘅幼崽能度過嬰兒期,佢哋嘅馬廄裡有更多稻草,跳蚤更少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他以尖銳快速的聲音讀出數字,詳細地向它們證明,它們比在瓊斯時代有更多的燕麥、更多的乾草、更多的蘿蔔,它們工作的時間更短,飲水質量更好,它們活得更長,更大比例的幼崽能度過嬰兒期,它們的馬廄裡有更多稻草,跳蚤更少。

passages.original: The animals believed every word of it.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋對此嘅每個字都相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們對此的每個字都相信。

passages.original: Truth to tell, Jones and all he stood for had almost faded out of their memories.
passages.vernacular: 講實話,瓊斯同佢所代表嘅一切,喺佢哋嘅記憶中幾乎已經淡去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說實話,瓊斯和他所代表的一切,在它們的記憶中幾乎已經淡去。

passages.original: They knew that life nowadays was harsh and bare, that they were often hungry and often cold, and that they were usually working when they were not asleep.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋知道如今嘅生活嚴酷而貧乏,佢哋常常飢餓、常常寒冷,不瞓覺時通常都喺工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們知道如今的生活嚴酷而貧乏,它們常常飢餓、常常寒冷,不睡覺時通常都在工作。

passages.original: But doubtless it had been worse in the old days.
passages.vernacular: 但無疑過去嘅日子更糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但無疑過去的日子更糟。

passages.original: They were glad to believe so.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋樂於咁樣相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們樂於這樣相信。

passages.original: Besides, in those days they had been slaves and now they were free, and that made all the difference, as Squealer did not fail to point out.
passages.vernacular: 此外,嗰時佢哋係奴隸,而家係自由嘅,呢就有天淵之別,尖嗓子都不忘指出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,那時它們是奴隸,現在是自由的,這就有天淵之別,尖嗓子也不忘指出。

passages.original: There were many more mouths to feed now.
passages.vernacular: 而家要養活嘅嘴多得多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在要養活的嘴多得多了。

passages.original: In the autumn the four sows had all littered about simultaneously, producing thirty-one young pigs between them.
passages.vernacular: 秋天,嗰四頭母豬幾乎同時都產咗仔,一共生咗三十一頭小豬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 秋天,那四頭母豬幾乎同時都產了仔,一共生了三十一頭小豬。

passages.original: The young pigs were piebald, and as Napoleon was the only boar on the farm, it was possible to guess at their parentage.
passages.vernacular: 小豬係花斑嘅,因為拿破崙係農場上唯一嘅公豬,可以猜出佢哋嘅父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小豬是花斑的,因為拿破崙是農場上唯一的公豬,可以猜出它們的父親。

passages.original: It was announced that later, when bricks and timber had been purchased, a schoolroom would be built in the farmhouse garden.
passages.vernacular: 宣布以後,等買到磚同木材,將喺農舍花園裡建一所校舍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 宣布以後,等買到磚和木材,將在農舍花園裡建一所校舍。

passages.original: For the time being, the young pigs were given their instruction by Napoleon himself in the farmhouse kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 目前,小豬由拿破崙親自在農舍廚房裡教導。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 目前,小豬由拿破崙親自在農舍廚房裡教導。

passages.original: They took their exercise in the garden, and were discouraged from playing with the other young animals.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺花園裡鍛煉,不鼓勵佢哋同其他幼小動物玩耍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們在花園裡鍛煉,不鼓勵它們與其他幼小動物玩耍。

passages.original: About this time, too, it was laid down as a rule that when a pig and any other animal met on the path, the other animal must stand aside: and also that all pigs, of whatever degree, were to have the privilege of wearing green ribbons on their tails on Sundays.
passages.vernacular: 大約呢陣,仲規定咗一條規則:當豬同任何其他動物喺小路上相遇時,其他動物必須站到一邊:並且所有豬,無論等級如何,星期天有喺尾巴上繫綠絲帶嘅特權。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約這時,還規定了一條規則:當豬和任何其他動物在小路上相遇時,其他動物必須站到一邊:並且所有豬,無論等級如何,星期天有在尾巴上繫綠絲帶的特權。

passages.original: The farm had had a fairly successful year, but was still short of money.
passages.vernacular: 農場度過咗相當成功嘅一年,但仍然缺錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場度過了相當成功的一年,但仍然缺錢。

passages.original: There were the bricks, sand, and lime for the schoolroom to be purchased, and it would also be necessary to begin saving up again for the machinery for the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 要買校舍用嘅磚、沙同石灰,仲必須開始再次為風車嘅機器攢錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要買校舍用的磚、沙和石灰,還必須開始再次為風車的機器攢錢。

passages.original: Then there were lamp oil and candles for the house, sugar for Napoleon’s own table (he forbade this to the other pigs, on the ground that it made them fat), and all the usual replacements such as tools, nails, string, coal, wire, scrap-iron, and dog biscuits.
passages.vernacular: 仲有房子嘅燈油同蠟燭,拿破崙自己餐桌嘅糖(佢禁止其他豬食,理由係佢使佢哋變胖),以及所有通常嘅更換,如工具、釘子、繩子、煤、電線、廢鐵同狗餅乾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有房子的燈油和蠟燭,拿破崙自己餐桌的糖(他禁止其他豬吃,理由是它使它們變胖),以及所有通常的更換,如工具、釘子、繩子、煤、電線、廢鐵和狗餅乾。

passages.original: A stump of hay and part of the potato crop were sold off, and the contract for eggs was increased to six hundred a week, so that that year the hens barely hatched enough chicks to keep their numbers at the same level.
passages.vernacular: 賣掉咗一堆乾草同一部分馬鈴薯收成,蛋嘅合同增加到每週六百個,所以嗰年母雞勉強孵出嘅小雞只夠維持數量不變。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 賣掉了一堆乾草和一部分馬鈴薯收成,蛋的合同增加到每週六百個,所以那年母雞勉強孵出的小雞只夠維持數量不變。

passages.original: Rations, reduced in December, were reduced again in February, and lanterns in the stalls were forbidden to save oil.
passages.vernacular: 十二月減少嘅口糧,二月又減少喇,為節省油,禁止喺馬廄裡用燈籠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十二月減少的口糧,二月又減少了,為節省油,禁止在馬廄裡用燈籠。

passages.original: But the pigs seemed comfortable enough, and in fact were putting on weight if anything.
passages.vernacular: 但豬似乎相當舒適,事實上如果講有乜嘢變化,就係喺增肥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但豬似乎相當舒適,事實上如果說有什麼變化,就是在增肥。

passages.original: One afternoon in late February a warm, rich, appetising scent, such as the animals had never smelt before, wafted itself across the yard from the little brew-house, which had been disused in Jones’s time, and which stood beyond the kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 二月下旬嘅一個下午,一股溫暖濃郁誘人嘅氣味,係動物哋從未聞過嘅,從瓊斯時代廢棄、位於廚房外面嘅小釀酒房飄過院子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 二月下旬的一個下午,一股溫暖濃郁誘人的氣味,是動物們從未聞過的,從瓊斯時代廢棄、位於廚房外面的小釀酒房飄過院子。

passages.original: Someone said it was the smell of cooking barley.
passages.vernacular: 有人講嗰個係煮大麥嘅氣味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人說那是煮大麥的氣味。

passages.original: The animals sniffed the air hungrily and wondered whether a warm mash was being prepared for their supper.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋飢餓地嗅住空氣,猜想係咪喺為佢哋嘅晚餐準備熱糊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們飢餓地嗅著空氣,猜想是否在為它們的晚餐準備熱糊。

passages.original: But no warm mash appeared, and on the following Sunday it was announced that from now onwards all barley would be reserved for the pigs.
passages.vernacular: 但冇熱糊出現,下個星期天宣布,從而家起所有大麥將留畀豬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但沒有熱糊出現,下個星期天宣布,從現在起所有大麥將留給豬。

passages.original: The field beyond the orchard had already been sown with barley.
passages.vernacular: 果園外面嘅田已經種上咗大麥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 果園外面的田已經種上了大麥。

passages.original: And the news soon leaked out that every pig was now receiving a ration of a pint of beer daily, with half a gallon for Napoleon himself, which was always served to him in the Crown Derby soup tureen.
passages.vernacular: 好快消息洩露,講而家每頭豬每天都有一品脫啤酒嘅口糧,拿破崙自己有半加侖,總是盛喺皇冠德比湯盆裡端畀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很快消息洩露,說現在每頭豬每天都有一品脫啤酒的口糧,拿破崙自己有半加侖,總是盛在皇冠德比湯盆裡端給他。

passages.original: But if there were hardships to be borne, they were partly offset by the fact that life nowadays had a greater dignity than it had had before.
passages.vernacular: 但如果有要忍受嘅艱苦,佢哋部分被如今嘅生活比以前更有尊嚴呢一事實所抵消。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果有要忍受的艱苦,它們部分被如今的生活比以前更有尊嚴這一事實所抵消。

passages.original: There were more songs, more speeches, more processions.
passages.vernacular: 有更多嘅歌、更多嘅演講、更多嘅遊行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有更多的歌、更多的演講、更多的遊行。

passages.original: Napoleon had commanded that once a week there should be held something called a Spontaneous Demonstration, the object of which was to celebrate the struggles and triumphs of Animal Farm.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙下令,每週應舉行一次叫做自發示威嘅活動,其目的係慶祝動物農莊嘅鬥爭同勝利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙下令,每週應舉行一次叫做自發示威的活動,其目的是慶祝動物農莊的鬥爭和勝利。

passages.original: At the appointed time the animals would leave their work and march round the precincts of the farm in military formation, with the pigs leading, then the horses, then the cows, then the sheep, and then the poultry.
passages.vernacular: 喺規定嘅時間,動物哋會離開工作,以軍隊隊形繞農場嘅範圍行進,豬喺前面領頭,然後係馬,然後係牛,然後係羊,然後係家禽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在規定的時間,動物們會離開工作,以軍隊隊形繞農場的範圍行進,豬在前面領頭,然後是馬,然後是牛,然後是羊,然後是家禽。

passages.original: The dogs flanked the procession and at the head of all marched Napoleon’s black cockerel.
passages.vernacular: 狗喺隊伍兩側,所有動物前面走住拿破崙嘅黑公雞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗在隊伍兩側,所有動物前面走著拿破崙的黑公雞。

passages.original: Boxer and Clover always carried between them a green banner marked with the hoof and the horn and the caption, “Long live Comrade Napoleon!”
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手同三葉草總是一起抬住一面綠旗,上面標有蹄子同角,並寫住標語:「拿破崙同志萬歲!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手和三葉草總是一起抬著一面綠旗,上面標有蹄子和角,並寫著標語:「拿破崙同志萬歲!」

passages.original: Afterwards there were recitations of poems composed in Napoleon’s honour, and a speech by Squealer giving particulars of the latest increases in the production of foodstuffs, and on occasion a shot was fired from the gun.
passages.vernacular: 之後有朗誦為拿破崙作嘅詩,同尖嗓子嘅演講,詳述食物產量最新嘅增長,有時從槍裡放一槍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後有朗誦為拿破崙作的詩,和尖嗓子的演講,詳述食物產量最新的增長,有時從槍裡放一槍。

passages.original: The sheep were the greatest devotees of the Spontaneous Demonstration, and if anyone complained (as a few animals sometimes did, when no pigs or dogs were near) that they wasted time and meant a lot of standing about in the cold, the sheep were sure to silence him with a tremendous bleating of “Four legs good, two legs bad!”
passages.vernacular: 羊係自發示威最熱心嘅追隨者,如果有邊個抱怨(有時冇豬或狗喺附近時,有少數動物會抱怨)佢哋浪費時間,意味住要喺寒冷中站好多時候,羊必定以巨大嘅咩咩聲「四條腿好,兩條腿壞!」使佢沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羊是自發示威最熱心的追隨者,如果有誰抱怨(有時沒有豬或狗在附近時,有少數動物會抱怨)它們浪費時間,意味著要在寒冷中站很多時候,羊必定以巨大的咩咩聲「四條腿好,兩條腿壞!」使他沉默。

passages.original: But by and large the animals enjoyed these celebrations.
passages.vernacular: 但大體上動物哋鍾意呢啲慶祝活動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但大體上動物們喜歡這些慶祝活動。

passages.original: They found it comforting to be reminded that, after all, they were truly their own masters and that the work they did was for their own benefit.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋發現被提醒畢竟佢哋真嘅係自己嘅主人、佢哋所做嘅工作係為了佢哋自己嘅利益,係令人安慰嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們發現被提醒畢竟它們真的是自己的主人、它們所做的工作是為了它們自己的利益,是令人安慰的。

passages.original: So that, what with the songs, the processions, Squealer’s lists of figures, the thunder of the gun, the crowing of the cockerel, and the fluttering of the flag, they were able to forget that their bellies were empty, at least part of the time.
passages.vernacular: 所以,有咗歌曲、遊行、尖嗓子嘅數字表、炮聲、公雞啼叫同旗幟飄揚,佢哋至少有部分時間可以忘記佢哋肚子係空嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,有了歌曲、遊行、尖嗓子的數字表、炮聲、公雞啼叫和旗幟飄揚,它們至少有部分時間可以忘記它們肚子是空的。

passages.original: In April, Animal Farm was proclaimed a Republic, and it became necessary to elect a President.
passages.vernacular: 四月,動物農莊被宣布為共和國,有必要選舉一位總統。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四月,動物農莊被宣布為共和國,有必要選舉一位總統。

passages.original: There was only one candidate, Napoleon, who was elected unanimously.
passages.vernacular: 只有一個候選人,拿破崙,佢被一致選舉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有一個候選人,拿破崙,他被一致選舉。

passages.original: On the same day it was given out that fresh documents had been discovered which revealed further details about Snowball’s complicity with Jones.
passages.vernacular: 同一天宣布,發現咗新嘅文件,揭示咗關於雪球同瓊斯共謀嘅更多細節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同一天宣布,發現了新的文件,揭示了關於雪球與瓊斯共謀的更多細節。

passages.original: It now appeared that Snowball had not, as the animals had previously imagined, merely attempted to lose the Battle of the Cowshed by means of a stratagem, but had been openly fighting on Jones’s side.
passages.vernacular: 而家睇來,雪球並不像動物哋以前想像嘅嗰樣,只係試圖通過一個詭計輸掉牛棚之戰,而係公開站喺瓊斯一邊作戰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在看來,雪球並不像動物們以前想像的那樣,只是試圖通過一個詭計輸掉牛棚之戰,而是公開站在瓊斯一邊作戰。

passages.original: In fact, it was he who had actually been the leader of the human forces, and had charged into battle with the words “Long live Humanity!” on his lips.
passages.vernacular: 事實上,佢才係人類軍隊嘅實際領導者,係嘴裡喊住「人類萬歲!」衝進戰鬥嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實上,他才是人類軍隊的實際領導者,是嘴裡喊著「人類萬歲!」衝進戰鬥的。

passages.original: The wounds on Snowball’s back, which a few of the animals still remembered to have seen, had been inflicted by Napoleon’s teeth.
passages.vernacular: 雪球背上嘅傷,啲動物仍然記得見過,係被拿破崙嘅牙齒咬嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球背上的傷,一些動物仍然記得見過,是被拿破崙的牙齒咬的。

passages.original: In the middle of the summer Moses the raven suddenly reappeared on the farm, after an absence of several years.
passages.vernacular: 仲夏,烏鴉摩西喺離開幾年之後,突然重新出而家農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仲夏,烏鴉摩西在離開幾年之後,突然重新出現在農場。

passages.original: He was quite unchanged, still did no work, and talked in the same strain as ever about Sugarcandy Mountain.
passages.vernacular: 佢完全冇變,仍然不工作,仍然以同樣嘅調子談論糖果山。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他完全沒變,仍然不工作,仍然以同樣的調子談論糖果山。

passages.original: He would perch on a stump, flap his black wings, and talk by the hour to anyone who would listen.
passages.vernacular: 佢會棲喺一個樹樁上,拍住黑翅膀,對任何肯聽嘅人一談就係幾個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他會棲在一個樹樁上,拍著黑翅膀,對任何肯聽的人一談就是幾個小時。

passages.original: “Up there, comrades,” he would say solemnly, pointing to the sky with his large beak--“up there, just on the other side of that dark cloud that you can see--there it lies, Sugarcandy Mountain, that happy country where we poor animals shall rest for ever from our labours!”
passages.vernacular: 「喺上面,同志哋,」佢會莊嚴地講,用佢嘅大嘴指住天空——「喺上面,就喺你哋睇到嘅嗰朵烏雲嘅另一邊——佢就喺嗰度,糖果山,嗰個快樂嘅國度,我哋可憐嘅動物將永遠從勞役中休息!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在上面,同志們,」他會莊嚴地說,用他的大嘴指著天空——「在上面,就在你們看到的那朵烏雲的另一邊——它就在那裡,糖果山,那個快樂的國度,我們可憐的動物將永遠從勞役中休息!」

passages.original: He even claimed to have been there on one of his higher flights, and to have seen the everlasting fields of clover and the linseed cake and lump sugar growing on the hedges.
passages.vernacular: 佢甚至聲稱喺一次飛得較高時去過嗰度,睇到咗永恆嘅三葉草田,同長喺樹籬上嘅亞麻籽餅同方糖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他甚至聲稱在一次飛得較高時去過那裡,看到了永恆的三葉草田,和長在樹籬上的亞麻籽餅與方糖。

passages.original: Many of the animals believed him.
passages.vernacular: 許多動物相信佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 許多動物相信他。

passages.original: Their lives now, they reasoned, were hungry and laborious; was it not right and just that a better world should exist somewhere else?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋推論,而家佢哋嘅生活飢餓又辛勞;別處存在一個更好嘅世界,唔係正確而公正嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們推論,現在它們的生活飢餓又辛勞;別處存在一個更好的世界,不是正確而公正的嗎?

passages.original: A thing that was difficult to determine was the attitude of the pigs towards Moses.
passages.vernacular: 好難確定嘅係豬對摩西嘅態度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很難確定的是豬對摩西的態度。

passages.original: They all declared contemptuously that his stories about Sugarcandy Mountain were lies, and yet they allowed him to remain on the farm, not working, with an allowance of a gill of beer a day.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都輕蔑地宣稱佢關於糖果山嘅故事係謊言,然而佢哋允許佢留喺農場,不工作,每天仲有一吉爾啤酒嘅津貼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們都輕蔑地宣稱他關於糖果山的故事是謊言,然而它們允許他留在農場,不工作,每天還有一吉爾啤酒的津貼。

passages.original: After his hoof had healed up, Boxer worked harder than ever.
passages.vernacular: 蹄子痊癒後,拳擊手比以前工作得更努力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蹄子痊癒後,拳擊手比以前工作得更努力。

passages.original: Indeed, all the animals worked like slaves that year.
passages.vernacular: 確實,嗰一年所有動物都像奴隸一樣工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,那一年所有動物都像奴隸一樣工作。

passages.original: Apart from the regular work of the farm, and the rebuilding of the windmill, there was the schoolhouse for the young pigs, which was started in March.
passages.vernacular: 除咗農場嘅日常工作同風車嘅重建之外,仲有為小豬建嘅校舍,三月開工。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了農場的日常工作和風車的重建之外,還有為小豬建的校舍,三月開工。

passages.original: Sometimes the long hours on insufficient food were hard to bear, but Boxer never faltered.
passages.vernacular: 有時,喺食物不足嘅情況下長時間工作好難忍受,但拳擊手從不動搖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時,在食物不足的情況下長時間工作很難忍受,但拳擊手從不動搖。

passages.original: In nothing that he said or did was there any sign that his strength was not what it had been.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢所講或所做嘅任何事情中,都冇跡象表明佢嘅力量已不如以往。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他所說或所做的任何事情中,都沒有跡象表明他的力量已不如以往。

passages.original: It was only his appearance that was a little altered; his hide was less shiny than it had used to be, and his great haunches seemed to have shrunken.
passages.vernacular: 只係佢嘅外貌略有改變;佢嘅皮毛不如過去嗰樣有光澤,佢巨大嘅臀部似乎收縮喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是他的外貌略有改變;他的皮毛不如過去那樣有光澤,他巨大的臀部似乎收縮了。

passages.original: The others said, “Boxer will pick up when the spring grass comes on”; but the spring came and Boxer grew no fatter.
passages.vernacular: 其他動物講,「春草長出嚟時,拳擊手就會好起嚟」;但春天嚟喇,拳擊手並冇長胖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他動物說,「春草長出來時,拳擊手就會好起來」;但春天來了,拳擊手並沒有長胖。

passages.original: Sometimes on the slope leading to the top of the quarry, when he braced his muscles against the weight of some vast boulder, it seemed that nothing kept him on his feet except the will to continue.
passages.vernacular: 有時喺通往採石場頂嘅斜坡上,當佢把肌肉繃緊靠喺某塊巨大圓石嘅重量上時,似乎除咗繼續嘅意志之外,冇乜嘢使佢站住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時在通往採石場頂的斜坡上,當他把肌肉繃緊靠在某塊巨大圓石的重量上時,似乎除了繼續的意志之外,沒有什麼使他站著。

passages.original: At such times his lips were seen to form the words, “I will work harder”; he had no voice left.
passages.vernacular: 呢種時候,睇到佢嘅嘴唇形成咗「我要更努力工作」嘅字樣;佢已冇聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種時候,看到他的嘴唇形成了「我要更努力工作」的字樣;他已沒有聲音。

passages.original: Once again Clover and Benjamin warned him to take care of his health, but Boxer paid no attention.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草同班傑明又一次警告佢要注意健康,但拳擊手不予理會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草和班傑明又一次警告他要注意健康,但拳擊手不予理會。

passages.original: His twelfth birthday was approaching.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅十二歲生日快到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的十二歲生日快到了。

passages.original: He did not care what happened so long as a good store of stone was accumulated before he went on pension.
passages.vernacular: 佢不在乎發生乜嘢,只要喺佢領養老金之前積累起足夠嘅石頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不在乎發生什麼,只要在他領養老金之前積累起足夠的石頭。

passages.original: Late one evening in the summer, a sudden rumour ran round the farm that something had happened to Boxer.
passages.vernacular: 夏天嘅一個傍晚,一個突如其嚟嘅傳聞傳遍農場,講拳擊手出事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏天的一個傍晚,一個突如其來的傳聞傳遍農場,說拳擊手出事了。

passages.original: He had gone out alone to drag a load of stone down to the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 佢獨自出去拖一車石頭到風車嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他獨自出去拖一車石頭到風車那裡。

passages.original: And sure enough, the rumour was true.
passages.vernacular: 果然,傳聞係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 果然,傳聞是真的。

passages.original: A few minutes later two pigeons came racing in with the news; “Boxer has fallen!
passages.vernacular: 幾分鐘後兩隻鴿子飛奔進嚟報告消息:「拳擊手倒下喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾分鐘後兩隻鴿子飛奔進來報告消息:「拳擊手倒下了!

passages.original: He is lying on his side and can’t get up!”
passages.vernacular: 佢側躺住,站不起嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他側躺著,站不起來!」

passages.original: About half the animals on the farm rushed out to the knoll where the windmill stood.
passages.vernacular: 農場上大約一半嘅動物衝出去,跑到風車所在嘅小丘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場上大約一半的動物衝出去,跑到風車所在的小丘。

passages.original: There lay Boxer, between the shafts of the cart, his neck stretched out, unable even to raise his head.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手躺喺嗰度,喺車轅之間,脖子伸直,連頭都抬不起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手躺在那裡,在車轅之間,脖子伸直,連頭也抬不起來。

passages.original: His eyes were glazed, his sides matted with sweat.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛呆滯,兩側被汗浸透。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的眼睛呆滯,兩側被汗浸透。

passages.original: A thin stream of blood had trickled out of his mouth.
passages.vernacular: 一股細細嘅血從佢嘴裡流出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一股細細的血從他嘴裡流出。

passages.original: Clover dropped to her knees at his side.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草喺佢身邊跪倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草在他身邊跪倒。

passages.original: “Boxer!” she cried, “how are you?”
passages.vernacular: 「拳擊手!」佢喊道,「你點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「拳擊手!」她喊道,「你怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “It is my lung,” said Boxer in a weak voice.
passages.vernacular: 「係我嘅肺,」拳擊手用微弱嘅聲音講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是我的肺,」拳擊手用微弱的聲音說。

passages.original: “It does not matter.
passages.vernacular: 「冇關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒關係。

passages.original: I think you will be able to finish the windmill without me.
passages.vernacular: 我想冇我,你哋都能完成風車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想沒有我,你們也能完成風車。

passages.original: There is a pretty good store of stone accumulated.
passages.vernacular: 已經積累咗相當好嘅一批石頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 已經積累了相當好的一批石頭。

passages.original: I had only another month to go in any case.
passages.vernacular: 無論如何,我只剩一個月喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何,我只剩一個月了。

passages.original: To tell you the truth, I had been looking forward to my retirement.
passages.vernacular: 講實話,我一直喺盼望我嘅退休。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說實話,我一直在盼望我的退休。

passages.original: And perhaps, as Benjamin is growing old too, they will let him retire at the same time and be a companion to me.”
passages.vernacular: 或者,既然班傑明都老喇,佢哋會讓佢同時退休,畀我作伴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許,既然班傑明也老了,他們會讓他同時退休,給我作伴。」

passages.original: “We must get help at once,” said Clover.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋必須即刻找幫助,」三葉草講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們必須立刻找幫助,」三葉草說。

passages.original: “Run, somebody, and tell Squealer what has happened.”
passages.vernacular: 「邊個去,跑去告訴尖嗓子發生咗乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰去,跑去告訴尖嗓子發生了什麼。」

passages.original: All the other animals immediately raced back to the farmhouse to give Squealer the news.
passages.vernacular: 所有其他動物即刻跑回農舍,把消息告訴尖嗓子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有其他動物立刻跑回農舍,把消息告訴尖嗓子。

passages.original: Only Clover remained, and Benjamin who lay down at Boxer’s side, and, without speaking, kept the flies off him with his long tail.
passages.vernacular: 只有三葉草留下,仲有班傑明,佢躺喺拳擊手身邊,一言不發,用佢嘅長尾巴替佢趕走蒼蠅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有三葉草留下,還有班傑明,他躺在拳擊手身邊,一言不發,用他的長尾巴替他趕走蒼蠅。

passages.original: After about a quarter of an hour Squealer appeared, full of sympathy and concern.
passages.vernacular: 大約過咗一刻鐘,尖嗓子出現喇,充滿同情同關切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約過了一刻鐘,尖嗓子出現了,充滿同情和關切。

passages.original: He said that Comrade Napoleon had learned with the very deepest distress of this misfortune to one of the most loyal workers on the farm, and was already making arrangements to send Boxer to be treated in the hospital at Willingdon.
passages.vernacular: 佢講拿破崙同志懷住最深切嘅悲痛得知農場上最忠誠嘅工作者之一遭遇咗呢個不幸,已經喺安排把拳擊手送到威靈頓嘅醫院治療。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說拿破崙同志懷著最深切的悲痛得知農場上最忠誠的工作者之一遭遇了這個不幸,已經在安排把拳擊手送到威靈頓的醫院治療。

passages.original: The animals felt a little uneasy at this.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋對此感到有些不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們對此感到有些不安。

passages.original: Except for Mollie and Snowball, no other animal had ever left the farm, and they did not like to think of their sick comrade in the hands of human beings.
passages.vernacular: 除咗茉莉同雪球,冇其他動物離開過農場,佢哋唔願想到佢哋生病嘅同志落喺人類手中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了茉莉和雪球,沒有其他動物離開過農場,它們不願想到它們生病的同志落在人類手中。

passages.original: However, Squealer easily convinced them that the veterinary surgeon in Willingdon could treat Boxer’s case more satisfactorily than could be done on the farm.
passages.vernacular: 然而,尖嗓子輕易地講服咗佢哋,威靈頓嘅獸醫能比喺農場上更令人滿意地治療拳擊手嘅病情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,尖嗓子輕易地說服了它們,威靈頓的獸醫能比在農場上更令人滿意地治療拳擊手的病情。

passages.original: And about half an hour later, when Boxer had somewhat recovered, he was with difficulty got on to his feet, and managed to limp back to his stall, where Clover and Benjamin had prepared a good bed of straw for him.
passages.vernacular: 大約半小時後,拳擊手稍微恢復咗啲,佢被艱難地弄站起嚟,設法一瘸一拐地回到佢嘅馬廄,三葉草同班傑明已為佢準備咗一張好稻草床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約半小時後,拳擊手稍微恢復了一些,他被艱難地弄站起來,設法一瘸一拐地回到他的馬廄,三葉草和班傑明已為他準備了一張好稻草床。

passages.original: For the next two days Boxer remained in his stall.
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟嘅兩天,拳擊手待喺佢嘅馬廄裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來的兩天,拳擊手待在他的馬廄裡。

passages.original: The pigs had sent out a large bottle of pink medicine which they had found in the medicine chest in the bathroom, and Clover administered it to Boxer twice a day after meals.
passages.vernacular: 豬哋送嚟一大瓶粉紅色嘅藥,係佢哋喺浴室藥箱裡找到嘅,三葉草每天兩次飯後畀拳擊手服用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬們送來一大瓶粉紅色的藥,是他們在浴室藥箱裡找到的,三葉草每天兩次飯後給拳擊手服用。

passages.original: In the evenings she lay in his stall and talked to him, while Benjamin kept the flies off him.
passages.vernacular: 晚上,佢躺喺佢嘅馬廄裡同佢講話,班傑明為佢趕蒼蠅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚上,她躺在他的馬廄裡同他說話,班傑明為他趕蒼蠅。

passages.original: Boxer professed not to be sorry for what had happened.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手聲稱不為所發生嘅事感到遺憾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手聲稱不為所發生的事感到遺憾。

passages.original: If he made a good recovery, he might expect to live another three years, and he looked forward to the peaceful days that he would spend in the corner of the big pasture.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢恢復得好,佢可以期望再活三年,佢期待住佢將喺大牧場一角度過嘅平靜日子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他恢復得好,他可以期望再活三年,他期待著他將在大牧場一角度過的平靜日子。

passages.original: It would be the first time that he had had leisure to study and improve his mind.
passages.vernacular: 嗰將係佢第一次有閒暇學習同增長心智。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那將是他第一次有閒暇學習和增長心智。

passages.original: He intended, he said, to devote the rest of his life to learning the remaining twenty-two letters of the alphabet.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,佢打算把餘生用於學習字母表中剩下嘅二十二個字母。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,他打算把餘生用於學習字母表中剩下的二十二個字母。

passages.original: However, Benjamin and Clover could only be with Boxer after working hours, and it was in the middle of the day when the van came to take him away.
passages.vernacular: 然而,班傑明同三葉草只能喺工作時間之後陪伴拳擊手,而貨車嚟帶走佢係喺中午。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,班傑明和三葉草只能在工作時間之後陪伴拳擊手,而貨車來帶走他是在中午。

passages.original: The animals were all at work weeding turnips under the supervision of a pig, when they were astonished to see Benjamin come galloping from the direction of the farm buildings, braying at the top of his voice.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋都喺一頭豬嘅監督下鋤蘿蔔,呢陣佢哋驚訝地睇到班傑明從農場建築嘅方向飛奔而嚟,扯住嗓子驢叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們都在一頭豬的監督下鋤蘿蔔,這時它們驚訝地看到班傑明從農場建築的方向飛奔而來,扯著嗓子驢叫。

passages.original: It was the first time that they had ever seen Benjamin excited--indeed, it was the first time that anyone had ever seen him gallop.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係佢哋第一次見到班傑明興奮——確實,係第一次有邊個見到佢奔跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是它們第一次見到班傑明興奮——確實,是第一次有誰見到他奔跑。

passages.original: “Quick, quick!” he shouted.
passages.vernacular: 「快,快!」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「快,快!」他喊道。

passages.original: “Come at once!
passages.vernacular: 「即刻嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬上來!

passages.original: They’re taking Boxer away!”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋要把拳擊手帶走!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們要把拳擊手帶走!」

passages.original: Without waiting for orders from the pig, the animals broke off work and raced back to the farm buildings.
passages.vernacular: 不等嗰頭豬嘅命令,動物哋停下工作,飛奔回農場建築。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不等那頭豬的命令,動物們停下工作,飛奔回農場建築。

passages.original: Sure enough, there in the yard was a large closed van, drawn by two horses, with lettering on its side and a sly-looking man in a low-crowned bowler hat sitting on the driver’s seat.
passages.vernacular: 果然,院子裡有一輛大嘅封閉貨車,由兩匹馬拉住,側面有字,一個神色狡猾、戴低頂圓頂禮帽嘅男人坐喺駕駛座上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 果然,院子裡有一輛大的封閉貨車,由兩匹馬拉著,側面有字,一個神色狡猾、戴低頂圓頂禮帽的男人坐在駕駛座上。

passages.original: And Boxer’s stall was empty.
passages.vernacular: 而拳擊手嘅馬廄空喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而拳擊手的馬廄空了。

passages.original: The animals crowded round the van.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋擠喺貨車周圍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們擠在貨車周圍。

passages.original: “Good-bye, Boxer!” they chorused, “good-bye!”
passages.vernacular: 「再見,拳擊手!」佢哋齊聲喊道,「再見!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見,拳擊手!」它們齊聲喊道,「再見!」

passages.original: “Fools!
passages.vernacular: 「傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「傻瓜!

passages.original: Fools!” shouted Benjamin, prancing round them and stamping the earth with his small hoofs.
passages.vernacular: 傻瓜!」班傑明喊道,喺佢哋周圍蹦跳,用佢嘅小蹄子跺住地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傻瓜!」班傑明喊道,在它們周圍蹦跳,用他的小蹄子跺著地。

passages.original: “Fools!
passages.vernacular: 「傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「傻瓜!

passages.original: Do you not see what is written on the side of that van?”
passages.vernacular: 你哋冇睇到嗰輛車側面寫住乜嘢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們沒看到那輛車側面寫著什麼嗎?」

passages.original: That gave the animals pause, and there was a hush.
passages.vernacular: 呢使動物哋停住喇,一片寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這使動物們停住了,一片寂靜。

passages.original: Muriel began to spell out the words.
passages.vernacular: 繆麗兒開始拼讀嗰啲字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繆麗兒開始拼讀那些字。

passages.original: But Benjamin pushed her aside and in the midst of a deadly silence he read:
passages.vernacular: 但班傑明把佢推到一邊,喺死一般嘅寂靜中佢念道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但班傑明把她推到一邊,在死一般的寂靜中他念道:

passages.original: “‘Alfred Simmonds, Horse Slaughterer and Glue Boiler, Willingdon.
passages.vernacular: 「『阿爾弗雷德·西蒙茲,威靈頓屠馬商兼熬膠商。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『阿爾弗雷德·西蒙茲,威靈頓屠馬商兼熬膠商。

passages.original: Dealer in Hides and Bone-Meal.
passages.vernacular: 皮革同骨粉經銷商。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 皮革和骨粉經銷商。

passages.original: Kennels Supplied.’
passages.vernacular: 供應犬舍。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 供應犬舍。』

passages.original: Do you not understand what that means?
passages.vernacular: 你哋不明白嗰個係乜嘢意思嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們不明白那是什麼意思嗎?

passages.original: They are taking Boxer to the knacker’s!”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋要把拳擊手帶到屠馬場去!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們要把拳擊手帶到屠馬場去!」
