passages.original: A cry of horror burst from all the animals.
passages.vernacular: 所有動物都爆發出恐怖嘅叫喊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物都爆發出恐怖的叫喊。

passages.original: At this moment the man on the box whipped up his horses and the van moved out of the yard at a smart trot.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣,座上嘅男人鞭打佢嘅馬,貨車以輕快嘅小跑駛出院子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時,座上的男人鞭打他的馬,貨車以輕快的小跑駛出院子。

passages.original: All the animals followed, crying out at the tops of their voices.
passages.vernacular: 所有動物都跟住,扯住嗓子喊叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物都跟著,扯著嗓子喊叫。

passages.original: Clover forced her way to the front.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草強行擠到咗前面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草強行擠到了前面。

passages.original: The van began to gather speed.
passages.vernacular: 貨車開始加速。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貨車開始加速。

passages.original: Clover tried to stir her stout limbs to a gallop, and achieved a canter.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草試圖使佢粗壯嘅四肢飛奔起嚟,只做到咗慢跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草試圖使她粗壯的四肢飛奔起來,只做到了慢跑。

passages.original: “Boxer!” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 「拳擊手!」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「拳擊手!」她喊道。

passages.original: “Boxer!
passages.vernacular: 「拳擊手!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「拳擊手!

passages.original: Boxer!
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手!

passages.original: Boxer!”
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手!」

passages.original: And just at this moment, as though he had heard the uproar outside, Boxer’s face, with the white stripe down his nose, appeared at the small window at the back of the van.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,好像聽到咗外面嘅喧鬧,拳擊手嘅臉,鼻子上有一道白條,出而家貨車後面嘅小窗口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,好像聽到了外面的喧鬧,拳擊手的臉,鼻子上有一道白條,出現在貨車後面的小窗口。

passages.original: “Boxer!” cried Clover in a terrible voice.
passages.vernacular: 「拳擊手!」三葉草用可怕嘅聲音喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「拳擊手!」三葉草用可怕的聲音喊道。

passages.original: “Boxer!
passages.vernacular: 「拳擊手!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「拳擊手!

passages.original: Get out!
passages.vernacular: 出嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 出來!

passages.original: Get out quickly!
passages.vernacular: 快出嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快出來!

passages.original: They’re taking you to your death!”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋要送你去死!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們要送你去死!」

passages.original: All the animals took up the cry of “Get out, Boxer, get out!”
passages.vernacular: 所有動物都跟住喊「出嚟,拳擊手,出嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物都跟著喊「出來,拳擊手,出來!」

passages.original: But the van was already gathering speed and drawing away from them.
passages.vernacular: 但貨車已喺加速,離佢哋越嚟越遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但貨車已在加速,離它們越來越遠。

passages.original: It was uncertain whether Boxer had understood what Clover had said.
passages.vernacular: 不確定拳擊手係咪聽懂咗三葉草講嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不確定拳擊手是否聽懂了三葉草說的話。

passages.original: But a moment later his face disappeared from the window and there was the sound of a tremendous drumming of hoofs inside the van.
passages.vernacular: 但片刻後佢嘅臉從窗口消失喇,貨車裡傳嚟蹄子猛烈敲打嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但片刻後他的臉從窗口消失了,貨車裡傳來蹄子猛烈敲打的聲音。

passages.original: He was trying to kick his way out.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺試圖踢出一條路出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在試圖踢出一條路出去。

passages.original: The time had been when a few kicks from Boxer’s hoofs would have smashed the van to matchwood.
passages.vernacular: 曾有一個時候,拳擊手嘅蹄子幾下就能把貨車踢成火柴棒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 曾有一個時候,拳擊手的蹄子幾下就能把貨車踢成火柴棒。

passages.original: But alas! his strength had left him; and in a few moments the sound of drumming hoofs grew fainter and died away.
passages.vernacular: 但可惜!佢嘅力量已離開咗佢;不一會兒,敲打蹄子嘅聲音變得微弱,消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但可惜!他的力量已離開了他;不一會兒,敲打蹄子的聲音變得微弱,消失了。

passages.original: In desperation the animals began appealing to the two horses which drew the van to stop.
passages.vernacular: 絕望中,動物哋開始向拉車嘅兩匹馬呼籲停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 絕望中,動物們開始向拉車的兩匹馬呼籲停下。

passages.original: “Comrades, comrades!” they shouted.
passages.vernacular: 「同志哋,同志哋!」佢哋喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同志們,同志們!」它們喊道。

passages.original: “Don’t take your own brother to his death!”
passages.vernacular: 「唔好把你哋自己嘅兄弟送去死!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不要把你們自己的兄弟送去死!」

passages.original: But the stupid brutes, too ignorant to realise what was happening, merely set back their ears and quickened their pace.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰兩個愚蠢嘅畜生,太無知,不明白正在發生乜嘢,只係把耳朵向後,加快咗步伐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那兩個愚蠢的畜生,太無知,不明白正在發生什麼,只是把耳朵向後,加快了步伐。

passages.original: Boxer’s face did not reappear at the window.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手嘅臉冇再出而家窗口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手的臉沒有再出現在窗口。

passages.original: Too late, someone thought of racing ahead and shutting the five-barred gate; but in another moment the van was through it and rapidly disappearing down the road.
passages.vernacular: 太遲喇,有人想到跑到前面關上五柵欄大門;但轉眼間貨車已穿過佢,迅速消失喺路上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太遲了,有人想到跑到前面關上五柵欄大門;但轉眼間貨車已穿過它,迅速消失在路上。

passages.original: Boxer was never seen again.
passages.vernacular: 再都冇人見過拳擊手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再也沒有人見過拳擊手。

passages.original: Three days later it was announced that he had died in the hospital at Willingdon, in spite of receiving every attention a horse could have.
passages.vernacular: 三天後宣布,佢儘管得到咗一匹馬所能得到嘅一切照顧,仍死喺威靈頓嘅醫院裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三天後宣布,他儘管得到了一匹馬所能得到的一切照顧,仍死在威靈頓的醫院裡。

passages.original: Squealer came to announce the news to the others.
passages.vernacular: 尖嗓子嚟向其他動物宣布呢個消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尖嗓子來向其他動物宣布這個消息。

passages.original: He had, he said, been present during Boxer’s last hours.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,佢喺拳擊手最後嘅時刻在場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,他在拳擊手最後的時刻在場。

passages.original: “It was the most affecting sight I have ever seen!” said Squealer, lifting his trotter and wiping away a tear.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我見過嘅最感人嘅景象!」尖嗓子講,抬起蹄子拭去一滴眼淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我見過的最感人的景象!」尖嗓子說,抬起蹄子拭去一滴眼淚。

passages.original: “I was at his bedside at the very last.
passages.vernacular: 「我喺佢最後時刻就喺佢嘅床邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在他最後時刻就在他的床邊。

passages.original: And at the end, almost too weak to speak, he whispered in my ear that his sole sorrow was to have passed on before the windmill was finished.
passages.vernacular: 最後,佢幾乎虛弱得講不出話,喺我耳邊低語講,佢唯一嘅悲傷係喺風車建成之前就去世喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後,他幾乎虛弱得說不出話,在我耳邊低語說,他唯一的悲傷是在風車建成之前就去世了。

passages.original: ‘Forward, comrades!’ he whispered.
passages.vernacular: 『前進,同志哋!』佢低語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『前進,同志們!』他低語。

passages.original: ‘Forward in the name of the Rebellion.
passages.vernacular: 『以造反嘅名義前進。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『以造反的名義前進。

passages.original: Long live Animal Farm!
passages.vernacular: 動物農莊萬歲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物農莊萬歲!

passages.original: Long live Comrade Napoleon!
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙同志萬歲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙同志萬歲!

passages.original: Napoleon is always right.’
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙總是對嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙總是對的。』

passages.original: Those were his very last words, comrades.”
passages.vernacular: 呢啲就係佢嘅最後遺言,同志哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些就是他的最後遺言,同志們。」

passages.original: Here Squealer’s demeanour suddenly changed.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣尖嗓子嘅神態突然改變喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時尖嗓子的神態突然改變了。

passages.original: He fell silent for a moment, and his little eyes darted suspicious glances from side to side before he proceeded.
passages.vernacular: 佢沉默咗片刻,小眼睛向兩邊投出懷疑嘅目光,然後才繼續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沉默了片刻,小眼睛向兩邊投出懷疑的目光,然後才繼續。

passages.original: It had come to his knowledge, he said, that a foolish and wicked rumour had been circulated at the time of Boxer’s removal.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,佢已得知,喺拳擊手被帶走時,散佈咗一個愚蠢而邪惡嘅傳聞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,他已得知,在拳擊手被帶走時,散佈了一個愚蠢而邪惡的傳聞。

passages.original: Some of the animals had noticed that the van which took Boxer away was marked “Horse Slaughterer,” and had actually jumped to the conclusion that Boxer was being sent to the knacker’s.
passages.vernacular: 啲動物注意到,帶走拳擊手嘅貨車上標住「屠馬商」,竟貿然得出結論,講拳擊手被送去咗屠馬場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一些動物注意到,帶走拳擊手的貨車上標著「屠馬商」,竟貿然得出結論,說拳擊手被送去了屠馬場。

passages.original: It was almost unbelievable, said Squealer, that any animal could be so stupid.
passages.vernacular: 尖嗓子講,任何動物能嗰樣愚蠢,幾乎令人難以置信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尖嗓子說,任何動物能那樣愚蠢,幾乎令人難以置信。

passages.original: Surely, he cried indignantly, whisking his tail and skipping from side to side, surely they knew their beloved Leader, Comrade Napoleon, better than that?
passages.vernacular: 佢憤怒地喊道,甩住尾巴,左右蹦跳,肯定佢哋比嗰更了解佢哋心愛嘅領袖拿破崙同志吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他憤怒地喊道,甩著尾巴,左右蹦跳,肯定它們比那更了解它們心愛的領袖拿破崙同志吧?

passages.original: But the explanation was really very simple.
passages.vernacular: 但解釋其實好簡單。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但解釋其實非常簡單。

passages.original: The van had previously been the property of the knacker, and had been bought by the veterinary surgeon, who had not yet painted the old name out.
passages.vernacular: 嗰輛貨車以前係屠馬商嘅財產,被獸醫買喇,佢仲冇把舊名字塗掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那輛貨車以前是屠馬商的財產,被獸醫買了,他還沒有把舊名字塗掉。

passages.original: That was how the mistake had arisen.
passages.vernacular: 錯誤就係咁樣產生嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 錯誤就是這樣產生的。

passages.original: The animals were enormously relieved to hear this.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋聽到呢個,極大地鬆咗一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們聽到這個,極大地鬆了一口氣。

passages.original: And when Squealer went on to give further graphic details of Boxer’s death-bed, the admirable care he had received, and the expensive medicines for which Napoleon had paid without a thought as to the cost, their last doubts disappeared and the sorrow that they felt for their comrade’s death was tempered by the thought that at least he had died happy.
passages.vernacular: 當尖嗓子接住畀出關於拳擊手臨終床邊嘅更多生動細節,佢受到嘅令人欽佩嘅照顧,以及拿破崙不顧代價所付錢嘅昂貴藥物時,佢哋最後嘅疑慮消失喇,佢哋為同志之死所感到嘅悲傷,因想到佢至少死得快樂而緩和喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當尖嗓子接著給出關於拳擊手臨終床邊的更多生動細節,他受到的令人欽佩的照顧,以及拿破崙不顧代價所付錢的昂貴藥物時,它們最後的疑慮消失了,它們為同志之死所感到的悲傷,因想到他至少死得快樂而緩和了。

passages.original: Napoleon himself appeared at the meeting on the following Sunday morning and pronounced a short oration in Boxer’s honour.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙本人喺下個星期天早晨嘅大會上出現,發表咗一篇紀念拳擊手嘅簡短演講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙本人在下個星期天早晨的大會上出現,發表了一篇紀念拳擊手的簡短演說。

passages.original: It had not been possible, he said, to bring back their lamented comrade’s remains for interment on the farm, but he had ordered a large wreath to be made from the laurels in the farmhouse garden and sent down to be placed on Boxer’s grave.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,唔可能把佢哋哀悼嘅同志嘅遺體帶回農場安葬,但佢已下令用農舍花園裡嘅月桂製作一個大花圈,送去放喺拳擊手嘅墳上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,不可能把它們哀悼的同志的遺體帶回農場安葬,但他已下令用農舍花園裡的月桂製作一個大花圈,送去放在拳擊手的墳上。

passages.original: And in a few days’ time the pigs intended to hold a memorial banquet in Boxer’s honour.
passages.vernacular: 幾天後豬哋打算為紀念拳擊手舉行一次追悼宴會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾天後豬們打算為紀念拳擊手舉行一次追悼宴會。

passages.original: Napoleon ended his speech with a reminder of Boxer’s two favourite maxims, “I will work harder” and “Comrade Napoleon is always right”--maxims, he said, which every animal would do well to adopt as his own.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙喺結束演講時提醒大家拳擊手最喜愛嘅兩句格言,「我要更努力工作」同「拿破崙同志總是對嘅」——佢講,呢兩句格言,每個動物都應該採用為自己嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙在結束演講時提醒大家拳擊手最喜愛的兩句格言,「我要更努力工作」和「拿破崙同志總是對的」——他說,這兩句格言,每個動物都應該採用為自己的。

passages.original: On the day appointed for the banquet, a grocer’s van drove up from Willingdon and delivered a large wooden crate at the farmhouse.
passages.vernacular: 宴會嘅規定日期,一輛雜貨商嘅貨車從威靈頓開嚟,喺農舍送下一個大木箱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 宴會的規定日期,一輛雜貨商的貨車從威靈頓開來,在農舍送下一個大木箱。

passages.original: That night there was the sound of uproarious singing, which was followed by what sounded like a violent quarrel and ended at about eleven o’clock with a tremendous crash of glass.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天夜裡有喧鬧嘅歌唱聲,隨後係聽起嚟像激烈爭吵嘅聲音,大約十啲以一聲巨大嘅玻璃破碎聲結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天夜裡有喧鬧的歌唱聲,隨後是聽起來像激烈爭吵的聲音,大約十一點以一聲巨大的玻璃破碎聲結束。

passages.original: No one stirred in the farmhouse before noon on the following day, and the word went round that from somewhere or other the pigs had acquired the money to buy themselves another case of whisky.
passages.vernacular: 第二天中午之前,農舍裡冇人動,傳聞講,豬哋唔知從邊度弄到咗錢,畀自己又買咗一箱威士忌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天中午之前,農舍裡沒有人動,傳聞說,豬們不知從哪裡弄到了錢,給自己又買了一箱威士忌。

chapters.title: Chapter X 第十章:豬變成人

passages.original: Years passed.
passages.vernacular: 歲月流逝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歲月流逝。

passages.original: The seasons came and went, the short animal lives fled by.
passages.vernacular: 季節嚟咗又去,動物短暫嘅生命飛逝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 季節來了又去,動物短暫的生命飛逝。

passages.original: A time came when there was no one who remembered the old days before the Rebellion, except Clover, Benjamin, Moses the raven, and a number of the pigs.
passages.vernacular: 到咗一個時候,除咗三葉草、班傑明、烏鴉摩西,同幾頭豬之外,冇人記得造反之前嘅舊日喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到了一個時候,除了三葉草、班傑明、烏鴉摩西,和幾頭豬之外,沒有人記得造反之前的舊日了。

passages.original: Muriel was dead; Bluebell, Jessie, and Pincher were dead.
passages.vernacular: 繆麗兒死喇;藍鈴、潔西和平徹死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繆麗兒死了;藍鈴、潔西和平徹死了。

passages.original: Jones too was dead--he had died in an inebriates’ home in another part of the country.
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯都死喇——佢死喺呢個國家另一處嘅一家戒酒所裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯也死了——他死在這個國家另一處的一家戒酒所裡。

passages.original: Snowball was forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 雪球被遺忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪球被遺忘了。

passages.original: Boxer was forgotten, except by the few who had known him.
passages.vernacular: 拳擊手被遺忘喇,除咗少數認識佢嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拳擊手被遺忘了,除了少數認識他的人。

passages.original: Clover was an old stout mare now, stiff in the joints and with a tendency to rheumy eyes.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草而家係一匹粗壯嘅老母馬,關節僵硬,眼睛容易發炎流淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草現在是一匹粗壯的老母馬,關節僵硬,眼睛容易發炎流淚。

passages.original: She was two years past the retiring age, but in fact no animal had ever actually retired.
passages.vernacular: 佢已超過退休年齡兩年,但事實上冇動物真正退休過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她已超過退休年齡兩年,但事實上沒有動物真正退休過。

passages.original: The talk of setting aside a corner of the pasture for superannuated animals had long since been dropped.
passages.vernacular: 關於留出牧場一角畀退役動物嘅講法,早已被擱置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 關於留出牧場一角給退役動物的說法,早已被擱置。

passages.original: Napoleon was now a mature boar of twenty-four stone.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙而家係一頭二十四英石嘅成年公豬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙現在是一頭二十四英石的成年公豬。

passages.original: Squealer was so fat that he could with difficulty see out of his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 尖嗓子胖得幾乎睇唔見外面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尖嗓子胖得幾乎看不見外面。

passages.original: Only old Benjamin was much the same as ever, except for being a little greyer about the muzzle, and, since Boxer’s death, more morose and taciturn than ever.
passages.vernacular: 只有老班傑明同以前差不多,只係口鼻有點更灰喇,自從拳擊手死後,比以前更鬱悶沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有老班傑明和以前差不多,只是口鼻有點更灰了,自從拳擊手死後,比以前更鬱悶沉默。

passages.original: There were many more creatures on the farm now, though the increase was not so great as had been expected in earlier years.
passages.vernacular: 農場上而家有更多嘅生物,雖然增加不如早些年預期嘅咁大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場上現在有更多的生物,雖然增加不如早些年預期的那麼大。

passages.original: Many animals had been born to whom the Rebellion was only a dim tradition, passed on by word of mouth, and others had been bought who had never heard mention of such a thing before their arrival.
passages.vernacular: 許多動物出生時,造反對佢哋只係口口相傳嘅模糊傳統,另啲係買嚟嘅,到來之前從冇聽講過呢種事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 許多動物出生時,造反對他們只是口口相傳的模糊傳統,另一些是買來的,到來之前從沒聽說過這種事。

passages.original: The farm possessed three horses now besides Clover.
passages.vernacular: 除咗三葉草,農場而家有三匹馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了三葉草,農場現在有三匹馬。

passages.original: They were fine upstanding beasts, willing workers and good comrades, but very stupid.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋係優良挺拔嘅野獸,肯工作都係好同志,但好愚蠢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們是優良挺拔的野獸,肯工作也是好同志,但非常愚蠢。

passages.original: None of them proved able to learn the alphabet beyond the letter B. They accepted everything that they were told about the Rebellion and the principles of Animalism, especially from Clover, for whom they had an almost filial respect; but it was doubtful whether they understood very much of it.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋冇一個能學會字母表超過字母B。佢哋接受別人告訴佢哋嘅關於造反同動物主義原則嘅一切,特別係從三葉草嗰度,佢哋對佢有近乎子女般嘅尊敬;但好懷疑佢哋係咪明白其中好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們沒有一個能學會字母表超過字母B。它們接受別人告訴它們的關於造反和動物主義原則的一切,特別是從三葉草那裡,它們對她有近乎子女般的尊敬;但很懷疑它們是否明白其中很多。

passages.original: The farm was more prosperous now, and better organised: it had even been enlarged by two fields which had been bought from Mr. Pilkington.
passages.vernacular: 農場而家更繁榮,組織得更好:佢甚至擴大咗兩塊從皮爾金頓先生嗰度買嘅田。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農場現在更繁榮,組織得更好:它甚至擴大了兩塊從皮爾金頓先生那裡買的田。

passages.original: The windmill had been successfully completed at last, and the farm possessed a threshing machine and a hay elevator of its own, and various new buildings had been added to it.
passages.vernacular: 風車終於成功建成,農場擁有自己嘅脫粒機同乾草升降機,仲增加咗各種新建築。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風車終於成功建成,農場擁有自己的脫粒機和乾草升降機,還增加了各種新建築。

passages.original: Whymper had bought himself a dogcart.
passages.vernacular: 溫珀畀自己買咗一輛雙輪輕馬車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫珀給自己買了一輛雙輪輕馬車。

passages.original: The windmill, however, had not after all been used for generating electrical power.
passages.vernacular: 然而,風車畢竟冇用於發電。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,風車畢竟沒有用於發電。

passages.original: It was used for milling corn, and brought in a handsome money profit.
passages.vernacular: 佢用於磨玉米,帶嚟一筆可觀嘅金錢利潤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它用於磨玉米,帶來一筆可觀的金錢利潤。

passages.original: The animals were hard at work building yet another windmill; when that one was finished, so it was said, the dynamos would be installed.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋正在辛苦地再建另一座風車;據講,嗰座建成後,就會安裝發電機。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們正在辛苦地再建另一座風車;據說,那座建成後,就會安裝發電機。

passages.original: But the luxuries of which Snowball had once taught the animals to dream, the stalls with electric light and hot and cold water, and the three-day week, were no longer talked about.
passages.vernacular: 但雪球曾教動物哋夢想嘅嗰啲奢侈,有電燈同冷熱水嘅馬廄,同三日工作週,唔再被談起喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但雪球曾教動物們夢想的那些奢侈,有電燈和冷熱水的馬廄,和三日工作週,不再被談起了。

passages.original: Napoleon had denounced such ideas as contrary to the spirit of Animalism.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙已譴責呢種想法違背動物主義精神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙已譴責這種想法違背動物主義精神。

passages.original: The truest happiness, he said, lay in working hard and living frugally.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,最真正嘅幸福在於努力工作同節儉生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,最真正的幸福在於努力工作和節儉生活。

passages.original: Somehow it seemed as though the farm had grown richer without making the animals themselves any richer-except, of course, for the pigs and the dogs.
passages.vernacular: 唔知怎嘅,似乎農場變得更富喇,卻冇使動物哋自己更富——當然,豬同狗除外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知怎的,似乎農場變得更富了,卻沒有使動物們自己更富——當然,豬和狗除外。

passages.original: Perhaps this was partly because there were so many pigs and so many dogs.
passages.vernacular: 或者呢部分係因為有咁多豬同咁多狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許這部分是因為有這麼多豬和這麼多狗。

passages.original: It was not that these creatures did not work, after their fashion.
passages.vernacular: 並唔係呢啲生物不工作,以佢哋嘅方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並不是這些生物不工作,以它們的方式。

passages.original: There was, as Squealer was never tired of explaining, endless work in the supervision and organisation of the farm.
passages.vernacular: 正如尖嗓子不倦地解釋嘅,農場嘅監督同組織有無窮無盡嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正如尖嗓子不倦地解釋的,農場的監督和組織有無窮無盡的工作。

passages.original: Much of this work was of a kind that the other animals were too ignorant to understand.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲工作大部分係其他動物太無知而無法理解嘅嗰種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些工作大部分是其他動物太無知而無法理解的那種。

passages.original: For example, Squealer told them that the pigs had to expend enormous labours every day upon mysterious things called “files,” “reports,” “minutes,” and “memoranda”.
passages.vernacular: 例如,尖嗓子告訴佢哋,豬每天必須喺叫做「檔案」、「報告」、「會議記錄」同「備忘錄」嘅神秘嘢上花費巨大嘅勞動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 例如,尖嗓子告訴它們,豬每天必須在叫做「檔案」、「報告」、「會議記錄」和「備忘錄」的神秘東西上花費巨大的勞動。

passages.original: These were large sheets of paper which had to be closely covered with writing, and as soon as they were so covered, they were burnt in the furnace.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲係必須密密寫滿字嘅大張紙,一旦寫滿,就喺爐子裡燒掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些是必須密密寫滿字的大張紙,一旦寫滿,就在爐子裡燒掉。

passages.original: This was of the highest importance for the welfare of the farm, Squealer said.
passages.vernacular: 尖嗓子講,呢對農場嘅福利至關重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尖嗓子說,這對農場的福利至關重要。

passages.original: But still, neither pigs nor dogs produced any food by their own labour; and there were very many of them, and their appetites were always good.
passages.vernacular: 但無論如何,豬同狗都不以自己嘅勞動生產任何食物;而佢哋有好多,佢哋嘅胃口總是好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但無論如何,豬和狗都不以自己的勞動生產任何食物;而它們有很多,它們的胃口總是很好。

passages.original: As for the others, their life, so far as they knew, was as it had always been.
passages.vernacular: 至於其他動物,據佢哋所知,佢哋嘅生活同一直以來一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於其他動物,據它們所知,它們的生活和一直以來一樣。

passages.original: They were generally hungry, they slept on straw, they drank from the pool, they laboured in the fields; in winter they were troubled by the cold, and in summer by the flies.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋通常飢餓,瞓喺稻草上,從池子裡飲水,喺田裡勞動;冬天為寒冷所苦,夏天為蒼蠅所苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們通常飢餓,睡在稻草上,從池子裡喝水,在田裡勞動;冬天為寒冷所苦,夏天為蒼蠅所苦。

passages.original: Sometimes the older ones among them racked their dim memories and tried to determine whether in the early days of the Rebellion, when Jones’s expulsion was still recent, things had been better or worse than now.
passages.vernacular: 有時其中年紀大嘅絞盡腦汁回憶,試圖確定喺造反嘅早期,瓊斯被驅逐不久時,情況係比而家好定係壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時其中年紀大的絞盡腦汁回憶,試圖確定在造反的早期,瓊斯被驅逐不久時,情況是比現在好還是壞。

passages.original: They could not remember.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋記不起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們記不起來。

passages.original: There was nothing with which they could compare their present lives: they had nothing to go upon except Squealer’s lists of figures, which invariably demonstrated that everything was getting better and better.
passages.vernacular: 冇任何嘢可以攞嚟同佢哋目前嘅生活比較:除咗尖嗓子嘅數字表,佢哋冇任何依據,嗰啲數字表總是證明一切都喺越變越好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有任何東西可以拿來與它們目前的生活比較:除了尖嗓子的數字表,它們沒有任何依據,那些數字表總是證明一切都在越變越好。

passages.original: The animals found the problem insoluble; in any case, they had little time for speculating on such things now.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋覺得呢個問題無法解決;無論如何,佢哋而家冇多少時間猜測呢類事情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們覺得這個問題無法解決;無論如何,它們現在沒有多少時間猜測這類事情。

passages.original: Only old Benjamin professed to remember every detail of his long life and to know that things never had been, nor ever could be much better or much worse--hunger, hardship, and disappointment being, so he said, the unalterable law of life.
passages.vernacular: 只有老班傑明聲稱記得佢漫長一生嘅每個細節,並知道事情從來冇、都唔可能好好多或壞好多——佢講,飢餓、艱難同失望係生活不可改變嘅法則。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有老班傑明聲稱記得他漫長一生的每個細節,並知道事情從來沒有、也不可能好很多或壞很多——他說,飢餓、艱難和失望是生活不可改變的法則。

passages.original: And yet the animals never gave up hope.
passages.vernacular: 然而動物哋從未放棄希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而動物們從未放棄希望。

passages.original: More, they never lost, even for an instant, their sense of honour and privilege in being members of Animal Farm.
passages.vernacular: 而且,佢哋從不曾失去,邊怕一刻,身為動物農莊成員嘅榮譽感同特權感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,它們從不曾失去,哪怕一刻,身為動物農莊成員的榮譽感和特權感。

passages.original: They were still the only farm in the whole county--in all England!--owned and operated by animals.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋仍然係整個郡——整個英格蘭!——唯一由動物擁有同經營嘅農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們仍然是整個郡——整個英格蘭!——唯一由動物擁有和經營的農場。

passages.original: Not one of them, not even the youngest, not even the newcomers who had been brought from farms ten or twenty miles away, ever ceased to marvel at that.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋中冇一個,甚至最年輕嘅,甚至從十英里或二十英里外嘅農場帶嚟嘅新嚟者,對此不停止驚歎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們中沒有一個,甚至最年輕的,甚至從十英里或二十英里外的農場帶來的新來者,對此不停止驚歎。

passages.original: And when they heard the gun booming and saw the green flag fluttering at the masthead, their hearts swelled with imperishable pride, and the talk turned always towards the old heroic days, the expulsion of Jones, the writing of the Seven Commandments, the great battles in which the human invaders had been defeated.
passages.vernacular: 當佢哋聽到炮響,睇到綠旗喺桅頂飄揚,佢哋嘅心膨脹住不朽嘅自豪,談話總是轉向舊日嘅英雄歲月,驅逐瓊斯,寫七誡,擊敗人類入侵者嘅大戰役。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當它們聽到炮響,看到綠旗在桅頂飄揚,它們的心膨脹著不朽的自豪,談話總是轉向舊日的英雄歲月,驅逐瓊斯,寫七誡,擊敗人類入侵者的大戰役。

passages.original: None of the old dreams had been abandoned.
passages.vernacular: 舊日嘅夢想冇一個被放棄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 舊日的夢想沒有一個被放棄。

passages.original: The Republic of the Animals which Major had foretold, when the green fields of England should be untrodden by human feet, was still believed in.
passages.vernacular: 少校預言嘅動物共和國,當英格蘭嘅綠色田野將唔再被人腳所踏,仍然被相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 少校預言的動物共和國,當英格蘭的綠色田野將不再被人腳所踏,仍然被相信。

passages.original: Some day it was coming: it might not be soon, it might not be with in the lifetime of any animal now living, but still it was coming.
passages.vernacular: 有一天佢會到來:或者唔會好快,或者不喺任何現今活住嘅動物嘅有生之年,但佢仍然會到來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天它會到來:也許不會很快,也許不在任何現今活著的動物的有生之年,但它仍然會到來。

passages.original: Even the tune of ‘Beasts of England’ was perhaps hummed secretly here and there: at any rate, it was a fact that every animal on the farm knew it, though no one would have dared to sing it aloud.
passages.vernacular: 甚至《英格蘭之獸》嘅調子或者喺呢度嗰度被秘密地哼住:無論如何,農場上每個動物都知道佢,雖然冇人敢大聲唱出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 甚至《英格蘭之獸》的調子也許在這裡那裡被秘密地哼著:無論如何,農場上每個動物都知道它,雖然沒有人敢大聲唱出來。

passages.original: It might be that their lives were hard and that not all of their hopes had been fulfilled; but they were conscious that they were not as other animals.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅生活可能艱難,並非所有嘅希望都實現喇;但佢哋意識到佢哋同其他動物不同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們的生活可能艱難,並非所有的希望都實現了;但它們意識到它們與其他動物不同。

passages.original: If they went hungry, it was not from feeding tyrannical human beings; if they worked hard, at least they worked for themselves.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋挨餓,唔係為了餵養暴虐嘅人類;如果佢哋努力工作,至少係為了佢哋自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果它們挨餓,不是為了餵養暴虐的人類;如果它們努力工作,至少是為了它們自己。

passages.original: No creature among them went upon two legs.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋中冇一個生物用兩條腿走路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們中沒有一個生物用兩條腿走路。

passages.original: No creature called any other creature “Master.”
passages.vernacular: 冇一個生物稱其他生物「主人」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有一個生物稱其他生物「主人」。

passages.original: All animals were equal.
passages.vernacular: 所有動物一律平等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物一律平等。

passages.original: One day in early summer Squealer ordered the sheep to follow him, and led them out to a piece of waste ground at the other end of the farm, which had become overgrown with birch saplings.
passages.vernacular: 初夏嘅一天,尖嗓子命令羊跟佢嚟,把佢哋領到農場另一端嘅一塊荒地,嗰度長滿咗樺樹苗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 初夏的一天,尖嗓子命令羊跟他來,把它們領到農場另一端的一塊荒地,那裡長滿了樺樹苗。

passages.original: The sheep spent the whole day there browsing at the leaves under Squealer’s supervision.
passages.vernacular: 羊喺尖嗓子嘅監督下整天喺嗰度食樹葉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羊在尖嗓子的監督下整天在那裡吃樹葉。

passages.original: In the evening he returned to the farmhouse himself, but, as it was warm weather, told the sheep to stay where they were.
passages.vernacular: 傍晚佢自己回農舍,但因為天氣暖同,叫羊留喺原地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傍晚他自己回農舍,但因為天氣暖和,叫羊留在原地。

passages.original: It ended by their remaining there for a whole week, during which time the other animals saw nothing of them.
passages.vernacular: 結果佢哋喺嗰度整整留咗一個星期,喺此期間其他動物完全冇見到佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果它們在那裡整整留了一個星期,在此期間其他動物完全沒見到它們。

passages.original: Squealer was with them for the greater part of every day.
passages.vernacular: 尖嗓子每天大部分時間同佢哋喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尖嗓子每天大部分時間與它們在一起。

passages.original: He was, he said, teaching them to sing a new song, for which privacy was needed.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,佢喺教佢哋唱一首新歌,需要隱秘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,他在教它們唱一首新歌,需要隱秘。

passages.original: It was just after the sheep had returned, on a pleasant evening when the animals had finished work and were making their way back to the farm buildings, that the terrified neighing of a horse sounded from the yard.
passages.vernacular: 就喺羊回嚟之後,一個愉快嘅傍晚,動物哋結束工作,正沿住回農場建築嘅路,院子裡傳嚟一匹馬恐懼嘅嘶鳴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在羊回來之後,一個愉快的傍晚,動物們結束工作,正沿著回農場建築的路,院子裡傳來一匹馬恐懼的嘶鳴。

passages.original: Startled, the animals stopped in their tracks.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋食咗一驚,停住咗腳步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們吃了一驚,停住了腳步。

passages.original: It was Clover’s voice.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係三葉草嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是三葉草的聲音。

passages.original: She neighed again, and all the animals broke into a gallop and rushed into the yard.
passages.vernacular: 佢又嘶鳴喇,所有動物都飛奔起嚟,衝進院子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她又嘶鳴了,所有動物都飛奔起來,衝進院子。

passages.original: Then they saw what Clover had seen.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋睇到咗三葉草所睇到嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後它們看到了三葉草所看到的。

passages.original: It was a pig walking on his hind legs.
passages.vernacular: 係一頭用後腿行走嘅豬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是一頭用後腿行走的豬。

passages.original: Yes, it was Squealer.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,係尖嗓子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,是尖嗓子。

passages.original: A little awkwardly, as though not quite used to supporting his considerable bulk in that position, but with perfect balance, he was strolling across the yard.
passages.vernacular: 有點笨拙,好像仲不太習慣用嗰個姿勢支撐佢龐大嘅身體,但完美平衡,佢正在院子裡漫步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有點笨拙,好像還不太習慣用那個姿勢支撐他龐大的身體,但完美平衡,他正在院子裡漫步。

passages.original: And a moment later, out from the door of the farmhouse came a long file of pigs, all walking on their hind legs.
passages.vernacular: 片刻後,從農舍嘅門裡出嚟一長列豬,全都用後腿走路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 片刻後,從農舍的門裡出來一長列豬,全都用後腿走路。

passages.original: Some did it better than others, one or two were even a trifle unsteady and looked as though they would have liked the support of a stick, but every one of them made his way right round the yard successfully.
passages.vernacular: 有些做得比別嘅好,有一兩個甚至有點不穩,睇起嚟好像想要一根棍子支撐,但每一個都成功地走完咗整個院子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些做得比別的好,有一兩個甚至有點不穩,看起來好像想要一根棍子支撐,但每一個都成功地走完了整個院子。

passages.original: And finally there was a tremendous baying of dogs and a shrill crowing from the black cockerel, and out came Napoleon himself, majestically upright, casting haughty glances from side to side, and with his dogs gambolling round him.
passages.vernacular: 最後一陣狗嘅巨大吠聲同黑公雞嘅尖銳啼叫,拿破崙本人走咗出嚟,威嚴地直立,向兩邊投出傲慢嘅目光,佢嘅狗喺佢周圍蹦跳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後一陣狗的巨大吠聲和黑公雞的尖銳啼叫,拿破崙本人走了出來,威嚴地直立,向兩邊投出傲慢的目光,他的狗在他周圍蹦跳。

passages.original: He carried a whip in his trotter.
passages.vernacular: 佢蹄子裡攞住一根鞭子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他蹄子裡拿著一根鞭子。

passages.original: There was a deadly silence.
passages.vernacular: 一片死寂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一片死寂。

passages.original: Amazed, terrified, huddling together, the animals watched the long line of pigs march slowly round the yard.
passages.vernacular: 驚訝、恐懼、擠成一團,動物哋睇住嗰一長列豬緩緩繞院子行進。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 驚訝、恐懼、擠成一團,動物們看著那一長列豬緩緩繞院子行進。

passages.original: It was as though the world had turned upside-down.
passages.vernacular: 好像世界顛倒過嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像世界顛倒過來了。

passages.original: Then there came a moment when the first shock had worn off and when, in spite of everything-in spite of their terror of the dogs, and of the habit, developed through long years, of never complaining, never criticising, no matter what happened--they might have uttered some word of protest.
passages.vernacular: 然後有一刻,當最初嘅震驚已經消退,儘管一切——儘管佢哋害怕狗,儘管長年形成嘅、無論發生乜嘢都從不抱怨、從不批評嘅習慣——佢哋或者會講出啲抗議嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後有一刻,當最初的震驚已經消退,儘管一切——儘管它們害怕狗,儘管長年形成的、無論發生什麼都從不抱怨、從不批評的習慣——它們也許會說出一些抗議的話。

passages.original: But just at that moment, as though at a signal, all the sheep burst out into a tremendous bleating of--
passages.vernacular: 但就喺嗰一刻,好像聽到信號,所有嘅羊爆發出巨大嘅咩咩叫——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但就在那一刻,好像聽到信號,所有的羊爆發出巨大的咩咩叫——

passages.original: “Four legs good, two legs BETTER!
passages.vernacular: 「四條腿好,兩條腿更好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「四條腿好,兩條腿更好!

passages.original: Four legs good, two legs BETTER!
passages.vernacular: 四條腿好,兩條腿更好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四條腿好,兩條腿更好!

passages.original: Four legs good, two legs BETTER!”
passages.vernacular: 四條腿好,兩條腿更好!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四條腿好,兩條腿更好!」

passages.original: It went on for five minutes without stopping.
passages.vernacular: 佢不停地持續咗五分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不停地持續了五分鐘。

passages.original: And by the time the sheep had quieted down, the chance to utter any protest had passed, for the pigs had marched back into the farmhouse.
passages.vernacular: 等羊安靜下嚟時,發出任何抗議嘅機會已經過去,因為豬已走回農舍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等羊安靜下來時,發出任何抗議的機會已經過去,因為豬已走回農舍。

passages.original: Benjamin felt a nose nuzzling at his shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明感到有一個鼻子喺蹭佢嘅肩膀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明感到有一個鼻子在蹭他的肩膀。

passages.original: He looked round.
passages.vernacular: 佢回頭睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他回頭看。

passages.original: It was Clover.
passages.vernacular: 係三葉草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是三葉草。

passages.original: Her old eyes looked dimmer than ever.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅老眼睛睇起嚟比以往更暗淡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的老眼睛看起來比以往更暗淡。

passages.original: Without saying anything, she tugged gently at his mane and led him round to the end of the big barn, where the Seven Commandments were written.
passages.vernacular: 佢乜嘢都冇講,輕輕拉佢嘅鬃毛,領佢繞到大穀倉嘅盡頭,七誡寫喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她什麼也沒說,輕輕拉他的鬃毛,領他繞到大穀倉的盡頭,七誡寫在那裡。

passages.original: For a minute or two they stood gazing at the tatted wall with its white lettering.
passages.vernacular: 一兩分鐘佢哋站住,凝視住嗰堵塗咗焦油、寫住白字嘅牆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一兩分鐘他們站著,凝視著那堵塗了焦油、寫著白字的牆。

passages.original: “My sight is failing,” she said finally.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅視力喺衰退,」佢最後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的視力在衰退,」她最後說。

passages.original: “Even when I was young I could not have read what was written there.
passages.vernacular: 「即使我年輕時,我都讀不咗寫喺嗰度嘅字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「即使我年輕時,我也讀不了寫在那裡的字。

passages.original: But it appears to me that that wall looks different.
passages.vernacular: 但喺我睇來,嗰堵牆睇起嚟不同喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在我看來,那堵牆看起來不同了。

passages.original: Are the Seven Commandments the same as they used to be, Benjamin?”
passages.vernacular: 七誡同以前一樣嗎,班傑明?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 七誡和以前一樣嗎,班傑明?」

passages.original: For once Benjamin consented to break his rule, and he read out to her what was written on the wall.
passages.vernacular: 呢一次班傑明同意打破佢嘅規矩,把寫喺牆上嘅字讀畀佢聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一次班傑明同意打破他的規矩,把寫在牆上的字讀給她聽。

passages.original: There was nothing there now except a single Commandment.
passages.vernacular: 而家嗰度除咗一條誡命之外乜嘢都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在那裡除了一條誡命之外什麼也沒有。

passages.original: It ran:
passages.vernacular: 佢係咁樣嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是這樣的:

passages.original: ALL ANIMALS ARE EQUAL BUT SOME ANIMALS ARE MORE EQUAL THAN OTHERS
passages.vernacular: 所有動物一律平等,但有些動物比其他動物更平等
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有動物一律平等,但有些動物比其他動物更平等

passages.original: After that it did not seem strange when next day the pigs who were supervising the work of the farm all carried whips in their trotters.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢之後,第二天監督農場工作嘅豬全都蹄子裡攞住鞭子,就不顯得奇怪喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這之後,第二天監督農場工作的豬全都蹄子裡拿著鞭子,就不顯得奇怪了。

passages.original: It did not seem strange to learn that the pigs had bought themselves a wireless set, were arranging to install a telephone, and had taken out subscriptions to ‘John Bull’, ‘Tit-Bits’, and the ‘Daily Mirror’.
passages.vernacular: 得知豬畀自己買咗一台無線電收音機,正在安排安裝電話,並訂閱咗《約翰牛》、《趣聞》同《每日鏡報》,都不顯得奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 得知豬給自己買了一台無線電收音機,正在安排安裝電話,並訂閱了《約翰牛》、《趣聞》和《每日鏡報》,也不顯得奇怪。

passages.original: It did not seem strange when Napoleon was seen strolling in the farmhouse garden with a pipe in his mouth--no, not even when the pigs took Mr. Jones’s clothes out of the wardrobes and put them on, Napoleon himself appearing in a black coat, ratcatcher breeches, and leather leggings, while his favourite sow appeared in the watered silk dress which Mrs. Jones had been used to wearing on Sundays.
passages.vernacular: 睇到拿破崙嘴裡叼住煙斗喺農舍花園裡漫步,都不顯得奇怪——不,甚至豬哋把瓊斯先生嘅衣服從衣櫃裡攞出嚟穿上,拿破崙自己穿住黑外套、捕鼠人馬褲同皮綁腿出現,而佢最寵愛嘅母豬穿住瓊斯太太過去習慣喺星期天穿嘅水紋絲綢連衣裙出現,都不顯得奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到拿破崙嘴裡叼著煙斗在農舍花園裡漫步,也不顯得奇怪——不,甚至豬們把瓊斯先生的衣服從衣櫃裡拿出來穿上,拿破崙自己穿著黑外套、捕鼠人馬褲和皮綁腿出現,而他最寵愛的母豬穿著瓊斯太太過去習慣在星期天穿的水紋絲綢連衣裙出現,也不顯得奇怪。

passages.original: A week later, in the afternoon, a number of dog-carts drove up to the farm.
passages.vernacular: 一週後嘅下午,有啲雙輪輕馬車駛到農場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一週後的下午,有一些雙輪輕馬車駛到農場。

passages.original: A deputation of neighbouring farmers had been invited to make a tour of inspection.
passages.vernacular: 一個鄰近農場主嘅代表團被邀請嚟視察。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個鄰近農場主的代表團被邀請來視察。

passages.original: They were shown all over the farm, and expressed great admiration for everything they saw, especially the windmill.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋被領住參觀整個農場,對所睇到嘅一切表示極大讚賞,特別係風車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們被領著參觀整個農場,對所看到的一切表示極大讚賞,特別是風車。

passages.original: The animals were weeding the turnip field.
passages.vernacular: 動物哋正在蘿蔔田裡除草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動物們正在蘿蔔田裡除草。

passages.original: They worked diligently hardly raising their faces from the ground, and not knowing whether to be more frightened of the pigs or of the human visitors.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋勤奮地工作,幾乎不抬頭離開地面,唔知道係該更怕豬,定係更怕人類訪客。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們勤奮地工作,幾乎不抬頭離開地面,不知道是該更怕豬,還是更怕人類訪客。

passages.original: That evening loud laughter and bursts of singing came from the farmhouse.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,農舍裡傳嚟大聲嘅笑同一陣陣歌聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,農舍裡傳來大聲的笑和一陣陣歌聲。

passages.original: And suddenly, at the sound of the mingled voices, the animals were stricken with curiosity.
passages.vernacular: 突然,聽到混雜嘅聲音,動物哋被好奇心攫住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然,聽到混雜的聲音,動物們被好奇心攫住了。

passages.original: What could be happening in there, now that for the first time animals and human beings were meeting on terms of equality?
passages.vernacular: 而家動物同人類第一次以平等嘅身分會面,裡面可能發生乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在動物和人類第一次以平等的身分會面,裡面可能發生什麼?

passages.original: With one accord they began to creep as quietly as possible into the farmhouse garden.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋一致開始盡可能安靜地爬進農舍花園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們一致開始盡可能安靜地爬進農舍花園。

passages.original: At the gate they paused, half frightened to go on but Clover led the way in.
passages.vernacular: 喺門口佢哋停下嚟,半係害怕唔敢往前走,但三葉草領頭進去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在門口它們停下來,半是害怕不敢往前走,但三葉草領頭進去了。

passages.original: They tiptoed up to the house, and such animals as were tall enough peered in at the dining-room window.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋踮住腳走近房子,嗰啲夠高嘅動物往餐廳窗子裡窺視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們踮著腳走近房子,那些夠高的動物往餐廳窗子裡窺視。

passages.original: There, round the long table, sat half a dozen farmers and half a dozen of the more eminent pigs, Napoleon himself occupying the seat of honour at the head of the table.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰度,長桌周圍坐住六七個農場主同六七頭較出名嘅豬,拿破崙本人坐喺桌子上首嘅榮譽席。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那裡,長桌周圍坐著六七個農場主和六七頭較出名的豬,拿破崙本人坐在桌子上首的榮譽席。

passages.original: The pigs appeared completely at ease in their chairs.
passages.vernacular: 豬哋坐喺椅子裡顯得完全自在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬們坐在椅子裡顯得完全自在。

passages.original: The company had been enjoying a game of cards but had broken off for the moment, evidently in order to drink a toast.
passages.vernacular: 呢一群人一直喺享受一局紙牌,但暫時中斷喇,顯然係為了乾杯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一群人一直在享受一局紙牌,但暫時中斷了,顯然是為了乾杯。

passages.original: A large jug was circulating, and the mugs were being refilled with beer.
passages.vernacular: 一個大壺喺傳遞,杯子喺重新斟滿啤酒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個大壺在傳遞,杯子在重新斟滿啤酒。

passages.original: No one noticed the wondering faces of the animals that gazed in at the window.
passages.vernacular: 冇人注意到從窗外往裡睇嘅動物哋驚奇嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人注意到從窗外往裡看的動物們驚奇的臉。

passages.original: Mr. Pilkington, of Foxwood, had stood up, his mug in his hand.
passages.vernacular: 狐林嘅皮爾金頓先生站起嚟,手裡攞住杯子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狐林的皮爾金頓先生站起來,手裡拿著杯子。

passages.original: In a moment, he said, he would ask the present company to drink a toast.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,過一會兒佢要請在座各位乾杯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,過一會兒他要請在座各位乾杯。

passages.original: But before doing so, there were a few words that he felt it incumbent upon him to say.
passages.vernacular: 但喺咁樣做之前,佢覺得有責任講幾句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在這樣做之前,他覺得有責任說幾句話。

passages.original: It was a source of great satisfaction to him, he said--and, he was sure, to all others present--to feel that a long period of mistrust and misunderstanding had now come to an end.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,令佢好滿意——佢相信所有在座嘅人都一樣——嘅係,感到一個長期嘅不信任同誤解時期而家已經結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,令他非常滿意——他相信所有在座的人也一樣——的是,感到一個長期的不信任和誤解時期現在已經結束。

passages.original: There had been a time--not that he, or any of the present company, had shared such sentiments--but there had been a time when the respected proprietors of Animal Farm had been regarded, he would not say with hostility, but perhaps with a certain measure of misgiving, by their human neighbours.
passages.vernacular: 曾經有一個時期——唔係佢,或任何在座嘅人曾有呢種情感——但曾有一個時期,動物農莊受尊敬嘅所有者,被佢哋嘅人類鄰居睇待,佢不講係敵意,但或者係帶住某種程度嘅疑慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 曾經有一個時期——不是他,或任何在座的人曾有這種情感——但曾有一個時期,動物農莊受尊敬的所有者,被他們的人類鄰居看待,他不說是敵意,但也許是帶著某種程度的疑慮。

passages.original: Unfortunate incidents had occurred, mistaken ideas had been current.
passages.vernacular: 發生過不幸嘅事件,流行過錯誤嘅想法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 發生過不幸的事件,流行過錯誤的想法。

passages.original: It had been felt that the existence of a farm owned and operated by pigs was somehow abnormal and was liable to have an unsettling effect in the neighbourhood.
passages.vernacular: 有人覺得由豬擁有同經營嘅農場嘅存在,唔知怎嘅係不正常嘅,可能對附近地區產生不安定嘅影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人覺得由豬擁有和經營的農場的存在,不知怎的是不正常的,可能對附近地區產生不安定的影響。

passages.original: Too many farmers had assumed, without due enquiry, that on such a farm a spirit of licence and indiscipline would prevail.
passages.vernacular: 太多農場主未經適當詢問,就假定喺咁樣嘅農場上會盛行放縱同無紀律嘅精神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太多農場主未經適當詢問,就假定在這樣的農場上會盛行放縱和無紀律的精神。

passages.original: They had been nervous about the effects upon their own animals, or even upon their human employees.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋曾為佢對佢哋自己動物,甚至對佢哋嘅人類雇員嘅影響而緊張。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們曾為它對他們自己動物,甚至對他們的人類雇員的影響而緊張。

passages.original: But all such doubts were now dispelled.
passages.vernacular: 但所有呢啲疑慮而家都消除喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但所有這些疑慮現在都消除了。

passages.original: Today he and his friends had visited Animal Farm and inspected every inch of it with their own eyes, and what did they find?
passages.vernacular: 今日佢同佢嘅朋友哋拜訪咗動物農莊,用自己嘅眼睛檢查咗佢嘅每一寸,佢哋發現咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天他和他的朋友們拜訪了動物農莊,用自己的眼睛檢查了它的每一寸,他們發現了什麼?

passages.original: Not only the most up-to-date methods, but a discipline and an orderliness which should be an example to all farmers everywhere.
passages.vernacular: 不僅係最現代嘅方法,而且係一種應成為各地所有農場主榜樣嘅紀律同秩序。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不僅是最現代的方法,而且是一種應成為各地所有農場主榜樣的紀律和秩序。

passages.original: He believed that he was right in saying that the lower animals on Animal Farm did more work and received less food than any animals in the county.
passages.vernacular: 佢相信佢講得對:動物農莊嘅下等動物比郡裡任何動物都做更多嘅工作,得到更少嘅食物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他相信他說得對:動物農莊的下等動物比郡裡任何動物都做更多的工作,得到更少的食物。

passages.original: Indeed, he and his fellow-visitors today had observed many features which they intended to introduce on their own farms immediately.
passages.vernacular: 確實,佢同今日嘅同行訪客觀察到許多特點,佢哋打算即刻喺自己嘅農場上引進。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,他和今天的同行訪客觀察到許多特點,他們打算立刻在自己的農場上引進。

passages.original: He would end his remarks, he said, by emphasising once again the friendly feelings that subsisted, and ought to subsist, between Animal Farm and its neighbours.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,佢將以再次強調動物農莊同其鄰居之間存在嘅、都應該存在嘅友好感情嚟結束佢嘅講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,他將以再次強調動物農莊與其鄰居之間存在的、也應該存在的友好感情來結束他的講話。

passages.original: Between pigs and human beings there was not, and there need not be, any clash of interests whatever.
passages.vernacular: 豬同人類之間冇、都不需要有任何利益衝突。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬和人類之間沒有、也不需要有任何利益衝突。

passages.original: Their struggles and their difficulties were one.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅鬥爭同困難係一樣嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們的鬥爭和困難是一樣的。

passages.original: Was not the labour problem the same everywhere?
passages.vernacular: 勞工問題喺各處不都係一樣嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勞工問題在各處不都是一樣的嗎?

passages.original: Here it became apparent that Mr. Pilkington was about to spring some carefully prepared witticism on the company, but for a moment he was too overcome by amusement to be able to utter it.
passages.vernacular: 講到呢度顯然皮爾金頓先生要向在座嘅人拋出一句精心準備嘅妙語,但有一刻佢被樂趣淹沒,以致講不出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說到這裡顯然皮爾金頓先生要向在座的人拋出一句精心準備的妙語,但有一刻他被樂趣淹沒,以致說不出來。

passages.original: After much choking, during which his various chins turned purple, he managed to get it out: “If you have your lower animals to contend with,” he said, “we have our lower classes!”
passages.vernacular: 嗆咗好久,其間佢嘅幾層下巴變成紫色,佢終於把佢講出嚟:「如果你哋要對付你哋嘅下等動物,」佢講,「我哋有我哋嘅下等階級!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗆了很久,其間他的幾層下巴變成紫色,他終於把它說出來:「如果你們要對付你們的下等動物,」他說,「我們有我們的下等階級!」

passages.original: This BON MOT set the table in a roar; and Mr. Pilkington once again congratulated the pigs on the low rations, the long working hours, and the general absence of pampering which he had observed on Animal Farm.
passages.vernacular: 呢句妙語使整張桌子哄堂大笑;皮爾金頓先生再次祝賀豬哋喺動物農莊所觀察到嘅低口糧、長工時,同普遍缺乏嬌慣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這句妙語使整張桌子哄堂大笑;皮爾金頓先生再次祝賀豬們在動物農莊所觀察到的低口糧、長工時,和普遍缺乏嬌慣。

passages.original: And now, he said finally, he would ask the company to rise to their feet and make certain that their glasses were full.
passages.vernacular: 而家,佢最後講,佢要請在座嘅人站起嚟,確保佢哋嘅杯子係滿嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,他最後說,他要請在座的人站起來,確保他們的杯子是滿的。

passages.original: “Gentlemen,” concluded Mr. Pilkington, “gentlemen, I give you a toast: To the prosperity of Animal Farm!”
passages.vernacular: 「先生哋,」皮爾金頓先生結束講,「先生哋,我敬你哋一杯:祝動物農莊繁榮昌盛!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「先生們,」皮爾金頓先生結束說,「先生們,我敬你們一杯:祝動物農莊繁榮昌盛!」

passages.original: There was enthusiastic cheering and stamping of feet.
passages.vernacular: 一陣熱烈嘅歡呼同跺腳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣熱烈的歡呼和跺腳。

passages.original: Napoleon was so gratified that he left his place and came round the table to clink his mug against Mr. Pilkington’s before emptying it.
passages.vernacular: 拿破崙咁高興,佢離開座位,繞過桌子,把佢嘅杯子同皮爾金頓先生嘅碰咗一下,然後才一飲而盡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿破崙那麼高興,他離開座位,繞過桌子,把他的杯子與皮爾金頓先生的碰了一下,然後才一飲而盡。

passages.original: When the cheering had died down, Napoleon, who had remained on his feet, intimated that he too had a few words to say.
passages.vernacular: 歡呼平息後,仍站住嘅拿破崙暗示佢都有幾句話要講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡呼平息後,仍站著的拿破崙暗示他也有幾句話要說。

passages.original: Like all of Napoleon’s speeches, it was short and to the point.
passages.vernacular: 像拿破崙所有嘅演講一樣,佢簡短而切題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像拿破崙所有的演講一樣,它簡短而切題。

passages.original: He too, he said, was happy that the period of misunderstanding was at an end.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,佢都好高興誤解嘅時期已經結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,他也很高興誤解的時期已經結束。

passages.original: For a long time there had been rumours--circulated, he had reason to think, by some malignant enemy--that there was something subversive and even revolutionary in the outlook of himself and his colleagues.
passages.vernacular: 長期以來有傳聞——佢有理由認為係某個惡毒嘅敵人散佈嘅——講佢同佢嘅同事哋嘅觀點中有某種顛覆性甚至革命性嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 長期以來有傳聞——他有理由認為是某個惡毒的敵人散佈的——說他和他的同事們的觀點中有某種顛覆性甚至革命性的東西。

passages.original: They had been credited with attempting to stir up rebellion among the animals on neighbouring farms.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋被指責試圖喺鄰近農場嘅動物中煽動造反。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們被指責試圖在鄰近農場的動物中煽動造反。

passages.original: Nothing could be further from the truth!
passages.vernacular: 再冇比呢更遠離事實嘅喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再沒有比這更遠離事實的了!

passages.original: Their sole wish, now and in the past, was to live at peace and in normal business relations with their neighbours.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋而家同過去唯一嘅願望,係同鄰居和平相處,保持正常嘅商業關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們現在和過去唯一的願望,是與鄰居和平相處,保持正常的商業關係。

passages.original: This farm which he had the honour to control, he added, was a co-operative enterprise.
passages.vernacular: 佢補充講,佢有幸控制嘅呢個農場,係一個合作企業。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他補充說,他有幸控制的這個農場,是一個合作企業。

passages.original: The title-deeds, which were in his own possession, were owned by the pigs jointly.
passages.vernacular: 地契喺佢自己手中,由豬共同擁有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 地契在他自己手中,由豬共同擁有。

passages.original: He did not believe, he said, that any of the old suspicions still lingered, but certain changes had been made recently in the routine of the farm which should have the effect of promoting confidence still further.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,佢不相信任何舊嘅疑慮仍然存在,但最近農場嘅日常工作中作咗某些改變,應該能進一步增進信任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,他不相信任何舊的疑慮仍然存在,但最近農場的日常工作中作了某些改變,應該能進一步增進信任。

passages.original: Hitherto the animals on the farm had had a rather foolish custom of addressing one another as “Comrade.”
passages.vernacular: 到目前為止,農場上嘅動物有一個相當愚蠢嘅習慣,互相稱呼為「同志」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到目前為止,農場上的動物有一個相當愚蠢的習慣,互相稱呼為「同志」。

passages.original: This was to be suppressed.
passages.vernacular: 呢將被取締。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這將被取締。

passages.original: There had also been a very strange custom, whose origin was unknown, of marching every Sunday morning past a boar’s skull which was nailed to a post in the garden.
passages.vernacular: 仲有一個好奇怪嘅習慣,起源不明,每個星期天早晨列隊走過釘喺花園裡一根柱子上嘅公豬頭骨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有一個非常奇怪的習慣,起源不明,每個星期天早晨列隊走過釘在花園裡一根柱子上的公豬頭骨。

passages.original: This, too, would be suppressed, and the skull had already been buried.
passages.vernacular: 呢都將被取締,頭骨已經埋葬喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這也將被取締,頭骨已經埋葬了。

passages.original: His visitors might have observed, too, the green flag which flew from the masthead.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅訪客可能仲觀察到桅頂飄揚嘅綠旗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的訪客可能還觀察到桅頂飄揚的綠旗。

passages.original: If so, they would perhaps have noted that the white hoof and horn with which it had previously been marked had now been removed.
passages.vernacular: 如果係咁樣,佢哋或者注意到,以前標喺上面嘅白色蹄子同角,而家已被除去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是這樣,他們也許注意到,以前標在上面的白色蹄子和角,現在已被除去。

passages.original: It would be a plain green flag from now onwards.
passages.vernacular: 從而家起佢將係一面素綠旗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從現在起它將是一面素綠旗。

passages.original: He had only one criticism, he said, to make of Mr. Pilkington’s excellent and neighbourly speech.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,佢對皮爾金頓先生極好嘅、鄰里般嘅講話只有一個批評。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,他對皮爾金頓先生極好的、鄰里般的講話只有一個批評。

passages.original: Mr. Pilkington had referred throughout to “Animal Farm.”
passages.vernacular: 皮爾金頓先生通篇提到「動物農莊」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 皮爾金頓先生通篇提到「動物農莊」。

passages.original: He could not of course know--for he, Napoleon, was only now for the first time announcing it--that the name “Animal Farm” had been abolished.
passages.vernacular: 佢當然唔可能知道——因為佢,拿破崙,而家才第一次宣布——「動物農莊」呢個名字已被廢除。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他當然不可能知道——因為他,拿破崙,現在才第一次宣布——「動物農莊」這個名字已被廢除。

passages.original: Henceforward the farm was to be known as “The Manor Farm”--which, he believed, was its correct and original name.
passages.vernacular: 從今以後,農場將被稱為「曼諾農場」——佢相信,嗰才係佢正確嘅原名。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從今以後,農場將被稱為「曼諾農場」——他相信,那才是它正確的原名。

passages.original: “Gentlemen,” concluded Napoleon, “I will give you the same toast as before, but in a different form.
passages.vernacular: 「先生哋,」拿破崙結束講,「我敬你哋同樣嘅酒,但以不同嘅形式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「先生們,」拿破崙結束說,「我敬你們同樣的酒,但以不同的形式。

passages.original: Fill your glasses to the brim.
passages.vernacular: 把你哋嘅杯子斟滿到杯口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你們的杯子斟滿到杯口。

passages.original: Gentlemen, here is my toast: To the prosperity of The Manor Farm!”
passages.vernacular: 先生哋,呢個係我嘅祝酒詞:祝曼諾農場繁榮昌盛!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生們,這是我的祝酒詞:祝曼諾農場繁榮昌盛!」

passages.original: There was the same hearty cheering as before, and the mugs were emptied to the dregs.
passages.vernacular: 同先前一樣熱烈嘅歡呼,杯子被飲得一滴不剩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 和先前一樣熱烈的歡呼,杯子被喝得一滴不剩。

passages.original: But as the animals outside gazed at the scene, it seemed to them that some strange thing was happening.
passages.vernacular: 但外面嘅動物哋凝視呢個場面時,佢哋覺得有某種奇怪嘅事情正在發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但外面的動物們凝視這個場面時,它們覺得有某種奇怪的事情正在發生。

passages.original: What was it that had altered in the faces of the pigs?
passages.vernacular: 豬嘅臉上改變咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豬的臉上改變了什麼?

passages.original: Clover’s old dim eyes flitted from one face to another.
passages.vernacular: 三葉草嘅老眼昏花嘅眼睛從一張臉掃到另一張臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三葉草的老眼昏花的眼睛從一張臉掃到另一張臉。

passages.original: Some of them had five chins, some had four, some had three.
passages.vernacular: 有些有五層下巴,有些四層,有些三層。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些有五層下巴,有些四層,有些三層。

passages.original: But what was it that seemed to be melting and changing?
passages.vernacular: 但似乎正在融化同改變嘅係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但似乎正在融化和改變的是什麼?

passages.original: Then, the applause having come to an end, the company took up their cards and continued the game that had been interrupted, and the animals crept silently away.
passages.vernacular: 然後,掌聲結束,大家攞起紙牌繼續被打斷嘅牌局,動物哋悄悄地爬走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,掌聲結束,大家拿起紙牌繼續被打斷的牌局,動物們悄悄地爬走了。

passages.original: But they had not gone twenty yards when they stopped short.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋走唔到二十碼就停住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它們走不到二十碼就停住了。

passages.original: An uproar of voices was coming from the farmhouse.
passages.vernacular: 農舍裡傳嚟一陣嘈雜嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農舍裡傳來一陣嘈雜的聲音。

passages.original: They rushed back and looked through the window again.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋跑回去,又一次透過窗子睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們跑回去,又一次透過窗子看。

passages.original: Yes, a violent quarrel was in progress.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,一場激烈嘅爭吵正在進行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,一場激烈的爭吵正在進行。

passages.original: There were shoutings, bangings on the table, sharp suspicious glances, furious denials.
passages.vernacular: 有叫喊聲,拍桌子嘅聲音,尖銳而懷疑嘅目光,憤怒嘅否認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有叫喊聲,拍桌子的聲音,尖銳而懷疑的目光,憤怒的否認。

passages.original: The source of the trouble appeared to be that Napoleon and Mr. Pilkington had each played an ace of spades simultaneously.
passages.vernacular: 麻煩嘅根源似乎係拿破崙同皮爾金頓先生各自同時打出咗一張黑桃A。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麻煩的根源似乎是拿破崙和皮爾金頓先生各自同時打出了一張黑桃A。

passages.original: Twelve voices were shouting in anger, and they were all alike.
passages.vernacular: 十二個聲音憤怒地喊叫,而且佢哋全都一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十二個聲音憤怒地喊叫,而且它們全都一樣。

passages.original: No question, now, what had happened to the faces of the pigs.
passages.vernacular: 而家毫無疑問,豬嘅臉上發生咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在毫無疑問,豬的臉上發生了什麼。

passages.original: The creatures outside looked from pig to man, and from man to pig, and from pig to man again; but already it was impossible to say which was which.
passages.vernacular: 外面嘅生物哋從豬睇到人,從人睇到豬,又從豬睇到人;但已經唔可能講出邊個係邊個喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 外面的生物們從豬看到人,從人看到豬,又從豬看到人;但已經不可能說出哪個是哪個了。
